title: The Library Moves Upstairs
text:
The school library at Tunas Jaya feels different this term. The old reading room was small and dark, so the head teacher moved it upstairs. Students now spread their books across long wooden tables near the tall windows. A teacher opens the room at seven and locks it after the final lesson.

Members of the library club manage the borrowing desk during every break. They record each title in a thick notebook and remind readers about the return date. The club also designs posters for recent arrivals and displays them near the canteen. Last month the members counted four hundred loans, roughly twice the total in January. Comics and short novels remain the most popular choice among younger pupils.

Not every idea has succeeded, though. The club wanted a quiet corner for group revision, but the room quickly became noisy. Teachers therefore suggested a simple timetable instead. Group discussion is allowed after two, while mornings stay silent. The club secretary says that both readers and chatty visitors now seem satisfied.

text:
Rani's class spent three weeks collecting old paper for the school recycling project. The idea originated with Rani, who noticed how many exam sheets ended up in the bins. Her class asked every teacher to keep used paper in a large box by the door. On Fridays two pupils carried the heavy boxes to the shop room behind the hall.

Rani admits that the job was harder than she expected. The shop room filled up quickly, so the classes arranged an earlier collection day. Next term the project will include plastic bottles as well. title: The Fish Tables at Dawn
text:
The fish part of Pasar Baru wakes long before the rest of the town. Boats reach the beach at four, and workers push heavy boxes straight to the tables. Sellers cover each table with crushed ice, which keeps the fish firm until midday. By half past five the narrow path is already crowded with shoppers.

Prices change every single morning. When the sea has been rough, fewer boats go out, so a kilo of fish may cost twice the usual amount. Careful shoppers therefore arrive early and ask several tables before they choose. Restaurant cooks want the biggest fish, while families prefer smaller ones for frying.

The sellers share one worry. Melted ice leaves dirty water across the floor, and the drains block easily. Last year the market office fitted a wider pipe near the gate. Sellers also take turns to wash the path after they close. Most of them agree that the area smells much fresher than before.

qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: When the sea has been rough, fewer boats go out, so a kilo of fish may cost twice the usual amount.
qs.why: Teks bilang kalau laut kasar, perahu yang melaut sedikit dan harga sekilo ikan bisa dua kali lipat — sama isinya dengan klaim.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak cocok karena arah harganya sama; “Not stated” juga nggak, sebab hubungan cuaca dan harga tertulis jelas.

author: local news writer
setting: a coastal town market

title: Futsal Team Loses, Then Learns
text:
The school futsal team lost its first district match by five goals to two. Bagas, the captain, says the score looked worse than the actual game. Our players scored twice in the opening half and controlled the ball well. After the break, however, three quick goals changed everything.

The coach watched the recording with the team on Tuesday. She counted eleven moments when nobody guarded the space in front of the goalkeeper. The team also lost the ball because passes travelled too slowly across the court. Bagas admits that the players ignored her warnings during the second half.

Practice sessions now look considerably different. The squad trains for ninety minutes twice a week instead of one long session. Half of that time goes to defending, which the players used to find boring. The coach has also invited a former league player to join two sessions. The team meets a stronger school next month, and Bagas expects a closer result.
qs: What does this report focus on?
how a captain lost his place after one defeat
how a coach prepared a team for the district cup
how a district match had to be replayed twice
how one defeat changed a team's training

qs.evidence: Practice sessions now look considerably different.
qs.answer: how one defeat changed a team's training
qs.why: Laporannya mulai dari kalah 5-2 lalu menelusuri perubahan pola latihan sesudahnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Bagas masih kapten dan justru bicara di laporan itu, persiapannya datang setelah kalah bukan sebelum, dan pertandingannya nggak diulang.

qs: When did the team score its goals?
in the closing minutes of the match
just after the three quick goals
in the first half of the match
during the Tuesday training session

qs.evidence: Our players scored twice in the opening half and controlled the ball well.
qs.answer: in the first half of the match
qs.why: Pemain mencetak dua gol di babak pertama sambil menguasai bola dengan baik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga gol cepat justru datang setelah jeda, dan hari Selasa cuma dipakai menonton rekaman.

qs.why: Sekarang tim latihan sembilan puluh menit dua kali sepekan, ganti satu sesi panjang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sesi panjang itu cara lama, latihannya bukan tiap malam, dan separuh waktu latihan buat bertahan bukan setengah jam harian.

qs: What does the coach believe the team must improve?
keeping the ball for longer in attack

qs.evidence: She counted eleven moments when nobody guarded the space in front of the goalkeeper.
qs.answer: guarding the area just before the goal
qs.why: Dia menghitung sebelas momen ruang depan kiper dibiarkan kosong, jadi bagian bertahan itulah yang harus dibenahi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Mencetak gol di babak pertama sudah jalan, bola justru hilang karena umpan terlalu lambat, dan rekaman ditonton sekali bukan tiap laga.

True
False

qs.answer: False

qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bentrok dengan kata “ignored”; “Not stated” salah karena teks memang membahas peringatan itu.

author: sports desk of the school paper
setting: a covered school court

title: New Bus Route East of the River
text:
A new school bus route starts on Monday the fourteenth. The bus will serve the villages east of the river, where about forty pupils live. It leaves the market corner at half past six and reaches the school gate before seven. On the way home it departs from the car park at four.

Parents should register their children at the school office before Friday afternoon. The monthly fee is thirty thousand rupiah, which the school collects with the other charges. Pupils who already receive a travel grant pay nothing. Please bring a copy of the family card when you register.

The old route through the town centre remains completely unchanged. Drivers have promised to wait five minutes at every stop, so nobody needs to hurry. If heavy rain floods the low road, the bus will follow the longer path beside the fields. The office will send a short message to parents whenever such a delay happens.
qs: What does this notice announce?
why monthly school charges will rise next term
how a new car park will serve nearby villages
a new morning service for pupils across the river
why lessons will start later for country pupils

qs.evidence: The bus will serve the villages east of the river, where about forty pupils live.
qs.answer: a new morning service for pupils across the river
qs.why: Pengumumannya soal rute bus baru untuk murid dari desa-desa di timur sungai beserta aturannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Iurannya cuma disebut jumlahnya tanpa kenaikan, tempat parkir sudah ada dan dipakai untuk pulang, dan jam pelajaran nggak berubah.

qs: Where does the bus begin its morning trip?
at the school gate before seven
at the market corner in the village
at the car park behind the school
at a stop in the town centre

qs.evidence: It leaves the market corner at half past six and reaches the school gate before seven.
qs.answer: at the market corner in the village
qs.why: Bus berangkat dari sudut pasar setengah tujuh dan tiba di gerbang sekolah sebelum jam tujuh.
qs.whyOthersFail: Gerbang sekolah itu tujuan pagi, tempat parkir dipakai saat pulang, dan pusat kota jalur lama.

qs: Who does not have to pay the fee?

qs.answer: children who receive help with fares

qs.whyOthersFail: Tinggal di timur sungai, mendaftar sebelum Jumat, atau ikut rute lama nggak bikin iurannya hilang.

qs: Why will the bus sometimes take the longer path?

The market corner closes in the morning

qs.evidence: If heavy rain floods the low road, the bus will follow the longer path beside the fields.
qs.answer: Floods may cover the usual route
qs.why: Jalur panjang dipakai kalau hujan lebat membanjiri jalan rendah, jadi alasannya cuaca.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sopir cuma janji menunggu lima menit, nggak ada permintaan halte baru, dan sudut pasar tetap dipakai tiap pagi.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Pupils going home board the bus in the school car park."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Pupils going home board the bus in the school car park.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: On the way home it departs from the car park at four.
qs.why: Teks bilang bus pulang berangkat dari tempat parkir sekolah jam empat, jadi klaim ini cuma ganti kata.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh isi yang dibalik, padahal tempatnya sama; “Not stated” gugur karena titik pulang memang ditulis.

author: school office
setting: a school notice board

title: Two Wheels to School
text:
More pupils in this district now ride to school on two wheels. The district council painted a narrow cycle lane along the market road last year. Shops along the street had to move their tables back by a metre. Since then the number of bicycles at the school racks has grown steadily.

The lane is far from perfect, however. Motorbikes often use it when the main road becomes crowded, and parked cars block the corners. Younger riders therefore prefer the quiet route behind the old market. Teachers ask every cyclist to wear a bright shirt in the rainy season, because the sky darkens early.

The council has promised two further improvements. Workers will build a covered rack for eighty bicycles beside the sports hall. A repair stand with a pump will stand next to it, free for any rider. Pupils who cycle three days a week will also receive a small card for the school shop.
qs: What is this article mainly about?
how repair work slowed a busy market road
how one district made room for young cyclists
how shopkeepers fought a plan for a cycle lane
how a new sports hall changed school journeys

qs.evidence: More pupils in this district now ride to school on two wheels.
qs.answer: how one district made room for young cyclists
qs.why: Artikelnya soal jalur sepeda, masalahnya, dan fasilitas berikutnya untuk murid yang bersepeda ke sekolah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jalan utama cuma disebut ramai tanpa perbaikan, toko-toko menuruti aturan tanpa perlawanan, dan aula olahraga hanya penanda lokasi rak baru.

qs: What did the shops have to do?
They painted a line along the street

qs.answer: They set their tables one metre further in
qs.why: Toko-toko di jalan itu harus menarik meja mereka masuk satu meter.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang mengecat jalur itu dewan distrik, dan teks nggak menyebut toko tutup di musim hujan atau jualan minuman.

qs.whyOthersFail: “Rack” memang bisa berarti rak buku, tapi kalimat itu jelas menghitung sepeda, bukan tempat berteduh atau lahan mobil.

qs: Why do teachers ask riders to wear bright shirts?

qs.answer: Riders are easier to see when it darkens

qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak bahas kain cepat kering, lampu jalan di jalur sepeda, atau rencana seragam.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The cycle lane cost the council more than the covered rack."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The cycle lane cost the council more than the covered rack.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: The district council painted a narrow cycle lane along the market road last year.
qs.why: Teks cuma cerita dewan mengecat jalur dan berencana bikin rak; nggak ada satu angka biaya, jadi dua hal itu nggak pernah dibandingkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” maupun “False” butuh perbandingan harga yang memang nggak pernah ditulis.

author: district news writer
setting: a small town with a new cycle lane

title: A Leaking Roof in Row Three
text:
To the market office, I am writing for the six fruit sellers in row three of the district market. Our roof has leaked since the storm in April, and rain now falls straight onto our tables. Last week I lost twelve boxes of bananas because the water reached the lower shelf. Two of my neighbours have already moved to the pavement outside.

We have paid our stall rent punctually every single month for years. A local builder visited the row and said the repair would take only three days. He offered a price of one million rupiah for the whole roof. We are willing to share half of that amount if the office pays the rest.

Please send someone to look at the row before the next rainy week. I am at the market from five in the morning until midday on any weekday. My telephone number appears below my signature. Thank you kindly for reading this letter, Sari.
qs: Why does Sari write to the market office?
to ask the office to mend a leaking roof
to protest against a rise in the stall rent
to request a larger stall in a drier row
to recommend a builder the office could hire

qs.evidence: Our roof has leaked since the storm in April, and rain now falls straight onto our tables.
qs.answer: to ask the office to mend a leaking roof
qs.why: Suratnya meminta kantor pasar menangani atap baris tiga yang bocor sejak badai April.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sewanya justru dibayar tepat waktu tanpa keluhan tarif, ukuran kios nggak pernah dibahas, dan tukangnya cuma disebut sebagai sumber harga.

qs: What did Sari lose last week?
the lower shelf under her table
a dozen crates of bananas

qs.answer: a dozen crates of bananas
qs.why: Minggu lalu dia kehilangan dua belas kotak pisang karena air sampai ke rak bawah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rak bawah cuma kena air bukan hilang, tiga hari itu lama perbaikan, dan atapnya bocor bukan lepas.

qs.why: Hujan jatuh langsung ke meja di bawah atap bocor, jadi dua tetangga itu pindah ke luar biar dagangannya aman.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak menyebut sewa lebih murah di trotoar, perintah dari kantor pasar, atau arah jalan pembeli.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: False

qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena polaritasnya dibalik; “Not stated” juga salah karena tawaran bayar separuh tertulis.

author: Sari
setting: a district market office

title: The Folded Ticket
text:
Ilham had never played outside his own village before last August. His uncle entered him for the district badminton tournament in the town sports hall. The floor there was smooth and the lights were far brighter than the lamps at home. During the opening match his shoes squeaked so loudly that he laughed at himself.

He won that match comfortably, then lost the second one in three tight sets. His clever opponent kept the shuttle low and forced him to bend for every single return. Afterwards an older player showed him a simple exercise for his knees. Ilham wrote the instructions on the back of his ticket.

He has practised that particular exercise every single evening since the tournament. His village club now meets twice a week instead of once, because eleven new members joined after they heard his story. Ilham still keeps the folded ticket inside his racket bag. He says it reminds him that a defeat sometimes teaches more than an easy victory.
qs: What is this story mainly about?
how a village club nearly lost its members
how an uncle trained a young badminton player
how a new sports hall drew players from villages
what a first tournament away taught a player

qs.evidence: Ilham had never played outside his own village before last August.
qs.answer: what a first tournament away taught a player
qs.why: Ceritanya soal turnamen pertama Ilham di luar kampungnya dan apa yang dia bawa pulang dari kekalahan itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Klubnya justru bertambah anggota, omnya hanya mendaftarkan bukan melatih, dan aula kota cuma tempat turnamen berlangsung.

qs: What did Ilham notice about the hall?
the lamps hanging above the seats
the bright lights above the court
the badminton nets across the room
the marks left on the wooden floor

qs.evidence: The floor there was smooth and the lights were far brighter than the lamps at home.
qs.answer: the bright lights above the court
qs.why: Lantainya mulus dan lampunya jauh lebih terang daripada lampu di kampungnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Lampu di kampungnya justru yang lebih redup, jaring dan bekas di lantai nggak pernah disebut — lantainya malah digambarkan mulus.

qs.answer: Eleven newcomers signed up after his story
qs.why: Sebelas anggota baru masuk setelah dengar ceritanya, jadi jadwal latihan ditambah karena pesertanya banyak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Omnya nggak jadi pelatih, latihan lutut Ilham dilakukan sendiri tiap malam, dan aula kota nggak berhubungan dengan klub kampung.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "An experienced player taught Ilham a movement for his knees."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: An experienced player taught Ilham a movement for his knees.

qs.evidence: Afterwards an older player showed him a simple exercise for his knees.
qs.why: Pemain yang lebih senior menunjukkan latihan sederhana buat lutut, isinya sama dengan klaim ini.

author: village club member
setting: a district sports hall

title: Four Guitars, Twenty Members
text:
The music club at a school in this town owns only four guitars. Twenty members share them during the long break on Tuesday and Thursday. Two teachers lend their own instruments whenever the club prepares for a concert. A retired driver who lives opposite the school repairs broken strings for free.

Learning happens in careful steps. Beginners spend the first month on three simple songs and a steady beat. The club leader believes that patience matters more than speed. Older members write short pieces about daily life, and one of them mentions the bus queue outside the gate.

The club performs twice a year in the school hall. Tickets cost five thousand rupiah, and the money buys fresh strings for the following term. Last December the members collected enough for a second microphone. Their leader hopes that a local shop will lend an electric piano next season.
qs: What is this article mainly about?
how twenty members share four school guitars
how a neighbour keeps a school band playing

qs.answer: how twenty members share four school guitars

True
False
Not stated

author: hobby column writer
setting: a school hall in a hill town

title: Soup Beats Crisps in the Canteen
text:
The canteen changed its menu at the start of this term after a survey of three hundred pupils. Fried snacks now share the counter with fresh fruit, boiled corn and vegetable soup. The cook, Bu Nining, admits that she doubted the plan at first. During the opening week she prepared thirty portions of soup and sold only nine.

Attitudes shifted once the prices appeared on a large board. A bowl of soup costs less than a packet of crisps, and the fruit is cheaper still. Teachers also agreed to leave the front of the queue for younger classes. By the fourth week the soup pot was empty before the second break.

Some problems remain unsolved. The canteen still has no cold water in the afternoon, so many pupils buy sweet drinks outside the gate. The school council will discuss a water cooler at the next meeting. Bu Nining hopes that a small garden behind the kitchen will supply her vegetables next year.
qs: What does this report describe?
how a canteen's new menu slowly caught on
how a survey changed what teachers eat at work
how cooking lessons reached the youngest pupils
how a kitchen garden supplied a school canteen

False

author: school council reporter
setting: a secondary school canteen

title: Two Papers Change Places
text:
The mid-term examination timetable has changed for two subjects. The maths paper moves from Tuesday morning to Thursday afternoon. The science paper takes the empty Tuesday slot instead. All other papers keep their original date and time.

The reason is straightforward. Building work on the science block roof continues for three more days, and the noise would disturb any test nearby. The head teacher visited the site with the builder last week. They agreed that a quiet hall matters more than a fixed arrangement.

Pupils should check the printed sheet outside the staff room before the first paper. Anyone who has already booked transport for Thursday must speak to the office today. Candidates must bring their own pens, a ruler and a clear water bottle. The library stays open until five every evening during the examination week, and the reading room will hold extra chairs.
qs: What is this notice about?
why roof work will delay the whole exam week
why two papers swapped their dates
how a longer examination week was arranged

False

author: examinations office
setting: a school notice outside the staff room

title: A Garden in Paint Tins
text:
A narrow yard behind a rented house can still feed a family. In Cimahi several households grow chilli plants, green leaves and spring onions in old paint tins. The tins cost nothing, because a garage on the corner gives them away. Each container needs three holes in the base, or the roots quickly die.

The sun decides the whole plan. Green leaves accept a dark wall, while chilli plants demand at least five hours of direct light. Families therefore keep the tins on wooden boards that they can move during the day. Kitchen waste such as fruit skin becomes food for the soil in a covered pot next to the water pipe.

The saving is small but steady. One household counted forty thousand rupiah less on vegetables each month. Children usually take charge of watering, which happens before school and again in the evening. Neighbours exchange young plants across the fence, so nobody buys the same seeds twice.
qs: What is this article mainly about?
how families in Cimahi found cheaper housing
how a garage turned its waste into planting pots
why the price of chillies keeps rising
how a tiny yard can feed a household

qs.evidence: A narrow yard behind a rented house can still feed a family.
qs.answer: how a tiny yard can feed a household
qs.why: Artikelnya soal halaman sempit yang tetap bisa menghasilkan sayur, lengkap dengan cara dan penghematannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rumah sewa cuma latar bukan soal harga, garasinya hanya memberikan kaleng tanpa mengolahnya, dan teks bicara penghematan bukan kenaikan harga cabai.

qs: Where do the families get their tins?
from a shop on the corner
free from a garage nearby
from a seed seller in the market
from neighbours across the fence

qs.evidence: The tins cost nothing, because a garage on the corner gives them away.
qs.answer: free from a garage nearby
qs.why: Kalengnya gratis karena garasi di pojok jalan membagikannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang di pojok itu garasi bukan toko, dan yang ditukar dengan tetangga adalah bibit muda, bukan kaleng.

qs: In this article, what does "base" mean?
the dark wall behind the tins
the soil that feeds the roots
the bottom of the container
the board that holds the tin

qs.evidence: Each container needs three holes in the base, or the roots quickly die.
qs.answer: the bottom of the container
qs.why: Lubangnya dibuat di bagian bawah wadah supaya air keluar dan akarnya nggak mati.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dinding gelap, tanah, dan papan kayu memang ada di teks, tapi bukan tempat tiga lubang itu dibuat.

qs: Why do families keep the tins on boards they can move?
Plants can be moved into the sunshine
Children can water them more quickly
The tins are too heavy to lift alone
Neighbours borrow the boards for seeds

qs.evidence: Families therefore keep the tins on wooden boards that they can move during the day.
qs.answer: Plants can be moved into the sunshine
qs.why: Cahaya matahari yang menentukan susunan, jadi papannya digeser biar tiap tanaman kena sinar sesuai kebutuhannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Anak-anak menyiram dua kali sehari tanpa kaitan papan, beratnya kaleng nggak disebut, dan yang dipinjamkan ke tetangga bibit bukan papan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Chilli plants grow well in a dark corner of the yard."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Chilli plants grow well in a dark corner of the yard.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Green leaves accept a dark wall, while chilli plants demand at least five hours of direct light.
qs.why: Teks bilang cabai butuh minimal lima jam sinar langsung, sedangkan yang tahan tempat teduh itu sayuran berdaun.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertukar pelaku dengan tanaman berdaun; “Not stated” salah karena kebutuhan cahaya cabai tertulis.

author: family life columnist
setting: narrow yards behind rented houses

title: A Grey Bag Under Seat Fourteen
text:
To the lost property office, I travelled on your evening service from the city centre to my home town last Thursday. When I left the bus at the terminal, I forgot a small grey bag under my seat. My seat number was fourteen, on the left side behind the driver. The vehicle continued towards the next city immediately after I stepped down.

The bag contains a school report, a charger and a blue pencil case. Nothing inside it is expensive, yet the report matters enormously to me. My teacher requires the signed pages before the end of the month. I have already asked the ticket desk twice, and the clerk suggested that I write to you.

Please check the office where your drivers deposit forgotten property. I can collect the bag on any afternoon except Wednesday, when I have extra lessons. My mother can also fetch it if you prefer to release it to an adult. Thank you sincerely for your help, Wisnu.
qs: Why has Wisnu sent this email?
to book a seat on the evening service
to claim the price of a ticket back
to report an item forgotten on a bus
to complain about a driver who left early

qs.evidence: When I left the bus at the terminal, I forgot a small grey bag under my seat.
qs.answer: to report an item forgotten on a bus
qs.why: Wisnu menulis karena tas kelabunya tertinggal di bawah kursi dan dia ingin tas itu dicari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dia nggak memesan kursi, nggak menuntut uang tiket, dan busnya memang langsung jalan tanpa dia menyalahkan sopir.

qs: Where was Wisnu sitting on the bus?
on the right, near the back door
in the seat beside his mother
at the very back of the bus
on the left, in row fourteen

qs.evidence: My seat number was fourteen, on the left side behind the driver.
qs.answer: on the left, in row fourteen
qs.why: Nomor kursinya empat belas, di sisi kiri persis di belakang sopir.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kursinya di kiri bukan kanan, dia bepergian sendiri, dan tempatnya di depan bukan di belakang bus.

qs.whyOthersFail: Sopirnya nggak pernah dihubungi, ibunya baru ditawarkan sebagai pengambil nanti, dan tasnya belum ketemu.

qs: Why does the report matter so much to Wisnu?

qs.answer: His teacher needs the signed pages soon

qs.whyOthersFail: Isi tasnya justru nggak mahal, dan teks nggak bilang ibunya atau petugas tiket ingin melihat rapor itu.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: True

qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh larangan yang lebih luas; “Not stated” gugur karena jadwal ambilnya jelas ditulis.

author: Wisnu
setting: an intercity bus company office

title: The Soup That Stayed the Same Price
text:
Every school holiday Nadia helps her grandmother at the soup stall in the old market. The two of them arrive at four, while the lamps above the meat tables are still burning. Nadia washes the bowls, cuts the cabbage and fills the huge kettle. Her grandmother tastes the broth carefully before the first customer appears.

Last August a food writer from the city stopped at the stall by accident. He published a short piece about the soup with a photograph of the kettle. Within a week the queue reached the fish section, and the family sold out before ten. Nadia's grandmother refused to raise the price, even when a cousin urged her to do so.

Those busy weeks taught the family a valuable lesson. The family now prepares half of the vegetables the previous night, so the morning feels calmer. Nadia keeps a notebook of every change they have tried since the article appeared. She insists the stall still smells precisely as it did when she was six.
qs: What is this story mainly about?
how a food writer learnt to cook a local soup
how a family holiday in the city began
how a girl helps at her family's soup stall
how one long queue upset the whole market

qs.evidence: Every school holiday Nadia helps her grandmother at the soup stall in the old market.
qs.answer: how a girl helps at her family's soup stall
qs.why: Ceritanya soal Nadia yang tiap libur sekolah membantu neneknya di kios sup pasar lama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis makanan cuma mampir sekali dan menulis, liburannya dipakai bekerja bukan pergi ke kota, dan antrean panjang nggak digambarkan mengganggu pasar.

qs: What jobs does Nadia do at the stall?
washing bowls and cutting cabbage
tasting the broth before customers come
serving the customers in the queue
writing the family recipe in a notebook

qs.evidence: Nadia washes the bowls, cuts the cabbage and fills the huge kettle.
qs.answer: washing bowls and cutting cabbage
qs.why: Nadia mencuci mangkuk, memotong kubis, dan mengisi kuali besar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang mencicipi kuah itu neneknya, dan buku catatan Nadia isinya perubahan yang dicoba, bukan resep atau daftar pesanan.

qs: What happened after the writer's piece appeared?

The stall sold out before ten

qs.answer: The stall sold out before ten
qs.why: Dalam sepekan antreannya sampai bagian ikan dan supnya habis sebelum jam sepuluh.
qs.whyOthersFail: Neneknya justru menolak menaikkan harga, sepupunya cuma menyarankan, dan keluarganya tetap di pasar lama.

qs: What does the grandmother's choice about the price show?

She wants to open a second stall soon

qs.answer: She puts her regular customers first

qs.whyOthersFail: Dia justru menolak saran sepupunya, dan teks nggak menyebut kios kedua atau harapan penulis itu kembali.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The food writer came back to the stall a second time."
True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: Not stated

author: market neighbour
setting: a busy town market before dawn

title: Twenty Carts After Dark
text:
The night market on Jalan Damai opens when the office workers head home. Twenty small stands wait in two neat rows under the strings of yellow lamps. Fish on sticks, banana cakes and sweet tea fill the air with heavy smells. The busiest hour arrives between seven and eight, especially at the end of the month.

Each seller has a different method of attracting attention. One woman rings a small bell whenever her pan of cakes is ready. Another stand offers a free glass of water to any customer who waits longer than ten minutes. The fish seller keeps her fire low, because burnt food drives people away.

Simple rules protect the whole row. Every stand must leave a gap of one metre for walking, and the owners sweep their own space at eleven. The neighbourhood association collects a small daily payment for rubbish and lighting. Sellers who ignore the sweeping rule lose their place for two weeks.
qs: What is this article mainly about?
how tea prices differ across the night market
how one seller's bell changed a night market
how office workers spend their evenings out
how a row of night stalls keeps order

qs.answer: how a row of night stalls keeps order
qs.why: Artikelnya soal cara satu deret lapak malam bekerja: jam sibuk, cara menarik pembeli, dan aturan bersama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Harga teh nggak pernah ditulis, belnya cuma trik satu penjual, dan pekerja kantor hanya penanda jam buka.

qs: When is the market at its busiest?
around eleven at night
in the first hour after seven
as soon as the offices close
just after the lamps are lit

qs.answer: in the first hour after seven
qs.why: Jam tersibuk datang antara tujuh dan delapan, terutama di akhir bulan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jam sebelas justru waktu menyapu, dan pasar baru buka saat pekerja kantor pulang — bukan langsung sibuk.

qs.whyOthersFail: Air gratis itu cara lapak lain, api kecil urusan penjual ikan, dan lampu kuning menerangi seluruh deret.

qs.answer: Burnt food loses her customers
qs.why: Api dijaga kecil karena makanan yang hangus bikin orang menjauh.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak menyebut harga kayu bakar atau panas lampu, dan jarak satu meter itu aturan jalan, bukan soal api.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Traders who forget the sweeping rule may keep their place."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Traders who forget the sweeping rule may keep their place.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Sellers who ignore the sweeping rule lose their place for two weeks.
qs.why: Yang mengabaikan aturan menyapu justru kehilangan tempat selama dua pekan, jadi klaim ini kebalikan aturannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bentrok dengan hukuman yang ditulis; “Not stated” salah karena sanksinya jelas ada.

author: town life writer
setting: a street market in the evening

title: The Running Club Finds a Safer Route
text:
The running club has grown from nine members to thirty-four since March. Pupils meet at half past five in the morning, before the sun becomes strong. They run three laps of the field, then follow the quiet road towards the bridge. A parent on a motorbike rides behind the last runner for safety.

Two changes explain the sudden interest. The club now measures every member's time with a borrowed stopwatch and writes the results on a chart. Runners can therefore notice small improvements each week, which keeps them coming back. The school also allows members to shower before the first lesson.

Not everything has gone smoothly this term. Three members hurt their ankles on the rough path near the bridge, so the coach changed the route. The club has asked the district office to repair that stretch of road. Meanwhile the group runs twice around the market square, which the members find less pleasant but safer.

how a broken road held back a running club
how a running club grew and changed its ways
how a school race against neighbours was won

qs.whyOthersFail: Jalur rusak cuma satu masalah dan klubnya tetap jalan, nggak ada lomba antar sekolah, dan pelatihnya masih memimpin.

True
False
Not stated

author: school paper sports desk
setting: a school field and the road nearby

title: Rubbish Cart Twice a Week
text:
From the first of next month the rubbish cart will visit our street twice a week. The new days are Tuesday and Saturday, both in the early morning. Households should place their bags outside the gate before six. Bags left after the cart has passed will stay on the pavement until the following visit.

The change follows two months of complaints about the smell near the corner shop. The old single collection could not hold the waste of forty families. Our monthly payment rises from eight thousand to twelve thousand rupiah. The office will collect that amount together with the security fee.

Please separate bottles and tins into the blue basket beside the guard post. A collector from the recycling group empties the basket every Friday and pays the money into our street fund. Kitchen waste belongs in the ordinary bags, not in the basket. Any household with a question may visit the office at the weekend.

True
False
Not stated

author: neighbourhood office
setting: a residential street notice board

title: A Small Station Grows Up
text:
Ten years ago the small station at Kedungjati served only six trains a day. Today twenty-two trains stop there, and the waiting room is often full by seven. Workers have widened the platform and added a metal roof over half of it. A ticket machine now stands beside the office, though many passengers still prefer the counter.

The majority of travellers come from the villages north of the line. They arrive on motorbikes and leave them in a guarded yard for two thousand rupiah. The yard fills before eight, so latecomers park along the fence and worry all day. A local group has asked the railway company for a second parking area.

Trains are not the only recent change. Two food stalls have opened near the entrance, and a small shop sells cheap umbrellas in the rainy season. Announcements are now read in two languages instead of one. The station master says that the greatest problem remains the narrow road that leads to the gate.
qs: What is the main subject of this article?
why parking a motorbike has become expensive
how a new road reached a village station
how a small station changed in ten years
how umbrella sellers survive the rainy season

qs.evidence: Workers have widened the platform and added a metal roof over half of it.
qs.answer: how a small station changed in ten years
qs.why: Artikelnya membandingkan stasiun kecil sepuluh tahun lalu dengan sekarang: kereta, peron, dan fasilitasnya bertambah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tarif parkir tetap dua ribu tanpa cerita kenaikan, jalan ke gerbang justru masih sempit, dan payung cuma satu dagangan kecil.

qs: How many trains stop at the station now?
about ten trains a day
twenty-two trains a day
six trains every morning

qs.evidence: Today twenty-two trains stop there, and the waiting room is often full by seven.
qs.answer: twenty-two trains a day
qs.why: Sekarang dua puluh dua kereta berhenti di stasiun itu setiap hari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Enam kereta itu angka sepuluh tahun lalu, dan dua puluh dua itu hitungan harian — bukan per jam.

qs: In this article, what does "counter" mean?
a machine that prints tickets
the number printed on a ticket
a desk with a clerk behind it

qs.evidence: A ticket machine now stands beside the office, though many passengers still prefer the counter.
qs.answer: a desk with a clerk behind it
qs.why: Banyak penumpang lebih suka “counter”, yaitu meja layanan yang ada petugasnya, bukan mesin tiket.
qs.whyOthersFail: “Counter” memang bisa berarti alat penghitung atau meja warung, tapi kalimatnya justru mempertentangkannya dengan mesin tiket.

qs: Why do some riders worry all day?
The ticket counter may close early
Their bikes stand outside the guarded yard
The metal roof covers only half
Their train may leave before eight

qs.evidence: The yard fills before eight, so latecomers park along the fence and worry all day.
qs.answer: Their bikes stand outside the guarded yard
qs.why: Yang datang telat parkir di pinggir pagar, di luar halaman berpenjaga, makanya motornya nggak terjaga.
qs.whyOthersFail: Loket tetap dilayani petugas, atap separuh cuma soal peron, dan jam delapan itu batas halaman penuh — bukan jadwal kereta.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Passengers can hear station announcements in more than one language."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Passengers can hear station announcements in more than one language.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Announcements are now read in two languages instead of one.
qs.why: Pengumuman sekarang dibacakan dalam dua bahasa, jadi klaim soal lebih dari satu bahasa memang benar.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh jumlah bahasa yang dibalik; “Not stated” gugur karena teks menyebutnya langsung.

author: transport page writer
setting: a rural station on a busy line

title: Sixty Old Shops on the Wall
text:
Dear Ibu Ratna, I am writing on behalf of the media club about our photo project. We have collected sixty pictures of old shops in the town centre. Each picture carries a short caption with the name of the owner and the year of opening. Two members have also recorded short interviews on a borrowed phone.

We would like to display the entire collection in the library corridor during the annual reading week. The frames would occupy roughly eight metres of wall, which the librarian has already offered. Printing the whole set costs one hundred thousand rupiah altogether. The club can pay half from last year's fund, so we ask the school for the rest.

Could we possibly meet you later this week after the fourth lesson to discuss the arrangement? We shall bring a printed sample plus the complete list of participating shops. If that does not suit you, any afternoon next week remains possible. Thank you for your patience with our numerous questions, Yoga.
qs: Why has Yoga written this email?
to invite a teacher to the annual reading week
to order sixty frames from a local shop
to report a club phone that was damaged
to ask the school to support a photo display

qs.evidence: We would like to display the entire collection in the library corridor during the annual reading week.
qs.answer: to ask the school to support a photo display
qs.why: Yoga meminta dukungan sekolah untuk memajang enam puluh foto, termasuk sisa biaya cetaknya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dia justru meminta waktu bertemu bukan mengundang, bingkainya nggak dipesan dari toko, dan ponsel pinjaman nggak dilaporkan rusak.

qs: What information do the captions give?
the year the club was founded
who owned the shop and when it opened
a short interview with each owner
the name of the club photographer

qs.evidence: Each picture carries a short caption with the name of the owner and the year of opening.
qs.answer: who owned the shop and when it opened
qs.why: Tiap foto punya keterangan pendek berisi nama pemilik dan tahun toko itu buka.
qs.whyOthersFail: Wawancara direkam terpisah lewat ponsel, dan tahun berdirinya klub maupun nama pemotretnya nggak pernah ditulis.

qs: What have two members already finished?
printed all sixty photographs
made a few audio recordings
put the pictures into frames
paid the librarian for the wall

qs.evidence: Two members have also recorded short interviews on a borrowed phone.
qs.answer: made a few audio recordings
qs.why: Dua anggota sudah merekam wawancara pendek memakai ponsel pinjaman.
qs.whyOthersFail: Cetakannya belum dibayar, bingkainya baru rencana, dan dinding koridor ditawarkan pustakawan tanpa biaya.

qs: What does the club want from the school?
a longer stretch of corridor wall
permission to borrow a school phone
the other half of the printing cost
an extra lesson for the media club

qs.evidence: The club can pay half from last year's fund, so we ask the school for the rest.
qs.answer: the other half of the printing cost
qs.why: Klub sanggup bayar separuh dari dana tahun lalu, jadi yang diminta ke sekolah adalah sisa biaya cetak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dindingnya sudah ditawarkan pustakawan, ponselnya sudah dipinjam, dan jam pelajaran cuma dipakai buat waktu bertemu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The club photographed every old shop in the town."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The club photographed every old shop in the town.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: We have collected sixty pictures of old shops in the town centre.
qs.why: Teks cuma menyebut enam puluh foto toko lama di pusat kota; apakah itu semua toko lama di kota nggak pernah dibilang.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” butuh cakupan yang nggak ditulis; “False” juga nggak bisa karena teks nggak menyebut toko yang terlewat.

author: Yoga
setting: a school library corridor

title: Nine Pairs, One Council
text:
Nine pairs of candidates stood for the student council this year, the largest number since the school opened. Each pair made a poster and a short speech for the Friday assembly. The teachers allowed no printed leaflets, so most pairs used social media instead. Voting happened in the hall between the second and the fourth lesson.

The winning pair promised three practical measures. They want a covered shelter at the bicycle gate, longer library hours and a suggestion box beside the canteen. Their speech mentioned the price of drinks, which drew loud applause from the youngest classes. Four hundred and twelve pupils voted, roughly eighty per cent of the school.

The losing candidates have not disappeared. Two of them took places on the environment team, which the new leaders created last week. A teacher will check every promise at the end of each term. The head of the council says that the shelter may take longer than the pupils expect.
qs: What does this report describe?
how a bicycle shelter was finally approved
how longer library hours changed revision
how drink prices decided a school vote
how a school chose its new council leaders

qs.evidence: Nine pairs of candidates stood for the student council this year, the largest number since the school opened.
qs.answer: how a school chose its new council leaders
qs.why: Laporannya soal pemilihan pengurus dengan sembilan pasang calon, proses pemungutan, dan apa yang terjadi sesudahnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Halte baru justru diperkirakan lama, jam perpustakaan masih janji, dan harga minuman hanya satu bagian pidato — bukan penentu suara.

qs: How did most pairs reach the voters?
through posts on social media
with leaflets printed at school
by visiting each classroom in turn
during the Friday assembly only

qs.evidence: The teachers allowed no printed leaflets, so most pairs used social media instead.
qs.answer: through posts on social media
qs.why: Karena selebaran cetak dilarang guru, sebagian besar pasangan pakai media sosial.
qs.whyOthersFail: Selebaran justru dilarang, kunjungan ke kelas nggak pernah disebut, dan upacara Jumat cuma tempat pidato singkat.

qs: In this report, what does "measures" mean?
the sizes of the planned shelter
the words used in a speech
steps that will be carried out
the votes counted in the hall

qs.evidence: The winning pair promised three practical measures.
qs.answer: steps that will be carried out
qs.why: Tiga hal yang dijanjikan pemenang semuanya rencana tindakan, jadi “measures” berarti langkah yang akan dikerjakan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “Measure” memang bisa berarti ukuran, tapi kalimatnya menyebut tiga janji praktis — bukan dimensi halte atau hitungan suara.

qs: Why did the youngest classes applaud so loudly?
They already knew both candidates well
Cheaper drinks would save them money
They wanted the library open longer
They disliked the rule about leaflets

qs.evidence: Their speech mentioned the price of drinks, which drew loud applause from the youngest classes.
qs.answer: Cheaper drinks would save them money
qs.why: Yang disebut dalam pidato itu harga minuman, hal yang paling kena ke kantong murid kecil, makanya mereka bertepuk keras.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak bilang mereka kenal kandidatnya, dan jam perpustakaan maupun aturan selebaran nggak dikaitkan dengan tepuk tangan itu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The council will check its own promises without any teacher."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The council will check its own promises without any teacher.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: A teacher will check every promise at the end of each term.
qs.why: Yang memeriksa tiap janji di akhir semester justru seorang guru, jadi klaim tanpa guru itu bertentangan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” membalik siapa yang memeriksa; “Not stated” gugur karena tugas guru itu ditulis.

author: school paper reporter
setting: a school hall on voting day

title: Five Pictures Every Sunday
text:
Twelve pupils in Klaten devote their Sunday mornings to photographing streets with ordinary phones. The group began after a teacher demonstrated how the light shifts shortly before eight. Members walk the identical three roads every month and compare the results afterwards. Nobody owns a costly camera, and nobody seems bothered.

The rules of the group are peculiar but genuinely useful. Each member may keep only five pictures from a whole morning, which forces careful choices. Every photograph must include something that moves, such as a bicycle or a flag. Members write one sentence about each picture, because a caption often explains more than the image itself.

The project has gradually reached a wider audience. A coffee shop near the square hangs six pictures each month and pays nothing for them. Two members now run a brief session at the primary school every Saturday afternoon. The group leader says the greatest reward is noticing details that she walked past for years.
qs: What is this article mainly about?
how a coffee shop found free decoration
how a teacher's photographs reached a gallery
how primary pupils learnt to use a camera
how a photo group works with plain phones

qs.evidence: Twelve pupils in Klaten devote their Sunday mornings to photographing streets with ordinary phones.
qs.answer: how a photo group works with plain phones
qs.why: Artikelnya soal dua belas murid yang memotret jalanan tiap Minggu pagi hanya dengan ponsel biasa dan aturan mereka.
qs.whyOthersFail: Warung kopi dan sesi di SD cuma dampak proyeknya, dan gurunya hanya menunjukkan soal cahaya di awal tanpa memamerkan karyanya.

qs: What must every photograph include?
the name of the road
something that is moving
a member of the group
one shop in the square

qs.evidence: Every photograph must include something that moves, such as a bicycle or a flag.
qs.answer: something that is moving
qs.why: Setiap foto wajib memuat sesuatu yang bergerak, misalnya sepeda atau bendera.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nama jalan cuma bagian rute bulanan, dan teks nggak mewajibkan ada anggota atau toko di dalam foto.

qs: In this article, what does "reward" mean?
a prize given by the coffee shop
money earned from the pictures
a place in the Saturday session
the best thing the work brings

qs.evidence: The group leader says the greatest reward is noticing details that she walked past for years.
qs.answer: the best thing the work brings
qs.why: Buat ketua grup, hal paling berharga yang dia dapat adalah mulai melihat detail kecil, jadi “reward” di sini hasil batin.
qs.whyOthersFail: “Reward” memang sering berarti hadiah atau uang, tapi warung kopi nggak membayar apa pun dan sesi Sabtu bukan imbalan.

qs: Why does the group limit the number of pictures?
The phones have very little space
The coffee shop hangs only six
Members must choose with care
The teacher checks each file

qs.evidence: Each member may keep only five pictures from a whole morning, which forces careful choices.
qs.answer: Members must choose with care
qs.why: Batas lima foto memaksa anggota memilih dengan hati-hati, artinya mereka mikir dulu sebelum memotret.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak menyebut memori ponsel, jumlah enam itu yang dipajang warung kopi, dan gurunya nggak memeriksa berkas.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "A coffee shop displays the group's photographs without paying for them."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: A coffee shop displays the group's photographs without paying for them.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: A coffee shop near the square hangs six pictures each month and pays nothing for them.
qs.why: Warung kopi dekat lapangan memasang enam gambar tiap bulan dan tidak membayar apa pun, sama dengan isi klaim.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh pembayaran atau penolakan yang nggak ada; “Not stated” gugur karena kalimatnya jelas.

author: hobby page writer
setting: town streets on Sunday mornings

title: A Shelf in the Kitchen Cupboard
text:
When their father accepted a post in another town, Ayu and her younger brother moved into their grandparents' house. The rooms there smelled faintly of wood and ancient paper. Ayu lost the desk she had used for three years and had to study at the dining table. Her grandmother emptied one shelf in the kitchen cupboard for her books.

The initial weeks proved awkward for absolutely everybody. Ayu's grandfather woke at four and immediately switched on the radio at maximum volume. Her brother grumbled about the walk to school. The journey took twenty minutes longer than previously. Their grandmother solved half of these problems with a quiet timetable stuck on the fridge.

By the third month the household had established its own steady daily pattern. Ayu now studies from seven until nine while her grandfather listens to the radio through borrowed headphones. She has learnt to prepare two dishes that her mother never managed to teach her. When her father telephones on Sundays, she tells him the house feels smaller but somehow warmer.
qs: What is this story mainly about?
how a father's new post split a family up
how a longer walk changed a school day
how a household settled into living together
how a loud radio divided a small household

qs.evidence: When their father accepted a post in another town, Ayu and her younger brother moved into their grandparents' house.
qs.answer: how a household settled into living together
qs.why: Ceritanya mengikuti Ayu dan adiknya dari minggu-minggu awal yang serba salah sampai rumah itu punya pola sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keluarganya nggak terpecah, jalan ke sekolah dan radio hanya dua kesulitan awal yang akhirnya diatasi.

qs: Where does Ayu do her school work now?
at the desk she used for three years
on a shelf in the kitchen cupboard
at a small table beside the fridge
at the table where the family eats

qs.evidence: Ayu lost the desk she had used for three years and had to study at the dining table.
qs.answer: at the table where the family eats
qs.why: Ayu kehilangan mejanya, jadi dia belajar di meja makan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rak dapur dipakai menaruh buku, mejanya yang lama tertinggal di rumah lama, dan kulkas cuma tempat jadwal ditempel.

qs: What did the grandmother do about the early problems?
She moved the radio into the kitchen
She put up a shared daily plan
She bought a second desk for Ayu
She walked the children to school

qs.evidence: Their grandmother solved half of these problems with a quiet timetable stuck on the fridge.
qs.answer: She put up a shared daily plan
qs.why: Neneknya menyelesaikan separuh masalah itu dengan jadwal tenang yang ditempel di kulkas.
qs.whyOthersFail: Radionya nggak dipindah, mejanya nggak diganti, dan yang mengeluh soal jalan ke sekolah adalah adiknya sendiri.

qs: Why does the grandfather use headphones now?
So Ayu's evening study stays quiet
So the kitchen shelf stays free
Because the old radio is broken
Because his hearing has got worse

qs.evidence: Ayu now studies from seven until nine while her grandfather listens to the radio through borrowed headphones.
qs.answer: So Ayu's evening study stays quiet
qs.why: Ayu belajar dari jam tujuh sampai sembilan, jadi kakeknya pakai headphone supaya jam belajar itu tetap tenang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rak dapur nggak berhubungan dengan radio, dan teks nggak bilang radionya rusak atau pendengaran kakeknya menurun.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Ayu's father visits the grandparents' house every month."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Ayu's father visits the grandparents' house every month.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: When her father telephones on Sundays, she tells him the house feels smaller but somehow warmer.
qs.why: Yang tertulis cuma telepon tiap Minggu; apakah ayahnya pernah datang berkunjung sama sekali nggak disebut.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” butuh jadwal kunjungan yang nggak ada; “False” juga nggak bisa karena teks nggak bilang dia tak pernah datang.

author: family diary writer
setting: a grandparents' house in a quiet street

title: Thirty Minutes at a Time
text:
Teachers at a school in Metro asked ninety pupils how they prepare for tests. Two thirds of them study in blocks of thirty minutes with a short pause between. The remainder prefer one long evening session, usually after the news programme. Both groups agree that the toughest part is beginning rather than continuing.

The school now demonstrates a simple method during form time. Pupils write the topic on the left of a page and three questions on the right. They conceal the left column and answer their own questions from memory. Those who attempted the method for a month recalled more names and dates than previously.

Sleep still determines a great deal. The pupils who sleep before eleven score higher in morning tests, according to the school's own records. Phones cause the largest number of interruptions, so many families keep them in the front room overnight. One teacher advises pupils to write tomorrow's first task on paper before bed.
qs: What is the main subject of this article?
how one school rebuilt its evening timetable
how pupils get ready for their examinations
why phones cost families more than they think
why an evening news programme shapes bedtimes

qs.evidence: Teachers at a school in Metro asked ninety pupils how they prepare for tests.
qs.answer: how pupils get ready for their examinations
qs.why: Artikelnya merangkum kebiasaan belajar sembilan puluh murid sebelum ujian, dari cara mencatat sampai jam tidur.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sekolahnya nggak mengubah jadwal malam, harga ponsel nggak pernah ditulis, dan acara berita cuma penanda waktu belajar.

qs: How do two thirds of the pupils work?
in short spells of half an hour
in one long session each evening
with a friend straight after school
while the news programme is on

qs.evidence: Two thirds of them study in blocks of thirty minutes with a short pause between.
qs.answer: in short spells of half an hour
qs.why: Dua pertiga murid belajar dalam blok tiga puluh menit dengan jeda pendek di antaranya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sesi panjang malam itu pilihan sepertiga sisanya, dan teks nggak menyebut belajar bareng teman atau sambil menonton berita.

qs: What do pupils put on the right of the page?
the answers written from memory
the title of the whole topic
the date of the next test
three questions for themselves

qs.evidence: Pupils write the topic on the left of a page and three questions on the right.
qs.answer: three questions for themselves
qs.why: Murid menulis topik di kiri halaman dan tiga pertanyaan di kanan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Topiknya justru di kolom kiri, jawaban diucapkan dari ingatan setelah kolom kiri ditutup, dan tanggal tes nggak ikut ditulis.

qs: Why do many families keep phones in the front room?
to protect the hours of sleep
to write down tomorrow's first task
to keep the school records safe
to help pupils remember more names

qs.evidence: Phones cause the largest number of interruptions, so many families keep them in the front room overnight.
qs.answer: to protect the hours of sleep
qs.why: Ponsel penyebab gangguan paling banyak, jadi disimpan di ruang depan biar jam tidurnya aman.
qs.whyOthersFail: Menulis tugas pertama itu saran guru yang lain, catatan sekolah cuma sumber data, dan hafalan nama datang dari metode kolom.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Learners who go to bed before eleven do better in morning tests."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Learners who go to bed before eleven do better in morning tests.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The pupils who sleep before eleven score higher in morning tests, according to the school's own records.
qs.why: Catatan sekolah menunjukkan murid yang tidur sebelum jam sebelas nilainya lebih tinggi di tes pagi.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh arah nilai yang dibalik; “Not stated” gugur karena data itu memang ditulis.

author: education page writer
setting: a secondary school before examinations

title: The Notebook on the Wall
text:
A small notebook on the wall has changed how the Pratama household spends money. Every purchase above five thousand rupiah goes into the book on the same day. The parents check the pages together on Sunday evening, never during the week. Their two children record their own entries, including sweets and bus fares.

The habit began after a difficult month last year. Petrol, school fees and a broken pump arrived within the same fortnight, and nothing was left by the twentieth. The family then agreed on three envelopes for food, transport and emergencies. Money in the third envelope may not be touched for anything else.

The results are noticeable but hardly dramatic. The household saves about two hundred thousand rupiah each month, which now covers the electricity bill. The children argue less about small purchases, because the notebook answers most questions. Their mother says the real gain is the calm on the day the bills arrive.
qs: What is this article mainly about?
how one hard month emptied a family's savings
why electricity bills keep climbing each year
how children learn to spend their pocket money
how one household keeps track of its money

qs.evidence: A small notebook on the wall has changed how the Pratama household spends money.
qs.answer: how one household keeps track of its money
qs.why: Artikelnya soal keluarga Pratama yang mencatat tiap belanja di buku kecil di dinding dan hasilnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Bulan berat itu cuma pemicu kebiasaan, tagihan listrik justru kini tertutup, dan jajan anak hanya salah satu catatan.

qs: When do the parents look at the pages?
once a week, on Sunday night
every school day after work
on the twentieth of the month
just after every purchase

qs.evidence: The parents check the pages together on Sunday evening, never during the week.
qs.answer: once a week, on Sunday night
qs.why: Orang tuanya memeriksa halaman buku itu bareng tiap Minggu malam, nggak pernah di tengah pekan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Justru di hari kerja mereka tidak membukanya; tanggal dua puluh itu bulan sulit tahun lalu, dan pencatatan harian dilakukan anak-anak.

qs: What are the three envelopes for?
sweets, bus fares and school fees
petrol, water and electricity
meals, travel and unexpected costs
rent, school and clothing

qs.evidence: The family then agreed on three envelopes for food, transport and emergencies.
qs.answer: meals, travel and unexpected costs
qs.why: Keluarga itu sepakat memakai tiga amplop: makan, transportasi, dan keperluan darurat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jajan dan ongkos bus cuma contoh catatan anak, sedangkan bensin, listrik, dan sekolah muncul sebagai tagihan — bukan nama amplop.

qs: Why do the children argue less than before?
The written record settles most doubts
They now receive more pocket money
Their parents check the pages daily
The third envelope is always full

qs.evidence: The children argue less about small purchases, because the notebook answers most questions.
qs.answer: The written record settles most doubts
qs.why: Catatan di buku itu menjawab hampir semua pertanyaan soal belanja kecil, jadi nggak ada lagi bahan berdebat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Uang jajan nggak pernah disebut naik, orang tua memeriksa cuma sekali sepekan, dan amplop ketiga justru tidak boleh disentuh.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The family may spend the emergency envelope on ordinary shopping."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The family may spend the emergency envelope on ordinary shopping.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Money in the third envelope may not be touched for anything else.
qs.why: Uang di amplop ketiga tidak boleh dipakai untuk hal lain, jadi klaim boleh dipakai belanja biasa bertentangan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” melanggar aturan yang tertulis; “Not stated” gugur karena larangannya disebut langsung.

author: family life columnist
setting: a family home in a small town

title: Why City Air Stays Warm
text:
Anyone who walks through a big city in the afternoon knows the feeling. The pavement burns, and the air stays warm long after sunset. Scientists call this the urban heat island. Roads, roofs and walls take in sunlight all day and hold it. At night the stored heat leaves the concrete slowly, so the city cools far later than the fields around it.

Green space changes the picture. A row of trees can drop the temperature under it by a few degrees, because leaves give shade and release water vapour. Light-coloured roofs help too, since pale paint sends sunlight back to the sky. In Bandung, one school painted its roof white and watched the classrooms for a month. The rooms stayed cooler in the afternoon, and the fans were switched on less often.

Small choices matter here. Every new tree, garden and pale wall takes a little heat out of the street, and the whole neighbourhood shares the benefit.
qs: What is the main point of the article?
Roads take in sunlight, so fans are the only answer.
Trees give shade, and pale walls make streets warmer.
Cities hold heat, but plants and pale surfaces cool them.
A school painted its roof, but the rooms stayed as hot.

qs.evidence: Every new tree, garden and pale wall takes a little heat out of the street, and the whole neighbourhood shares the benefit.
qs.answer: Cities hold heat, but plants and pale surfaces cool them.
qs.why: Kalimat penutup nyimpulin dua hal: kota nyimpen panas dan tanaman plus warna pucat nurunin panas itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jalan memang nyimpen panas, tapi teks nggak pernah bilang kipas satu-satunya jalan keluar. Dinding pucat justru nurunin panas, bukan naikin. Sekolah di Bandung disebut sebagai contoh yang berhasil, jadi “ruangnya tetap panas” berlawanan.

qs: Why does the city cool down later than the land around it?
Because the fields around it hold much more water.
Because hard surfaces let go of the trapped warmth slowly.
Because tall buildings block the wind along the streets.
Because the pavement takes in sunlight after sunset.

qs.evidence: At night the stored heat leaves the concrete slowly, so the city cools far later than the fields around it.
qs.answer: Because hard surfaces let go of the trapped warmth slowly.
qs.why: “Hard surfaces” itu jalan dan beton; teks bilang panasnya keluar pelan-pelan dari beton.
qs.whyOthersFail: Air di ladang sekitar nggak pernah dibahas teks. Angin yang ketahan gedung tinggi juga nggak disebut sama sekali. Trotoar memang nyerap sinar, tapi siang hari, bukan sesudah matahari terbenam.

qs: In paragraph 1, what does "take in" mean?
hold on to the day's heat
throw the sunlight back at the sky
let warmth escape into the air
soak up energy from the sun

qs.evidence: Roads, roofs and walls take in sunlight all day and hold it.
qs.answer: soak up energy from the sun
qs.why: Di sini “take in” dipasangin sama “hold it”, jadi maksudnya nyerap, bukan nolak.
qs.whyOthersFail: “Menahan panas” itu bagian “hold it”, kerja sesudah menyerap, bukan arti “take in”. Memantulkan cahaya ke langit justru kerja cat pucat. Melepas panas ke udara itu tahap malam di teks.

qs: What can we conclude about pale roofs?
They cut the amount of warmth entering a building.
They need a fresh coat of pale paint every year.
They cool a street better than a row of trees.
They keep the rooms warmer once the sun has set.

qs.evidence: Light-coloured roofs help too, since pale paint sends sunlight back to the sky.
qs.answer: They cut the amount of warmth entering a building.
qs.why: Kalau cahaya dibalikin ke langit, panas yang masuk ke bangunan jadi lebih sedikit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak nyebut cat harus diulang tiap tahun. Teks juga nggak pernah bandingin atap pucat sama pohon, cuma bilang dua-duanya menolong. Kamar jadi hangat sesudah matahari turun itu kebalikan dari hasil di Bandung.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Trees lower the temperature partly by giving off water vapour."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Trees lower the temperature partly by giving off water vapour.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: A row of trees can drop the temperature under it by a few degrees, because leaves give shade and release water vapour.
qs.why: Teks nulis daun ngasih naungan dan “release water vapour”; klaimnya cuma ganti kata jadi “giving off”.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak bisa karena nggak ada proposisi yang dibalik; “Not stated” nggak bisa karena sebabnya ditulis di kalimat itu.

author: Environment desk
setting: a warm Indonesian city

title: Choir Takes Silver at the District Festival
text:
The school choir came home from the district festival on Saturday with a silver medal. Forty singers from Years 10 and 11 travelled to the city hall by bus. They performed two pieces: a traditional song from Flores and a gentle song in English.

The judges praised the group for clear words. However, they marked it down on balance. The report sheet records that the male voices were too soft in the second piece. Ms Ratna, who has trained the singers since March, said the result was fair. "We practised the English song for only three weeks," she remarked. "Next time we shall begin earlier."

Practice continues on Wednesday afternoon in the music room. The group requires eight more voices, and any pupil may join after an informal listening test. Ms Ratna will arrange the tests during the first week of the new term. The list of times is already on the board outside the staff room.
qs: What does the report mainly tell readers?
How the judges scored balance, and why clear words matter.
What the singers achieved and what they plan next.
How forty singers travelled, and where they will sing again.
When the tests happen, and who may join the choir.

qs.evidence: The school choir came home from the district festival on Saturday with a silver medal.
qs.answer: What the singers achieved and what they plan next.
qs.why: Laporannya dua bagian: hasil lomba plus rencana latihan dan tes anggota baru.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penilaian juri dan pentingnya artikulasi cuma satu bagian laporan. Perjalanan empat puluh penyanyi juga latar, dan tempat tampil berikutnya nggak ditulis. Jadwal tes memang ada, tapi itu langkah lanjutan, bukan isi pokoknya.

qs: What weakness did the judges find?
The men in the group sang too quietly in one piece.
The singers did not pronounce the words clearly.
The choir sang the English song faster than planned.
The group was smaller than the other choirs there.

qs.evidence: The report sheet records that the male voices were too soft in the second piece.
qs.answer: The men in the group sang too quietly in one piece.
qs.why: “Male voices were too soft” sama artinya sama cowok-cowoknya nyanyi terlalu pelan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Soal kejelasan kata, juri justru memuji, jadi itu kebalikannya. Tempo lagu Inggris dan jumlah anggota dibanding paduan suara lain nggak pernah ditulis di laporan.

qs: What must a pupil do before joining the choir?
Bring a note from a parent to Ms Ratna
Learn the song from Flores before the first practice
Sit a brief test of the ear with the teacher
Practise with the group on Wednesday afternoon first

qs.evidence: The group requires eight more voices, and any pupil may join after an informal listening test.
qs.answer: Sit a brief test of the ear with the teacher
qs.why: “Listening test” itu tes dengar singkat; teks bilang siapa pun boleh masuk sesudah tes itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Surat izin orang tua nggak disebut sebagai syarat. Lagu Flores memang dinyanyiin di festival, tapi nggak jadi syarat masuk. Latihan Rabu itu kegiatan rutin, bukan langkah sebelum diterima.

qs: Why did Ms Ratna call the silver medal fair?
Because silver is the usual result for a first year
Because the judges found fault with the clear words
Because the choir is still eight voices short
Because the group had little time on one song

qs.evidence: "We practised the English song for only three weeks," she remarked.
qs.answer: Because the group had little time on one song
qs.why: Dia langsung nyambungin hasilnya sama latihan yang cuma tiga minggu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak bilang perak itu hasil biasa buat pendatang baru. Kata-kata yang jelas justru dipuji juri. Kurang delapan suara itu urusan rekrutmen, bukan alasan nilainya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Ms Ratna has led the choir since the start of this term."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Ms Ratna has led the choir since the start of this term.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Ms Ratna, who has trained the singers since March, said the result was fair.
qs.why: Teks bilang dia latih paduan suara sejak Maret, jadi waktu mulainya beda dari “awal term ini”.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena titik waktunya ditukar; “Not stated” salah karena lama dia melatih memang ditulis.

author: School news team
setting: a secondary school and the district festival hall

title: Why the Group Chat Feels So Loud
text:
A class group chat can send a hundred messages before breakfast. Most of them are useful: a photo of the homework, a question about the bus, a reminder about football practice, a joke. The trouble begins when the device buzzes for every single message. Each buzz breaks your concentration, and you need about a minute to recover.

Three habits make the noise easier to live with. First, mute the chat and open it twice a day, at lunch and after dinner. Second, agree on one channel for urgent notices, so nobody has to scroll past jokes to find an exam date. Third, keep replies brief; a simple symbol is enough.

Rina, a Year 11 pupil, tried this plan for two weeks. She still examined every message, but she checked the chat only at fixed times. Her marks did not change, she says, yet her evenings felt longer and far more peaceful.
qs: What is the article mainly saying?
Chats are useful, and a few habits keep them bearable.
Every buzz breaks focus, and marks fall as a result.
One channel carries notices, and the rest can be muted.
Rina muted her chat, and her marks rose by a grade.

qs.evidence: Three habits make the noise easier to live with.
qs.answer: Chats are useful, and a few habits keep them bearable.
qs.why: Teks ngakui chat itu berguna, terus nawarin tiga kebiasaan biar nggak berisik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak bilang nilai jatuh gara-gara notifikasi; yang disebut fokus terganggu semenit. Soal satu kanal itu usulan, bukan pokok tulisan, dan teks nggak nyuruh matiin sisanya. Nilai Rina justru nggak turun, bukan naik satu tingkat.

qs: What happens every time the phone buzzes?
The message moves to the top of the chat list.
Most pupils reply at once with a short symbol.
Your focus leaves the task for roughly a minute.
The homework photo opens on your screen.

qs.evidence: Each buzz breaks your concentration, and you need about a minute to recover.
qs.answer: Your focus leaves the task for roughly a minute.
qs.why: Sekali bunyi, fokusmu pecah dan butuh sekitar satu menit buat balik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Urutan pesan di daftar chat nggak pernah dibahas teks. Balasan pakai simbol itu saran ketiga, bukan yang terjadi tiap getaran. Foto PR cuma contoh isi chat, bukan efek bunyinya.

qs: Which habit does the article suggest first?
Agreeing on one channel for urgent notices
Silencing the chat and opening it twice daily
Keeping every reply as short as possible
Checking the chat only after dinner each day

qs.evidence: First, mute the chat and open it twice a day, at lunch and after dinner.
qs.answer: Silencing the chat and opening it twice daily
qs.why: Saran nomor satu: senyapin chatnya, terus buka dua kali sehari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Satu kanal buat kabar penting itu saran kedua dan balasan singkat saran ketiga, jadi urutannya salah. Buka cuma sesudah makan malam juga keliru: teks minta dua kali sehari.

qs: What does Rina's fortnight suggest?
Muting a chat may lift a pupil's marks a little.
Reading fewer messages tends to make pupils miss news.
A busy class chat probably suits older pupils best.
Opening a chat less often need not cost you marks.

qs.evidence: Her marks did not change, she says, yet her evenings felt longer and far more peaceful.
qs.answer: Opening a chat less often need not cost you marks.
qs.why: Nilainya tetap padahal dia buka chat cuma di jam tertentu, jadi ngurangin akses nggak otomatis bikin nilai turun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang nilainya nggak berubah, jadi nilai naik pun nggak didukung. Rina tetap baca semua pesan, jadi soal ketinggalan kabar nggak nyambung. Umur pengguna chat nggak pernah dibahas.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Rina skipped none of the messages during her two weeks."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Rina skipped none of the messages during her two weeks.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: She still examined every message, but she checked the chat only at fixed times.
qs.why: Teks nulis dia tetap baca semua pesan, artinya nggak ada yang dilewat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh bagian yang dibalik dan nggak ada; “Not stated” nggak pas karena kebiasaan bacanya disebut langsung.

author: Digital habits column
setting: phones and chat groups of Year 11 pupils

title: Email: About Your Sleep Diary
text:
Dear Adit, thank you for submitting your sleep diary last Friday. I have examined all seven days, and the pattern is obvious. On school nights you go to bed at about half past midnight, and you rise at five. That allows you roughly four and a half hours of rest. A teenager of sixteen requires far more.

Your diary also reveals the effect. You fall asleep during lessons, you buy sweet drinks in the break, and you feel hungry an hour afterwards. Sugar lifts your energy for a brief period, then the effect disappears. Short sleep and sugar are working against each other here.

I suggest one experiment with you for a fortnight. Put your phone on the shelf by the door at ten o'clock, and read a novel until you feel sleepy. Please record the time you wake up, but ignore the rest. Please attend the clinic on Thursday during the long break. Kind regards, Nurse Dewi.
qs: What is the main message of the email?
Sugar lifts energy, and the clinic can supply more advice.
Adit sleeps too little, so one habit should change.
Adit records his waking time, and the diary looks fine.
The clinic opens on Thursday, so the diary must be ready.

qs.evidence: I suggest one experiment with you for a fortnight.
qs.answer: Adit sleeps too little, so one habit should change.
qs.why: Isi utamanya: tidurnya kurang, terus nurse nawarin satu perubahan kecil.
qs.whyOthersFail: Gula dan jam klinik memang disebut, tapi keduanya rincian, dan teks nggak menaruh nasihat tambahan di klinik. Catatan jam bangun justru yang diminta, bukan yang sudah beres. Kesiapan buku catatan buat hari Kamis nggak pernah ditulis.

qs: How much rest does the diary show on school nights?
Roughly seven hours and fifteen minutes
Roughly six hours and forty minutes
Roughly five hours and thirty minutes
Roughly four hours and thirty minutes

qs.evidence: That allows you roughly four and a half hours of rest.
qs.answer: Roughly four hours and thirty minutes
qs.why: “Four and a half hours” sama dengan empat jam tiga puluh menit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga angka lain kedengeran wajar buat remaja, tapi teks nulis empat setengah jam: tidur setengah satu malam sampai jam lima. Nggak ada angka lima, enam, atau tujuh jam di email itu.

qs: What does "working against each other" mean here?
They cancel each other out, so no harm follows.
They take turns, and only one acts each day.
Each one makes the other problem worse.
They push his energy in the same direction.

qs.evidence: Short sleep and sugar are working against each other here.
qs.answer: Each one makes the other problem worse.
qs.why: Tidur kurang bikin dia ngantuk lalu beli minuman manis, dan gula itu balik lagi bikin lapar — saling memperburuk.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalau saling meniadakan, nggak ada masalah yang dijelasin nurse; teks justru nyebut rangkaian efek buruk. “Gantian tiap hari” nggak ada di teks, dan mendorong ke arah yang sama malah kebalikan dari “against”.

qs: What does the nurse expect the phone rule to do?
Help Adit reach sleep earlier in the evening
Stop him buying sweet drinks in the break
Give him something to read for his lessons
Let the nurse check his diary more easily

qs.evidence: Put your phone on the shelf by the door at ten o'clock, and read a novel until you feel sleepy.
qs.answer: Help Adit reach sleep earlier in the evening
qs.why: Telepon ditaruh jauh jam sepuluh biar dia ngantuk lebih awal, bukan buat urusan lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Minuman manis dibeli gara-gara ngantuk, bukan gara-gara telepon. Novel di aturan itu buat ngantuk, bukan tugas pelajaran. Buku catatannya cuma diminta nyatet jam bangun, bukan dipermudah buat nurse.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Adit buys three sweet drinks during every school break."
True
False
Not stated
