author: a consumer columnist
setting: a consumer column about phone shopping

title: A Notes App That Asks for Almost Nothing
text:
Quiet Notes is a free writing app that has become popular in schools, and its selling point is what it refuses to do. It requests no contact list, no location, and no advertising identifier. On first opening it displays a single screen listing every permission it will ever require. Honesty of that kind is rare enough to deserve a review.
As a notebook the app is competent rather than brilliant. Typing is quick, folders are simple to construct, and the search box locates a word across hundreds of pages in a second. Yet the design feels plain beside its commercial rivals, and there is no drawing tool at all. Notes are stored on the device itself and copied to one rented server abroad. The developers also publish an annual report on requests received from officials. Export options are limited to plain text and a single archive.
Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print. Its privacy notice extends to 600 words and is entirely free of the usual fog. Where it loses is in the features that many pupils actually want. If you need shared editing or handwriting, look elsewhere; if you want a place to think that does not study you, install it today. Four marks out of five, with one withheld for the missing drawing tool.
qs: What is the main idea of this review?
the app trades honesty for a longer feature list
the app offers fewer features but rare honesty
the app hides its practices behind long notices
the app matches its paid rivals on nearly every feature

qs.evidence: Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print.
qs.answer: the app offers fewer features but rare honesty
qs.why: Penilaian utama resensi: aplikasi ini menang di keterbukaan (“wins is in the small print”) walau daftar fiturnya biasa dan nggak punya alat gambar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pertukarannya justru kebalikan: fiturnya lebih sedikit tapi keterusterangannya langka; syarat penggunaannya disebut pendek dan berbahasa biasa, bukan disembunyikan di notis panjang; dan teks nyebut pesaing berbayar punya lebih banyak fitur, jadi aplikasi ini nggak menyamainya.

qs.answer: a screen naming the permissions it will request

qs.whyOthersFail: Server sewaan di luar negeri dan laporan tahunan memang ada, tapi keduanya dibahas belakangan, bukan di layar pertama; tempat penyimpanan catatan juga nggak ditampilkan saat pertama dibuka — yang muncul satu layar berisi semua izin yang akan diminta.

qs.evidence: Its privacy notice extends to 600 words and is entirely free of the usual fog.
qs.answer: the terms are short and written in plain language
qs.why: Aturan privasinya cuma 600 kata dan bebas dari kabut bahasa hukum yang biasa, dan itulah yang dipuji resensi soal “small print”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Semuanya akan mendukung pujian itu kalau ada di teks, tapi nggak ada pemeriksaan pengacara luar, nggak ada pengulangan janji lewat contoh, dan nggak ada daftar perusahaan penerima catatan — yang disebut cuma notis 600 kata tanpa kabut bahasa.

qs.answer: they will likely need a different app

qs.whyOthersFail: Desainnya yang polos justru disebut kelemahan, bukan daya tarik; nggak ada janji alat gambar bakal ditambahkan; dan pilihan ekspornya terbatas pada teks biasa dan satu arsip, jadi nggak menolong yang mau menggambar — teks nyuruh cari aplikasi lain kalau butuh tulisan tangan.

author: a technology reviewer
setting: a technology review page

title: Letter: Please Review the Evening Pool Timetable
text:
Dear Ms Halim, I am writing on behalf of the school swimming club. Our purpose is to request a review of the evening timetable, which was altered at the start of this term. Our club trains on four evenings weekly and has done so for eleven years. We recognize that demand for lanes is considerable and that the centre must balance competing groups. We accept that the centre must serve every category of user, and we submit our request in that spirit.
The difficulty is straightforward. Club training now commences at nine o'clock, an hour later than previously, and concludes at half past ten. Since the change, average attendance has declined from thirty-one swimmers to seventeen, and eight of our junior members have abandoned the sport. Parents state plainly that they refuse to collect a twelve-year-old at that hour. The new arrangement therefore protects the pool's evening income while quietly closing the club to children. The consequence is a session that excludes precisely the members who benefit most from regular exercise. Two independent coaches have described the situation as unsustainable for a junior programme.
We would prefer to propose a compromise rather than a complaint. Two lanes from eight until nine would enable our junior squad to train, while the remaining lanes remain available to the public. If the centre prefers, we are willing to transfer one session to weekend mornings and to pay the usual lane fee. Such a compromise would protect your evening income while restoring access for junior swimmers. I should be grateful for an opportunity to discuss this before the month concludes. Yours sincerely, Dita Rahman, club secretary.
qs: Why was this letter written?
to complain about other groups using the lanes
to request an earlier slot for the junior squad
to give notice that the club will move pools
to accept the new evening slot with minor conditions

qs.evidence: We would prefer to propose a compromise rather than a complaint.
qs.answer: to request an earlier slot for the junior squad

qs.whyOthersFail: Kelompok lain di lajur sebelah nggak pernah dikeluhkan; kepindahan kolam nggak disebut; dan surat ini justru nggak menerima slot malam yang baru, dia mengusulkan jam yang lebih awal buat regu junior.

qs.evidence: Since the change, average attendance has declined from thirty-one swimmers to seventeen, and eight of our junior members have abandoned the sport.
qs.answer: it fell to roughly half the earlier figure
qs.why: Kehadiran rata-rata turun dari 31 perenang jadi 17, jadi kira-kira separuh dari angka sebelumnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga puluh satu itu angka sebelum perubahan, bukan sesudahnya; penurunannya bukan cuma di anggota dewasa karena delapan anggota junior berhenti; dan turunnya dari 31 ke 17 jauh lebih dalam daripada seperlima.

qs.evidence: Parents state plainly that they refuse to collect a twelve-year-old at that hour.
qs.answer: families will not fetch a child of twelve so late
qs.why: Orang tua terang-terangan nolak jemput anak dua belas tahun di jam segitu, dan itu yang bikin slot baru nutup pintu buat anak-anak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Larangan usia, latihan bercampur orang dewasa, dan kenaikan iuran junior sama-sama akan jadi bukti yang kuat, tapi nggak satu pun disebut di surat; yang disebut orang tua menolak menjemput anak dua belas tahun jam segitu.

topic: a swimming club and pool hours
author: the club secretary
setting: a letter to the manager of a leisure centre

title: Yes, the Cycle Lane Deserves That Road Space
text:
Whenever a city paints a cycle lane, the same objection returns: why grant a third of the road to a handful of riders? It sounds reasonable, and it is wrong. The people who raise it are counting bicycles at eight in the morning on a street that has been unsafe for twenty years. Demand does not appear before the lane; it appears afterwards.
Consider the two claims side by side. Opponents insist that lanes remove space from vehicles which carry more passengers. Supporters answer that a protected lane moves up to five times as many people each hour as a queue of cars. Both sides can quote figures, yet only one of them has to explain why parents refuse to let their children ride. I have cycled to work in this district for nine years, and the reason most of my neighbours remain in their cars is fear rather than comfort.
None of this makes every lane sensible. A lane that stops at a busy roundabout, or one painted between parked cars and moving buses, is worse than nothing. What we should demand is a network joining schools, markets, and stations without a single frightening gap. Until then, complaining about empty lanes resembles blaming an unfinished bridge for the river. A network of that kind demands political courage and steady investment. Construct the network properly and the riders will arrive.

one morning count settles the question fairly

qs.answer: empty lanes show only that the network is unfinished
qs.why: Penulis nutup argumennya dengan perumpamaan jembatan yang belum jadi: jalur yang kelihatan kosong cuma nandain jaringannya belum nyambung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Hitungan satu pagi justru yang dianggap ukuran timpang oleh penulis; sepertiga jalan di setiap jalan nggak pernah dituntut; dan teks nggak menjanjikan jaringan bakal selesai begitu dana ada, itu justru bagian yang belum dikerjakan.

qs.whyOthersFail: Segelintir pesepeda tiap pagi adalah hitungan pihak penentang, bukan pendukung; dan pendukung justru bilang lajur terlindung mengangkut sampai lima kali lebih banyak orang per jam, jadi bukan lebih sedikit dari rute bus dan bukan setara antrean mobil.

qs.evidence: Both sides can quote figures, yet only one of them has to explain why parents refuse to let their children ride.
qs.answer: only one side must explain the fear families feel

author: a daily cyclist and columnist
setting: an opinion column in a city newspaper

title: Late Training, Short Sleep, and Tired Mornings
text:
A study at a sports academy has traced a chain that many coaches suspected but few had measured properly. For ten weeks, 84 young footballers wore simple wrist monitors and recorded the hour at which they trained. Half the participants concluded practice at seven in the evening; the remainder finished at half past nine. Everything else in their weekly routine remained identical. Coaches at rival academies had assumed the difference was negligible.
The later group slept 47 minutes less on training nights. That loss did not result from a later bedtime alone. Body temperature and excitement after severe exercise kept the players alert for roughly half an hour once they lay down. In morning tests of reaction and short-term memory the late group scored about a tenth lower, and reported muscle pain that lasted a day longer. Recovery therefore occupied more of the following morning than the coaches had estimated. The chain therefore runs from the timetable to the sleep, and from the sleep to the following day.
The researchers are cautious about what follows. They observed one academy, one season, and one age group, so the figures should not be transferred elsewhere without checking. Even so, the direction of the effect was consistent across both squads. Their recommendation to clubs is modest and inexpensive. End evening sessions before eight where possible, reduce the lighting afterwards, and treat a late finish as part of the training load. Such adjustments require no equipment and no additional expense for the club.
qs: What is this report mainly about?
why young players dislike wearing wrist monitors
how coaches pick the squad for a late session
how the timing of practice affects the next morning
how much sleep young athletes need each night

qs.answer: how the timing of practice affects the next morning
qs.why: Teks nyebut rantainya jelas: dari jadwal ke tidur, dan dari tidur ke hari berikutnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rasa nggak suka memakai monitor nggak pernah disebut; cara pelatih memilih regu bukan pokok laporan; dan angka kebutuhan tidur per malam nggak diukur, yang diukur adalah akibat jam latihan pada pagi berikutnya.

qs.answer: a little under fifty minutes

qs.whyOthersFail: Lebih dari sejam melebihi angka teks; sepersepuluh malam adalah besarnya penurunan skor tes, bukan lama tidur yang hilang; dan setengah jam itu waktu yang dibutuhkan pemain buat tenang setelah latihan keras — kehilangan tidurnya 47 menit.

qs.answer: morning scores for reaction and memory fell

qs.answer: a single academy in a single season proves little

qs.whyOthersFail: Peneliti nggak nyebut efeknya lebih kecil pada pemain yang lebih tua; mereka justru bilang angkanya jangan dipindah ke tempat lain tanpa pengujian; dan menghentikan semua latihan malam sekaligus bukan peringatan mereka.

author: a health science writer
setting: a football academy studied for ten weeks

title: Apprenticeship or Degree: Comparing Two Routes
text:
School leavers are frequently told that a degree is the safe route and an apprenticeship the practical one. The comparison is lazier than it sounds, because the two paths differ less in reputation than in the moment they force a decision. One of them purchases time; the other purchases experience.
Begin with money. An apprentice earns from the first month and finishes with no debt, while a graduate spends three or four years paying to study. Ten years later the picture alters in certain fields. Graduates in engineering and health tend to reach higher wages, whereas in software and building work the two groups end up close. The risk of regret is genuine on both sides, and neither route removes it entirely. Now consider flexibility. A degree in a broad subject leaves several doors open, while an apprenticeship trains you deeply for one trade and may be harder to leave at twenty-eight.
The correct choice depends on how certain you already are. If you know the work you want and can learn inside it, the apprenticeship route wastes fewer years. If your interests are still moving, paying for time to explore is not weakness but sense. What both routes share is the part nobody advertises. Employers increasingly value evidence of learning rather than the document itself. Whichever you select, you will continue learning long after the certificate arrives.
qs: What is the writer's purpose in this feature?
to show that apprentices tend to earn more in the end
to list the trades that accept school leavers each year
to show that one route now suits most school leavers
to show that the right route depends on the reader

qs.evidence: The correct choice depends on how certain you already are.
qs.answer: to show that the right route depends on the reader
qs.why: Teks nutup perbandingannya dengan “The correct choice depends on how certain you already are”, jadi tujuannya nunjukin pilihan itu bergantung pada pembacanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penghasilan akhir apprentice disebut bisa lebih tinggi cuma sebagai satu sisi, bukan tujuan tulisan; daftar bidang yang menerima lulusan sekolah nggak ada; dan teks justru menolak gagasan satu jalur cocok buat hampir semua orang.

qs: What does the article say about pay after ten years?
it tends to be higher for the apprentice
it is much the same in every trade and subject
it drops for graduates working in health care
it varies with the field of work concerned

qs.evidence: Graduates in engineering and health tend to reach higher wages, whereas in software and building work the two groups end up close.
qs.answer: it varies with the field of work concerned
qs.why: Setelah sepuluh tahun, lulusan teknik dan kesehatan cenderung berupah lebih tinggi, sementara di software dan konstruksi kedua kelompok berdekatan — jadi hasilnya tergantung bidang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Apprentice nggak digambarkan unggul di semua bidang; kesamaan upah cuma berlaku di dua bidang yang disebut, bukan di semua; dan lulusan kesehatan justru contoh yang upahnya naik, bukan turun.

qs: How do the two routes compare on keeping options open?
the trade route is the easier one to leave later
a wide subject keeps more doors open later on
both routes shut the same number of doors
neither route allows a change after ten years

qs.evidence: A degree in a broad subject leaves several doors open, while an apprenticeship trains you deeply for one trade and may be harder to leave at twenty-eight.
qs.answer: a wide subject keeps more doors open later on
qs.why: Gelar di bidang luas disebut ninggalin beberapa pintu terbuka, sedangkan apprenticeship melatih satu keahlian dalam-dalam dan bisa lebih susah ditinggal di umur dua puluh delapan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jalur keahlian dibilang lebih susah ditinggal, bukan lebih mudah; jumlah pintu yang tertutup nggak digambarkan setara; dan teks nggak nutup kemungkinan pindah jalur setelah sepuluh tahun, dia cuma bilang perpindahannya lebih berat.

qs: What does the writer imply about a reader who is still unsure of a career?
choosing a trade quickly would settle the question
the cost of study makes exploring a mistake
spending a few years exploring can be sensible
such a reader should choose the cheaper route first

qs.evidence: If your interests are still moving, paying for time to explore is not weakness but sense.
qs.answer: spending a few years exploring can be sensible
qs.why: Teks nyebut kalau minatmu masih bergerak, bayar buat waktu menjajaki itu bukan kelemahan tapi kewarasan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Memilih satu bidang cepat-cepat justru masuk akal buat orang yang sudah yakin, bukan yang masih ragu; biaya belajar nggak dijadikan alasan berhenti menjajaki; dan patokan yang dipakai teks bukan mana yang lebih murah, tapi seberapa yakin kamu sekarang.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "An apprentice leaves training owing money for the course."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: An apprentice leaves training owing money for the course.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: An apprentice earns from the first month and finishes with no debt, while a graduate spends three or four years paying to study.
qs.why: Teks nyebut apprentice selesai tanpa utang, jadi klaim soal ninggalin pelatihan sambil nanggung utang itu kebalikan langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena bertentangan sama teks; “Not stated” salah karena posisi utang apprentice disebut jelas.

author: a careers adviser
setting: a careers feature for school leavers

title: We Should Stop Paying for Speed We Do Not Need
text:
I ordered a phone charger last Tuesday and it arrived the same evening. I did not require it that evening. Nobody asked me whether I did, because the shop's app had already selected the fastest option on my behalf. Somewhere between convenience and habit we have accepted a promise that costs far more than the delivery fee suggests.
The bill is paid by other people. Same-day delivery produces half-empty vans, drivers working to a timetable they cannot control, and packaging chosen for speed rather than weight. A parcel despatched within two hours may travel in a van carrying six items, whereas a parcel despatched within three days travels with two hundred. The saving in time belongs to me alone. The additional fuel, the additional traffic, and the pressure on the driver are shared by everybody in the district.
The remedy is not to shame shoppers. Make the slower option the default, display the difference in plain language at the moment of payment, and offer a modest credit to customers who wait. Where retailers have attempted this, the majority of buyers selected the slower box without complaint. I want an online market that treats patience as normal rather than as a setting you must hunt for. Speed should be something we request, not something we are given.
qs: What is the main argument of this column?
the real cost of fast delivery falls on the shops
the real cost of fast delivery is paid by others
shoppers order too often and should feel guilty
drivers set the timetables that suit them best

qs.evidence: The saving in time belongs to me alone.
qs.answer: the real cost of fast delivery is paid by others
qs.why: Inti kolomnya: penghematan waktu cuma dinikmati si pembeli, sementara bahan bakar, kemacetan, dan tekanan ke kurir ditanggung seluruh distrik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nyebut biayanya jatuh ke pengemudi, jalan, dan udara — bukan ke tokonya; penulis eksplisit nggak mau membuat pembeli merasa bersalah; dan jadwal justru ditentukan janji pengiriman, bukan kemauan pengemudi.

qs: What does the writer say about the packaging used for fast orders?
it is heavier than the packaging on slow orders
it is chosen to protect fragile goods
it is designed to cut waste at the depot
it is selected to save time, not to cut bulk

qs.evidence: Same-day delivery produces half-empty vans, drivers working to a timetable they cannot control, and packaging chosen for speed rather than weight.
qs.answer: it is selected to save time, not to cut bulk
qs.why: Teks nyebut kemasan buat pengiriman hari-sama dipilih demi kecepatan, bukan demi bobot.
qs.whyOthersFail: Berat kemasan pengiriman lambat nggak dibandingkan; perlindungan barang mudah pecah dan pengurangan sampah di depo nggak disebut — kemasan pengiriman cepat dipilih demi kecepatan, bukan demi berat.

qs: How does a two-hour parcel compare with a three-day parcel?
it weighs less than the slower parcel does
it travels with about two hundred other items
it shares its van with far fewer parcels
it costs the shop nothing extra to send

qs.evidence: A parcel despatched within two hours may travel in a van carrying six items, whereas a parcel despatched within three days travels with two hundred.
qs.answer: it shares its van with far fewer parcels
qs.why: Paket dua jam bisa jalan di van berisi enam barang, sementara paket tiga hari jalan bareng dua ratus barang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Bobot paket nggak dibandingin di teks; angka dua ratus justru punya paket tiga hari, bukan paket dua jam; dan teks bilang ada tambahan bahan bakar dan tekanan, jadi mustahil tanpa biaya tambahan.

qs: Which statement best restates what the writer wants shops to do?
make waiting normal and reward it a little
charge a higher fee for the slower option
ban the fastest option in every online shop
reward the faster choice and explain why

qs.evidence: Make the slower option the default, display the difference in plain language at the moment of payment, and offer a modest credit to customers who wait.
qs.answer: make waiting normal and reward it a little
qs.why: Usulannya: jadikan opsi lambat sebagai default, tampilkan bedanya dengan bahasa jelas saat bayar, dan kasih kredit kecil buat yang mau nunggu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Biaya lebih tinggi buat opsi lambat kebalikan dari usulan kredit kecil buat yang mau menunggu; pelarangan opsi tercepat nggak diusulkan; dan yang diminta adalah menjelaskan selisihnya saat pembayaran serta memberi imbalan pada yang menunggu, bukan pada yang tercepat.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Where shops tried the idea, most customers accepted the slower delivery."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Where shops tried the idea, most customers accepted the slower delivery.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Where retailers have attempted this, the majority of buyers selected the slower box without complaint.
qs.why: “the majority of buyers” sama artinya sama “most customers”, dan teks nyebut mereka milih kotak yang lebih lambat tanpa protes.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena nggak ada proposisi yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena hasil percobaan retailer itu disebut langsung.

topic: fast delivery and its hidden costs
author: a consumer affairs columnist
setting: an opinion column about online shopping

title: Why So Many Apps Ask for the Address Book
text:
A team of student researchers examined the permission requests of 200 free apps in order to discover what drives them. They did not inspect the code; instead they read every privacy notice and every request screen, then wrote to the developers. Ninety-two firms replied. The pattern that emerged had less to do with features than with revenue.
Two thirds of the apps requested the contact list, yet only a quarter used it for anything a user would notice. Where the request appeared, an advertising partner was named in the notice nine times out of ten. Developers explained the logic plainly. A network of contacts helps advertisers estimate who else might purchase, so the partner pays more for that space. The request therefore follows the business model, and the feature is invented afterwards to justify it.
The study suggests a simple test for readers. Ask what the app would lose if it never saw your contact list, then compare that answer with the section on partners. Where the two answers disagree, refusing the request costs you very little. The researchers also want app stores to place the reason for each request beside the button. Permission screens are cheap to write, whereas explanations are what actually alter behaviour. Regulators in two countries are already considering such a requirement.
qs: What is the purpose of this report?
to explain what lies behind a common request
to show which app features truly need the contact list
to show readers how to read an app's own code
to advertise a privacy tool aimed at parents

qs.evidence: The pattern that emerged had less to do with features than with revenue.
qs.answer: to explain what lies behind a common request
qs.why: Pola yang muncul dari studi disebut lebih berkaitan dengan pendapatan daripada dengan fitur, dan laporan ini menjelaskan alasan di balik permintaan daftar kontak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Laporan nggak menyusun daftar fitur yang benar-benar butuh daftar kontak, dia nyebut fiturnya ditemukan belakangan; peneliti menyatakan nggak memeriksa kode; dan nggak ada alat privasi yang dipromosikan.

qs: How many of the 200 developers answered the researchers' letters?
about two thirds of the total number
exactly nine out of every ten firms
slightly fewer than a hundred
a quarter of the firms in the study

qs.evidence: Ninety-two firms replied.
qs.answer: slightly fewer than a hundred
qs.why: Teks nyebut 92 perusahaan menjawab, jadi sedikit di bawah seratus dari 200 yang dihubungi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dua per tiga itu porsi aplikasi yang minta daftar kontak; sembilan dari sepuluh adalah seberapa sering mitra iklan disebut di notis; dan seperempat adalah porsi aplikasi yang benar-benar memakai kontak buat fitur yang kelihatan.

qs: Which finding best supports the claim that money drives the request?
the apps that asked for contacts earned more money
developers said the request raised their download totals
the request appeared most often in the paid versions
nearly every such request named an advertising firm

qs.evidence: Where the request appeared, an advertising partner was named in the notice nine times out of ten.
qs.answer: nearly every such request named an advertising firm
qs.why: Di mana permintaan itu muncul, mitra iklan disebut dalam notis sembilan dari sepuluh kali — kaitan langsung antara permintaan dan uang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya akan mendukung “uang yang mendorong permintaan”, tapi teks nggak membandingkan pendapatan antar aplikasi, nggak nyebut pengaruh ke jumlah unduhan, dan studinya cuma meneliti aplikasi gratis — jadi versi berbayar nggak ada.

qs: What can be inferred about the features that use a contact list?
many of them are added only as an excuse
most of them are noticed by ordinary users
they tend to be built before the notice is written
they raise the price the partner is willing to pay

qs.evidence: The request therefore follows the business model, and the feature is invented afterwards to justify it.
qs.answer: many of them are added only as an excuse
qs.why: Teks nyebut permintaan mengikuti model bisnis dan fiturnya baru ditemukan sesudahnya buat membenarkan permintaan itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Cuma seperempat aplikasi memakai kontak buat hal yang disadari pengguna, jadi bukan sebagian besar; urutannya justru kebalikan, fitur datang belakangan; dan yang bikin mitra bayar lebih mahal adalah jaringan kontaknya, bukan fiturnya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "All of the firms contacted by the researchers sent a reply."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: All of the firms contacted by the researchers sent a reply.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: A team of student researchers examined the permission requests of 200 free apps in order to discover what drives them.
qs.why: Dari 200 aplikasi yang diperiksa cuma 92 firma yang jawab, jadi klaim “all of the firms” bertentangan sama angka di teks.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena jumlah yang balas jauh di bawah total; “Not stated” salah karena jumlah pembalas ditulis eksplisit.

author: a science journalist
setting: a popular report on a student research project

title: Reviewing the City's New Travel Card App
text:
The city transport office has replaced its paper tickets with an app. After three weeks of daily use I can report that it is both better and worse than the system it removed. Purchasing a journey now takes eleven seconds instead of a queue. Losing your battery, however, now removes your ticket as well.
The advantages are genuine. The map displays the next three buses at a chosen stop. The fare is charged at the cheaper weekly rate automatically, and a single tap transfers a monthly pass to a new handset. Reliability, though, is uneven. Twice in three weeks the app refused to open underground, where there is no signal, and the offline ticket it promises required four attempts to appear. Elderly passengers at my stop have quietly returned to purchasing paper from the driver, a habit the office intends to end in June.
So is the app worth installing? For anyone travelling daily with a modern phone, certainly; the weekly limit alone repays the effort. For occasional riders, and for anyone whose handset is five years old, the app removes a functioning system and offers a fragile one. My verdict is three marks out of five. It would deserve four if the office retained paper tickets for the passengers who depend on them.
qs: What is the reviewer's overall verdict on the app?
clearly better than paper for every passenger
handy for daily riders, risky for occasional ones
worse than paper in almost every respect
risky for daily riders, handy for occasional ones

qs.evidence: My verdict is three marks out of five.
qs.answer: handy for daily riders, risky for occasional ones
qs.why: Nilai tiga dari lima itu hasil penimbangan: berguna banget buat yang naik tiap hari dengan ponsel baru, rapuh buat penumpang sesekali dan ponsel tua.
qs.whyOthersFail: Arahnya kebalikan: aplikasinya berguna buat penumpang harian dan berisiko buat yang jarang naik; dan tiga dari lima jelas bukan “jauh lebih baik dari kertas buat semua orang” maupun “lebih buruk di hampir semua hal”.

qs: What happened when the reviewer tried to open the app underground?
it refused to start on two occasions
it opened but lost the offline ticket
it opened after a delay of three minutes
it opened normally on every journey

qs.evidence: Twice in three weeks the app refused to open underground, where there is no signal, and the offline ticket it promises required four attempts to appear.
qs.answer: it refused to start on two occasions
qs.why: Dua kali dalam tiga minggu aplikasinya nolak kebuka di bawah tanah, tempat yang nggak ada sinyal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Aplikasinya bukan cuma lambat atau kehilangan tiket luring, dan jelas bukan berjalan normal: dua kali dalam tiga pekan dia menolak terbuka di bawah tanah karena nggak ada sinyal.

qs: How does the app compare with the paper system for older passengers?
both systems take the same eleven seconds
the app suits them better than paper for now
paper suits them better for the moment
the app saves them money every week

qs.evidence: Elderly passengers at my stop have quietly returned to purchasing paper from the driver, a habit the office intends to end in June.
qs.answer: paper suits them better for the moment
qs.why: Penumpang lanjut usia di pemberhentian penulis diam-diam balik beli tiket kertas dari pengemudi, jadi sistem kertas masih lebih pas buat mereka.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sebelas detik itu waktu pembelian di aplikasi, bukan angka yang sama buat kedua sistem; penumpang lanjut usia justru balik ke kertas, jadi aplikasinya belum lebih cocok dan belum menggantikan kertas; dan penghematan uang tiap minggu nggak disebut.

qs: What does the reviewer imply about the decision to withdraw paper tickets?
some passengers may lose a reliable option
queues at the stops will probably disappear
the weekly limit may become easier to reach
the office will likely restore paper next year

qs.evidence: It would deserve four if the office retained paper tickets for the passengers who depend on them.
qs.answer: some passengers may lose a reliable option
qs.why: Penulis bilang aplikasinya layak dapat empat kalau kantor tetap nyediain tiket kertas buat penumpang yang bergantung padanya — artinya penghapusan kertas nyabut pilihan yang bisa diandalkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Antrean di pemberhentian nggak dibahas hilang atau nggak; batas mingguan nggak jadi lebih mudah dicapai; dan kantor justru berniat menghentikan pembelian kertas dari pengemudi pada Juni, bukan mengembalikannya tahun depan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The app works out the cheaper weekly fare for the passenger."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The app works out the cheaper weekly fare for the passenger.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The fare is charged at the cheaper weekly rate automatically, and a single tap transfers a monthly pass to a new handset.
qs.why: Teks nyebut tarif otomatis dihitung pada rate mingguan yang lebih murah, jadi klaim ini cuma parafrasa fitur itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena nggak ada yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena fitur tarif mingguan disebut jelas.

author: a daily bus passenger
setting: a review of a city travel app

title: Privacy Belongs on the Timetable
text:
Our school teaches pupils how to compose a formal letter, how to interpret a graph, and how to swim. It teaches nothing whatever about the exchange they make daily when they open an app. That gap is not a minor one, and pretending it belongs to parents alone has ceased to be honest.
The problem appears in ordinary questions I cannot answer for my class. Why does a free game request the microphone? What does a shop learn from a loyalty card, and who else receives it? Pupils are not careless; they simply possess no vocabulary for the thing being taken. A survey of our own Year Ten discovered that most could name a virus, yet almost none could explain the function of an advertising identifier.
A remedy would fit inside the existing timetable. Six lessons a year, taught in the subject where devices are already used, would cover permissions, passwords, data brokers, and the right to ask what a company holds. Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher. What it demands is the decision that this counts as literacy. Employers, regulators and universities all assume this knowledge already exists. Until we reach that decision, we are teaching children to read every text except the one they agree to every day.
qs: What is the writer's purpose in this article?
to blame pupils for accepting permissions carelessly
to describe how loyalty cards gather information
to argue that privacy is best taught at home
to argue that privacy belongs in the timetable

qs.evidence: What it demands is the decision that this counts as literacy.
qs.answer: to argue that privacy belongs in the timetable
qs.why: Penulis minta keputusan bahwa hal ini dihitung sebagai literasi, yaitu privasi jadi bagian pelajaran resmi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis nggak menyalahkan murid yang menerima izin sembarangan, dia nyalahin sekolah yang nggak ngajarin; cara kartu loyalitas mengumpulkan data cuma contoh; dan yang dituntut justru pelajaran di jadwal sekolah, bukan penyerahan urusan ini ke rumah.

qs: What did the survey of Year Ten pupils reveal?
most could explain an advertising identifier
they knew one threat by name but not the other
few of them could name a computer virus
they wanted lessons on passwords instead of games

qs.evidence: A survey of our own Year Ten discovered that most could name a virus, yet almost none could explain the function of an advertising identifier.
qs.answer: they knew one threat by name but not the other
qs.why: Survei Year Ten nemu sebagian besar bisa nyebut nama virus, tapi hampir nggak ada yang bisa jelasin fungsi advertising identifier.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kebalikan yang benar: hampir nggak ada yang bisa menjelaskan pengenal iklan, sementara sebagian besar justru bisa menyebut virus; dan permintaan pelajaran kata sandi nggak pernah disurvei.

qs: Which point best supports the claim that the change would be cheap?
the plan asks for no fresh spending at all
the lessons would replace an hour of swimming
the materials are provided free by the regulator
other schools ran the plan without extra cost

qs.evidence: Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher.
qs.answer: the plan asks for no fresh spending at all
qs.why: Kalimat “Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher” persis nunjukin usulannya nggak nambah biaya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Menukar jam renang, bahan gratis dari regulator, dan pengalaman sekolah lain sama-sama akan membuktikan murahnya, tapi nggak satu pun ada di teks; yang ada cuma pernyataan bahwa rencana ini nggak butuh alat baru atau guru tambahan.

qs: What does the writer imply about pupils who accept every permission?
they lack the words for what they are giving up
they are less careful than pupils in other years
they have already been warned by their parents
they grasp the exchange but choose to ignore it

qs.evidence: Pupils are not careless; they simply possess no vocabulary for the thing being taken.
qs.answer: they lack the words for what they are giving up
qs.why: Teks nyebut murid bukan lalai, mereka cuma nggak punya kosakata buat hal yang sedang diambil dari mereka.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kelalaian justru dibantah langsung, dan nggak ada perbandingan antar tingkatan kelas; peringatan dari orang tua nggak pernah disebut ada; dan kalau mereka paham pertukarannya, kalimat soal ketiadaan kosakata jadi nggak masuk akal.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer's school already teaches two of the six proposed lessons."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer's school already teaches two of the six proposed lessons.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Six lessons a year, taught in the subject where devices are already used, would cover permissions, passwords, data brokers, and the right to ask what a company holds.
qs.why: Teks cuma ngusulin enam pelajaran baru dan nyebut sekolah belum ngajarin apa pun soal itu; jumlah yang “sudah diajarkan” nggak pernah dirinci.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena angka itu nggak ada di teks; “False” salah karena teks nggak nyatain kebalikannya secara spesifik, cuma diam soal rincian itu.

author: a secondary school teacher
setting: an opinion piece by a classroom teacher

title: Part-time Work and School Marks: How Many Hours?
text:
Does a weekend job damage school results? Earlier investigations had produced contradictory conclusions on the question. A three-year study of 1,200 pupils in nine schools suggests that the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours. The researchers followed the same learners from Year Ten to the end of Year Twelve and compared their marks with records of paid work.
Up to eight hours a week, working pupils performed slightly better than those without employment at all. Their teachers described them as better organized and noticeably more willing to plan ahead. Beyond twelve hours the pattern reversed sharply: marks declined, absence increased, and sleep dropped by nearly an hour on working nights. The cause was not the employment itself but what it replaced. Pupils in the heaviest group surrendered revision and rest first, because those were the only parts of the week nobody was paying for.
The report resists a simple rule. Some learners in the long-hours group were supporting families and had no choice, and the study did not measure the value of the money they earned. The authors nevertheless recommend that schools ask about working hours early in the year. They also urge employers of young staff to avoid evening shifts before examinations. The authors describe the relationship as reliable but modest in scale. A small job appears to assist; a second job appears to cost more than it pays.
qs: What is the central finding of this study?
pupils with jobs tend to outperform the rest
the effect of a job depends on its hours
any weekend job tends to damage a pupil's progress
the effect of a job depends on the pupil's subject

qs.evidence: Earlier investigations had produced contradictory conclusions on the question. A three-year study of 1,200 pupils in nine schools suggests that the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours.
qs.answer: the effect of a job depends on its hours
qs.why: Studi tiga tahun atas 1.200 murid nyimpulin jawabannya hampir sepenuhnya bergantung pada jumlah jam kerja.
qs.whyOthersFail: Murid yang bekerja nggak selalu unggul dan nggak selalu rugi, karena yang menentukan jumlah jamnya; dan mata pelajaran yang diambil murid nggak pernah jadi variabel di studi ini.

qs: What happened to pupils working more than twelve hours a week?
their results fell and their sleep was cut
their marks rose while attendance quietly fell
their teachers found them better organized
their families reported no change at all

qs.evidence: Beyond twelve hours the pattern reversed sharply: marks declined, absence increased, and sleep dropped by nearly an hour on working nights.
qs.answer: their results fell and their sleep was cut
qs.why: Di atas dua belas jam pola berbalik tajam: nilai turun, absen naik, dan tidur berkurang hampir satu jam pada malam kerja.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nilai mereka turun, bukan naik; pujian soal kerapian justru buat kelompok di bawah delapan jam; dan laporan keluarga nggak pernah dikutip di teks.

qs: Which explanation does the report give for the fall in marks?
employers refused to move the evening shifts
study time and rest went before anything else
the work itself left the pupils physically tired
those pupils were already behind in Year Ten

qs.evidence: Pupils in the heaviest group surrendered revision and rest first, because those were the only parts of the week nobody was paying for.
qs.answer: study time and rest went before anything else
qs.why: Teks nyebut kelompok jam terberat nyerahin revisi dan istirahat lebih dulu karena cuma bagian itu yang nggak ada yang bayar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penolakan pemberi kerja soal shift malam cuma imbauan penulis laporan, bukan sebab; teks tegas bilang penyebabnya bukan pekerjaan itu sendiri melainkan apa yang tergeser; dan nggak ada data yang bilang mereka sudah tertinggal sejak Year Ten.

qs: What does the report imply about pupils who work long hours from necessity?
their results are likely to improve next year
their marks fell less than the rest of that group
their schools had probably offered them help
the figures may not capture their situation

qs.evidence: Some learners in the long-hours group were supporting families and had no choice, and the study did not measure the value of the money they earned.
qs.answer: the figures may not capture their situation
qs.why: Sebagian murid jam panjang menopang keluarga dan nggak punya pilihan, sementara nilai uang yang mereka dapat nggak diukur — jadi angka studi nggak nangkep keadaan mereka sepenuhnya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The study followed the pupils for a single school year."
True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: The researchers followed the same learners from Year Ten to the end of Year Twelve and compared their marks with records of paid work.

author: an education researcher
setting: a three-year study in nine secondary schools

title: Gym Membership or the Park: Which Habit Lasts?
text:
Two acquaintances resolved to become fit in January. Their experiment was accidental, yet it illustrates a genuine dilemma. One purchased a year at a gym; the other acquired a pair of shoes and began running in the park. A year later both were fitter, yet their reasons for continuing were entirely different, and that difference matters more than any comparison of equipment.
The gym offers structure. Machines guide the movement, an instructor corrects mistakes, and severe weather becomes irrelevant. In exchange it charges a monthly fee and demands a journey, which is the point at which most memberships quietly die. Park running costs almost nothing and starts at the front door, yet it provides no instruction, punishes poor shoes, and disappears in heavy rain. Neither arrangement guarantees continued attendance beyond the initial enthusiasm. Strength is easier to build indoors, whereas the habit itself is easier to build outdoors, because the barrier is lower on a tired evening.
If your aim is muscle, or you need supervision after an injury, the fee purchases something real. If your aim is a routine you will maintain in October as well as January, the cheaper option is usually the stronger one. The honest advice is to choose according to the obstacle rather than the ambition. Motivation, in other words, responds to circumstances rather than to intentions. Ask what will stop you in month four, then select the option that removes it.
qs: What is the writer's main purpose in this feature?
to show that gym fees are usually wasted money
to help readers choose by their likely obstacle
to list the machines a beginner should use first
to help readers choose by their main ambition

qs.evidence: The honest advice is to choose according to the obstacle rather than the ambition.
qs.answer: to help readers choose by their likely obstacle
qs.why: Nasihat jujur di teks: pilih menurut hambatan yang bakal menghentikanmu, bukan menurut ambisimu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Biaya gym nggak disebut sebagai uang terbuang, dia punya keunggulan sendiri; daftar mesin buat pemula nggak ada; dan sarannya justru memilih berdasar hambatan, bukan berdasar ambisi.

qs: What does the article identify as the weak point of a gym membership?
the absence of anyone to correct your movement
the journey members have to make each time
the poor condition of its indoor machines
the effect of heavy rain on its opening hours

qs.evidence: In exchange it charges a monthly fee and demands a journey, which is the point at which most memberships quietly die.
qs.answer: the journey members have to make each time
qs.why: Teks nyebut gym menuntut biaya bulanan dan sebuah perjalanan, dan di titik perjalanan itulah keanggotaan biasanya mati diam-diam.
qs.whyOthersFail: Justru gym yang punya instruktur pembenar gerakan; kondisi mesinnya nggak pernah dikeluhkan; dan cuaca buruk disebut nggak relevan di dalam ruangan, itu masalah lari di taman.

qs: How do the two options compare on building a lasting habit?
the outdoor route builds strength more quickly
the indoor route wins on both counts at once
the outdoor arrangement is the easier one to keep
neither arrangement survives the fourth month

qs.evidence: Neither arrangement guarantees continued attendance beyond the initial enthusiasm. Strength is easier to build indoors, whereas the habit itself is easier to build outdoors, because the barrier is lower on a tired evening.
qs.answer: the outdoor arrangement is the easier one to keep
qs.why: Teks bilang kekuatan lebih mudah dibangun di dalam ruangan, sedangkan kebiasaannya sendiri lebih mudah dibangun di luar karena hambatannya lebih rendah di malam yang lelah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kekuatan justru pos unggul gym, bukan taman; gym menang di kekuatan tapi kalah di kebiasaan, jadi bukan dua-duanya; dan bulan keempat disebut sebagai titik rawan, bukan batas mati kedua pilihan.

they should build the habit outdoors first

qs.evidence: If your aim is muscle, or you need supervision after an injury, the fee purchases something real.
qs.answer: paying for guidance is worth the cost for them
qs.why: Kalau tujuanmu otot atau kamu butuh pengawasan setelah cedera, teks bilang biaya gym membeli sesuatu yang nyata.
qs.whyOthersFail: Taman disebut menang di soal kebiasaan, bukan di soal keamanan setelah cedera; penurunan iuran nggak dibahas; dan urutan “kebiasaan dulu” bukan sarannya buat orang yang butuh pengawasan — buat mereka iuran gym membeli sesuatu yang nyata.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: True

author: a sports and fitness writer
setting: a health feature comparing two exercise habits

title: Letter: A Question About Our Loyalty Card Data
text:
Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing about the loyalty card issued in my name last spring. Last week your company sent a letter to my home. The letter offered baby products at a substantial discount. My household has never purchased such items in your shops, and I should therefore like to establish how that particular offer was selected.
Two related matters concern me, and both involve the same missing information. First, the conditions of the card state that purchase records are used to improve the shopping experience. That wording does not reveal whether the records are shared with other firms. Second, a member of your staff informed me by telephone that offers are constructed from similar households, a phrase that appears nowhere in those conditions. If my address is being grouped with other addresses, that arrangement should have been declared plainly at the moment I signed. A vague sentence about experience is not consent. Transparency of that kind is a legal obligation rather than a courtesy.
I should therefore like to request three things, none of which ought to be difficult. Please send me a copy of the data held under my card number, and please state which companies receive it. Please also confirm whether I may keep the card while refusing the grouping. Comparable requests are routinely granted elsewhere in the industry. I have remained a customer for nine years and should prefer to continue. Your response will determine whether I renew the arrangement when the card expires. I look forward to a written reply within fourteen days, as the regulations require. Yours faithfully, Anwar Salim.
qs: Why has this letter been written?
to ask how the writer's data produced that offer
to close the account and return the loyalty card
to object to the price of the baby products
to ask the shop to send fewer offers each month

qs.evidence: My household has never purchased such items in your shops, and I should therefore like to establish how that particular offer was selected.
qs.answer: to ask how the writer's data produced that offer
qs.why: Penulis nyatain rumahnya nggak pernah beli barang semacam itu dan pengin tahu bagaimana tawaran itu dipilih untuk dia.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis nggak menutup akun maupun mengembalikan kartu, dia minta penjelasan; harga produk bayi nggak dipersoalkan; dan yang diminta bukan pengurangan jumlah penawaran, melainkan asal-usul penawaran yang satu itu.

qs: What did the member of staff say on the telephone?
offers are chosen by the manager of each shop
offers go only to customers of nine years' standing
offers are built from groups of comparable homes
offers follow the records of a single household

qs.evidence: Second, a member of your staff informed me by telephone that offers are constructed from similar households, a phrase that appears nowhere in those conditions.
qs.answer: offers are built from groups of comparable homes
qs.why: Staf lewat telepon bilang tawaran disusun dari rumah tangga yang serupa — frasa yang justru nggak ada di syarat kartu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Manajer tiap toko nggak pernah disebut sebagai pemilih tawaran; sembilan tahun itu lama penulis jadi pelanggan, bukan syarat penerima tawaran; dan penjelasan stafnya bicara soal kelompok rumah tangga, bukan catatan satu rumah saja.

qs: Which point best supports the writer's claim that the card's conditions are unclear?
the conditions were sent only after the card arrived
the wording says nothing about sharing with firms
the conditions run to several thousand words
the staff refused to explain the card's conditions

qs.evidence: That wording does not reveal whether the records are shared with other firms.
qs.answer: the wording says nothing about sharing with firms
qs.why: Syarat kartu cuma nyebut catatan pembelian dipakai buat memperbaiki pengalaman berbelanja, tanpa ngungkap apakah catatan itu dibagi ke perusahaan lain — itulah ketidakjelasannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Waktu pengiriman syarat, panjangnya ribuan kata, dan penolakan staf semuanya akan mendukung tuduhan ketidakjelasan, tapi nggak ada di surat — staf malah menjelaskan lewat telepon, dan yang dipersoalkan justru isi kalimatnya yang bisu soal pembagian data.

qs.answer: a general phrase cannot count as real permission

qs.whyOthersFail: Panjang syaratnya nggak pernah dikeluhkan, yang dikeluhkan kaburnya; penjelasan staf justru dianggap nambah masalah karena frasanya nggak ada di syarat; dan penulis melihat kata-kata itu melindungi perusahaan, bukan pelanggan.

True

Not stated

qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena surat ini nggak minta pembatalan; “Not stated” salah karena keinginan tetap jadi pelanggan ditulis eksplisit.

author: a long-standing customer
setting: a letter of complaint to a supermarket chain

title: School Sport Should Not Be Marked Like Maths
text:
Every July our pupils receive a grade for physical education, and every July a few of them conclude that their bodies are a subject they have failed. I have taught the lesson for twelve years, and I no longer believe the grade achieves anything. The argument for marking it is respectable, which is precisely why it deserves an answer. Colleagues elsewhere have reached an identical conclusion independently.
Defenders of the grade insist that sport is a subject like any other, and that without marks it will be treated as a break. They also argue that a mark rewards effort from pupils who will never be quick. Against this stands a simpler fact. The child who is graded lowest is usually the child who most needs the habit. Maths does not lose you friends in the playground, whereas a low mark for running certainly can. Humiliation is a poor instrument of motivation. Comparing sport with an academic subject ignores how public the performance is.
There is a middle path. Replace the grade with a record of participation, personal progress, and one skill of the pupil's own choosing. Retain assessment for those who take sport as an examination subject, where a mark is expected and useful. If the aim of school sport is an adult who still moves at forty, then measuring speed at fifteen is beside the point. Such a record would still demand effort and honesty from pupils. I would rather produce a person who enjoys walking than one who remembers a number.
qs: What does the writer argue in this column?
a written record should take the place of the mark
sport should be dropped from the school timetable
pupils ought to be graded on their effort alone
marks for sport should stay but be kept private

qs.evidence: Replace the grade with a record of participation, personal progress, and one skill of the pupil's own choosing.
qs.answer: a written record should take the place of the mark

qs.whyOthersFail: Menghapus olahraga dari jadwal justru ditolak penulis; menilai murid dari usaha saja bukan usulannya; dan dia nggak minta nilai olahraga dirahasiakan, dia minta nilainya diganti catatan partisipasi dan kemajuan.

the quickest pupils will lose their reward
the lesson will be treated as free time
teachers will refuse to plan the lesson
pupils will stop attending it in July

qs.evidence: Defenders of the grade insist that sport is a subject like any other, and that without marks it will be treated as a break.
qs.answer: the lesson will be treated as free time

qs.whyOthersFail: Hadiah buat murid cepat nggak pernah jadi kekhawatiran mereka — yang mereka sebut justru hadiah buat usaha murid yang nggak akan pernah cepat; sikap guru soal perencanaan nggak dibahas; dan Juli itu bulan nilai keluar, bukan bulan murid berhenti hadir.

qs: How does the writer contrast sport with an academic subject?

a poor result in maths is harder to recover from

qs.evidence: Maths does not lose you friends in the playground, whereas a low mark for running certainly can.
qs.answer: a poor result in sport is visible to everyone

qs.whyOthersFail: Pemulihan dari nilai matematika buruk nggak pernah dibandingkan; ketatnya penilaian kedua mata pelajaran juga nggak dibahas; dan usaha justru disebut sebagai yang diklaim dihargai nilai olahraga, bukan monopoli matematika.

qs: What does the writer imply about the purpose of school sport?
it should find the fastest pupils in each year

qs.evidence: If the aim of school sport is an adult who still moves at forty, then measuring speed at fifteen is beside the point.

qs.whyOthersFail: Nyari murid tercepat justru yang dianggap melenceng dari tujuan; persiapan ujian cuma dipertahankan buat yang ambil olahraga sebagai mata ujian, bukan buat semua; dan penilaian lewat nilai adalah hal yang penulis mau ganti.

author: a physical education teacher
setting: an opinion column by a physical education teacher

title: What a Price Label Does to a Shopping Basket
text:
A supermarket chain permitted researchers to alter the labels on its shelves for eleven weeks, and the results were larger than anyone expected. Nothing else was changed: the same products, the same prices, the same positions. Only the manner in which the cost was printed on the label was different.
During the first period the shelves displayed the price per packet alone. In the second, the price per hundred grams appeared beside it in the same size. Sales of the cheapest option per gram rose by 14 per cent. Sales of the large family packets declined, because many of them were not in fact cheaper by weight. Shoppers had not suddenly grown wiser; they were simply able to compare without arithmetic in the aisle. The clearest effect appeared among customers shopping in a hurry, whose baskets altered most of all.
The study raises an awkward question for retailers. If clearer labels move money towards better value, the current design is not an accident but a choice. The researchers stop short of blaming anyone, noting that label rules differ between regions and that some chains had already begun the change. Their recommendation is narrow and testable. Print the unit price in the same size as the packet price, and allow shoppers to do the rest.
qs: What is the main finding of this study?
shoppers in a hurry buy more than careful ones
large family packets are poor value by weight
the design of a label changes what people buy
the wording of a label changes what shops charge

qs.evidence: Only the manner in which the cost was printed on the label was different.
qs.answer: the design of a label changes what people buy
qs.why: Cuma cara harga dicetak di label yang diubah, dan pola belanja tetap bergeser — jadi temuannya soal pengaruh desain label.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pembeli yang tergesa-gesa nggak dibandingkan dengan yang teliti; nilai kemasan keluarga cuma satu contoh temuan; dan harga di rak nggak berubah selama percobaan — yang berubah cuma cara harga dicetak.

qs: What was added to the labels in the second period?
a warning about the largest family packets
the price of the same item in other shops
the cost for each hundred grams of product
a note about the position on the shelf

qs.evidence: In the second, the price per hundred grams appeared beside it in the same size.
qs.answer: the cost for each hundred grams of product
qs.why: Pada periode kedua, harga per seratus gram muncul di samping harga paket dengan ukuran huruf yang sama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nggak ada peringatan apa pun yang ditempel di label; harga di toko lain nggak pernah dicetak; dan posisi rak justru bagian yang sengaja dibiarkan sama persis.

qs: Which result best supports the claim that the labels helped comparison?
buying moved towards the cheaper option by weight
shoppers spent longer choosing between the packets
fewer shoppers asked staff about the prices
shoppers in a hurry bought the largest packets

qs.evidence: Sales of the cheapest option per gram rose by 14 per cent.
qs.answer: buying moved towards the cheaper option by weight
qs.why: Penjualan pilihan termurah per gram naik 14 persen, dan itu yang nunjukin label barunya benar-benar bikin perbandingan jadi bisa dilakukan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Waktu memilih dan pertanyaan ke staf nggak pernah diukur; dan pembeli yang tergesa-gesa justru menggeser belanjaannya ke pilihan yang lebih murah per gram, sementara kemasan keluarga besar penjualannya turun.

qs.answer: an unhelpful label may be a choice, not an accident

qs.whyOthersFail: Mengajari pembeli berhitung bukan pertanyaan yang bikin toko nggak nyaman; keseragaman aturan antar wilayah nggak dibahas; dan justru intinya label yang menyusahkan itu pilihan, bukan kecelakaan yang tinggal dibetulkan.

author: a consumer research writer
setting: an eleven-week experiment in a supermarket chain

title: An Online Careers Course, Reviewed Honestly
text:
I spent six weeks on a heavily advertised online course promising to prepare school leavers for a first job. I finished with mixed feelings, and with a clear view of where the money goes. The teaching is considerably better than the marketing implies, and the marketing is the worst feature of the product. Anyone paying the full fee deserves to know which sections earn their money.
The strongest section is the third week, which concerns written applications and their revision. You produce four genuine documents, receive comments from a human reviewer within two days, and then rewrite them. The interview week, by contrast, is remarkably thin. It contains two videos, a quiz, and a list of questions available free elsewhere. Nothing in the programme addresses salary, contracts, or resigning from a position honourably. The discussion forum is silent, and the promised mentor proved to be a monthly group call with ninety participants.
Would I recommend it? At the reduced price, certainly, and chiefly for the application week, which is genuinely useful and difficult to find elsewhere. At the full price it represents poor value, because half the material repeats what schools already supply without charge. The verdict is three marks out of five, weighted almost entirely by one week. The certificate at the end carries no recognized value with employers. Purchase it when it is cheap, work through the third week twice, and ignore the remainder without guilt.

one week is worth the money and the rest is not
the course is fair value at the price advertised
the marketing describes the teaching accurately
the whole course is worth the money at the lower price

author: a reviewer who took the course
setting: a review of a six-week online course

title: Free Mail or Paid Mail: What Are You Trading?
text:
Most people use a free mail service, and a growing number now pay a small annual fee for one instead. The two look almost identical on the screen, which is why the choice is usually settled by habit. The genuine difference sits behind the window, in what each company requires from you in order to survive.
A free service earns its living from attention. Its notice permits the scanning of messages to construct interest groups, and its storage is generous because the mail itself is the product. A paid service earns from the fee, so its notice can promise no scanning and no advertising partners. Against that, paid services are smaller. They offer fewer tools, weaker protection against junk mail, and a real risk that the company closes and your address disappears. Free services also win on recovery, since a forgotten password is easier to resolve when millions share the same system.
Neither answer suits everybody. If your mail carries medical letters, contracts, or a business, the annual fee is cheap insurance and the shorter feature list is bearable. If you mainly receive receipts and messages from friends, paying to hide them from an advertiser may not be worth the expense. What matters is deciding deliberately. A service you never chose is still a service you are paying for, in one currency or another.
qs: What is the writer's purpose in this comparison?
to urge every reader to pay the annual fee
to explain how a lost password is recovered
to show what each service needs from its users
to show that the two services differ little in practice

qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis nggak mendorong semua orang bayar; pemulihan kata sandi nggak dibahas; dan perbandingan ini nunjukin perbedaan yang nyata di balik jendela, bukan bahwa keduanya nyaris sama.

qs: What does the article say a free service does with messages?
it reads them to sort users into interest groups
it deletes them once the storage limit is reached
it hides them from every advertising partner

habit is a reliable guide to this decision

qs.whyOthersFail: Justru semua opsi punya harga, entah uang entah data; kebiasaan disebut penuntun yang buruk; dan teks nggak memprediksi layanan gratis bakal mulai menarik biaya tahunan.

True
False
