author: a technology writer
setting: a comparison article on email providers

title: Unpaid Internships Choose the Wrong People
text:
Every summer, offices fill with capable young people working for nothing. Every autumn we wonder why the same families keep appearing in the same professions. The two facts are connected, and the connection is hardly a mystery. An unpaid position does not select the strongest candidate; it selects the candidate who can afford to be unpaid.
Follow the chain. A three-month placement in a large city costs a student rent, travel, and food, which together exceed what many families earn in that period. The applicants who remain are therefore those with a spare room in the city or a parent able to send money. Employers then report, honestly enough, that their interns were excellent, and they recruit from that group. The outcome is a profession which resembles a family album, and a set of employers convinced that they chose on merit.
The remedy is not to abolish placements but to pay for them. Where the law has required a minimum wage for interns, the number of positions fell slightly and the range of applicants widened sharply. That exchange seems worth making. I would go further and invite any organization unable to pay an intern to ask whether it truly needs one. Work that deserves to be done is work that deserves to be paid.
qs: What is the writer arguing in this column?
placements ought to be abolished in every field
unpaid places select by ability, not by money
interns are rarely as able as employers claim
unpaid places select by money, not by ability

qs.evidence: An unpaid position does not select the strongest candidate; it selects the candidate who can afford to be unpaid.
qs.answer: unpaid places select by money, not by ability
qs.why: Teks nyebut posisi tanpa upah nggak milih kandidat terkuat, tapi kandidat yang mampu bekerja tanpa dibayar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Arahnya kebalikan: tempat tanpa upah menyaring yang mampu membiayai diri, bukan yang paling cakap; penghapusan penempatan di semua bidang nggak diusulkan; dan penulis nggak nyebut intern kurang cakap, dia nyebut penyaringnya salah.

qs: What does the writer say a three-month placement costs a student?
more than many households make in that time
about the same as three months of city rent
less than the wage an employer would have paid
about a month of an intern's own travel

qs.evidence: A three-month placement in a large city costs a student rent, travel, and food, which together exceed what many families earn in that period.
qs.answer: more than many households make in that time
qs.why: Sewa, transport, dan makan selama tiga bulan di kota besar disebut melebihi penghasilan banyak keluarga pada periode yang sama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga bulan sewa kota dan sebulan biaya transpor bukan patokan yang dipakai teks, dan upah yang seharusnya dibayar pemberi kerja juga bukan; teks nyebut sewa, transpor, dan makan selama tiga bulan digabung melebihi penghasilan banyak keluarga pada periode itu.

qs: Which evidence does the writer use to defend paying interns?
paid interns stayed longer and worked harder
unpaid interns produced weaker work than paid ones
a legal wage widened the field and cut few places
employers who paid reported cheaper recruitment later

qs.evidence: Where the law has required a minimum wage for interns, the number of positions fell slightly and the range of applicants widened sharply.
qs.answer: a legal wage widened the field and cut few places
qs.why: Di tempat hukum mewajibkan upah minimum buat intern, jumlah posisi cuma turun sedikit sementara ragam pelamar melebar tajam — itu bukti pertukaran yang penulis anggap layak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya akan jadi pembelaan yang masuk akal buat pengupahan, tapi teks nggak membandingkan lama bertahan, mutu kerja, maupun biaya rekrutmen; buktinya cuma satu — di tempat upah minimum diwajibkan, jumlah posisi turun sedikit sementara sebaran pelamar melebar tajam.

qs: What does the writer imply about employers who praise their interns?
they knowingly mislead the public about pay
they mistake a narrow selection for a fair one
they usually recruit from outside that group
they know the placement excluded poorer students

qs.evidence: Employers then report, honestly enough, that their interns were excellent, and they recruit from that group.
qs.answer: they mistake a narrow selection for a fair one
qs.why: Pemberi kerja melapor dengan jujur bahwa intern mereka bagus lalu merekrut dari kelompok itu, jadi mereka mengira seleksi yang sempit sebagai seleksi yang adil.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks justru nyebut laporan mereka jujur, jadi bukan menyesatkan; perekrutan dilakukan dari kelompok intern itu sendiri, bukan dari luar; dan kesadaran bahwa murid miskin tersingkir adalah hal yang teks bilang mereka tidak punya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "An employer who cannot pay an intern should question whether it needs one."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: An employer who cannot pay an intern should question whether it needs one.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: I would go further and invite any organization unable to pay an intern to ask whether it truly needs one.
qs.why: Kalimat penutupnya persis minta organisasi yang nggak mampu bayar buat nanya apa mereka benar-benar butuh intern, jadi klaim ini parafrasa langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena saran itu nggak dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena ajakan itu ditulis eksplisit di paragraf ketiga.

author: a columnist on work and education
setting: an opinion column on entry into the professions

title: The Night Bus Problem Nobody Measured
text:
Why do so few women use the final bus of the evening? A city university devoted a year to the question and discovered that the answer had almost nothing to do with the bus itself. Researchers rode 240 late services, counted passengers, and interviewed 500 residents who had decided not to travel.
The refusals gathered around two points that no timetable mentions. The first was the walk from the stop to the door, which averaged nine minutes and crossed unlit ground in most districts. The second obstacle was the period of waiting itself, particularly at isolated stops. A stop without other people felt unsafe long before any incident occurred. Nine of every ten interviewees described precisely the same anxiety, independently of each other. Reported offences along the routes remained low, and the passengers already using them felt entirely secure. The problem therefore sat at the edges of the journey rather than inside the vehicle.
Their conclusion challenges an assumption embedded in most transport planning. That finding points towards remedies of remarkably modest expense. The team recommends lighting the final streets rather than the main road. It also proposes publishing accurate arrival times so that nobody waits in the dark, and permitting passengers to leave the bus between stops after ten o'clock. None of these measures demands a fresh route or an additional vehicle. Where two of the three were attempted on one line, the number of women travelling late rose by a third within four months. The authors describe the result as encouraging rather than conclusive.
qs: What is the main point of this report?
late buses are too crowded for comfort
crime along the late routes has been rising
the risk sits around the journey, not on the bus
the risk sits inside the bus, not around the journey

qs.evidence: The problem therefore sat at the edges of the journey rather than inside the vehicle.
qs.answer: the risk sits around the journey, not on the bus
qs.why: Laporan nyimpulin masalahnya duduk di tepi-tepi perjalanan — jalan kaki dan penantian — bukan di dalam kendaraannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Arahnya kebalikan: masalahnya duduk di tepi perjalanan, bukan di dalam kendaraan; kepadatan bus nggak pernah dikeluhkan; dan jumlah kejahatan dilaporkan tetap rendah, bukan naik.

qs: How long was the average walk from the stop to the door?
roughly nine minutes on foot
about ten minutes on foot
close to four minutes on foot
roughly fourteen minutes on foot

qs.evidence: The first was the walk from the stop to the door, which averaged nine minutes and crossed unlit ground in most districts.
qs.answer: roughly nine minutes on foot
qs.why: Jalan dari pemberhentian ke pintu rumah rata-rata sembilan menit dan melewati tanah tanpa lampu di sebagian besar distrik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sepuluh menit, empat menit, dan empat belas menit nggak ada di laporan; jalan dari pemberhentian ke pintu rumah rata-rata sembilan menit.

qs: Which finding best supports the claim that fear was not caused by crime?
police records showed offences falling year by year
no passenger had been robbed on a late service
offences stayed rare and regular riders felt safe
the late routes matched daytime routes for crime

qs.evidence: Reported offences along the routes remained low, and the passengers already using them felt entirely secure.
qs.answer: offences stayed rare and regular riders felt safe
qs.why: Kejahatan yang dilaporkan di rute-rute itu tetap rendah dan penumpang yang sudah memakainya merasa benar-benar aman — jadi rasa takutnya bukan buah angka kejahatan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tren tahunan kejahatan, ketiadaan perampokan, dan perbandingan dengan rute siang semuanya akan mendukung klaim itu, tapi nggak ada di laporan; yang dilaporkan cuma pelanggaran yang tetap rendah dan penumpang tetap yang merasa aman.

qs: What does the report imply about the cost of the proposed measures?
they can be introduced without a large purchase
they cost more than the city can now afford
they need extra staff at the isolated stops
they will require a completely new bus route

qs.evidence: None of these measures demands a fresh route or an additional vehicle.
qs.answer: they can be introduced without a large purchase
qs.why: Teks nyebut nggak satu pun langkah itu menuntut rute baru atau kendaraan tambahan, jadi biayanya kecil.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nyebut nggak satu pun langkah itu menuntut rute baru atau kendaraan tambahan, dan biayanya disebut sangat sederhana; petugas tambahan di pemberhentian terpencil juga nggak pernah masuk usulan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Passengers waiting in pairs reported the same anxiety as those alone."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Passengers waiting in pairs reported the same anxiety as those alone.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Nine of every ten interviewees described precisely the same anxiety, independently of each other.
qs.why: Teks cuma nyebut sembilan dari sepuluh orang yang diwawancara ngerasain kecemasan yang sama; yang nunggu berdua dan yang nunggu sendirian nggak pernah dipisah jadi dua kelompok.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena perbandingan antara penumpang berdua dan penumpang sendirian nggak ada datanya di teks; “False” juga salah karena teks nggak nyatain kelompok berdua ngerasa berbeda — soal itu dia memang diam.

author: an urban research writer
setting: a year-long university study of late bus services

title: A Fitness Band That Solves the Wrong Problem
text:
The band I have worn for a month costs as much as a decent pair of running shoes. It promises to solve a genuine difficulty, since most people abandon exercise in the fourth week. Its answer is constant measurement. After thirty days I am fitter, better informed, and slightly less persuaded by the promise.
As equipment it is excellent. The battery survives nine days, the strap tolerates rain and a swimming pool, and the step count matched a careful manual count within two per cent. Heart rate during steady running was close to a chest monitor, although it drifted badly during sudden efforts. The sleep score, however, is the weak point. On two nights when I slept badly the band awarded me a high score, and on one restful night it reported broken sleep.
The deeper difficulty is what the app does with all this information. It sends four notifications a day, sets targets I never chose, and converts a missed walk into a broken record. Anyone who already worries about exercise will find that pressure unhelpful, and the switch that silences it lies three menus deep. Purchase the band for its honest numbers, then spend ten minutes disabling the encouragement. Three and a half marks out of five: a reliable instrument wrapped in a nagging coach.
qs: What is the reviewer's main criticism of the band?
the battery gives out after only nine days
the step count is less accurate than claimed
the software gives too little guidance
the software pushes the wearer too hard

qs.evidence: It sends four notifications a day, sets targets I never chose, and converts a missed walk into a broken record.
qs.answer: the software pushes the wearer too hard
qs.why: Keluhan utamanya soal aplikasi: empat notifikasi sehari, target yang nggak pernah dipilih pemakai, dan jalan yang terlewat dihitung sebagai rekor rusak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Baterai sembilan hari dipuji, bukan dikeluhkan; hitungan langkahnya akurat dalam dua persen; dan keluhannya bukan tuntunan yang terlalu sedikit, justru dorongan yang terlalu banyak: empat notifikasi sehari dan target yang nggak dipilih pemakai.

qs: What does the review say about the heart rate readings?
they were out by about two per cent all day
they held up except during sudden changes of effort
they matched a chest monitor during sudden efforts
they were the strongest feature of the band

qs.evidence: Heart rate during steady running was close to a chest monitor, although it drifted badly during sudden efforts.
qs.answer: they held up except during sudden changes of effort
qs.why: Denyut saat lari stabil mendekati monitor dada, tapi melenceng jauh ketika usahanya berubah mendadak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Selisih dua persen itu soal hitungan langkah; kecocokan dengan monitor dada berlaku saat lari stabil, justru melenceng ketika usahanya berubah mendadak; dan bagian terkuat perangkat ini bukan denyutnya.

qs: Which example best supports the reviewer's doubts about the sleep score?
a bad night scored well and a good one badly
the score changed after the app was updated
the score differed from a clinic's own measurement
the band gave no score at all on two nights

qs.evidence: On two nights when I slept badly the band awarded me a high score, and on one restful night it reported broken sleep.
qs.answer: a bad night scored well and a good one badly
qs.why: Dua malam dengan tidur buruk malah dikasih skor tinggi, sementara satu malam yang nyaman dilaporkan sebagai tidur terputus.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pembaruan aplikasi, pembanding dari klinik, dan malam tanpa skor sama-sama akan jadi contoh keraguan yang sah, tapi nggak satu pun disebut; contoh yang dipakai adalah malam tidur buruk yang diberi skor tinggi dan malam nyaman yang dilaporkan terputus.

qs: What does the reviewer imply about anxious exercisers?
they should ignore the numbers the band gives
they will gain most from the four daily messages
the reminders may do them more harm than good
they ought to buy a chest monitor instead

qs.evidence: Anyone who already worries about exercise will find that pressure unhelpful, and the switch that silences it lies three menus deep.
qs.answer: the reminders may do them more harm than good
qs.why: Teks bilang siapa pun yang sudah cemas soal olahraga akan merasa tekanan itu nggak menolong, dan tombol buat mematikannya susah dicari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Angka-angkanya justru direkomendasikan (“Purchase the band for its honest numbers”); empat pesan sehari adalah sumber tekanan itu, bukan manfaat; dan monitor dada cuma dipakai sebagai pembanding ketepatan, bukan saran beli.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: False

qs.why: Teks nyebut harganya setara sepatu lari yang bagus, jadi klaim “far less” ngebalik perbandingan harganya.

author: a fitness equipment reviewer
setting: a review of a wrist fitness band

title: Letter: Request to Adjust the School Bus Timetable
text:
Dear Ms Wijaya, I am writing as chair of the parents' committee about route 14, which serves our school gate each morning. Since the timetable changed at the start of term, the bus has been timed to reach the gate at 7:41, nine minutes before the first lesson. We are grateful for the additional service, yet the new arrangement is producing daily difficulty. Reliable timing of this kind is an administrative necessity rather than a preference.
The difficulty is the distance between the published plan and the actual road. Between the market and the school the bus crosses two junctions which hold traffic for several minutes. Our observations across six weeks indicate an average arrival at 7:52. On eleven separate mornings the bus reached the gate considerably after eight o'clock. Pupils then enter the lesson late, are recorded as absent, and the office spends its first hour correcting the register. The drivers are not at fault; the timetable simply does not match the street.
We should like to suggest two possible changes, either of which would assist. The simplest is to move the departure from the terminus five minutes earlier, which our figures suggest would remove most late arrivals. Alternatively, the route could turn before the second junction and stop at the corner, a walk of two minutes for the children. Similar adjustments have apparently succeeded on neighbouring routes. Our committee is happy to supply the full record of arrival times and to meet at your convenience. Yours sincerely, Bima Setiawan, committee chair.

to propose changes that would end the late arrivals
to complain about the conduct of the bus drivers
to ask for an entirely new route past the school
to accept the new arrival time as workable

qs.answer: to propose changes that would end the late arrivals
qs.why: Surat ini mengusulkan dua perubahan — berangkat lima menit lebih awal atau berhenti di tikungan sebelum persimpangan kedua — supaya keterlambatan berhenti.

nine minutes before the first lesson

qs.whyOthersFail: Sembilan menit sebelum pelajaran adalah rencana di atas kertas, bukan kenyataan; lima menit lebih awal itu usulan perubahan keberangkatan; dan ketepatan persis dibantah oleh rata-rata 7:52.

False
Not stated

author: the chair of a parents' committee
setting: a letter to a city transport office

title: Walking or Cycling to School: An Even Contest
text:
Ask two parents how a child should reach school and you will receive two confident answers. Walking is safer; cycling is quicker. Neither option is universally superior, whatever confident parents assert. Both statements are accurate, and neither settles the question, because the two journeys suit different distances and different streets.
Walking wins on cost and on independence at an early age. It demands no equipment, no lock, and no repair, and a nine-year-old can manage it alone in most neighbourhoods. Beyond about two kilometres, however, walking consumes an hour of the day and delivers wet shoes. Cycling covers four kilometres in the time walking covers one, and it produces the stronger training effect for the heart. The price is a bicycle, a lock, a dry place to keep it, and a route where a child is not obliged to share a lane with lorries.
Local circumstances therefore determine the appropriate arrangement. The sensible test is the map rather than the principle. Under two kilometres on quiet pavements, walking is difficult to beat and demands nothing from anybody. Beyond that distance, cycling repays its cost where a safe route exists, and is a poor idea where none does. Where neither option works, the answer is a bus for part of the way and feet for the remainder. What matters is that the journey happens without a car, whichever pair of legs performs the work.
qs: What is the writer's purpose in this feature?
to prove that walking is the safer choice
to persuade parents to buy a bicycle this year
to show that distance and streets decide it
to show that the safer option is always the better one

qs.evidence: Neither option is universally superior, whatever confident parents assert. Both statements are accurate, and neither settles the question, because the two journeys suit different distances and different streets.
qs.answer: to show that distance and streets decide it
qs.why: Teks nyebut nggak ada pilihan yang unggul secara mutlak, karena kedua perjalanan cocok buat jarak dan jalan yang berbeda.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keamanan jalan kaki diakui sebagai satu pernyataan yang benar tapi disebut nggak menyelesaikan pertanyaannya, jadi bukan yang paling aman otomatis paling baik; dan nggak ada dorongan beli sepeda tahun ini.

qs: What does the article say a young child needs in order to walk to school?
a lock and a dry place to keep it
nothing beyond the shoes already worn
a route that avoids the quiet pavements
a companion for the first two kilometres

qs.evidence: It demands no equipment, no lock, and no repair, and a nine-year-old can manage it alone in most neighbourhoods.
qs.answer: nothing beyond the shoes already worn

qs.whyOthersFail: Kunci dan tempat penyimpanan kering adalah harga bersepeda; trotoar yang sepi justru kondisi terbaik buat jalan kaki, bukan yang dihindari; dan pendamping nggak pernah disebut sebagai syarat.

qs: How does cycling compare with walking over the same period of time?
it covers about twice the distance instead
it covers roughly four times the distance
it takes an hour longer over the same trip
it gives a weaker training effect for the heart

qs.evidence: Cycling covers four kilometres in the time walking covers one, and it produces the stronger training effect for the heart.
qs.answer: it covers roughly four times the distance
qs.why: Bersepeda menempuh empat kilometer dalam waktu yang dipakai jalan kaki buat satu kilometer.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dua kali jarak nggak sesuai angka teks; satu jam itu waktu yang dimakan jalan kaki di atas dua kilometer, bukan tambahan waktu bersepeda; dan efek latihan bersepeda disebut lebih kuat, bukan lebih lemah.

qs: What does the writer imply about a long journey on a road used by lorries?
walking becomes quicker than cycling there
a child should cycle only with an adult along
the family should buy a stronger lock for it
cycling is the wrong choice in those conditions

qs.evidence: Beyond that distance, cycling repays its cost where a safe route exists, and is a poor idea where none does.
qs.answer: cycling is the wrong choice in those conditions
qs.why: Teks bilang di luar dua kilometer bersepeda membayar biayanya kalau ada rute aman, dan merupakan ide buruk kalau rute aman itu nggak ada.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jalan kaki nggak jadi lebih cepat, dia cuma jadi pilihan yang mungkin di jarak pendek; pendampingan orang dewasa nggak pernah diusulkan; dan kunci yang lebih kuat nggak nyelesaikan soal lajur yang dibagi dengan lorry.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer recommends a car for journeys longer than two kilometres."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer recommends a car for journeys longer than two kilometres.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: What matters is that the journey happens without a car, whichever pair of legs performs the work.
qs.why: Teks justru nekenin perjalanan mesti tanpa mobil, jadi klaim yang nyaranin mobil itu kebalikan langsung dari kalimat penutup.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena penulis nolak mobil; “Not stated” salah karena sikap soal mobil ditulis eksplisit.

topic: ways for children to travel to school
author: a family health writer
setting: a comparison feature on school journeys

title: Mend It First: Why Replacement Wins Unfairly
text:
My kettle failed in May, and replacing it would have cost less than mending it. That single sentence explains most of what has gone wrong with the way we buy things. The market has made repair resemble a hobby for the patient, and that impression is neither natural nor permanent.
Defenders of replacement have arguments worth hearing. New appliances consume less electricity, arrive with a guarantee, and are built in factories where safety can be inspected. A mended kettle may fail again next winter, and nobody guarantees it. Yet the comparison is usually made with the wrong figures. It counts the electricity of the new machine and ignores the metal, the plastic, and the shipping behind it. Recycling arrives far too late in the process to repair that particular arithmetic. It also ignores the small workshops which disappear when nobody brings anything to be mended.
None of this difficulty is solved by lecturing individual shoppers about their choices. Manufacturers should be obliged to sell spare parts at a fair price for ten years. Repair should also carry the lower rate of tax that new goods already enjoy through scale. Where such rules exist, small workshops have reopened and the price gap has narrowed. I would rather live in a street containing somebody who can mend a kettle. Mending is not nostalgia; it is simply arithmetic performed honestly and in full.
qs: What is the writer arguing in this column?
new appliances are more dangerous to use
shoppers who replace goods deserve blame
rules, not shoppers, should make repair cheap
shoppers, not rules, will make repair cheap again

qs.evidence: None of this difficulty is solved by lecturing individual shoppers about their choices.
qs.answer: rules, not shoppers, should make repair cheap
qs.why: Teks nyebut kesulitan ini nggak selesai dengan menceramahi pembeli satu per satu, lalu ngusulin kewajiban suku cadang dan tarif pajak yang lebih rendah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pabrik justru disebut tempat keselamatan bisa diperiksa, jadi barang baru nggak digambarkan lebih berbahaya; menyalahkan pembeli ditolak eksplisit; dan teks nyebut kesulitan ini nggak selesai lewat pilihan pembeli, tapi lewat aturan.

qs: What does the writer accept about newly made appliances?
they are cheaper to mend than older machines
they support the small workshops in each street
they are built from recycled metal and plastic
they use less power and are checked for safety

qs.evidence: New appliances consume less electricity, arrive with a guarantee, and are built in factories where safety can be inspected.
qs.answer: they use less power and are checked for safety
qs.why: Penulis mengakui alat baru memakai listrik lebih sedikit, datang dengan garansi, dan dibuat di pabrik yang keselamatannya bisa diperiksa.
qs.whyOthersFail: Biaya perbaikan alat baru nggak pernah dibandingkan; bengkel kecil justru menghilang kalau semua orang beli baru; dan bahan daur ulang nggak disebut — daur ulang malah dibilang datang terlalu telat dalam prosesnya.

qs: Which point best supports the claim that the usual comparison is unfair?
the guarantee on a new machine is rarely used
the electricity saving is smaller than claimed
the cost of the old machine is counted twice
the metal and transport of the new one are ignored

qs.evidence: It counts the electricity of the new machine and ignores the metal, the plastic, and the shipping behind it.
qs.answer: the metal and transport of the new one are ignored
qs.why: Perbandingan yang biasa cuma menghitung listrik mesin baru dan mengabaikan logam, plastik, serta pengapalannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Garansi yang jarang dipakai, penghematan listrik yang dibesar-besarkan, dan penghitungan ganda biaya mesin lama semuanya akan membuat perbandingan itu timpang, tapi nggak satu pun dinyatakan; yang dinyatakan hitungannya mengabaikan logam, plastik, dan pengapalan.

qs: Which statement best restates the writer's proposal?
make makers cut the price of new appliances
ban the sale of goods without spare parts
make makers sell cheap parts for a decade
ask shoppers to mend their kettles at home

qs.evidence: Manufacturers should be obliged to sell spare parts at a fair price for ten years.
qs.answer: make makers sell cheap parts for a decade
qs.why: Usulan intinya: produsen wajib menjual suku cadang dengan harga yang wajar selama sepuluh tahun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang diusulkan bukan menurunkan harga alat baru melainkan mewajibkan suku cadang murah; larangan penjualan nggak pernah diusulkan; dan penulis tegas bilang masalahnya nggak selesai dengan menyuruh pembeli memperbaiki sendiri.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Where such rules have been introduced, the cost difference has shrunk."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Where such rules have been introduced, the cost difference has shrunk.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Where such rules exist, small workshops have reopened and the price gap has narrowed.
qs.why: “the price gap has narrowed” sama artinya sama selisih biaya yang menyempit, jadi klaim ini parafrasa langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena arah perubahannya nggak dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena efek aturan itu disebut eksplisit.

author: a consumer affairs columnist
setting: an opinion column on consumer goods

title: One Roof, One Year
text:
Every dry season our school pays an electricity bill that nobody wants to read aloud. The fans run all day, the computer lab hums until the last bell, and the charge quietly eats money that could have bought books. That is the problem, and it will not be solved by asking pupils to switch off the lights more politely. The solution sits above our heads, on the flat roof of the school hall.

Teachers in the staff room raise a fair objection: solar panels are expensive, and thick cloud covers this town for weeks. Yet that objection only measures the first year. Prices have dropped sharply since the district grant scheme opened, and installers now compete for small orders. A modest set of panels on the hall roof would still supply about a third of our daytime demand. Having compared three quotations myself, I am convinced the equipment would pay for itself within seven years.

The wider gain, though, is not financial. A school that makes its own power teaches energy in the most honest way, which is by measuring it. Pupils could check the display each morning, draw the curve and argue about the figures instead of copying them out of a textbook. I therefore favour a small, reversible first step: one roof, one year, one public report. Another dry season of complaining about the bill would teach nobody anything.
qs: What is the writer's main purpose in this column?
To urge the school to test panels on a single roof first.
To warn that solar panels rarely suit towns with weeks of thick cloud.
To propose that pupils record the meter readings for a whole year.
To press the district to widen its grant scheme to more schools.

qs.evidence: I therefore favour a small, reversible first step: one roof, one year, one public report.
qs.answer: To urge the school to test panels on a single roof first.
qs.why: Penutup teks jelas: penulis mau langkah kecil yang bisa dibatalkan, satu atap dulu, lalu laporan terbuka. Itu tujuan tulisan opini ini.
qs.whyOthersFail: Awan tebal disebut sebagai keberatan yang penulis bantah, bukan peringatan yang ia sampaikan. Pencatatan meter oleh murid memang muncul, tapi sebagai keuntungan tambahan setelah panel ada, bukan usulan pokok kolom ini. Perluasan skema hibah tidak pernah diminta; skema itu hanya disebut sebagai sebab harga turun.

qs: According to the writer, what has changed since the district grant scheme opened?
Grant money now covers most of the cost of a school installation.
Installers have grown less interested in orders as small as a school's.
Panel costs fell and firms now bid against each other for small jobs.
Panel prices have held steady while installation charges have risen.

qs.evidence: Prices have dropped sharply since the district grant scheme opened, and installers now compete for small orders.
qs.answer: Panel costs fell and firms now bid against each other for small jobs.
qs.why: Kalimat itu menyebut dua akibat sejak skema hibah dibuka: harga turun tajam dan pemasang bersaing untuk pesanan kecil. Kunci menyatakan hal sama dengan kata lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks hanya bilang skema hibah dibuka, bukan bahwa hibah menanggung sebagian besar biaya. Pemasang justru disebut bersaing untuk pesanan kecil, jadi dua opsi lain membalik arah kalimat itu: minat pemasang naik, dan harga panel turun tajam.

qs: Which piece of evidence does the writer use to support the claim about paying for itself?
A reading of the school's own bills across several dry seasons.
A district report on the daytime demand a hall roof could meet.
An installer's estimate of how many years the panels would last.
A personal check of three separate price offers for the work.

qs.evidence: Having compared three quotations myself, I am convinced the equipment would pay for itself within seven years.
qs.answer: A personal check of three separate price offers for the work.
qs.why: Dasar klaim tujuh tahun itu satu hal: penulis sendiri membandingkan tiga penawaran harga. Nggak ada bukti lain yang dipakai untuk klaim ini.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tagihan sekolah dan angka sepertiga permintaan siang hari memang muncul di teks, tapi bukan sebagai dasar klaim tujuh tahun itu. Laporan distrik dan perkiraan umur panel tidak pernah disebut sama sekali; satu-satunya dasar yang diberikan penulis adalah tiga penawaran harga yang ia bandingkan sendiri.

qs: What does the writer imply about the teachers who object to the panels?
They doubt a roof this size could supply a third of daytime demand.
Their sums stop too early and ignore the later savings.
They expect the grant scheme to close before any work could begin.
They would rather the money were spent on books for the pupils.

qs.evidence: Yet that objection only measures the first year.
qs.answer: Their sums stop too early and ignore the later savings.
qs.why: Kata "only measures the first year" menyiratkan hitungan guru berhenti terlalu cepat, jadi penghematan tahun-tahun berikutnya nggak masuk hitungan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Isi keberatan guru cuma dua hal: harga dan awan. Angka sepertiga adalah klaim penulis, bukan keraguan guru; penutupan skema hibah tidak pernah disinggung; dan buku disebut sebagai hal yang tergerus tagihan listrik, bukan pilihan belanja yang guru tuntut.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Roof panels above the hall could meet roughly a third of the school's daytime electricity needs."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Roof panels above the hall could meet roughly a third of the school's daytime electricity needs.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: A modest set of panels on the hall roof would still supply about a third of our daytime demand.
qs.why: Ini parafrasa penuh: “supply about a third of our daytime demand” sama artinya dengan memenuhi kira-kira sepertiga kebutuhan listrik siang hari. Jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena nggak ada proposisi yang dibalik. "Not stated" salah karena angkanya jelas tertulis di paragraf kedua.

topic: rooftop solar power for a school
author: opinion column by a school science teacher
setting: a secondary school in a dry upland town

title: What a Famous Waterfall Does to a Village
text:
A small research team spent last year counting visitors in four highland villages, and the findings have just been published. The question was simple. What happens to a village when its waterfall becomes famous online? The team interviewed 240 households and recorded arrivals at every gate. Because the four villages lie within an hour of one another, the comparison is unusually fair.

The chain of cause and effect shows up clearly in the figures. Once photographs of the upper falls spread across social media, weekend arrivals in the nearest village rose fivefold. That rise pushed up rents along the main lane. Several families therefore moved their food stalls to cheaper ground behind the car park. As a result, the money earned from visitors was shared far less evenly than the team had expected. In the two villages that kept a daily booking limit, income grew more slowly but stayed with local owners.

The report avoids easy conclusions, yet its authors do state one opinion plainly. They argue that a district which counts only arrivals is measuring the wrong thing. The figure they recommend instead is the share of visitor spending still held in the village after three months. I find that suggestion convincing, because it turns a boast into a test. Without such a test, a famous waterfall may enrich a district while leaving its neighbours poorer.
qs: What is the main idea of this report?
Rising rents push food stalls to cheaper ground behind a car park.
Daily booking limits raise a village's income faster than open access.
Four highland villages now depend on one waterfall for their income.
Sudden fame changes who keeps the money a village earns.

qs.evidence: As a result, the money earned from visitors was shared far less evenly than the team had expected.
qs.answer: Sudden fame changes who keeps the money a village earns.
qs.why: Inti laporan: setelah air terjun viral, uang dari wisatawan masuk tapi pembagiannya berubah dan jadi jauh lebih nggak merata. Kunci merangkum itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pindahnya warung memang terjadi, tapi itu satu mata rantai, bukan gagasan utama laporan. Desa berbatas pemesanan justru tumbuh lebih lambat, dan teks tidak pernah bilang keempat desa bergantung pada satu air terjun; tiga desa lain dipakai sebagai pembanding.

qs: How did the team gather its data?
By talking to 240 households and logging arrivals at each entrance.
By counting weekend visitors at the upper falls for a single season.
By comparing rent records kept by the four village offices.
By asking stall owners to keep a diary of their weekend takings.

qs.evidence: The team interviewed 240 households and recorded arrivals at every gate.
qs.answer: By talking to 240 households and logging arrivals at each entrance.
qs.why: Metodenya dua hal: wawancara 240 rumah tangga dan pencatatan kedatangan di setiap gerbang. Kunci menyebut keduanya dengan kata lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pencatatan dilakukan setahun dan di setiap gerbang desa, bukan satu musim di air terjun atasnya. Kenaikan sewa adalah temuan, bukan sumber data, dan tidak ada buku harian pemilik warung dalam metode tim ini.

qs: How did the villages with a daily booking limit differ from the nearest village?
Their earnings rose less quickly but remained in local hands.
Their rents rose more slowly, so their food stalls were able to stay.
Their weekend arrivals climbed just as sharply once photographs spread.
Their households shared the visitor money less evenly than before.

qs.evidence: In the two villages that kept a daily booking limit, income grew more slowly but stayed with local owners.
qs.answer: Their earnings rose less quickly but remained in local hands.
qs.why: Bedanya: pendapatan naik lebih lambat tapi tetap dipegang pemilik setempat. Kunci mengulang isi itu tanpa memakai frasa aslinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang dikatakan teks soal dua desa berbatas hanya ini: pendapatan naik lebih lambat tapi tetap di tangan pemilik setempat. Soal sewa dan warung pindah terjadi di desa terdekat, kenaikan lima kali lipat juga milik desa itu, dan pembagian yang makin tidak merata justru gejala di desa tanpa batas.

qs: Why do the authors prefer their recommended figure to a count of arrivals?
Because arrival counts reach a district office too late to be useful.
Because spending figures are simpler for a small office to collect.
Because a count of arrivals hides how fast rents on a lane rise.
Because it forces a district to prove where the money settles.

qs.evidence: I find that suggestion convincing, because it turns a boast into a test.
qs.answer: Because it forces a district to prove where the money settles.
qs.why: "Turns a boast into a test" berarti angka baru itu memaksa distrik membuktikan ke mana uangnya berhenti, bukan cuma memamerkan jumlah pengunjung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kedatangan justru berhasil dicatat di setiap gerbang, jadi soal terlambat tidak ada dasarnya. Teks juga tidak mengklaim angka belanja lebih mudah dikumpulkan, dan kenaikan sewa disebut sebagai akibat, bukan alasan penulis memilih angka baru itu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The four villages studied lie more than a day's journey apart."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The four villages studied lie more than a day's journey apart.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Because the four villages lie within an hour of one another, the comparison is unusually fair.
qs.why: Teks bilang keempat desa berjarak dalam satu jam perjalanan, jadi klaim "lebih dari sehari" bertentangan langsung. Kuncinya False.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena angka jaraknya dibalik. "Not stated" salah karena jarak antar desa disebut jelas di paragraf pertama.

topic: research on the effects of viral tourism in highland villages
author: popular science report by a tourism research team
setting: four neighbouring villages in a highland district

title: The Screen at Home and the Screen in Town
text:
Two habits of film-watching now exist side by side in this district, and they satisfy quite different appetites. A streaming subscription costs less than two cinema tickets a month, and it never closes its doors. The old cinema on the square opens at four, seats 180 people and shows one title at a time. On price and sheer convenience the contest appears settled.

The counter-argument concerns attention rather than expense. At home a film competes with messages, cooking and a doorbell, so many viewers finish it in three sittings. In the cinema the lights fade and the audience surrenders two uninterrupted hours together. Streaming also hides its choices: the catalogue changes quietly, and titles vanish without warning. The cinema publishes a printed programme a fortnight ahead, which lets a school or a family plan properly. Against that advantage, its range remains narrow, and a viewer unimpressed by the single title must wait a week.

My own view is that the two are not rivals but different goods, and the town needs both. Streaming wins on breadth and cost, while the cinema wins on undivided attention and shared reaction. The mistake would be to judge the cinema by the measure that suits its competitor. If the hall on the square survives, it will not be because it is cheaper. It will be because ninety strangers laughing at once is something no subscription can deliver.
qs: What point does this article make about the two ways of watching?
They serve different needs, so the town gains from keeping both.
Streaming has the stronger case, though the cinema still suits some families.
The cinema deserves support mainly because its tickets stay good value.
Neither habit will last unless the town decides which one to support.

qs.evidence: My own view is that the two are not rivals but different goods, and the town needs both.
qs.answer: They serve different needs, so the town gains from keeping both.
qs.why: Penulis menyatakan sikapnya langsung: keduanya bukan pesaing melainkan barang berbeda, dan kota butuh dua-duanya. Itu gagasan utamanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis menolak menimbang keduanya dengan satu ukuran, jadi "streaming lebih kuat" bukan kesimpulannya. Harga murah justru ditolak sebagai alasan bioskop bertahan, dan teks berpendapat sebaliknya soal memilih satu: kota disebut membutuhkan dua-duanya.

qs: What does the article say about the cinema on the square?
It opens at midday and shows two titles on its 180 seats.
It seats about ninety people and changes its film each fortnight.
It opens in the afternoon and runs a single film for its 180 seats.
It shows one title a week and sells a monthly pass to regulars.

qs.evidence: The old cinema on the square opens at four, seats 180 people and shows one title at a time.
qs.answer: It opens in the afternoon and runs a single film for its 180 seats.
qs.why: Tiga detailnya: buka jam empat, 180 tempat duduk, satu film sekali tayang. Kunci menyatukan ketiganya dengan kata lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Bioskop itu buka jam empat, bukan tengah hari, dan hanya satu film sekali tayang. Angka sembilan puluh adalah jumlah penonton yang tertawa bersama di kalimat penutup, sementara paket bulanan adalah ciri layanan streaming.

qs: Which difference does the article stress when it discusses planning ahead?
The cinema decides its programme late, while streaming publishes months ahead.
The cinema announces its films early, while a catalogue can shrink overnight.
Streaming warns subscribers before a title leaves, while the cinema does not.
Both publish their coming titles about a fortnight before showing them.

qs.evidence: The cinema publishes a printed programme a fortnight ahead, which lets a school or a family plan properly.
qs.answer: The cinema announces its films early, while a catalogue can shrink overnight.
qs.why: Bioskop mengumumkan jadwal dua minggu lebih dulu, sedangkan katalog streaming berubah tanpa pemberitahuan. Kunci menggabungkan kontras itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pelakunya tertukar di dua opsi pertama: bioskop yang mencetak program dua minggu lebih dulu, dan katalog streaming justru berubah tanpa pemberitahuan. Opsi terakhir menyamakan keduanya, padahal seluruh paragraf dua dibangun di atas perbedaan itu.

qs: What does the article suggest about watching a film at home?
Viewers at home tend to choose shorter films to avoid interruption.
Interruptions there tend to break a film into separate pieces.
A film seen at home can be followed more closely than one in a hall.
Home viewers often lose interest once a title leaves the catalogue.

qs.evidence: At home a film competes with messages, cooking and a doorbell, so many viewers finish it in three sittings.
qs.answer: Interruptions there tend to break a film into separate pieces.
qs.why: Kalimat itu menyiratkan gangguan di rumah memecah film jadi beberapa bagian, sampai selesai dalam tiga kali duduk.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks tidak bilang penonton rumah memilih film pendek; yang disebut adalah film panjang diselesaikan dalam tiga kali duduk. Perhatian di rumah disebut terbagi, bukan lebih terpusat, dan hilangnya judul dari katalog dipakai untuk soal perencanaan, bukan minat menonton.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The cinema on the square receives a yearly grant from the district council."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The cinema on the square receives a yearly grant from the district council.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: If the hall on the square survives, it will not be because it is cheaper.
qs.why: Teks membahas bertahannya bioskop tapi nggak pernah menyebut sumber dananya, apalagi hibah tahunan dari pemerintah distrik. Atribusi seperti itu nggak ada, jadi Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" butuh pernyataan soal hibah yang nggak ada. "False" juga salah karena teks nggak menyangkal adanya bantuan; ia cuma diam soal itu.

topic: comparison of streaming services and a small local cinema
author: comparison feature for a regional culture magazine
setting: a district town with one surviving cinema

title: Wax, Cloth and a Loud Room
text:
The travelling batik exhibition that opened last Friday is worth an hour of anyone's Saturday, though not for the reason the posters suggest. The posters promise treasures. What the show actually delivers is process. Its strongest room holds no finished cloth at all, only copper stamps, cracked wax bowls and a bench where two makers work in front of you.

The weakness is the labelling. Each piece carries a long paragraph about trade routes, yet almost nothing about the hands that made it. One indigo panel from the north coast is dated to within a decade, but its maker is described merely as a workshop. That silence matters, because the exhibition's own argument is that batik is a craft of individuals. The curators contradict themselves in small print, and a visitor who reads carefully will notice.

Even so, I would send every school in the city here before the show moves on in October. Children who watch the wax being drawn understand in five minutes what a textbook cannot teach in a term. The demonstration bench is free, the guides answer questions without hurrying, and the noise in that room is a good sign. My advice is to walk through the galleries backwards, starting with the makers and ending with the treasures. Seen in that order, the cloth on the far wall stops being decoration and becomes evidence.
qs: What is the reviewer's overall judgement of the exhibition?
Worth visiting chiefly for the rare finished cloth, whatever the labels say.
Worth visiting for its live craft, despite careless written notes.
Worth a short visit, though the demonstration room is too noisy to enjoy.
Worth waiting for, since the labelling is to be rewritten before October.

qs.evidence: The travelling batik exhibition that opened last Friday is worth an hour of anyone's Saturday, though not for the reason the posters suggest.
qs.answer: Worth visiting for its live craft, despite careless written notes.
qs.why: Penilaian penulis: pameran ini layak dikunjungi, tapi bukan karena kain jadinya, melainkan proses yang hidup; label tertulisnya justru lemah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kain jadi justru bukan alasan penulis merekomendasikan pameran; ruang terbaik malah tanpa kain jadi. Keramaian di ruang peraga disebut "a good sign", bukan gangguan, dan tidak ada janji perbaikan label; Oktober adalah bulan pameran pindah.

qs: What does the reviewer say is in the exhibition's strongest room?
The oldest finished cloths, hung together along one long wall.
A printed timeline of the trade routes that carried the cloth.
Tools, wax bowls and two makers working in view of visitors.
A bench where visitors may try drawing the wax themselves.

qs.evidence: Its strongest room holds no finished cloth at all, only copper stamps, cracked wax bowls and a bench where two makers work in front of you.
qs.answer: Tools, wax bowls and two makers working in view of visitors.
qs.why: Ruang terbaik justru tanpa kain jadi: ada cap tembaga, mangkuk lilin yang pecah, dan dua perajin bekerja di depan pengunjung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ruang terkuat itu justru tidak memuat kain jadi sama sekali. Jalur dagang hanya muncul di paragraf label tiap benda, dan bangku di ruang itu dipakai dua perajin yang bekerja, bukan pengunjung yang mencoba menggambar.

qs: Which example does the reviewer give to show that the labels fail the makers?
A long label on trade routes printed in type too small to read.
A copper stamp displayed without any note of where it was made.
A precisely dated cloth credited to no individual at all.
A poster promising treasures that the galleries never show.

qs.evidence: One indigo panel from the north coast is dated to within a decade, but its maker is described merely as a workshop.
qs.answer: A precisely dated cloth credited to no individual at all.
qs.why: Contoh konkretnya panel indigo: tanggalnya presisi sampai satu dekade, tapi pembuatnya cuma ditulis sebagai sebuah sanggar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keluhan penulis bukan soal ukuran huruf label, melainkan isinya yang membisu soal pembuat. Cap tembaga disebut sebagai kekuatan ruang peraga, bukan contoh label buruk, dan poster yang menjanjikan treasures dipakai di pembuka untuk soal harapan pengunjung.

qs: Which sentence best restates the reviewer's advice about how to see the show?
Begin where the craft is being done and finish with the display pieces.
Begin with the finished cloth so that the tools make sense afterwards.
Take the galleries in the printed order, but allow a full hour for them.
Skip the labels altogether and follow one of the guides through the rooms.

qs.evidence: My advice is to walk through the galleries backwards, starting with the makers and ending with the treasures.
qs.answer: Begin where the craft is being done and finish with the display pieces.
qs.why: Saran penulis: mulai dari perajin, berakhir di kain pamer. Kunci menyatakan itu tanpa memakai kata "backwards" atau "treasures".
qs.whyOthersFail: Urutan yang penulis sarankan justru kebalikan opsi pertama: mulai dari perajin, berakhir di kain pamer. Ia juga tidak menyuruh mengikuti urutan cetak maupun mengabaikan label; pemandu dipuji, tapi bukan sebagai pengganti rute yang ia anjurkan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Visitors pay nothing extra to watch the demonstration at the bench."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Visitors pay nothing extra to watch the demonstration at the bench.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The demonstration bench is free, the guides answer questions without hurrying, and the noise in that room is a good sign.
qs.why: "The demonstration bench is free" sama artinya dengan pengunjung nggak perlu bayar tambahan untuk menontonnya. Jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena nggak ada yang dibalik. "Not stated" salah karena teks menyebut gratis secara terang.

author: exhibition review for a weekend arts page

title: Letter to the District Office: The River Clean-Up
text:
I write on behalf of the sixty volunteers who have cleared the riverbank on the first Sunday of every month since March. Our purpose is not to complain about the district office, which has always answered our letters promptly. Nor do we seek additional funding. It is to describe a problem we can no longer solve with goodwill alone, and to propose a remedy that costs little.

The problem is what happens after the work is finished. Each Sunday we fill forty or fifty sacks and haul them to the market lane corner, since no collection point exists. That corner is unguarded. By Tuesday the sacks have usually been torn open by animals, so a part of the rubbish returns to the water. Volunteers who spent four hours on the bank watch that happen, and several have stopped coming. The proper measure of our effort, in other words, is not sacks filled but rubbish permanently kept out of the water.

We therefore submit two requests. First, a locked container at the market lane corner, emptied every Monday morning. Second, permission to display the monthly weight on the noticeboard outside your office. The second request may seem minor, yet in our view a public figure would keep both sides accountable. We would gladly accompany your staff along the bank on any Sunday, to demonstrate why the present arrangement wastes the effort it receives.
qs: Why has the group written to the district office?
To report the season's results and ask for a lorry every Monday morning.
To request money for the sacks and tools the volunteers can no longer buy.
To set out a difficulty after clean-ups and ask for two measures.
To warn that the volunteers will stop unless a lorry collects the sacks.

qs.evidence: It is to describe a problem we can no longer solve with goodwill alone, and to propose a remedy that costs little.
qs.answer: To set out a difficulty after clean-ups and ask for two measures.
qs.why: Suratnya menjelaskan masalah sesudah kerja bakti lalu mengusulkan solusi murah, dan di paragraf tiga solusinya ada dua butir.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kelompok itu meminta wadah terkunci yang dikosongkan tiap Senin, bukan lorry penjemput, dan suratnya bukan laporan hasil semusim. Teks juga menolak dua hal lain: mereka tidak mencari dana tambahan, dan tidak pernah mengancam berhenti; yang disebut hanya beberapa relawan yang sudah tidak datang.

qs: What happens to the filled sacks under the present arrangement?
Animals open them at the lane corner before anyone collects them.
They wait at the market lane corner until a lorry empties them on Monday.
Volunteers carry them to the district office at the end of each Sunday.
They are weighed and the total is written up on the office noticeboard.

qs.evidence: By Tuesday the sacks have usually been torn open by animals, so a part of the rubbish returns to the water.
qs.answer: Animals open them at the lane corner before anyone collects them.
qs.why: Karung ditinggal di sudut jalan pasar, lalu sebelum diangkut sudah dirobek binatang, sehingga sampah balik ke sungai.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pengangkutan hari Senin dan penimbangan di papan pengumuman baru diusulkan di paragraf tiga, jadi belum terjadi. Karung dibawa ke sudut jalan pasar, bukan ke kantor distrik; di situlah binatang merobeknya sebelum ada yang mengangkut.

qs: Which fact does the letter offer as proof that the present arrangement discourages helpers?
Some helpers have left after seeing their long day undone.
Forty or fifty sacks are filled by the group on a single Sunday.
Sixty volunteers have kept the work going every month since March.
Rubbish returns to the water within two days of every clean-up.

qs.evidence: Volunteers who spent four hours on the bank watch that happen, and several have stopped coming.
qs.answer: Some helpers have left after seeing their long day undone.
qs.why: Buktinya: sebagian relawan berhenti datang setelah melihat hasil kerja empat jam mereka sia-sia.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga angka itu ada di surat, tapi tidak satu pun dipakai untuk menunjukkan relawan jadi enggan. Jumlah karung dan jumlah relawan menggambarkan besarnya kerja, dan sampah yang kembali ke air adalah kerusakan yang dilihat, sedangkan buktinya adalah beberapa relawan berhenti datang.

qs: Why does the group ask to publish the monthly weight?
Because the office has asked for a written record before it will act.
Because a monthly figure would show which lanes need clearing next.
Because volunteers want their work noticed by people in the district.
Because an open number would hold each side to its promise.

qs.evidence: The second request may seem minor, yet in our view a public figure would keep both sides accountable.
qs.answer: Because an open number would hold each side to its promise.
qs.why: Alasannya angka terbuka membuat dua pihak sama-sama terikat janji, bukan sekadar pengumuman.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kantor tidak pernah meminta catatan; permintaan itu datang dari kelompok. Angka bulanan juga tidak diusulkan untuk memilih lokasi kerja, dan alasan yang ditulis bukan soal pengakuan melainkan supaya kedua pihak sama-sama terikat pada janjinya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The volunteers clear the riverbank once a week throughout the year."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The volunteers clear the riverbank once a week throughout the year.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: I write on behalf of the sixty volunteers who have cleared the riverbank on the first Sunday of every month since March.
qs.why: Teks bilang kerja bakti tiap Sunday pertama dalam sebulan, jadi "sekali sepekan" bertentangan dengan frekuensi yang tertulis.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena frekuensinya diubah. "Not stated" salah karena jadwalnya disebut jelas di kalimat pembuka.

author: formal letter from a volunteer group secretary

title: Dance Belongs in the Timetable
text:
Our district has spent four years treating traditional dance as a performance for guests, and that is the wrong place for it. Twice a year the best twenty pupils rehearse for a visiting delegation, while everybody else watches from plastic chairs. The dances survive on the stage and disappear from the corridors. A tradition kept only for visitors is a tradition already halfway lost.

The obstacle is not indifference but the absence of ordinary time. When I questioned a Year 9 class, thirty of thirty-four said they enjoyed the movements, yet only six had ever practised outside a rehearsal for guests. Their difficulty was practical: no timetable slot, no space after four o'clock, no teacher paid for it. Enthusiasm cannot compete with a locked hall. Nor can a single annual audition replace a weekly habit.

The remedy costs one period a fortnight. Give every class forty minutes with a local dancer, mark it on the timetable, and abandon the selection of twenty. Performance would then grow out of a habit instead of replacing it. I accept that examinations crowd the week and that heads of department guard their hours jealously. Even so, a district which finds time for two spectacles a year can surely find time for something quieter and far more durable.
qs: What is the writer's central argument?
The twice-yearly performances should be rehearsed far more thoroughly.
Dance is fading mainly because pupils have lost interest in it.
Traditional dance should sit inside normal lessons, not only in shows.
Examinations leave so little room that dance is best kept for guests.

qs.evidence: A tradition kept only for visitors is a tradition already halfway lost.
qs.answer: Traditional dance should sit inside normal lessons, not only in shows.
qs.why: Penulis menuntut tari masuk pelajaran biasa, bukan cuma tampil untuk tamu; kalimat itu jadi ringkasan sikapnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis tidak menuntut gladi yang lebih rapi; ia menuntut jam pelajaran biasa. Hilangnya minat justru dibantah angka 30 dari 34, dan meski ia mengakui ujian memadatkan pekan, kesimpulannya bukan menyerahkan tari kepada acara tamu.

qs: What did the writer find in the Year 9 class?
About six pupils in thirty-four said they enjoyed the movements at all.
Most had practised at home, yet few wanted to perform for guests.
Around thirty had joined a rehearsal for a visiting delegation.
Nearly all liked the movements, but hardly any danced outside rehearsals.

qs.evidence: When I questioned a Year 9 class, thirty of thirty-four said they enjoyed the movements, yet only six had ever practised outside a rehearsal for guests.
qs.answer: Nearly all liked the movements, but hardly any danced outside rehearsals.
qs.why: Angkanya jelas: 30 dari 34 suka gerakannya, tapi cuma 6 yang pernah berlatih di luar gladi untuk tamu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Enam adalah jumlah yang pernah berlatih di luar gladi, bukan jumlah yang menyukai gerakannya. Latihan di rumah tidak pernah disebut, dan tiga puluh adalah jumlah yang menyukai tari, bukan yang ikut gladi untuk delegasi.

qs: Which evidence supports the writer's claim that the barrier is practical?
Only twenty pupils in the school were selected for the guest performance.
There was nowhere to rehearse, no free period and nobody paid to teach.
Heads of department were unwilling to give up any of their teaching hours.
The hall was locked for repairs during most of the previous term.

qs.evidence: Their difficulty was practical: no timetable slot, no space after four o'clock, no teacher paid for it.
qs.answer: There was nowhere to rehearse, no free period and nobody paid to teach.
qs.why: Tiga hal praktis disebut berurutan: nggak ada jam di jadwal, nggak ada ruang sesudah jam empat, nggak ada guru yang dibayar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kuota dua puluh dipakai untuk menggambarkan pola yang penulis tolak, bukan kesulitan praktis murid. Sikap kepala jurusan muncul sebagai keberatan yang penulis akui di akhir, dan perbaikan aula tidak pernah disebut; yang tertulis hanya aula terkunci sebagai kiasan.

qs: What does the writer imply about the twice-yearly performances?
They can conceal how seldom the dances are done at other times.
They may raise the standard of the twenty pupils who are chosen.
They probably matter more to the visiting delegations than to the district.
They tend to encourage pupils to keep practising through the rest of the year.

qs.evidence: The dances survive on the stage and disappear from the corridors.
qs.answer: They can conceal how seldom the dances are done at other times.
qs.why: Kalimat itu menyiratkan pertunjukan menutupi kenyataan: di luar panggung tarinya nggak hidup lagi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Mutu dua puluh penari tidak pernah dinilai teks, dan kepentingan delegasi juga tidak dibahas. Opsi terakhir berlawanan langsung: tari disebut hidup di panggung lalu hilang dari koridor, jadi pertunjukan justru tidak melahirkan kebiasaan sepanjang tahun.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Under the writer's plan, a visiting dancer would work with every class, not a chosen few."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Under the writer's plan, a visiting dancer would work with every class, not a chosen few.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Give every class forty minutes with a local dancer, mark it on the timetable, and abandon the selection of twenty.
qs.why: Usulnya memang begitu: semua kelas dapat empat puluh menit dengan penari setempat dan pemilihan dua puluh dihapus. Jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena nggak ada proposisi yang dibalik. "Not stated" salah karena usul itu tertulis lengkap di paragraf akhir.

author: opinion piece by a district arts teacher
setting: district schools that stage dance for official visitors

title: Bins Are Cheap, Explaining Is Not
text:
A study that lasted a whole year in two city wards has measured what really happens to household waste after people have sorted it. Both wards were given the same green bins in January. Only one of them also received a weekly visit from a collector trained to explain the system. The researchers weighed 1,200 sampled bags every fortnight and photographed the contents.

The numbers show a clear chain of cause and effect. Where collectors explained the rules, contamination of the food waste bin fell from 31 per cent to 9 per cent. Cleaner food waste let the compost yard sell what it made, and that money paid for two more collection rounds. In the ward without visits, contamination remained near a third, so the yard diverted much of the material to landfill. Equipment by itself altered very little. Conversation altered a great deal.

The authors are careful about wider claims, yet their advice is blunt. They urge councils to budget for people rather than for containers, because the cheaper item is the one that quietly fails. Bins are visible and easy to announce, while patient explanation seldom appears in any press release. My own reading of these figures is that the invisible half of such a scheme performs most of the work. A ward that buys only the visible half should expect only half a result.
qs: What does the study mainly show?
Explaining the scheme, rather than supplying containers, produced the change.
Contamination falls in any ward once identical green bins are provided.
Compost sales can cover the cost of extra collection rounds in a year.
Sorting improves slowly, so one year is too short to judge such a scheme.

qs.evidence: Equipment by itself altered very little.
qs.answer: Explaining the scheme, rather than supplying containers, produced the change.
qs.why: Temuan pokoknya: alatnya sendiri hampir nggak mengubah apa pun, penjelasan dari petugaslah yang mengubah hasil.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kedua ward menerima tong yang sama, dan di ward tanpa kunjungan kontaminasi tetap sekitar sepertiga, jadi tong saja tidak menurunkan apa pun. Penjualan kompos memang membayari dua ronde tambahan, tapi itu akibat, bukan temuan pokok, dan teks tidak menyoal panjang masa penelitian.

qs: How did the researchers collect their data?
Households in both wards filled in a fortnightly form about sorting.
Collectors noted the contents of every bin they emptied each week.
Compost yard staff weighed the material arriving from each ward.
Sample bags were put on the scales and pictured every two weeks.

qs.evidence: The researchers weighed 1,200 sampled bags every fortnight and photographed the contents.
qs.answer: Sample bags were put on the scales and pictured every two weeks.
qs.why: Metodenya menimbang 1.200 kantong sampel setiap dua pekan sekaligus memotret isinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang ditimbang dan difoto adalah 1.200 kantong sampel oleh peneliti, bukan seluruh tong oleh petugas maupun bahan masuk oleh pekerja kompos. Formulir warga tidak pernah ada; kunjungan petugas adalah perlakuan yang diuji, bukan cara mengumpulkan data.

qs: How did the two wards differ in what happened to the sorted material?
One ward filled its green bins twice as fast as the other did.
One ward sorted glass and paper, while the other sorted only food waste.
Both wards sent about a third of their food waste to landfill.
One ward's waste was sold as compost; the other's largely went to a dump.

qs.evidence: In the ward without visits, contamination remained near a third, so the yard diverted much of the material to landfill.
qs.answer: One ward's waste was sold as compost; the other's largely went to a dump.
qs.why: Di ward tanpa kunjungan, bahannya banyak dibuang ke tempat pembuangan; di ward satunya kompos bisa dijual.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kecepatan mengisi tong dan jenis bahan yang dipilah tidak pernah diukur; angka sepertiga adalah tingkat kontaminasi, bukan porsi yang dibuang. Bedanya justru pada tujuan akhir bahan: satu ward bisa menjual kompos, satu lagi banyak masuk pembuangan.

qs: Why do the authors call the cheaper item the one that fails?
Because bins are bought once, while explaining has to be paid for weekly.
Because bins alone leave the sorting mistakes untouched.
Because a council that buys bins has little budget left for its staff.
Because contamination stayed near a third even in the ward with visits.

qs.evidence: They urge councils to budget for people rather than for containers, because the cheaper item is the one that quietly fails.
qs.answer: Because bins alone leave the sorting mistakes untouched.
qs.why: Barang murah itu tong: tanpa penjelasan, kesalahan memilah tetap jalan, jadi belanja tong saja nggak menyelesaikan apa-apa.
qs.whyOthersFail: Perbandingan biaya sekali beli dan biaya rutin tidak dibuat teks, begitu pula soal anggaran yang habis untuk tong. Opsi terakhir membalik angka: di ward yang dikunjungi kontaminasi turun dari 31 ke 9 persen, dan yang tetap sekitar sepertiga adalah ward tanpa kunjungan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Collectors trained to explain the scheme visited households in both wards."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Collectors trained to explain the scheme visited households in both wards.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Only one of them also received a weekly visit from a collector trained to explain the system.
qs.why: Teks tegas: hanya satu ward yang mendapat kunjungan petugas terlatih, jadi klaim "kedua ward" bertentangan langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena cakupannya diperluas dari satu ke dua. "Not stated" salah karena perbedaan itu justru inti rancangan penelitian.

author: popular research summary for a city environment bulletin
setting: two urban wards trialling a green bin scheme

title: A Room in a House or a Room in a Hotel
text:
Visitors to this coastal town now choose between two very distinct arrangements, and the brochures rarely mention the trade-off. A homestay provides a room inside a family house for roughly a third of the hotel rate. The two hotels on the harbour road offer a locked door, a key card and breakfast at a fixed hour. Both arrangements provide shelter, yet the experiences are scarcely comparable.

Homestays win decisively on money and on knowledge. A host who has fished the bay for thirty years will reveal which boat leaves at dawn and which guide overcharges. Hotels, by contrast, win on predictability, because a guest arriving at midnight is never an inconvenience. Homestays also transfer more of the payment to households, since roughly four fifths of the fee stays in the town. Against that, standards vary sharply from one lane to the next, and a visitor who requires quiet may find none. Hotels are duller and more expensive, yet nobody has to negotiate the bathroom.

In my judgement the sensible advice depends on the traveller rather than on the accommodation. A family with small children and an early flight should reserve the hotel without embarrassment. A visitor whose purpose is to understand the bay should choose a household. What the town must not do is impose a single model on everyone through licensing rules. Two imperfect options, honestly described, serve more visitors than one polished standard.
qs: What is the writer's main point about the two arrangements?
Each suits a different kind of traveller, so both deserve to remain.
Homestays serve the town better, though hotels remain useful in emergencies.
Licensing rules should set one standard that both kinds of lodging must meet.
Brochures should describe the trade-off, which would settle the choice for visitors.

qs.evidence: In my judgement the sensible advice depends on the traveller rather than on the accommodation.
qs.answer: Each suits a different kind of traveller, so both deserve to remain.
qs.why: Sikap penulis: pilihannya tergantung siapa yang bepergian, jadi kota sebaiknya menjaga dua-duanya tetap ada.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis tidak menobatkan satu pihak sebagai pelayan kota yang lebih baik; ia bilang nasihatnya bergantung pada siapa yang bepergian. Satu standar lewat aturan izin justru yang ia larang, dan brosur disebut jarang menyebut pertukarannya, bukan sebagai penentu pilihan.

qs: What do the two hotels on the harbour road provide?
A room at about a third of the homestay rate and a late breakfast.
A private lock, an electronic key and a set breakfast time.
A guide to the bay and a place on a boat that leaves at dawn.
A quiet room, a key card and a choice of breakfast hours.

qs.evidence: The two hotels on the harbour road offer a locked door, a key card and breakfast at a fixed hour.
qs.answer: A private lock, an electronic key and a set breakfast time.
qs.why: Yang ditawarkan hotel: pintu terkunci, kartu kunci, dan sarapan pada jam tetap. Kunci menyebut ketiganya dengan kata lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tarif sepertiga itu milik homestay, bukan hotel, dan pengetahuan soal perahu subuh datang dari tuan rumah homestay. Hotel memang memberi kartu kunci, tapi sarapannya pada jam tetap, bukan jam pilihan.

qs: On which point does the article say hotels are clearly stronger?
A guest is told which local guide charges visitors too much.
A guest keeps four fifths of the fee inside the coastal town.
A guest pays less for a room than in any house along the lanes.
A guest who turns up very late causes the staff no trouble.

qs.evidence: Hotels, by contrast, win on predictability, because a guest arriving at midnight is never an inconvenience.
qs.answer: A guest who turns up very late causes the staff no trouble.
qs.why: Keunggulan hotel yang disebut: bisa diandalkan, sampai-sampai tamu yang datang tengah malam pun nggak jadi masalah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Info soal pemandu yang mematok terlalu tinggi adalah kelebihan homestay, begitu juga empat perlima uang yang tinggal di kota. Hotel justru disebut lebih mahal, jadi opsi ketiga membalik perbandingan harga di paragraf dua.

qs: What does the writer suggest is the risk of choosing a homestay?
Hosts may have less time for guests during the fishing season.
A guest may end up paying more than a hotel once meals are counted.
Quality is uneven, so a guest cannot be sure what a room will be like.
Much of the money paid may leave the town before the season ends.

qs.evidence: Against that, standards vary sharply from one lane to the next, and a visitor who requires quiet may find none.
qs.answer: Quality is uneven, so a guest cannot be sure what a room will be like.
qs.why: Risikonya mutu yang nggak seragam antar gang, jadi tamu nggak bisa memastikan kamarnya seperti apa.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kesibukan tuan rumah dan biaya makan tidak pernah disinggung teks. Soal uang yang keluar dari kota justru dibantah: sekitar empat perlima pembayaran homestay disebut tetap di dalam kota.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Most visitors to the coastal town arrive between June and August."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Most visitors to the coastal town arrive between June and August.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Visitors to this coastal town now choose between two very distinct arrangements, and the brochures rarely mention the trade-off.
qs.why: Teks bicara soal pilihan menginap tapi nggak pernah menyebut bulan atau musim kedatangan. Nggak ada angka waktu, jadi Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" butuh data musim yang nggak ada di teks. "False" juga salah karena teks nggak menyangkal pola kedatangan itu; ia diam.

author: travel comparison column for a weekend supplement
setting: a coastal town with homestays and two small hotels

title: A Documentary That Trusts Its Silence
text:
The documentary screened on the opening night of the film week runs for eighty-four minutes and contains almost no narration. That deliberate restraint is the making of it. Instead of a commentary telling us that the catch has shrunk, we watch three families count what emerges from the nets over eleven months. The figures appear as chalk marks on a boat, and they are more persuasive than any voice could be.

Not everything works. The middle section repeats itself, and two long sequences of mending nets add texture without adding meaning. The music, arriving suddenly in the final reel, tells the audience how to feel about a scene that had already earned its own weight. A tighter edit would have removed twelve minutes and gained considerable force. I would also have appreciated one interview with the buyers who set the price, since their absence leaves a hole in the argument.

Even with those faults, this is the most honest local film I have seen this year, and I recommend it warmly. It credits its audience with sufficient judgement to reach a conclusion unaided. Anyone who has been told that fishing communities are simply disappearing should watch the sequence in which a daughter rejects her father's advice and remains. The film declines to settle that dispute. It merely shows us that the argument is being had.
qs: What is the reviewer's overall verdict on the documentary?
Honest in its method, though its silence will lose most of its audience.
Flawed in its editing and music, yet honest and well worth seeing.
Convincing about the catch, yet weakened past rescue by its slow middle.
Valuable chiefly as a record, though its argument never quite convinces.

qs.evidence: Even with those faults, this is the most honest local film I have seen this year, and I recommend it warmly.
qs.answer: Flawed in its editing and music, yet honest and well worth seeing.
qs.why: Penilaiannya jelas: ada cacat penyuntingan dan musik, tapi filmnya paling jujur tahun ini dan direkomendasikan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketenangan film disebut sebagai kekuatan, bukan sebab penonton lari. Bagian tengah yang berulang memang dikritik, tapi filmnya tetap direkomendasikan hangat, dan angka kapur di perahu disebut lebih meyakinkan daripada narasi apa pun.

qs: How does the film present the decline in the catch?
A narrator sets out the figures over shots of empty nets.
A buyer explains how the price paid at the harbour has fallen.
A daughter reads her father's catch records from eleven years back.
Three families record their hauls for nearly a year in chalk.

qs.evidence: Instead of a commentary telling us that the catch has shrunk, we watch three families count what emerges from the nets over eleven months.
qs.answer: Three families record their hauls for nearly a year in chalk.
qs.why: Penurunan hasil ditunjukkan lewat tiga keluarga yang mencatat tangkapan selama sebelas bulan, angkanya ditulis pakai kapur.
qs.whyOthersFail: Film ini justru hampir tanpa narasi, dan pembeli yang menentukan harga tidak pernah diwawancarai; ketiadaan itu malah dikeluhkan penulis. Anak perempuan muncul di adegan lain, dan angka sebelas mengacu pada sebelas bulan pencatatan, bukan sebelas tahun.

qs: Which detail does the reviewer use to show that the music is a mistake?
It appears late and instructs viewers about a scene already strong enough.
It plays throughout the long sequences of nets being mended.
