title: Let the Hill Temple Breathe
text:
Nobody appreciates being told that a public place is full, which is why the proposed daily limit at the hill temple has been received so badly. The complaint is understandable. A limit seems like a fence around something that belongs to everyone. Yet the argument against limits ignores what is happening to the stone.

The problem is measurable rather than sentimental. Conservators recorded the wear on the eastern staircase and found that the upper steps have lost eleven millimetres of surface in nine years. On festival weekends four thousand people use a stairway built for a few hundred pilgrims a day. Guides are pushed to hurry groups through, so nobody explains the carvings, and the visit becomes a queue with a view. The site loses its stone and its meaning at the same time.

A daily cap of twelve hundred, with free tickets released in advance, would treat both losses at once. Those turned away could be directed to the lower shrine, which is nearly empty and equally ancient. I would go further and charge nothing at all, since a limit that operates through price excludes exactly the wrong people. Critics call this rationing, and in a sense it is. The alternative is to let everyone in until there is nothing left worth queueing for.
qs: What is the writer trying to achieve in this column?
To explain why a public place feels different once it becomes crowded.
To ask for the eastern staircase to be repaired before the next festival.
To argue that visitors should be sent to the lower shrine instead.
To defend a cap on numbers as a way of protecting the site.

qs.evidence: A daily cap of twelve hundred, with free tickets released in advance, would treat both losses at once.
qs.answer: To defend a cap on numbers as a way of protecting the site.
qs.why: Tujuan kolom ini membela pembatasan jumlah pengunjung sebagai cara menyelamatkan situs, lengkap dengan angka dan mekanismenya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Rasa sesak hanya pembuka, bukan tujuan tulisan. Perbaikan tangga tidak pernah diminta; yang diusulkan adalah pembatasan jumlah. Kuil bawah disebut sebagai tempat alih bagi yang ditolak, satu bagian usulan, bukan maksud utama kolom.

qs: What did the conservators measure on the eastern staircase?
How many pilgrims the stairway was first built to carry.
How long each guided group spends beside the carvings.
How many people use the eastern staircase on a festival weekend.
How much stone the highest steps had gradually lost.

qs.evidence: Conservators recorded the wear on the eastern staircase and found that the upper steps have lost eleven millimetres of surface in nine years.
qs.answer: How much stone the highest steps had gradually lost.
qs.why: Yang diukur konservator: batu yang terkikis di bagian tangga paling atas, sebelas milimeter dalam sembilan tahun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kapasitas asli tangga dan angka empat ribu pengunjung dipakai penulis sebagai pembanding, bukan hasil pengukuran konservator. Waktu pemandu bersama tiap kelompok tidak pernah diukur; yang diukur adalah kikisan sebelas milimeter pada anak tangga teratas.

qs: Which fact does the writer offer as proof that crowding damages the visit itself?
Four thousand people climb a stairway built for a few hundred.
Groups are rushed along, so the carvings go unexplained.
The upper steps have lost eleven millimetres of surface in nine years.
The lower shrine stands nearly empty on the same festival weekends.

qs.evidence: Guides are pushed to hurry groups through, so nobody explains the carvings, and the visit becomes a queue with a view.
qs.answer: Groups are rushed along, so the carvings go unexplained.
qs.why: Buktinya soal pengalaman berkunjung: pemandu terpaksa mempercepat kelompok sampai ukiran nggak dijelaskan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Angka empat ribu membuktikan kepadatan dan sebelas milimeter membuktikan kerusakan batu, bukan rusaknya pengalaman berkunjung. Kuil bawah yang lengang adalah bagian usulan pengalihan pengunjung, bukan bukti.

qs: Why does the writer reject a system based on ticket prices?
Because charging would keep out the visitors least able to pay.
Because a price would leave the staircase as crowded as it is now.
Because ticket income might be spent away from the temple itself.
Because free tickets released in advance are simpler to control.

qs.evidence: I would go further and charge nothing at all, since a limit that operates through price excludes exactly the wrong people.
qs.answer: Because charging would keep out the visitors least able to pay.
qs.why: Alasannya: pembatasan lewat harga menyaring orang yang paling nggak sanggup bayar, dan itu justru salah sasaran.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks tidak mengklaim tarif gagal mengurangi kepadatan, dan tidak pernah membahas ke mana uang tiket pergi. Kemudahan mengelola tiket gratis juga bukan alasannya; alasan yang ditulis adalah tarif menyaring justru orang yang paling tidak sanggup bayar.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The lower shrine is much more recent than the temple on the hill."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The lower shrine is much more recent than the temple on the hill.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Those turned away could be directed to the lower shrine, which is nearly empty and equally ancient.
qs.why: Teks bilang kuil bawah sama tuanya, jadi klaim "jauh lebih baru" membalik proposisi yang tertulis.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena usianya dipertukarkan. "Not stated" salah karena umur kuil bawah disebut lewat kata "equally ancient".

author: opinion column by a heritage conservation volunteer

title: Why Teenagers Went Back to Listening
text:
For a decade, researchers assumed that teenagers had abandoned audio for video, and the assumption was reasonable. A survey of 2,400 secondary pupils across nine districts now suggests something more complicated. Video still occupies most of their screen time, yet spoken audio has quietly regained an hour a day. The interesting part is not the total but the reason.

The team asked pupils to keep a diary for two weeks, noting what they listened to and what else they were doing. Almost nobody listened while sitting still. Audio grew because it survives movement: it accompanies a bus ride, a kitchen shift or a walk to a tuition class. Where video demands the eyes, spoken programmes demand only patience, so they fit into gaps that video cannot enter. The consequence is that listening rose fastest among pupils with the longest journeys, not among those with the best equipment. Ownership of expensive headphones explained almost none of the difference.

The report draws one firm conclusion, and I think it is right. Producers who chase attention with shorter and louder material have misread their audience. The diaries show teenagers choosing episodes of forty minutes precisely because a journey lasts that long. Cutting an episode to three minutes does not suit a listener with an hour to fill. If the industry wants these listeners, it should study timetables rather than trends.
qs: What does the survey mainly reveal about teenage listening?
It has grown fastest among the pupils who own the best headphones.
It has grown because programmes have become shorter and livelier.
It has grown because audio fits around travel and chores.
It has grown mainly among pupils who spend their evenings at home.

qs.evidence: Audio grew because it survives movement: it accompanies a bus ride, a kitchen shift or a walk to a tuition class.
qs.answer: It has grown because audio fits around travel and chores.
qs.why: Temuan utamanya: mendengarkan tumbuh karena audio bertahan saat orang bergerak, misalnya di bus, saat kerja di dapur, atau jalan ke tempat les.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kepemilikan headphone mahal disebut hampir tidak menjelaskan perbedaan apa pun. Episode pendek justru dianggap salah baca pasar, dan pertumbuhan paling cepat ada pada murid dengan perjalanan terpanjang, bukan yang paling banyak di rumah.

qs: What did pupils in the study have to do?
Report each week how long the journey to school had taken.
List the video channels they had stopped watching that year.
Record for a fortnight what they heard and what they were doing.
Note for a month which programmes they had chosen themselves.

qs.evidence: The team asked pupils to keep a diary for two weeks, noting what they listened to and what else they were doing.
qs.answer: Record for a fortnight what they heard and what they were doing.
qs.why: Tugas mereka menulis buku harian dua pekan: apa yang didengar dan kegiatan apa yang sedang dilakukan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tugasnya buku harian dua pekan, bukan laporan pekanan atau catatan sebulan. Waktu perjalanan dan kanal video memang dibahas di bagian temuan, tapi murid tidak pernah diminta mencatat keduanya.

qs: How does the report contrast video with spoken programmes?
Video needs a viewer's eyes, while listening only needs time.
Video suits a bus ride, while audio suits a pupil sitting still.
Video episodes last about forty minutes, while audio ones are shorter.
Video reaches pupils with long journeys, while audio reaches those nearby.

qs.evidence: Where video demands the eyes, spoken programmes demand only patience, so they fit into gaps that video cannot enter.
qs.answer: Video needs a viewer's eyes, while listening only needs time.
qs.why: Kontrasnya: video menuntut mata, sedangkan siaran suara cuma menuntut kesabaran alias waktu, jadi bisa masuk ke celah kegiatan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga opsi menukar pelakunya. Audio yang bertahan saat bergerak, empat puluh menit adalah durasi episode audio yang dipilih pendengar, dan justru murid dengan perjalanan terpanjang yang paling banyak mendengarkan.

qs: Why does the writer think shorter episodes are a mistake?
Because listeners pick length to match the time a trip takes.
Because short episodes cost producers more for every minute made.
Because teenagers say they dislike being interrupted by advertisements.
Because pupils with the longest journeys own the cheapest equipment.

qs.evidence: The diaries show teenagers choosing episodes of forty minutes precisely because a journey lasts that long.
qs.answer: Because listeners pick length to match the time a trip takes.
qs.why: Pendengar memilih durasi yang pas dengan lama perjalanan, jadi memotong episode jadi tiga menit malah nggak cocok.
qs.whyOthersFail: Biaya produksi dan iklan tidak pernah disebut dalam laporan ini. Soal alat murah memakai kata dari teks tapi salah kaitan: kepemilikan alat justru dinyatakan tidak menjelaskan perbedaan, sedangkan alasan penulis adalah durasi yang dipilih mengikuti lama perjalanan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The study covered pupils from more than eight different districts."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The study covered pupils from more than eight different districts.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: A survey of 2,400 secondary pupils across nine districts now suggests something more complicated.
qs.why: Sembilan distrik berarti lebih dari delapan, jadi klaim ini parafrasa angka yang tertulis dan kuncinya True.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena angkanya nggak dibalik. "Not stated" salah karena jumlah distrik disebut di paragraf pertama.

author: popular research article for a media studies bulletin

title: Letter to the Tourism Office: The Cave Path Signs
text:
On behalf of the eleven registered guides at the cave, I am writing to request a decision on the path signs before the next holiday season. We raised the matter in April and were informed that a survey was under way. Four months later the survey has not reached us, and the season begins in six weeks.

The situation on the ground has altered since our first letter. The upper path was widened in June, so visitors now reach the second chamber without encountering any guide at all. Two parties last month entered with torches after the last patrol had departed. Nobody was hurt, but the floor of that chamber is wet limestone. Our members are no longer willing to be described as responsible for safety they cannot see. The single wooden notice at the car park is faded and mentions a route that was closed in 2019.

We propose three practical measures, none of which requires new funding. First, replace the notice with two boards, one at the car park and one at the fork above it. Second, mark the closing time on both boards in figures rather than in words. Third, confirm in writing that the association's duty ends at the marked barrier. We remain willing to meet you at the site on any weekday morning, and we would appreciate a written reply within a fortnight.
qs: Why is the association writing to the tourism office?
To report that the survey promised in April has now reached the guides.
To ask for funding so that two new boards can be put up at the cave.
To press for a decision on signs before visitors arrive in numbers.
To warn that the eleven guides will not work during the coming season.

qs.evidence: On behalf of the eleven registered guides at the cave, I am writing to request a decision on the path signs before the next holiday season.
qs.answer: To press for a decision on signs before visitors arrive in numbers.
qs.why: Isi permintaannya jelas: keputusan soal papan penunjuk sebelum musim liburan datang, karena tinggal enam pekan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Surat justru bilang hasil survei belum sampai setelah empat bulan. Usulannya ditegaskan tidak butuh dana baru, dan pemandu tidak menyatakan mogok; mereka menolak disebut bertanggung jawab atas keselamatan yang tidak bisa mereka lihat.

qs: What changed at the site in June?
A second notice was put up at the fork above the car park.
A patrol was added to check the second chamber after closing time.
A route that had been closed in 2019 was opened again.
A broader upper track now lets visitors pass the guides entirely.

qs.evidence: The upper path was widened in June, so visitors now reach the second chamber without encountering any guide at all.
qs.answer: A broader upper track now lets visitors pass the guides entirely.
qs.why: Perubahan Juni: jalur atas diperlebar, akibatnya pengunjung bisa sampai ruang kedua tanpa bertemu pemandu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Papan kedua di percabangan adalah usulan pertama surat, jadi belum ada. Patroli tambahan tidak pernah disebut, dan rute 2019 tetap tertutup; ia hanya masih tertulis di papan lama yang pudar.

qs: Which incident does the letter use to justify its concern about safety?
A visitor slipped on the wet limestone floor of the second chamber.
The wooden notice at the car park has faded past reading.
Visitors went in with torches once the patrol had finished.
Guides found a party lost inside the second chamber in April.

qs.evidence: Two parties last month entered with torches after the last patrol had departed.
qs.answer: Visitors went in with torches once the patrol had finished.
qs.why: Kejadian yang dipakai: dua kelompok masuk membawa obor setelah patroli terakhir pergi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Surat menegaskan tidak ada yang cedera, jadi tidak ada yang tergelincir. Papan yang pudar dipakai untuk soal informasi keliru, bukan sebagai kejadian, dan tidak ada kelompok tersesat pada April; yang ada dua kelompok masuk membawa obor bulan lalu.

qs: Which sentence best restates the association's third proposal?
They want the closing time shown on both boards in figures.
They want a barrier built just above the fork on the upper path.
They want a written reply from the office within two weeks.
They want it stated on paper where their responsibility stops.

qs.evidence: Third, confirm in writing that the association's duty ends at the marked barrier.
qs.answer: They want it stated on paper where their responsibility stops.
qs.why: Usul ketiga minta pernyataan tertulis bahwa tanggung jawab asosiasi berakhir di pembatas yang ditandai.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jam tutup berupa angka adalah usul kedua, dan balasan tertulis dalam dua pekan adalah permintaan penutup, bukan usul ketiga. Pembatas baru tidak pernah diminta; surat hanya menyebut pembatas yang sudah ditandai sebagai batas tanggung jawab.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The association first raised the question of the signs six weeks ago."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The association first raised the question of the signs six weeks ago.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: We raised the matter in April and were informed that a survey was under way.
qs.why: Teks bilang perkaranya diajukan pada April, sementara enam pekan adalah jarak menuju musim liburan. Waktunya ditukar, jadi False.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena angka waktunya dipindah. "Not stated" salah karena bulan pengajuan pertama disebut jelas.

title: Two Ways to Boil Water
text:
A household in this village that replaces its wood stove must choose between a biogas unit and bottled gas. The two are not simply cheap and expensive versions of one thing. A bottled cylinder arrives on a truck and works within minutes. A biogas digester must be dug, fed daily and repaired locally.

On convenience the cylinder wins easily. It needs no space, no cattle and no daily attention, which matters greatly to households where both adults work away from the village. Biogas, by contrast, wins on running cost and on waste. A family with three cows can cook for nothing and still obtain fertilizer for the garden. The comparison shifts again when supply is considered. Cylinder prices here rose twice last year and deliveries stop whenever the river road floods. A digester, once built, is indifferent to the road, although it produces less gas in a cold month and nothing at all if the animals are sold.

My conclusion is that the village should stop presenting these options as rivals for the same household. Families with livestock and someone at home should be offered digesters; families without either should be offered cylinders at a fair price. The present scheme, which promotes one technology to everybody, guarantees that half the equipment will stand unused. A choice made honestly is more durable than a target met quickly.
qs: What is the writer's main argument about the two options?
Biogas is the better buy for most households once running costs are counted.
Each fits a different household, so promoting only one wastes money.
Cylinders are the safer choice while the river road remains unreliable.
The village should fix a fair price for cylinders before promoting digesters.

qs.evidence: My conclusion is that the village should stop presenting these options as rivals for the same household.
qs.answer: Each fits a different household, so promoting only one wastes money.
qs.why: Kesimpulan penulis: keduanya bukan pesaing untuk rumah tangga yang sama, jadi mempromosikan satu teknologi ke semua orang itu pemborosan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Biogas hanya menang untuk rumah tangga tertentu, yaitu yang punya ternak dan orang di rumah. Tabung justru yang berhenti datang kalau jalan sungai banjir, jadi opsi kedua membalik keadaan, dan harga wajar tabung adalah satu butir usulan, bukan pokok argumennya.

qs: What does the article say a biogas unit requires?
Digging, daily feeding and repairs carried out nearby.
A cylinder delivered to the house and lit within a few minutes.
Three cows, a garden and a spare cylinder kept for cold months.
A daily payment to the village scheme and a yearly repair visit.

qs.evidence: A biogas digester must be dug, fed daily and repaired locally.
qs.answer: Digging, daily feeding and repairs carried out nearby.
qs.why: Syaratnya tiga: digali, diisi tiap hari, dan diperbaiki di tempat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pengiriman dan menyala dalam beberapa menit adalah ciri tabung gas, bukan digester. Tiga ekor sapi dan taman muncul sebagai hasil pemakaian, bukan syarat pemasangan, dan tidak ada iuran harian maupun kunjungan perbaikan tahunan dalam teks.

qs: How do the two options differ when the road is flooded?
A digester needs repairs, whereas cylinders arrive by boat instead.
Both stop working until the river road has been reopened.
A digester keeps working, whereas cylinders cannot be brought in.
Cylinder prices fall, whereas digesters produce less gas in the wet.

qs.evidence: A digester, once built, is indifferent to the road, although it produces less gas in a cold month and nothing at all if the animals are sold.
qs.answer: A digester keeps working, whereas cylinders cannot be brought in.
qs.why: Digester nggak peduli kondisi jalan, sementara pengiriman tabung berhenti kalau jalan sungai banjir.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tidak ada pengiriman lewat perahu di teks, dan digester disebut tidak peduli keadaan jalan, jadi keduanya tidak berhenti bersama. Harga tabung juga disebut naik dua kali tahun lalu, bukan turun, dan gas digester berkurang pada bulan dingin, bukan bulan basah.

qs: What does the writer imply about the present village scheme?
It offers cylinders to the families that keep the most livestock.
It has driven cylinder prices up twice within a single year.
It works well enough for households where both adults are at home.
Pushing a single technology leaves much of it standing idle.

qs.evidence: The present scheme, which promotes one technology to everybody, guarantees that half the equipment will stand unused.
qs.answer: Pushing a single technology leaves much of it standing idle.
qs.why: Menyodorkan satu teknologi ke semua orang bikin separuh alatnya nggak terpakai, itu isyarat penulis soal skema sekarang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Skema sekarang mendorong satu teknologi kepada semua orang, jadi ia tidak memilah keluarga berternak. Kenaikan harga tabung disebut sebagai keadaan pasar, bukan akibat skema, dan teks tidak menilai skema itu berhasil untuk rumah tangga mana pun.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The village council pays part of the cost of installing a digester."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The village council pays part of the cost of installing a digester.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Families with livestock and someone at home should be offered digesters; families without either should be offered cylinders at a fair price.
qs.why: Teks membahas siapa yang cocok dapat digester, tapi nggak sekali pun menyebut siapa yang menanggung biaya pemasangan. Nggak ada atribusi dana, jadi Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" butuh keterangan subsidi yang nggak ada. "False" juga salah sebab teks nggak menyangkal adanya bantuan biaya.

title: Please Do Not Make Volunteering Compulsory
text:
The proposal to require forty hours of community service from every school leaver comes from a generous instinct. It will nonetheless damage the very thing it admires. I coordinated volunteers in this district for six years. The people who stayed were never the ones sent to us.

Consider what compulsion does to an organization. A shelter that receives thirty willing helpers can plan a rota; the same shelter receiving thirty reluctant ones must supervise, sign forms and repeat instructions. The cost of that supervision falls on staff who are already stretched, and it is paid in hours nobody counts. Worse, compulsory schemes teach a lesson opposite to the intended one. A young person who has been made to sweep a yard for a signature learns that service is a fee charged by adults, not a choice worth making. Our records showed that helpers recruited through friends stayed on average eleven months, while those completing required hours stayed under seven weeks.

There is a better route, and it is unglamorous. Fund three part-time coordinators, publish honest descriptions of each task, and let schools offer the hours as a genuine option. Districts that did this reported waiting lists rather than empty rotas. I would rather have twelve volunteers who return next month than forty who leave with a certificate and no intention of coming back.
qs: What is the writer arguing for in this column?
A shorter requirement of twenty hours, with honest descriptions of each task.
Certificates given only to school leavers who return after their hours.
Voluntary schemes supported by paid organizers instead of a requirement.
An end to school schemes, since shelters manage better without helpers.

qs.evidence: Fund three part-time coordinators, publish honest descriptions of each task, and let schools offer the hours as a genuine option.
qs.answer: Voluntary schemes supported by paid organizers instead of a requirement.
qs.why: Penulis menolak kewajiban dan menawarkan jalan lain: bayar koordinator, terbitkan deskripsi tugas yang jujur, dan biarkan jamnya bersifat pilihan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis menolak kewajiban dalam bentuk apa pun, jadi memperpendek jamnya bukan usulnya. Sertifikat justru yang ia sindir sebagai akhir yang kosong, dan ia tidak bilang shelter lebih baik tanpa relawan; ia ingin dua belas relawan yang kembali.

qs: What difference did the writer's own records show?
Helpers completing required hours stayed about eleven months on average.
Helpers who came through friends lasted far longer than required ones.
Shelters kept thirty willing helpers on the rota for seven weeks.
Helpers recruited by schools stayed longer than those found through friends.

qs.evidence: Our records showed that helpers recruited through friends stayed on average eleven months, while those completing required hours stayed under seven weeks.
qs.answer: Helpers who came through friends lasted far longer than required ones.
qs.why: Catatannya membandingkan dua kelompok: lewat teman rata-rata sebelas bulan, yang disuruh memenuhi jam wajib kurang dari tujuh pekan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sebelas bulan adalah angka relawan yang datang lewat teman, sementara yang memenuhi jam wajib bertahan di bawah tujuh pekan. Tiga puluh orang dipakai untuk contoh rota, bukan lamanya bertahan, dan arah perbandingannya justru kebalikan opsi ketiga.

qs: Which example shows the hidden cost of compulsory helpers?
Shelters must find thirty new helpers before a rota can be planned.
Districts must employ three part-time coordinators to run the scheme.
Young people must be given a signature for each hour they finish.
Staff must watch over unwilling helpers and explain tasks repeatedly.

qs.evidence: A shelter that receives thirty willing helpers can plan a rota; the same shelter receiving thirty reluctant ones must supervise, sign forms and repeat instructions.
qs.answer: Staff must watch over unwilling helpers and explain tasks repeatedly.
qs.why: Biaya tersembunyinya kerja pengawasan: staf harus mengawasi, menandatangani formulir, dan mengulang instruksi untuk helper yang nggak niat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Angka tiga puluh dipakai untuk membandingkan relawan rela dan tidak rela, bukan syarat menyusun rota. Tiga koordinator paruh waktu adalah usulan penulis, bukan biaya kewajiban, dan tanda tangan dipakai di contoh soal pelajaran yang salah, bukan sebagai beban staf.

qs: What does the writer suggest compulsory service teaches young people?
That a certificate is worth more to the adults than to the young themselves.
That community work is easier when it is done alongside school friends.
That helping others is a charge imposed rather than a decision taken.
That shelters could not keep going without help from school leavers.

qs.why: Pelajaran yang tertanam justru salah: menolong dianggap iuran yang dipaksakan orang dewasa, bukan pilihan sendiri.

title: Counting the Speakers of a Small Language
text:
A district survey of language use has produced a result that neither the optimists nor the pessimists expected. Interviewers visited 900 homes and asked which language was used for four ordinary activities: scolding a child, bargaining at the market, praying and joking. The choice of activities was deliberate, because a single question about the mother tongue tends to collect polite answers rather than accurate ones.

The pattern that emerged runs along function rather than age. Grandparents used the local language for all four activities. Parents used it for scolding and bargaining but switched to the national language for prayer. Pupils aged twelve to seventeen used it almost exclusively for joking, which the researchers had not predicted. The consequence is that the language is not so much dying as narrowing: it retains warmth and humour while losing formality. Because school prizes, official forms and sermons all belong to the wider language, its retreat is fastest in exactly the settings that carry prestige.

The report ends with an argument rather than a lament, which I find refreshing. Its authors maintain that revival campaigns aimed at children misunderstand the problem, since children already use the language every day for jokes. What has disappeared is any adult occasion that requires it. They therefore recommend that councils conduct one public meeting a month in the local language. A language survives where it is needed, not where it is admired.
qs: What is the main finding of the survey?
The language is passing out of use one generation at a time.
The language is shrinking into informal uses rather than vanishing.
The language is holding its ground because the young still joke in it.
The language is used mostly for prayer, which keeps it formal.

qs.evidence: The consequence is that the language is not so much dying as narrowing: it retains warmth and humour while losing formality.
qs.answer: The language is shrinking into informal uses rather than vanishing.
qs.why: Temuan pokoknya: bahasanya menyempit ke pemakaian nggak resmi, bukan lenyap; kehangatan dan humor tinggal, keresmian hilang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Polanya disebut mengikuti fungsi, bukan usia, jadi bukan soal satu generasi demi satu generasi. Lelucon anak muda memang bertahan, tapi teks menyebut bahasanya menyempit, bukan bertahan utuh, dan doa justru sudah beralih ke bahasa nasional.

qs: Which four situations did the interviewers ask about?
Filling in forms, praying, joking and greeting neighbours.
Bargaining, singing, listening to sermons and scolding.
Telling off a child, haggling, prayer and making jokes.
Praying, joking, teaching lessons and reading notices.

qs.evidence: Interviewers visited 900 homes and asked which language was used for four ordinary activities: scolding a child, bargaining at the market, praying and joking.
qs.answer: Telling off a child, haggling, prayer and making jokes.
qs.why: Empat situasinya: memarahi anak, menawar di pasar, berdoa, dan bercanda.
qs.whyOthersFail: Empat kegiatan yang ditanyakan adalah memarahi anak, menawar, berdoa, dan bercanda. Formulir, khotbah, dan hadiah sekolah muncul di kalimat lain sebagai ranah prestise, sementara menyapa tetangga, menyanyi, mengajar, dan membaca pengumuman tidak masuk daftar.

qs: Which result did the researchers say they had not expected?
Grandparents preferred the national language when joking with friends.
Teenagers kept the language almost entirely for humour.
Parents used the national language for scolding but not for prayer.
Households gave more accurate answers to one direct question.

qs.evidence: Pupils aged twelve to seventeen used it almost exclusively for joking, which the researchers had not predicted.
qs.answer: Teenagers kept the language almost entirely for humour.
qs.why: Yang di luar dugaan: remaja 12-17 tahun hampir cuma memakai bahasa itu untuk bercanda.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kakek-nenek dilaporkan memakai bahasa lokal untuk keempat kegiatan, dan orang tua memakainya untuk memarahi lalu beralih justru saat berdoa, jadi dua opsi itu menukar ranahnya. Pertanyaan tunggal soal bahasa ibu disebut mengumpulkan jawaban sopan, bukan jawaban akurat.

qs: Why do the authors doubt campaigns aimed at children?
Because children copy whichever language their grandparents use at home.
Because campaigns aimed at children have been tried before and failed.
Because the young already speak it daily, while adult uses have gone.
Because school prizes and official forms use only the wider language.

qs.evidence: Its authors maintain that revival campaigns aimed at children misunderstand the problem, since children already use the language every day for jokes.
qs.answer: Because the young already speak it daily, while adult uses have gone.
qs.why: Kampanye untuk anak dianggap salah sasaran: anak-anak sudah memakainya tiap hari, yang hilang justru acara orang dewasa yang menuntut bahasa itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Peniruan bahasa kakek-nenek tidak pernah dibahas, dan tidak ada catatan kampanye sebelumnya yang gagal. Hadiah sekolah dan formulir dipakai untuk menjelaskan di ranah mana bahasa itu mundur, bukan alasan penulis meragukan kampanye untuk anak.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Parents in the survey used the national language when bargaining at the market."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Parents in the survey used the national language when bargaining at the market.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Parents used it for scolding and bargaining but switched to the national language for prayer.
qs.why: Teks bilang orang tua memakai bahasa lokal untuk menawar dan beralih ke bahasa nasional saat berdoa, jadi klaim ini menukar ranahnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena kegiatannya dipertukarkan. "Not stated" salah karena kebiasaan orang tua dirinci di paragraf kedua.

title: A Walking Guide That Knows When to Stop Talking
text:
Most walking guides to this port quarter appear designed for readers who will never arrive. They begin with three centuries of commerce and reach the first street on page forty. The new pocket guide, issued in June, adopts the reverse approach. Its history occupies four pages, and the rest belongs to the pavement.

The maps constitute its chief achievement. Each of the six walks fits on a single spread, with the turnings drawn as a walker sees them rather than as a surveyor would. A marginal note beside the fish market specifies the hours when the alley becomes impassable, which no rival guide mentions. The deficiencies are equally conspicuous. Photographs are printed too dark to be useful, and the index omits two of the mosques described in the text. Prices quoted for the ferry were already wrong in July. A guide that dates so quickly should carry the month of printing on its cover.

I would nevertheless purchase it, and purchase it before arrival rather than at the station kiosk. Read at home, its second walk explains why the warehouses stand at an angle to the sea, and that single paragraph rearranges the whole quarter for a visitor. A guidebook is not a historical study and should not pretend otherwise. This one knows the difference, which is why its faults are forgivable.
qs: What is the reviewer's overall opinion of the new guide?
Its maps are useful, though a rival guide covers the quarter more fully.
Its errors are minor, yet the short history leaves the quarter unexplained.
Its practical strengths outweigh the errors it undoubtedly contains.
Its faults are forgivable only because no better guide is on sale.

qs.evidence: This one knows the difference, which is why its faults are forgivable.
qs.answer: Its practical strengths outweigh the errors it undoubtedly contains.
qs.why: Penilaian akhirnya: buku ini paham fungsinya sebagai panduan jalan, jadi kekurangannya bisa dimaafkan karena sisi praktisnya menang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Panduan pesaing justru disebut tidak menyebut jam gang pasar dan menunda pembaca sampai halaman empat puluh. Sejarah empat halaman dinilai cukup, sebab satu paragraf soal gudang miring dianggap menjelaskan seluruh kawasan, dan alasan memaafkan cacatnya adalah buku ini tahu fungsinya, bukan ketiadaan saingan.

qs: What does the reviewer say about the maps in the guide?
Each of the six routes is drawn the way a surveyor would record it.
Every route sits on two facing pages and follows a walker's view.
Four routes are mapped, and the fish market alley is left unmarked.
The maps fold out from the back and mark the ferry stops clearly.

qs.evidence: Each of the six walks fits on a single spread, with the turnings drawn as a walker sees them rather than as a surveyor would.
qs.answer: Every route sits on two facing pages and follows a walker's view.
qs.why: Petanya: satu rute satu halaman ganda, dan tikungannya digambar sebagaimana terlihat oleh pejalan, bukan gaya juru ukur.
qs.whyOthersFail: Cara juru ukur justru yang ditolak; tikungan digambar sebagaimana dilihat pejalan. Rutenya enam bukan empat, dan gang pasar ikan punya catatan tepi khusus soal jam tidak bisa dilewati. Peta lipat di belakang tidak pernah disebut.

qs: Which fault does the reviewer report to show the book will date quickly?
The index leaves out two of the mosques described in the text.
The photographs are printed too dark to be of any use.
The history is compressed into only four pages of the book.
Ferry fares given in the book were out of date within weeks.

qs.evidence: Prices quoted for the ferry were already wrong in July.
qs.answer: Ferry fares given in the book were out of date within weeks.
qs.why: Tanda buku cepat kedaluwarsa: tarif kapal yang dicetak sudah salah pada Juli, cuma sebulan setelah terbit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Indeks bolong dan foto gelap adalah cacat cetak yang tidak berubah seiring waktu, jadi tidak menunjukkan buku cepat kedaluwarsa. Sejarah empat halaman justru dipuji sebagai pilihan yang tepat; yang menandai kedaluwarsa adalah tarif kapal yang sudah salah pada Juli.

qs: Which statement best restates the reviewer's advice on when to read the guide?
Carry it on the walk and leave the history section for afterwards.
Study it before the journey, since one passage reshapes the whole area.
Read it after the visit, when the history will finally make sense.
Buy it at the station kiosk, since the fares inside change monthly.

qs.evidence: Read at home, its second walk explains why the warehouses stand at an angle to the sea, and that single paragraph rearranges the whole quarter for a visitor.
qs.answer: Study it before the journey, since one passage reshapes the whole area.
qs.why: Sarannya baca di rumah sebelum jalan, sebab satu paragraf soal gudang miring itu mengubah cara melihat seluruh kawasan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Sarannya membaca di rumah sebelum berangkat, jadi membaca sesudah kunjungan berlawanan. Penulis juga menolak membeli di kios stasiun, dan tarif kapal disebut sudah salah, bukan berubah tiap bulan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The guide devotes far more space to the streets than to the past."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The guide devotes far more space to the streets than to the past.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Its history occupies four pages, and the rest belongs to the pavement.
qs.why: Sejarah cuma empat halaman dan sisanya soal jalanan, jadi klaim ini parafrasa yang tepat dan kuncinya True.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena perbandingannya nggak dibalik. "Not stated" salah karena porsi halaman disebut jelas.

title: The Problem Is Not the Length of the Video
text:
Every term I am told that short videos have destroyed the attention of the young, and every term the pupils in my library disprove it. The same fifteen-year-old who abandons a page after four lines will watch a two-hour repair video without moving. Something is occurring, but it is not a simple loss of patience.

What the short clip has altered is the cost of leaving. A film in a hall or a chapter in a novel makes departure awkward. A video that offers a replacement every three seconds makes staying an active decision. Pupils are therefore learning to judge material within moments, and they judge accurately. The trouble is that the skill they are developing is selection rather than endurance. When a text rewards patience slowly, as history and mathematics both do, that skill misfires. Our reading survey revealed that pupils who described themselves as heavy clip watchers were no worse at reading, yet they abandoned unfamiliar texts twice as often.

So I do not seek a ban, which schools cannot enforce and which teaches nothing. I want the difficulty named out loud. Tell a class that the first four pages of a novel are deliberately slow, and many of them will hold on. Deprived of that warning, they read the slowness as failure and go elsewhere. The attention is intact; what has vanished is the assumption that boredom might be a promise.
qs: What is the writer's purpose in this column?
To argue that the loss of patience among the young has been exaggerated.
To reframe the issue as one of quitting habits, not lost attention.
To argue that libraries should limit clip watching during school hours.
To explain why history and mathematics reward patient reading.

qs.evidence: Something is occurring, but it is not a simple loss of patience.
qs.answer: To reframe the issue as one of quitting habits, not lost attention.
qs.why: Tujuannya membingkai ulang soalnya: yang berubah kebiasaan cepat pergi, bukan hilangnya kemampuan memperhatikan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis justru mengakui ada perubahan nyata, jadi bukan sekadar membantah bahwa kesabaran menurun. Pembatasan klip ia tolak karena tidak bisa ditegakkan, dan mata pelajaran yang menuntut kesabaran dipakai sebagai contoh, bukan bahasan utama.

qs: What did the school's reading survey find?
Heavy clip watchers read as well but gave up on new texts more often.
Heavy clip watchers read a good deal worse than the other pupils.
Pupils who watched few clips abandoned unfamiliar texts twice as often.
Heavy clip watchers finished long texts as often as short ones.

qs.evidence: Our reading survey revealed that pupils who described themselves as heavy clip watchers were no worse at reading, yet they abandoned unfamiliar texts twice as often.
qs.answer: Heavy clip watchers read as well but gave up on new texts more often.
qs.why: Hasil survei: penonton klip berat nggak lebih buruk kemampuan membacanya, tapi dua kali lebih sering meninggalkan teks yang belum dikenal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Survei menyebut penonton klip berat tidak lebih buruk kemampuan membacanya, jadi opsi pertama membalik hasil. Angka dua kali lebih sering meninggalkan teks juga milik kelompok itu, bukan kelompok yang sedikit menonton, dan panjang teks tidak dibandingkan.

qs: How does the writer contrast a novel with a short video?
A novel rewards patience, while a repair video rewards selection.
Walking out of a book feels harder than moving on from a clip.
A novel is judged within moments, while a clip is judged slowly.
A novel holds a reader's attention longer than any clip can.

qs.evidence: A film in a hall or a chapter in a novel makes departure awkward. A video that offers a replacement every three seconds makes staying an active decision.
qs.answer: Walking out of a book feels harder than moving on from a clip.
qs.why: Kontrasnya soal biaya keluar: meninggalkan bab novel terasa nggak enak, sedangkan pindah dari klip gampang sekali.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kontras yang dibangun penulis adalah biaya untuk pergi, bukan jenis ganjaran. Penilaian dalam sekejap justru sifat klip, dan contoh remaja yang menonton video reparasi dua jam membantah klaim bahwa novel selalu menahan perhatian lebih lama.

qs: What does the writer imply teachers should do about slow openings?
Choose novels whose opening pages move a good deal more quickly.
Let pupils put a text down once they have judged it fairly.
Warn pupils in advance that the dullness is intended.
Show that a slow opening can be skipped without losing the story.

qs.evidence: Tell a class that the first four pages of a novel are deliberately slow, and many of them will hold on.
qs.answer: Warn pupils in advance that the dullness is intended.
qs.why: Isyaratnya: beri tahu dulu kalau bagian awal memang sengaja lambat, maka banyak murid akan bertahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis tidak menyarankan ganti novel maupun melewati bagian awal; justru bagian lambat itu yang ia minta dinamai terlebih dahulu. Membiarkan murid berhenti juga berlawanan, sebab tujuannya membuat mereka bertahan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Pupils at the school watch about three hours of short videos each day."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Pupils at the school watch about three hours of short videos each day.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: The same fifteen-year-old who abandons a page after four lines will watch a two-hour repair video without moving.
qs.why: Teks menyebut satu video dua jam sebagai contoh, tapi nggak pernah memberi jumlah jam menonton klip per hari. Kuantitasnya nggak disebut, jadi Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" butuh angka harian yang nggak ada. "False" juga salah karena teks nggak membantah angka itu; ia cuma nggak mengukurnya.

title: What Actually Brings Donors Back
text:
A district blood service has published the results of an experiment on repeat donation, and the findings unsettle a familiar assumption. Campaign posters usually appeal to duty. The service wanted to know whether duty is what actually brings a donor back a second time.

Four thousand first-time donors were divided into three groups. One group received a message thanking them and stating that their unit had been used within nine days. The second received a reminder of the district's continuing shortage. The third received nothing beyond the standard card. Sixteen weeks later, the first group had returned at almost twice the rate of the third, while the shortage reminder produced no measurable effect at all. Because the three groups were similar in age and occupation, the difference is unlikely to be an accident of sampling.

The authors interpret the result cautiously, and their explanation seems sound to me. A shortage message tells a donor that the problem is endless, whereas a use message tells her that her own contribution finished a job. Duty may bring somebody in the first time; evidence of effect brings her back. If that is right, the campaign posters in every clinic corridor are addressing the wrong moment. The money spent on them would be better spent on nine hundred short messages telling donors where their blood went.
qs: What does the experiment suggest about repeat donation?
Donors return more often when reminded that the shortage continues.
Donors decide about returning within nine days of their first visit.
Donors respond to any message, whichever kind of appeal it makes.
Donors return when told their own gift achieved something specific.

qs.evidence: Duty may bring somebody in the first time; evidence of effect brings her back.
qs.answer: Donors return when told their own gift achieved something specific.
qs.why: Temuannya: bukti bahwa sumbangan sendiri terpakai itulah yang menarik donor kembali, bukan seruan kewajiban.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pengingat kelangkaan disebut tidak memberi efek terukur sama sekali. Sembilan hari adalah lamanya kantong darah terpakai, bukan tenggat keputusan donor, dan hasilnya justru berbeda tajam antar jenis pesan.

qs: What did the first group of donors receive?
Thanks and word that their blood reached a patient in nine days.
Thanks together with a warning that the district shortage was continuing.
A standard card and nothing else during the sixteen weeks.
A reminder sent nine weeks after their first donation.

qs.evidence: One group received a message thanking them and stating that their unit had been used within nine days.
qs.answer: Thanks and word that their blood reached a patient in nine days.
qs.why: Kelompok pertama dapat ucapan terima kasih plus keterangan bahwa kantongnya terpakai dalam sembilan hari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Peringatan kelangkaan adalah pesan kelompok kedua, dan kartu biasa tanpa tambahan adalah kelompok ketiga. Angka sembilan mengacu pada hari, bukan pekan; enam belas pekan adalah jarak pengukuran hasil.

qs: How did the three groups differ in their rate of return?
Both groups that received a message came back more than the third.
The group reminded of the shortage returned twice as often as the others.
Only the group told about the use of their blood came back more.
All three groups returned at about the same rate after four months.

qs.evidence: Sixteen weeks later, the first group had returned at almost twice the rate of the third, while the shortage reminder produced no measurable effect at all.
qs.answer: Only the group told about the use of their blood came back more.
qs.why: Yang naik hampir dua kali lipat cuma kelompok pertama; pengingat kelangkaan nggak memberi efek terukur.
qs.whyOthersFail: Hanya kelompok pertama yang kembali hampir dua kali lipat dibanding kelompok ketiga; pesan kelangkaan tidak menaikkan apa pun. Karena itu kedua kelompok berpesan tidak sama-sama naik, dan tiga kelompok itu jelas tidak seimbang hasilnya.

qs: Why do the authors think corridor posters address the wrong moment?
Because posters cost more than the short messages the service could send.
Because posters speak to newcomers, not to donors deciding to return.
Because corridors are read in a hurry by people waiting for tests.
Because appeals to duty were shown to keep first-time donors away.

qs.evidence: If that is right, the campaign posters in every clinic corridor are addressing the wrong moment.
qs.answer: Because posters speak to newcomers, not to donors deciding to return.
qs.why: Poster menyapa orang yang belum pernah datang, padahal keputusan penting terjadi saat donor menimbang mau kembali atau nggak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Biaya poster memang disebut di kalimat terakhir, tapi bukan alasan momennya salah. Suasana koridor tidak dibahas, dan seruan kewajiban justru diakui bisa membawa orang datang pertama kali; yang gagal adalah menariknya kembali.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The three groups of donors differed sharply in age and in the work they did."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The three groups of donors differed sharply in age and in the work they did.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Because the three groups were similar in age and occupation, the difference is unlikely to be an accident of sampling.
qs.why: Teks bilang ketiga kelompok mirip umur dan pekerjaannya, jadi klaim "berbeda tajam" membalik pernyataan itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena polaritasnya dibalik. "Not stated" salah karena kesamaan kelompok disebut untuk membela hasil.

title: Two Ways to Pay for a Festival
text:
Two villages an hour apart celebrate the identical harvest festival yet finance it in opposite ways. One sells naming rights to a telephone company and a fertilizer dealer. The other collects a modest levy from every household and declines outside money. Both festivals occurred last month, and the contrast rewards a comparison.

The sponsored festival is plainly richer. It hired a sound system, printed a schedule and paid three troupes from the provincial capital. Attendance was roughly four thousand, and nobody had to be asked for a contribution. The levy festival raised about a tenth of that budget and used volunteers throughout. Yet its programme contained six local forms that the sponsored village has not performed since 2016, including the long procession that sponsors consider too slow for photographs. The sponsored village, meanwhile, has an audience its neighbour cannot match, and audiences keep traditions alive as surely as committees do.

My own view is that the two villages are buying different things and should admit it. Sponsorship buys scale and comfort at the price of editing. The levy buys control at the price of reach, and control is worth little if only three hundred people watch. A sensible compromise exists: accept sponsorship for the stage and the lighting, but keep the running order in the hands of the households. Whoever chooses the programme owns the festival, whatever the banners say.
qs: What is the writer's main point about the two festivals?
Each funding route buys something the other gives up.
Sponsorship is worth accepting as long as the sums involved are published.
A household levy buys control, which is worth a much smaller audience.
Both villages would draw larger audiences by holding one joint festival.

qs.evidence: My own view is that the two villages are buying different things and should admit it.
qs.answer: Each funding route buys something the other gives up.
qs.why: Pokok pendapatnya: dua desa itu membeli hal berbeda, satu skala satu kendali, dan sebaiknya diakui terbuka.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penerbitan angka sponsor tidak pernah diusulkan; yang diusulkan adalah menjaga susunan acara di tangan warga. Iuran memang membeli kendali, tapi teks bilang kendali bernilai kecil kalau hanya tiga ratus orang menonton, dan festival gabungan tidak pernah dibahas.

qs: What did the sponsored village spend its money on?
Volunteers, six older dance forms and one very long procession.
A sound system, a levy collector and two provincial troupes.
Amplification, a printed programme and troupes from the capital.
Banners, naming rights and a photographer from the provincial capital.

qs.evidence: It hired a sound system, printed a schedule and paid three troupes from the provincial capital.
qs.answer: Amplification, a printed programme and troupes from the capital.
qs.why: Uangnya dipakai untuk tata suara sewaan, jadwal cetak, dan tiga sanggar dari ibu kota provinsi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Relawan, enam bentuk lokal, dan prosesi panjang adalah ciri desa beriuran. Sanggar yang dibayar ada tiga, bukan dua, dan tidak ada penarik iuran di desa bersponsor; hak penamaan adalah sumber dananya, bukan belanjanya.

qs: What advantage does the article say the levy festival has?
It draws about four thousand visitors from the nearby districts.
It still performs older items that its neighbour has dropped.
It spends roughly ten times as much on its stage equipment.
It pays local troupes rather than groups from the provincial capital.

qs.evidence: Yet its programme contained six local forms that the sponsored village has not performed since 2016, including the long procession that sponsors consider too slow for photographs.

title: Letter to the Mill: Dust on the Southern Lane
text:
We write as the committee representing the ninety households of the southern lane, which lies directly downwind of your saw shed. Our purpose is to describe a measurable problem and to propose a specific remedy. We have deliberately avoided the language of complaint. We would much prefer an agreement to a dispute.

Since the second saw line opened in March, wood dust has settled on the lane every working day. Two of our members recorded the deposit on identical glass plates for eight weeks. The plate nearest your fence collected roughly five times the dust of the plate at the far end of the lane. Three families have relocated their drying racks indoors. The primary school has since closed the windows on that side. We accept that the mill provides work for many of our own households, and we are not asking for the second line to be shut.

We request two measures and one commitment. First, the extraction hood over the second line should be fitted with the filter your engineer described to us in April. Second, the yard should be dampened before the afternoon shift, when the wind strengthens. Our commitment is to continue the plate readings and to publish them monthly, whatever they show. If the readings fall, your neighbours will know it; if they do not, we shall have a shared record rather than an argument about impressions.
qs: Why has the committee written to the mill?
To ask for the second saw line to be closed until a filter is fitted.
To record that the mill has ignored its engineer's advice since April.
To seek payment for the drying racks three families moved indoors.
To set out measured evidence and suggest two workable changes.

qs.evidence: Our purpose is to describe a measurable problem and to propose a specific remedy.
qs.answer: To set out measured evidence and suggest two workable changes.

title: Keep the Parents on the Touchline
text:
The district has offered our small football club a qualified coach for two afternoons a week, and the committee is delighted. I am not, although my reason has nothing to do with quality. The offer arrives with a condition: the parents who currently run the sessions would step back. That condition is the whole difficulty.

Consider the effect on the club. A visiting coach improves technique, and nobody sensible denies it. Yet a coach who arrives at four and leaves at six cannot notice that a boy has stopped speaking to his brother. The parents on the touchline are unqualified, inconsistent and occasionally embarrassing, but they are permanent. When rain cancelled sessions for three weeks in February, it was two fathers who telephoned every family. A district timetable, however professional, produces attendance rather than attachment.

The sensible arrangement is obvious and slightly awkward to negotiate. Accept the coach for one afternoon, keep the parents on the other, and let the coach spend an hour a month teaching them what he knows. Skill can be transferred; belonging cannot be delivered by timetable. If the district insists that its coach works alone, the committee should politely decline the offer. A club with worse passing and forty children who feel expected is stronger than a club with neither.
qs: What is the writer trying to persuade the committee to do?
Accept the coach for both afternoons and thank the district for the offer.
Ask the district for a coach who could stay well beyond six o'clock.
Share the sessions so that the parents keep their role at the club.
Decline the offer, since technique matters less than a child's belonging.

qs.evidence: Accept the coach for one afternoon, keep the parents on the other, and let the coach spend an hour a month teaching them what he knows.
qs.answer: Share the sessions so that the parents keep their role at the club.

title: Who Actually Rides the Shared Bicycles
text:
The shared bicycle scheme in this town was justified by an argument about traffic, and a new study has tested it. Planners predicted that riders would abandon motorbikes. Researchers followed 600 registered users for five months and matched their trips against their previous habits.

The result is awkward for the original argument. Only 14 per cent of shared bicycle journeys replaced a motorbike trip. Nearly half replaced a walk, and a quarter replaced a ride on a minibus. Because walking produces no emissions, that substitution weakens the scheme's environmental case considerably. The pattern arises from where the docking points stand: fourteen of the twenty sit inside a single flat district that was already walkable. Users living on the hill, who own most of the town's motorbikes, reported that the nearest dock was too far to be convenient.

The authors do not recommend closing the scheme, and neither would I. Their argument is that its stated purpose should be corrected or its map redrawn. Moving six docks to the hill would test the traffic claim honestly for the first time. Leaving the docks where they are is defensible too, provided the town stops describing the bicycles as a measure against motorbike traffic. A scheme judged by the wrong promise will be called a failure even when it is useful.

It is not doing the job it was publicly promised to do.
It has taken a useful share of motorbike trips off the town's roads.
It should be closed, since the walks it replaced produced no emissions.
It works best for the hill residents who own most of the motorbikes.

qs.answer: It is not doing the job it was publicly promised to do.

title: A Volunteer Company Attempts a Difficult Play
text:
A company of volunteers chose one of the hardest plays in the repertoire for its autumn production, and the choice was braver than it was wise. The text requires eleven actors who can hold a silence. The company has seven, three of whom joined in August.

What they achieved is nevertheless remarkable in places. The set, built from borrowed scaffolding and grey cloth, turns a shallow stage into two rooms without a single wasted plank. The lighting, operated from a stepladder, is the best I have seen in this hall. The costumes, borrowed from a school store, were the one element that looked improvised. The second act, which depends on two characters saying almost nothing for twelve minutes, held an audience of ninety absolutely still. The first act did not: lines were rushed, entrances collided, and the difficult opening speech was delivered towards the wings.

So the honest verdict is mixed, and I offer it as encouragement rather than complaint. This company should not have attempted this play with seven actors and six weeks. It should attempt it again next autumn with nine actors and twelve weeks, because the second act proved the ambition was not misplaced. Volunteer theatre earns nothing by being praised indiscriminately. It earns a great deal by being told, accurately, which twelve minutes worked.
qs: What is the reviewer's overall assessment of the production?

A careful production whose faults lie mainly in its borrowed costumes.
A brave choice that the company should not repeat for some years.

title: Count the Old Trees Before Planting New Ones
text:
Our city has promised to plant fifty thousand saplings, and the announcement was greeted with the applause such promises always receive. I would applaud too if the same month had not seen four mature trees removed from the market road. A planting figure is easy to celebrate. A felling figure is rarely published at all.

The arithmetic behind my objection is not complicated. A sapling planted this year gives almost no shade for a decade, and about a third of the last campaign's trees died within two summers. The four trees on the market road, by contrast, were cooling a bus stop and holding a bank of soil. They also supported birds that no sapling will attract for twenty years. Trading them for saplings is not a gain but a delay disguised as progress. Nobody counted what was lost, because nothing obliges anyone to count it.

So I want two lines added to the campaign, not the campaign cancelled. First, publish the number of mature trees felled beside the number planted, in the same document. Second, require a written reason whenever a tree above a certain girth is removed. Neither line costs money, and both would make the promise honest. Planting is a pleasure; protecting is a duty, and duties are what get quietly dropped.

qs.answer: Saving established trees matters more than announcing new plantings.

title: Folk Tales on Air and on Demand
text:
The same body of folk tales now reaches this region through two very different channels, and the difference is not merely technical. The evening radio programme has told one story a week since 1994. The podcast series, begun three years ago, releases three episodes a month and keeps everything available.

Radio wins on discipline and on chance. A storyteller with seven minutes must cut, and the cutting produces versions that grandparents recognize from their own childhood. Listeners also encounter tales they did not choose, which is how anybody meets an unfamiliar story. The podcast wins on depth and on record: an episode may run forty minutes, include the storyteller's own explanation and preserve a dialect version beside a standard one. Against that, its listeners search for what they already know, so the strange tales are heard least. The archive is fuller, while the audience is narrower.

In my view the region needs both formats, and it needs them to talk to each other. The radio programme should announce which podcast episode extends the story it has just told. The podcast should let the radio hosts choose one episode a month, precisely because their taste is less predictable than a search box. Preservation without circulation becomes a locked cupboard. Circulation without preservation becomes a rumour that fades.
qs: What does the writer conclude about the two channels?
Both are needed, and each should point listeners to the other.
The podcast preserves more, so it should gradually take over from radio.
Radio matters more, since a full archive is of little use to listeners.
Whichever format reaches more listeners should get the region's support.

qs.evidence: In my view the region needs both formats, and it needs them to talk to each other.
qs.answer: Both are needed, and each should point listeners to the other.

qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis menolak menyerahkan semuanya ke satu format; arsip disebut berguna tapi sepi kalau tidak diedarkan. Ia juga tidak memilih berdasarkan jangkauan, melainkan meminta kedua format saling merujuk pendengar.

title: The Quiet Arrival of the Watching Camera
text:
Few shoppers pause at the small notice fixed beside the entrance, and fewer still read it. Yet in a growing number of retail centres, cameras no longer merely record; they measure faces and compare them against a privately held list. What is marketed to retailers as a defence against theft has quietly become an instrument for sorting the public. The change arrived without debate, and its defenders have relied on that silence rather more than they admit. A measure that would once have demanded a public argument now requires only a purchase order and a compliant landlord.

Supporters of the technology advance a reasonable case: retail staff face genuine risks, and a small minority of repeat offenders accounts for much of the loss. If recognition software can identify such a person at the door, the argument runs, everybody benefits. What the argument omits is the cost carried by the thousands of innocent faces measured every hour. Nothing in the design of these systems distinguishes a suspect from a customer buying milk. They are not suspects; they are merely the raw material of the method.

There remains the awkward question of authority. The lists are compiled by private security firms rather than by courts, and the standard of proof is whatever a firm finds convenient. A shopper wrongly included has no reliable route to discovering the fact, still less to having the entry deleted. Nor is there any independent body to which a complaint might sensibly be addressed. Errors of this kind are distributed unevenly, since such systems are documented as performing worse on darker and younger faces. A tool that fails hardest on those already watched most closely can hardly be described as neutral.

None of this requires that the cameras be removed tomorrow. It does require that the burden of justification rest with whoever installs them. Publish the rules, provide an appeal, delete what is unnecessary, and demonstrate that losses genuinely decline. Retailers who genuinely fear theft should welcome such tests, since a system that survives them commands a confidence mere assertion can never buy. Until those conditions are satisfied, shoppers are being asked to accept permanent inspection in exchange for a promise that nobody has audited. That is not security; it is convenience dressed as safety.
qs: Which best describes what the writer is doing in this piece?
recommending that retail staff be given better protection from theft
arguing that a technology already in use must be made to justify itself
setting out how privately held lists might be compiled more accurately
urging shoppers to read the notice fixed beside the shop entrance

qs.evidence: It does require that the burden of justification rest with whoever installs them.
qs.answer: arguing that a technology already in use must be made to justify itself
qs.why: Penulis nggak menolak kameranya; dia menuntut pihak yang memasang membuktikan dulu bahwa alat itu layak dipakai.
qs.whyOthersFail: Perlindungan staf memang diakui sebagai kekhawatiran pendukung teknologi, bukan tujuan tulisan ini; teks nggak pernah menyarankan cara menyusun daftar yang lebih rapi, justru mempersoalkan siapa yang berwenang menyusunnya; dan pemberitahuan di pintu cuma dipakai sebagai gambaran pembuka bahwa perubahan ini terjadi tanpa perdebatan, bukan seruan agar pembeli membacanya.

author: Editorial comment
setting: shopping centres and the firms that police them

title: When a Finding Refuses to Repeat
text:
A decade ago a curious pattern began to trouble psychologists. Studies that had been taught for years, cited in textbooks and rehearsed in lectures, produced far weaker results when other laboratories ran them again. In several well-known cases the effect disappeared altogether. The discovery was uncomfortable, yet in a narrow sense it was also a triumph for the method, because the discipline had caught itself out without outside help. Nobody had set out to test the memory of an entire field, yet that is precisely what the exercise became.

The reasons proved less dramatic than fraud. Many original studies had used small samples, sometimes fewer than thirty volunteers, which makes any single result unstable. Researchers also enjoyed considerable freedom in how they measured and analysed what they collected, and small choices made in good faith tend to favour the outcome an investigator expects. Journals compounded the problem by preferring surprising findings to ordinary ones, so the published record filled with the loudest results rather than the steadiest.

Reform followed, and much of it has been strikingly practical. Teams now register their predictions and their procedures before gathering data, which makes any later adjustment visible to a reader. Sample sizes have grown, several laboratories often run the same procedure together, and raw measurements are increasingly published alongside the paper itself. Editors at several journals now accept a paper on the strength of its design alone, before a single result is known. Where these habits have taken hold, replication rates have improved, though nobody claims the problem is settled.

For a general reader the lesson is not that psychology is unreliable but that a single study is a weak thing. Confidence ought to accumulate slowly, through repetition, and should be withheld from any headline resting on one experiment. A reader who waits for the second and third attempt is not being awkward; she is behaving exactly as the evidence requires. Researchers who keep insisting on the point are occasionally accused of dampening enthusiasm. In truth they are protecting the only asset the discipline has, which is the right to be believed.
qs: Which statement best captures the central argument of the article?
weak single studies rather than dishonesty explain the failures
the reforms have now settled the problem for the discipline
registering predictions in advance is standard across the field
the discipline was rescued by scrutiny from outside it

qs.evidence: For a general reader the lesson is not that psychology is unreliable but that a single study is a weak thing.
qs.answer: weak single studies rather than dishonesty explain the failures
qs.why: Artikel menyimpulkan bahwa satu studi tunggal itu lemah, dan sebab-sebab kegagalan replikasi lebih membosankan daripada kecurangan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Klaim bahwa masalahnya selesai bertentangan dengan kalimat bahwa nggak ada yang mengaku masalah itu sudah beres; pendaftaran prediksi disebut berlaku di tim yang sudah mengubah kebiasaan, bukan di seluruh bidang; dan penyelamatan dari luar bertabrakan dengan kalimat bahwa disiplin itu menangkap dirinya sendiri tanpa bantuan pihak luar.

qs: What does the article give as one concrete reason why early results were unstable?

some studies rested on samples of under thirty people

qs.evidence: Many original studies had used small samples, sometimes fewer than thirty volunteers, which makes any single result unstable.
qs.answer: some studies rested on samples of under thirty people

qs.whyOthersFail: Soal asisten yang tahu prediksi memang masuk akal di dunia riset, tapi teks cuma menyebut kebebasan peneliti dalam mengukur dan menganalisis, bukan siapa yang mengambil data; sukarelawan yang ikut beberapa studi nggak pernah disinggung; dan urutan pendaftaran prediksi justru dibalik, karena teks menempatkannya sebelum data dikumpulkan sebagai bagian reformasi.

qs.answer: approving, while refusing to treat the problem as solved

qs.answer: they are defending the public's reason to trust findings

True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Journals in that period favoured ordinary findings over surprising ones.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Journals compounded the problem by preferring surprising findings to ordinary ones, so the published record filled with the loudest results rather than the steadiest.

setting: psychology laboratories and the journals that publish them

title: Two Markers, One Pile of Essays
text:
Every autumn, university departments confront the same arithmetic: more essays, the same number of markers, and a promise that feedback will reach students within three weeks. Software that scores student writing automatically is offered as the obvious remedy. Two colleagues in one faculty describe that proposal in strikingly different terms, and the distance between them is instructive. Neither is arguing in bad faith, which is what makes the disagreement worth setting out at length.

The first, who teaches a first-year module of four hundred students, is briskly pragmatic. Her markers currently spend whole weekends on structure and referencing, matters a machine can check consistently and without fatigue. Released from that drudgery, staff could turn their attention to argument, which is where trained judgement genuinely adds something. She also observes that the software is at least predictable, whereas a tired marker working towards midnight is not. Consistency, she adds, is a form of fairness, since two identical essays ought not to attract different marks.

Her colleague in literature remains unpersuaded. What such systems reward, he argues, is fluent conformity: tidy structure, familiar vocabulary, sentences of moderate length. An essay that takes a genuine risk and half succeeds may well score below one that says nothing gracefully. The risk, on his account, is not that machines mark badly but that students rapidly learn what machines reward. He concedes that the workload problem is real, yet insists the proposed remedy shifts the definition of good writing towards whatever the model happens to count.

Neither colleague disputes the arithmetic; their quarrel concerns what marking is for. If marking measures compliance with a form, automation will serve it perfectly well. If marking is instead a conversation about thinking, software may prepare the ground but cannot conduct the exchange. Departments weighing the two accounts should notice which description of their own work they are quietly adopting, because the choice of tool will settle the question long before anyone votes on it. That is a decision about values, and it deserves to be made deliberately rather than absorbed from a procurement document.
qs: Why does the writer set the two colleagues' positions side by side?
to expose a deeper disagreement about the purpose of marking
to describe the workload markers carry at the start of each year
to recommend that the department buy the marking software
to warn that markers should not be asked to work late at night

qs.evidence: Neither colleague disputes the arithmetic; their quarrel concerns what marking is for.
qs.answer: to expose a deeper disagreement about the purpose of marking
qs.why: Penulis menaruh dua pendapat berdampingan supaya terlihat bahwa perselisihannya soal fungsi penilaian, bukan soal hitung-hitungan beban kerja.
qs.whyOthersFail: Beban kerja tiap musim gugur memang dibuka di paragraf pertama, tapi kedua dosen sama-sama menerimanya, jadi itu latar bukan pokok tulisan; rekomendasi pembelian bertentangan dengan penutup yang justru meminta keputusan itu diambil sadar setelah nilai-nilainya dipikirkan; dan kerja sampai tengah malam cuma satu contoh yang dipakai dosen pertama, bukan peringatan penulis.

qs.evidence: Her markers currently spend whole weekends on structure and referencing, matters a machine can check consistently and without fatigue.
qs.answer: checking how essays are structured and sources listed
qs.why: Teks menyebut pemeriksa sekarang menghabiskan akhir pekan untuk struktur dan penulisan rujukan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Menilai argumen justru pekerjaan yang ingin direbut kembali kalau mesin mengambil alih hal teknis, jadi bukan keadaan sekarang; nasihat soal keberanian menulis adalah kekhawatiran dosen sastra, bukan tugas pemeriksa; dan perbandingan nilai manusia dengan nilai software nggak pernah dilaporkan terjadi.

qs: Which observation most clearly conveys the writer's own view rather than a colleague's?
the claim that trained judgement adds most when argument is judged

the promise that written feedback will arrive within three weeks
the warning that a purchase may quietly redefine the work

qs.evidence: That is a decision about values, and it deserves to be made deliberately rather than absorbed from a procurement document.
qs.answer: the warning that a purchase may quietly redefine the work
qs.why: Tiga pilihan lain adalah janji institusi atau suara salah satu dosen; peringatan bahwa keputusan pembelian bisa menggeser makna pekerjaan itu penilaian penulis sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Soal pertimbangan terlatih adalah argumen dosen pertama yang dikutip penulis, bukan pendapatnya; keberatan tentang keseragaman yang lancar milik dosen sastra; dan janji umpan balik tiga minggu adalah janji jurusan yang dibuka sebagai latar administratif.

False
Not stated

qs.answer: True
