author: Higher education review
setting: a large humanities faculty

title: Credit Where No Wage Is Paid
text:
Ask a university why an unpaid placement carries academic credit and the answer arrives smoothly: students gain experience, employers gain fresh energy, and nobody pays for the privilege. The arrangement looks like a gift. Examined a little longer, it looks more like a charge quietly transferred from the employer to the student, and from the student to whoever supports her.

Consider who can accept such an offer. A student whose family can cover three months of rent in a costly city may take the placement and profit from it. A student supporting relatives, or paying her own rent from evening shifts, cannot, and the credit she forgoes is not optional. It appears on the same transcript, weighed by the same admissions panels, read by the same recruiters. The transcript records what was achieved, never what could be afforded. Employers, meanwhile, receive an applicant filtered by household wealth and mistake the outcome for merit. What was presented as an equal opportunity therefore reproduces the advantage that already existed.

Defenders reply that the labour market is competitive and that experience must be obtained somewhere. That is true, and it is precisely the difficulty. Because the credit makes the placement part of a degree, the university lends its authority to work it does not pay for and often does not inspect. Placement diaries are marked; the hours behind them are rarely audited. Nor is the practice confined to glamorous industries; it now reaches accountancy, publishing and local government alike. Where an employer substitutes a stream of unpaid students for a junior post, the university has become a supplier rather than an educator.

The remedy need not be dramatic: universities could require that any credit-bearing placement pay at least a modest stipend. They could also publish the proportion of students who complete one, and treat an unpaid offer as a matter for negotiation rather than gratitude. None of that abolishes competition for good positions; it merely stops an institution funded to widen access from certifying an arrangement that narrows it.
qs: Which best states the writer's central claim?
employers gain more from these placements than students do
universities should stop awarding credit for any placement
credit-bearing unpaid placements pass a cost on to students
recruiters read a transcript without knowing what it cost

qs.evidence: Examined a little longer, it looks more like a charge quietly transferred from the employer to the student, and from the student to whoever supports her.
qs.answer: credit-bearing unpaid placements pass a cost on to students
qs.why: Inti tulisan: biaya yang seharusnya ditanggung pemberi kerja dipindahkan diam-diam ke mahasiswa dan siapa pun yang menopangnya.

the rent a student pays while living in a costly city
the hours actually worked during a placement

brisk and factual, setting out how placements are arranged
sympathetic towards employers who are short of junior staff

True
False

author: Opinion column
setting: universities and the employers they place students with

title: Reading the Temperature of a Street
text:
A city does not have a single temperature. On a still afternoon in late September, a bus stop on a wide commercial road may register eight degrees above a shaded lane in the same district. The two sit four hundred metres apart, and official statistics rarely capture such a gap. The instruments that generate them stand in open ground, deliberately distant from traffic, and their purpose is comparison between years rather than between streets.

Researchers have therefore begun measuring at the height of a walking body, using compact sensors strapped to lamp posts or carried on cargo bicycles. Others are fitted to refuse lorries, which already follow fixed routes through every neighbourhood. The technique yields a reading every few seconds along thousands of streets. The resulting maps show heat gathering in predictable places: broad junctions, open car parks, and roads lined with dark surfaces and little else. Shade, it emerges, governs the pattern more powerfully than any single building material.

The underlying mechanism is not mysterious: hard surfaces absorb radiation through the day and release it slowly after dark. A street beneath continuous tree cover therefore receives less heat and sheds it faster. Across one summer, a mature avenue held night temperatures three degrees below a treeless equivalent. That advantage was widest precisely when a resting body most needs relief. Modelling indicates that planting achieves most where existing cover is thinnest, which is seldom where planting budgets have historically been directed.

Such findings matter only if they reach the departments that dig holes. Where sensor readings have been published street by street, residents have asked why their own road was excluded from a planting programme. That question is considerably harder to deflect than a general appeal for greener cities: officials can dispute a slogan, whereas a table of measurements is more stubborn. A number attached to one particular road creates an obligation that a vague civic ambition never does. Measurement, in other words, does not merely describe an inequality of shade. It converts that inequality into something a council can be asked to answer for.
qs: What is the main purpose of the article?
to explain why official weather instruments stand away from traffic
to recommend that a heat sensor be fitted to every lamp post
to show how fine-grained heat data change what a council must answer for
to argue that planting trees should replace other cooling measures

qs.evidence: It converts that inequality into something a council can be asked to answer for.
qs.answer: to show how fine-grained heat data change what a council must answer for
qs.why: Penutupnya jelas: pengukuran rinci mengubah ketimpangan naungan jadi hal yang bisa dituntut jawabannya dari pemerintah kota.
qs.whyOthersFail: Letak alat resmi memang dijelaskan, tapi cuma untuk menerangkan kenapa selisih antar jalan tak tertangkap; pemasangan sensor di setiap lampu jalan nggak pernah diusulkan, sebab teks menyebut sensor dibawa kendaraan yang sudah berkeliling; dan penggantian cara pendinginan lain juga nggak ada, karena naungan cuma disebut lebih menentukan daripada bahan bangunan.

qs: How do researchers obtain readings from thousands of streets?
equipment travels on vehicles that already serve fixed rounds
readings are modelled from the height of a walking body
residents report the temperature of their own road each day
one instrument in open ground records the whole district

qs.evidence: Others are fitted to refuse lorries, which already follow fixed routes through every neighbourhood.
qs.answer: equipment travels on vehicles that already serve fixed rounds
qs.why: Sensor ditempelkan pada truk sampah yang memang sudah punya rute tetap ke setiap lingkungan, jadi alatnya bergerak bersama kendaraan yang beroperasi rutin.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketinggian tubuh yang berjalan adalah tinggi tempat sensor mengukur, bukan hasil pemodelan; laporan harian warga muncul sebagai akibat setelah data diterbitkan, bukan cara mengumpulkannya; dan alat tunggal di lahan terbuka justru pengukuran resmi yang dikritik karena melewatkan selisih antar jalan.

qs: Which finding gives the strongest support for the claim about shade?
tree-covered streets stayed cooler right through the night
the gap was widest at the hottest point of the afternoon
official instruments recorded eight degrees of difference
sensors were carried through every neighbourhood by lorries

qs.evidence: Across one summer, a mature avenue held night temperatures three degrees below a treeless equivalent.
qs.answer: tree-covered streets stayed cooler right through the night
qs.why: Selisih tiga derajat pada malam hari antara jalan berpohon dewasa dan jalan gundul adalah bukti paling langsung untuk klaim soal naungan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Waktu selisih terlebar disebut justru saat tubuh yang beristirahat paling butuh kelegaan, yaitu malam, bukan sore; selisih delapan derajat diukur di ketinggian tubuh oleh peneliti, bukan oleh alat resmi yang berdiri jauh dari jalan; dan cara sensor dibawa hanya soal metode, bukan bukti tentang naungan.

qs: What does the article imply about where trees have been planted in the past?
planting has tended to follow the readings of the new sensors
planting has often missed the streets with least cover already
planting has been concentrated on the widest junctions and car parks
planting has cooled most roads by about three degrees at night

qs.evidence: Modelling indicates that planting achieves most where existing cover is thinnest, which is seldom where planting budgets have historically been directed.
qs.answer: planting has often missed the streets with least cover already
qs.why: Kalau tempat paling efektif untuk menanam jarang jadi tujuan anggaran, berarti jalan yang paling gundul justru sering terlewat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Data sensor baru tersedia belakangan, jadi anggaran lama nggak mungkin mengikutinya; simpang lebar dan lahan parkir disebut sebagai tempat panas menumpuk, bukan tempat pohon ditanam; dan selisih tiga derajat berlaku untuk satu jalan berpohon dewasa dibanding jalan gundul, bukan untuk sebagian besar jalan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Official measuring instruments are placed close to busy traffic."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Official measuring instruments are placed close to busy traffic.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: The instruments that generate them stand in open ground, deliberately distant from traffic, and their purpose is comparison between years rather than between streets.
qs.why: Teks bilang alat resmi berdiri di lahan terbuka dan sengaja dijauhkan dari lalu lintas, jadi klaim ini kebalikannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" bertabrakan langsung dengan kalimat itu; "Not stated" salah karena posisi alat memang disebutkan.

setting: a city measuring its own hottest streets

title: Street Lighting Replacement: Two-Year Review
text:
This report reviews the first two years of the street lighting replacement programme and sets out four recommendations. Of the borough's twenty-nine thousand lamps, roughly two-thirds have now been converted to light-emitting units. Energy consumption on converted routes has fallen by about forty per cent, and maintenance visits have become markedly less frequent. The financial case, on those figures alone, is secure. The programme is on course to finish next winter, and the first bills have already come in lower.

Resident feedback complicates the picture. Complaints recorded through the council's portal fall into two groups: light spilling into bedrooms, and a colour of illumination described repeatedly as harsh. Both objections concentrate in streets fitted during the first year, before the specification was revised towards a warmer tone and a shallower angle. Comparable complaints from second-year streets are far fewer, which suggests the revision worked rather than that residents grew accustomed to the change. Most of the letters come from a small number of roads, which is worth keeping in mind.

Two risks deserve attention. First, the programme's savings have been calculated against a tariff agreed in the previous financial year; a rise in unit prices would reduce the margin without altering the physical benefit. Second, the decision to dim converted lamps after midnight was taken without consultation, and the evidence connecting that measure to reported feelings of safety remains thin. Officers should not assume public tolerance of dimming merely because complaints have been few. Neither risk threatens the programme, yet neither has been recorded in the published summaries.

Four recommendations follow. Fit first-year streets with the revised specification within eighteen months, beginning with residential roads rather than main routes. Publish route-level energy figures each quarter instead of annually, and commission an independent assessment of dimming before extending it to any further streets. Finally, record complaints by street rather than by ward, since the present arrangement conceals precisely the variation this programme needs to understand. None of this asks the council to slow down; it asks the council to look where it is going.
qs: Which statement best summarizes the position taken by the report?
the conversion should be paused until residents have been consulted
complaints about colour and glare are the programme's central finding
dimming after midnight has been the programme's clearest gain
the savings hold, yet parts of the programme need revisiting

qs.evidence: The financial case, on those figures alone, is secure.
qs.answer: the savings hold, yet parts of the programme need revisiting
qs.why: Laporan menerima sisi keuangannya sebagai kokoh, lalu menuntut perbaikan pada spesifikasi tahun pertama, pelaporan, dan pemudaran lampu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penghentian sementara bertabrakan dengan penutupnya, yang menyatakan laporan ini nggak meminta dewan kota melambat; keluhan warna dan cahaya masuk kamar memang dibahas panjang, tapi ditempatkan sebagai satu bagian gambaran, bukan temuan pokok; dan pemudaran setelah tengah malam justru disebut punya bukti yang masih tipis kaitannya dengan rasa aman.

qs.answer: they are much less numerous than first-year complaints
qs.why: Teks menyebut keluhan sebanding dari jalan tahun kedua jauh lebih sedikit dibanding jalan tahun pertama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penjelasan 'warga sudah terbiasa' persis yang ditolak teks, karena selisih keluhan disebut menunjukkan revisi spesifikasi yang bekerja; kaitan dengan pemudaran nggak pernah dilaporkan, dan pemudaran dibahas terpisah sebagai risiko kedua; dan keluhan cahaya masuk kamar disebut menumpuk di jalan tahun pertama, bukan tahun kedua.

qs.answer: wary, and unwilling to treat silence as approval

qs.whyOthersFail: Rasa tenang karena keluhan sedikit persis yang dilarang oleh kalimat itu; perluasan pemudaran justru diminta menunggu penilaian independen lebih dulu, dan tarif dibahas sebagai risiko terpisah; dan sikap menyerah pada penghematan bertabrakan dengan adanya empat rekomendasi yang menyangkut kenyamanan warga.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: True

title: The Hierarchy Nobody Writes Down
text:
Every capital budget contains a hierarchy, and it is rarely written down anywhere. Nobody defends that hierarchy openly, and the silence is part of how it survives. Money for a new flyover is found; money for a continuous footway is postponed. Ask which decision moved more people and the answer becomes inconvenient. The footway carries the schoolchild, the market trader and the person pushing a wheelchair, all of whom are counted, if at all, as an afterthought.

The bias is partly a matter of measurement. Traffic engineers have decades of vehicle counts, delay models and cost-benefit conventions, every one of them calibrated to time saved by drivers. Walking generates no comparable statistics, so a scheme that removes a hazard for a thousand pedestrians a day competes against one that saves ninety seconds for four thousand cars, and loses on paper. A number that exists will always defeat a number that does not, whatever either of them measures. What cannot be counted in the accepted unit tends to be treated as sentiment.

The consequences are visible at any junction after rain. A footway that ends without warning, a crossing timed for an athlete, a drain positioned so that a bus soaks the queue: none of these is an accident of nature. Each represents a choice made where the loudest interest held the better data. The people who wait at that crossing were never consulted about what their own time was worth. Meanwhile the flyover, having attracted the traffic it was built to relieve, produces a fresh demand for another.

None of this argues against major road works, some of which are unavoidable. It argues for symmetry. Count pedestrians as carefully as vehicles, publish the cost of a schoolchild's detour, and require any scheme above a stated threshold to report its effect on people walking. Cities that have adopted such rules did not stop building; they simply stopped pretending the choice was technical rather than political. A preference dressed up as engineering necessity persists precisely because nobody signs it. The hierarchy will survive until somebody writes it down and asks who consented to it.
qs: Which best captures the central claim of the essay?
cost-benefit conventions overstate the time that drivers save
a new flyover tends to attract the traffic it was built to relieve
walking loses out because it is not counted as carefully
councils deliberately hide their spending priorities from the public

qs.evidence: What cannot be counted in the accepted unit tends to be treated as sentiment.
qs.answer: walking loses out because it is not counted as carefully
qs.why: Argumen intinya: apa pun yang nggak terukur dalam satuan resmi dianggap perasaan belaka, dan berjalan kaki kalah justru karena itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak menuduh konvensi biaya-manfaat membesar-besarkan waktu pengemudi; keluhannya adalah waktu pejalan kaki tak punya angka sama sekali; soal jalan layang yang memanggil lalu lintasnya sendiri memang ada di paragraf ketiga, tapi itu satu contoh akibat, bukan klaim pokok; dan penyembunyian yang disengaja bertabrakan dengan penjelasan teks bahwa hierarki ini bertahan karena tak pernah ditulis atau ditandatangani siapa pun.

qs: What comparison does the writer use to show how schemes are judged?
the delay suffered by buses against the delay suffered by cars
removing a hazard for walkers against seconds saved for drivers
the cost of a child's detour against the cost of a new crossing
a flyover in one city measured against a flyover in another

qs.evidence: Walking generates no comparable statistics, so a scheme that removes a hazard for a thousand pedestrians a day competes against one that saves ninety seconds for four thousand cars, and loses on paper.
qs.answer: removing a hazard for walkers against seconds saved for drivers
qs.why: Perbandingan di teks memang antara menghilangkan bahaya bagi seribu pejalan kaki sehari dan menghemat sembilan puluh detik bagi empat ribu mobil.
qs.whyOthersFail: Bus cuma muncul sebagai kendaraan yang menyiram antrean di halte, tanpa perbandingan keterlambatan; biaya jalan memutar anak sekolah adalah angka yang penulis usulkan diterbitkan nanti, bukan pembanding yang sudah dipakai; dan dua kota nggak pernah dibandingkan di teks ini.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards the way such decisions are presented?
critical of a choice dressed up as pure technique
understanding, since engineers can only use the numbers they have
impressed by how carefully the conventions handle delay
detached, content to describe the practice without judging it

qs.evidence: Cities that have adopted such rules did not stop building; they simply stopped pretending the choice was technical rather than political.
qs.answer: critical of a choice dressed up as pure technique
qs.why: Frasa "stopped pretending the choice was technical rather than political" menunjukkan penulis menuduh keputusan politis dibungkus sebagai urusan teknis.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pengertian pada insinyur bertabrakan dengan tuntutan penulis agar pejalan kaki ikut dihitung, yang berarti kekurangan angka itu bisa diperbaiki; kekaguman pada konvensi juga salah, karena konvensi itu disebut dikalibrasi hanya untuk waktu pengemudi; dan sikap berjarak nggak cocok dengan paragraf penutup yang mengajukan empat tuntutan.

it was approved only after pedestrians had been counted

qs.whyOthersFail: Penghitungan pejalan kaki baru diusulkan di paragraf akhir, jadi mustahil jadi syarat persetujuan; teks justru menyebut muncul permintaan pembangunan berikutnya, bukan berkurangnya alasan membangun; dan sumber dananya nggak pernah dijelaskan, cuma disebut uang untuk trotoar selalu ditunda.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer maintains that large road projects are never necessary."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer maintains that large road projects are never necessary.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: None of this argues against major road works, some of which are unavoidable.
qs.why: Penulis menulis terang-terangan bahwa sebagian proyek jalan besar tak terhindarkan, jadi klaim ini kebalikan posisinya.

author: Opinion essay
setting: a city deciding what to build next

title: What the Ticket Machine Knows
text:
For most of the twentieth century a bus timetable was an act of informed guesswork. Planners counted passengers by hand for a fortnight, extrapolated, and rewrote the timetable every few years. Electronic ticketing altered the raw material available to them, because every tap of a card registers a boarding, a stop and a minute. What was once a sample has become something close to a census, and the change was quiet, arriving without anybody commissioning a new survey of passengers.

The findings have not always flattered established practice. On many routes the published interval bore little relation to the observed one: buses arrived in pairs separated by long gaps, a pattern familiar to passengers and long denied by operators. The cause is well understood mathematically. A bus that falls slightly behind collects more waiting passengers, loses further time at each stop, and is steadily caught by the vehicle behind. Once the pattern was visible in the records, the argument about whether it existed simply ended.

Ticketing records also revealed journeys that no timetable had anticipated. Substantial flows appeared between outer districts, bypassing the centre altogether, and these were served by routes designed on the assumption that everybody travelled inward each morning. Where operators added direct connections, use rose faster than any model had predicted. That suggests suppressed demand had existed for years without leaving a trace in the older counts.

Data of this kind is not self-interpreting. Card records show boardings, not intentions; they cannot say whether a passenger changed vehicles reluctantly or preferred to walk part of the way. Nor do they capture anybody who abandoned the service long ago. Used carefully, alongside interviews and street observation, the records make bus planning far less speculative than it was. A timetable remains a promise made to people, and no promise can be derived from a table alone. Treated as an oracle, they simply automate the assumptions already built into the network.
qs: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the article?
card data has made interviews with passengers unnecessary
operators stopped denying bus bunching once passengers complained
ticket records improve planning but still require interpretation
outer districts were well served long before the records existed

qs.evidence: Used carefully, alongside interviews and street observation, the records make bus planning far less speculative than it was.
qs.answer: ticket records improve planning but still require interpretation
qs.why: Artikel menutup dengan syarat: catatan kartu memang membuat perencanaan jauh kurang spekulatif, tapi hanya kalau dibaca bersama wawancara dan pengamatan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Wawancara justru disebut tetap perlu dan dipakai berdampingan dengan catatan; penyangkalan operator disebut berakhir ketika polanya terlihat di catatan, bukan karena keluhan penumpang; dan rute antar daerah luar baru ditambahkan setelah data muncul, jadi daerah itu sebelumnya tidak terlayani.

qs: Why, mathematically, do buses end up travelling in pairs?
drivers hold at stops to keep to the published interval
a late bus picks up more waiting passengers and slows further
planners counted passengers by hand for only a fortnight
flows between outer districts crowd the buses in the centre

qs.evidence: A bus that falls slightly behind collects more waiting passengers, loses further time at each stop, and is steadily caught by the vehicle behind.
qs.answer: a late bus picks up more waiting passengers and slows further
qs.why: Bus yang tertinggal sedikit mengumpulkan lebih banyak penumpang menunggu, kehilangan waktu di setiap halte, lalu dikejar bus di belakangnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penahanan bus di halte demi jadwal masuk akal di dunia nyata, tapi teks nggak menyebutnya sebagai sebab; hitungan manual dua minggu adalah praktik lama sebelum tiket elektronik, bukan penyebab penumpukan; dan arus antar daerah luar justru temuan terpisah tentang perjalanan yang melewati pusat kota.

qs: How does the writer regard the operators' earlier denials of this pattern?
forgiving, since the mathematics behind it was worked out only lately
detached, treating the dispute as a matter for operators alone
cautious, since the records may still measure the wrong thing
unimpressed, because passengers had observed it all along

qs.evidence: On many routes the published interval bore little relation to the observed one: buses arrived in pairs separated by long gaps, a pattern familiar to passengers and long denied by operators.
qs.answer: unimpressed, because passengers had observed it all along
qs.why: Penulis menyandingkan "familiar to passengers" dengan "long denied by operators", jadi penyangkalan itu ditampilkan sebagai sikap yang sulit dibela.
qs.whyOthersFail: Alasan bahwa matematikanya baru dipahami bertabrakan dengan kalimat bahwa sebabnya sudah lama dipahami secara matematis; sikap menyerahkan urusan ke operator nggak cocok karena penulis justru menilai penyangkalan mereka; dan kehati-hatian soal apa yang diukur memang ada di paragraf akhir, tapi itu ditujukan pada tafsir data, bukan pada penyangkalan penumpukan bus.

qs: Which restatement is closest to the writer's warning in the final paragraph?

title: Eleven Streets, Two Calendars
text:
The plan is modest on paper: eleven streets in the old centre closed to private vehicles between eight in the morning and seven in the evening, with deliveries permitted before nine. It has nonetheless produced a dispute in which both sides speak with evident sincerity. The strongest arguments, as often happens, are not the loudest ones. Both cases deserve to be stated at full strength, which is not how either has been reported.

For the traders' association the objection is arithmetic. Its members sell furniture, tiles and building materials, goods that customers arrive to collect by car and would never carry on a tram. A shop that loses its kerbside loses the transaction, not merely the convenience, and rents in the centre already assume a certain turnover. The association also notes, reasonably enough, that consultation took place through an online form during a fortnight in August.

The planning department answers with a different set of numbers. Counts on the same streets show pedestrians outnumbering car passengers by roughly nine to one, and most arrivals by car are visitors passing through rather than customers. Similar schemes elsewhere, it argues, produced a temporary decline in trade followed by a slow recovery, particularly for cafés and small retailers. The department also points out that the closure hours were chosen to protect early morning trade. It accepts that furniture merchants are a genuine exception and has offered loading permits.

What the exchange reveals is a mismatch of time horizons. The trader's difficulty is immediate and specific; the planner's benefit is gradual and general, and gradual benefits are poor compensation for a rent due in March. A scheme of this sort can still be defended, but only where the transition is funded rather than merely announced. Neither side is asking the other to disappear; each is asking to be counted properly. Whether the council has grasped that distinction is, on the evidence of its consultation, unclear.

to argue that the August consultation ought to be run again

title: Eleven Small Charges
text:
A decade ago the household ledger was mostly a list of purchases; now it is a list of arrangements. Streaming, storage, insurance, software, a monthly delivery of razor blades: each removes a small sum every month, and each was designed to be easier to begin than to end. The individual amounts are trivial, which is precisely the mechanism. Nobody signs up intending to forget, and that is exactly why the arrangement works so well.

Consider how the choice is presented. A trial costs nothing for a month and requires payment details at the outset. Cancellation is available, though rarely on the page where the subscription began, and the reminder that would prompt it is seldom sent. None of this is fraud; every term appears somewhere in the agreement. The wording is honest and the placement is not, and only one of those is regulated. The design simply relies on a well-documented feature of human attention: we discount small recurring costs and overestimate how carefully we monitor them.

The aggregate is not trivial at all. Surveys of household spending routinely find that people underestimate their monthly commitments by about a third, and that the shortfall is widest among those with the least room to absorb it. A charge of four pounds is easy to ignore; eleven such charges are a utility bill. Firms understand this arithmetic better than their customers do, since only one party sees the whole ledger. The firm, meanwhile, enjoys revenue that requires no further persuasion, which is exactly why investors value it so highly.

Regulation here need not be heavy. Require that cancellation be no harder than subscription, that a reminder precede any annual renewal, and that the yearly total appear beside the monthly figure. Firms confident of their value have little to fear from such rules; those relying on inattention will object loudly, and their objection is itself the evidence. Households, for their part, might usefully audit their own arrangements once a year, in the same spirit as checking a bank statement.

qs.answer: small recurring charges exploit predictable inattention

title: The Clock That Will Not Be Argued With
text:
Shift work is often discussed as a matter of preference, as though the only difficulty were that some people dislike early mornings. Laboratory evidence suggests something considerably less negotiable. The internal clock that governs body temperature, hormone release and alertness runs on a cycle of roughly twenty-four hours, and it takes its instructions chiefly from light. Ask that clock to invert its cycle and it complies slowly, incompletely, and never for good. It is not a habit that a worker can be talked out of.

The consequences are measurable within days. Volunteers kept awake at night under controlled conditions show reduced glucose tolerance, raised blood pressure and impaired attention on tasks demanding sustained vigilance. Performance declines most sharply between three and five in the morning, precisely when hospital wards, lorry cabs and control rooms are least supervised. Errors at that hour are not evidence of carelessness; they are a predictable output of the rota. Nobody chooses to be least capable at the moment of greatest responsibility; the pattern shows up in the same hours, week after week, on every kind of site.

Not every rota is equally punishing. Studies of rotating patterns consistently find that shifts advancing forwards, from morning to afternoon to night, are tolerated better than those which jump backwards. Longer runs on a single pattern allow partial adjustment, whereas a week alternating between days and nights prevents any adjustment at all. Access to daylight after a night shift, and darkness during recovery sleep, matters more than the total hours logged. These are cheap adjustments, and they are frequently the last to be considered.

None of this argues for the abolition of night work, which some services plainly require. It argues that the rota is a piece of safety equipment, and should be designed with the same seriousness as any other. Where employers have redesigned patterns on the evidence, absence and error rates have fallen without any reduction in output. Rotas are drawn up months ahead, so the chance to get them right comes round often. Where they have not, the cost is still paid, simply by somebody else.

the body clock can be retrained if one pattern is kept long enough

qs.evidence: It argues that the rota is a piece of safety equipment, and should be designed with the same seriousness as any other.
qs.answer: night work imposes measurable costs that rotas can lessen

title: Advice on Publishing Admissions Figures
text:
This paper responds to a request for advice on publishing university admissions data. Institutions currently release the number of applications and offers by course, but not the distribution of grades among those admitted, nor the proportion of places filled through routes other than the standard one. Applicants therefore plan against a picture that is accurate in outline and misleading in detail. That gap is small in law and large in practice. Most applicants apply to five courses and hear back from all but one of them.

Three arguments for fuller publication are persuasive. Where entry requirements are advertised as higher than those actually accepted, applicants from schools without experienced advisers are the ones most likely to be deterred. Publication also permits scrutiny of contextual offers, which several institutions defend in principle while declining to say how often they are made. Finally, the present opacity protects nobody except the institution, since rejected applicants learn nothing whatever about why. Nobody should have to guess at a rule that has already been written down.

Two objections deserve a serious answer. Small courses cannot publish grade distributions without effectively identifying individuals, so any scheme must set a minimum cohort size. More broadly, institutions fear that fuller data will be compressed into a league table rewarding the selection of already advantaged applicants. That risk is real, though it argues for publishing alongside a measure of progress after entry, not for publishing nothing. Refusing to measure is itself a decision about who bears the uncertainty. A bad table is a reason to build a better one.

None of this asks a single institution to lower its bar. We recommend that the department require annual publication of grade distributions for courses above a threshold of forty admitted students, together with the number of offers made on contextual grounds. Publication should be centralized in a single register rather than left to individual prospectuses. The department should also fund one longitudinal study of how applicants actually use such information, since the case for transparency currently rests more on principle than on evidence about behaviour.

title: A Private Habit Made Public
text:
Not long ago, few people outside research had heard of a preprint. A study posted directly to a public server, without review by other specialists, was an internal convenience: a way for colleagues to read work early and comment on it. Then such papers began appearing in news bulletins within hours of posting, and a habit developed inside the profession became a public instrument almost overnight.

The gains are real and should not be surrendered. Rapid posting allowed methods to be shared during an emergency in weeks rather than months, and mistakes were sometimes identified in public within a day. Speed of circulation is itself a scientific value when the question is urgent. Review by journals is slow, unpaid and unevenly performed; treating it as a guarantee of truth was always a comfortable fiction. Anyone who has seen a reviewed paper retracted knows the seal was never worth what readers assumed.

The difficulty lies not in posting but in translation. A preprint carries no signal a general reader can use, and the phrase 'not yet reviewed' does no work in a headline. Coverage therefore treats a first draft and a settled finding as equivalent claims, and the correction, when it comes, reaches a fraction of the original audience. A reader sees a study, a number and a headline, and very little else. Trust is spent at the moment of announcement and can only be repaid slowly.

Responsibility here is shared and mostly unclaimed, though servers could readily require a plain statement of what remains untested. Institutions could stop issuing press releases about work nobody outside the group has examined. Reporters could resist the verb 'shows' where 'suggests' would be accurate. None of that slows research by a single day; it merely stops a useful internal habit from being sold to the public as a finished product. None of these interventions imposes expenditure or requires additional institutional machinery.

press offices should stop announcing work nobody has examined

qs.evidence: None of that slows research by a single day; it merely stops a useful internal habit from being sold to the public as a finished product.
qs.answer: preprints help research but are poorly translated in public
qs.why: Penulis mempertahankan manfaat praktik itu di dalam riset dan mempersoalkan cara praktik itu dijual ke publik sebagai produk selesai.
qs.whyOthersFail: Soal tinjauan jurnal yang lambat dan tak seandal dugaan memang ditulis, tapi itu satu langkah dalam argumen, bukan pokoknya; usulan agar lembaga berhenti mengeluarkan rilis pers adalah satu dari beberapa saran di paragraf akhir; dan kehati-hatian jurnalis baru diusulkan, bukan sesuatu yang sudah terjadi.

qs: What does the essay say a preprint lacks?
a record of which specialists have commented on it
a marker of status that a lay reader can interpret
an audience large enough to notice a later correction
a server that can publish it within a few hours

qs.evidence: A preprint carries no signal a general reader can use, and the phrase 'not yet reviewed' does no work in a headline.
qs.answer: a marker of status that a lay reader can interpret
qs.why: Teks menyebut preprint nggak membawa penanda apa pun yang bisa dipakai pembaca umum, dan frasa 'belum ditinjau' tak bekerja di judul berita.
qs.whyOthersFail: Catatan siapa saja yang mengomentari memang bukan bagian dari preprint, tapi teks nggak pernah menyebutnya sebagai yang hilang; jangkauan koreksi adalah akibat di ranah pemberitaan, bukan sesuatu yang seharusnya ada di preprintnya; dan server cepat justru tersedia, itulah sebab makalah bisa terbit dalam hitungan jam.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards review by journals?
even-handed, treating it as slow but broadly reliable
grateful that it filters weak work before publication
unimpressed by the authority readers grant it
worried chiefly that reviewers are unpaid and overworked

qs.evidence: Anyone who has seen a reviewed paper retracted knows the seal was never worth what readers assumed.
qs.answer: unimpressed by the authority readers grant it
qs.why: Menyebut "the seal was never worth what readers assumed" berarti penulis meragukan wibawa yang diberikan pembaca pada tinjauan jurnal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penilaian 'lambat tapi cukup andal' hanya separuh benar, sebab keandalannya justru yang dibantah lewat contoh makalah tertinjau yang ditarik; rasa syukur pada penyaringan bertabrakan dengan kalimat yang sama; dan status tak dibayar disebut sebagai keterangan tentang mutu tinjauan, bukan keprihatinan utama penulis.

qs: What does the essay suggest about corrections issued after a story appears?
they reach much the same audience as the original claim
they are usually issued by the reporters who wrote the story
they rebuild trust faster than the announcement spent it
they arrive too late to reach most of the readers

qs.evidence: Coverage therefore treats a first draft and a settled finding as equivalent claims, and the correction, when it comes, reaches a fraction of the original audience.
qs.answer: they arrive too late to reach most of the readers
qs.why: Koreksi disebut hanya sampai ke sebagian kecil khalayak awal, jadi bagi kebanyakan pembaca ia datang terlambat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Khalayak yang sama persis kebalikan dari 'a fraction of the original audience'; siapa yang menerbitkan koreksi nggak pernah disebut, jadi penunjukan reporter tak berdasar; dan teks menyatakan kepercayaan hanya bisa dibayar kembali perlahan, bukan lebih cepat daripada saat ia dibelanjakan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer argues that posting papers before review should stop."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer argues that posting papers before review should stop.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: The gains are real and should not be surrendered.
qs.why: Penulis menyatakan keuntungan praktik itu nyata dan tak boleh dilepaskan, jadi klaim ini berlawanan dengan posisinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" bertabrakan dengan kalimat itu; "Not stated" salah karena sikapnya soal melanjutkan praktik itu dinyatakan langsung.

topic: preprints and the reporting of new research
author: Argumentative essay
setting: public servers, newsrooms and research institutions

title: The Number a Rule Chooses to Notice
text:
Complaints about railway noise are usually met with an average. The figure quoted, a level averaged across the whole day, is the measure written into most regulations, and by that measure many flats beside a busy line are comfortably compliant. Residents who cannot sleep are therefore told, in effect, that their experience is not the thing being measured. The reply is legally sound and beside the point.

Research on sleep disturbance suggests those residents are describing something the average conceals. A body asleep responds not to the mean level but to the change: the rise from a quiet background to the pass-by of a freight train. Recordings made in bedrooms show heart rate increases and brief awakenings that the sleeper never remembers. These events track the number of individual trains rather than the daily total of sound energy. Two lines with identical averages can therefore produce quite different nights.

The practical implications are unwelcome for planners. A freight service moved to the small hours to relieve daytime congestion improves the average while worsening exactly the events that matter. Barriers help, but chiefly for the upper floors they were never designed to shield. The most effective single measure, according to several studies, is maintenance: grinding the rail and truing the wheels reduce the sharp components of the sound that wake people. That work helps along the whole route, not at one screened point.

What follows is not that averages are useless, but that a rule written around one quantity will be defended in that quantity's terms. Until events during the night are counted, an operator can satisfy every requirement while a street sleeps badly. That is not a scientific difficulty, since the measurements exist and are not expensive; rather, regulatory metrics acquire an authority disproportionate to their original justification. The choice of measure is itself a policy, and it has been made already. It is a question of which number a rule chooses to notice.
qs: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the article?
noise barriers are the most effective measure now available
rail maintenance costs less than building any noise barrier
residents beside busy lines have little legal ground to complain
the regulated average misses what actually wakes people

qs.evidence: The choice of measure is itself a policy, and it has been made already.
qs.answer: the regulated average misses what actually wakes people
qs.why: Seluruh artikel menunjukkan aturan memilih angka yang salah: rata-rata harian melewatkan peristiwa yang sungguh membangunkan orang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penghalang justru disebut menolong terutama lantai atas yang tak dirancang untuk dilindunginya, sedangkan yang paling efektif adalah perawatan rel; perbandingan biaya antara perawatan dan penghalang nggak pernah dibuat; dan soal dasar hukum keluhan penghuni nggak dibahas, teks cuma menyebut jawaban operator sah secara hukum dan tak menjawab persoalannya.

qs: According to the research, what does a sleeping body react to?
the number of trains passing during the working day
the total sound energy accumulated across a day
each abrupt jump in loudness when a train goes past
the average level written into most regulations

qs.evidence: A body asleep responds not to the mean level but to the change: the rise from a quiet background to the pass-by of a freight train.
qs.answer: each abrupt jump in loudness when a train goes past
qs.why: Tubuh yang tidur disebut menanggapi perubahan, yaitu lonjakan dari latar sunyi ke suara kereta yang melintas.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jumlah kereta memang penting, tapi teks mengaitkannya dengan peristiwa terbangun pada malam, bukan lalu lintas siang; energi bunyi harian justru yang tidak dirasakan tubuh; dan rata-rata dalam regulasi adalah ukuran yang sedang dikritik.

qs: Which finding gives the strongest support for the claim that averages mislead?
barriers can help the floors they were not meant to shield
identical daily figures can hide very unequal nights
regulations are written around a level averaged over the day
grinding the rail reduces the sharp components of the sound

qs.evidence: Two lines with identical averages can therefore produce quite different nights.
qs.answer: identical daily figures can hide very unequal nights
qs.why: Dua jalur dengan rata-rata sama bisa menghasilkan malam yang sangat berbeda; itu bukti paling langsung bahwa rata-rata menyesatkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Soal penghalang dan penggerindaan rel adalah pilihan penanganan, bukan bukti tentang cacat rata-rata; dan fakta bahwa regulasi ditulis di sekitar angka rata-rata cuma menjelaskan asal masalahnya, bukan menunjukkan bahwa angkanya salah.

qs: What does the article imply about moving freight trains to the night?
it lowers both the average and the number of awakenings
it improves the figure while making sleep worse
it satisfies residents living on the upper floors
it removes the need for grinding rails and truing wheels

qs.evidence: A freight service moved to the small hours to relieve daytime congestion improves the average while worsening exactly the events that matter.
qs.answer: it improves the figure while making sleep worse
qs.why: Perpindahan angkutan barang ke dini hari memperbaiki angka rata-rata sekaligus memperburuk persis peristiwa yang membangunkan orang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penurunan pada kedua ukuran bertabrakan dengan kalimat itu, sebab peristiwa malam justru bertambah buruk; lantai atas dibahas dalam soal penghalang, tanpa kaitan dengan jam operasi; dan perawatan rel disebut sebagai tindakan paling efektif, jadi kebutuhannya tidak hilang.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Freight trains wake nearby residents more often than passenger trains do."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Freight trains wake nearby residents more often than passenger trains do.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: These events track the number of individual trains rather than the daily total of sound energy.
qs.why: Kalimat terdekat cuma menghubungkan terbangun dengan jumlah kereta; perbandingan antara kereta barang dan kereta penumpang nggak pernah dibuat.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" butuh perbandingan yang nggak ada di teks; "False" juga salah karena teks nggak menyangkal perbandingan itu.

topic: railway noise and how it is measured
author: Applied acoustics feature
setting: flats beside a busy freight line

title: The Room and the Recording
text:
Three years after lecture halls reopened, attendance in many departments has not recovered, and the recorded lecture is the usual suspect. Two heads of department, in the same university and looking at the same figures, draw opposite conclusions. Their disagreement is worth following, because each is arguing from something real. The disagreement concerns interpretation rather than arithmetic: what an attendance figure is presumed to represent.

The first sees a straightforward matter of access. Her cohort includes students working two evening shifts, students caring for relatives, and students commuting ninety minutes each way. For them a recording is not an alternative to attending; it is the difference between studying and withdrawing. Attendance figures, she adds, were never a measure of learning but a measure of presence, and nobody has yet shown that students watching later perform worse. Her argument is one of proportionality: a policy defended as protection should not fall hardest on those with the least discretion over their own time.

Her colleague accepts every word of that and reaches a different conclusion. What has quietly disappeared, he argues, is the room: the question asked badly and answered patiently, the argument overheard between two students on the stairs. A recording preserves the content and discards the encounter, and first-year students in particular do not know what they are missing. He notes that those most likely to watch alone are the ones already least connected to the department. His objection is developmental rather than administrative, since incidental exchanges accumulate into a sense of belonging that no recording transmits.

Both accounts rest on evidence chosen to fit the expectation each observer brought to it. The honest conclusion is that recordings redistribute something rather than simply adding it: they widen access to information while narrowing access to the incidental. A department that records everything and changes nothing else has made a choice without admitting it. So has one that refuses to record and calls the result community. Institutional honesty, on this reading, demands an explicit justification rather than an inherited arrangement.
qs: Which best captures the writer's own conclusion?
attendance figures were never a measure of learning
recordings trade one kind of access for another
departments ought to record every lecture as a matter of fairness
first-year students learn less from recordings than others do

qs.evidence: The honest conclusion is that recordings redistribute something rather than simply adding it: they widen access to information while narrowing access to the incidental.
qs.answer: recordings trade one kind of access for another
qs.why: Penulis menyimpulkan rekaman memindahkan sesuatu: akses ke informasi melebar, akses ke hal tak terjadwal menyempit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalimat bahwa angka kehadiran bukan ukuran belajar adalah argumen kepala jurusan pertama, bukan kesimpulan penulis; kewajiban merekam semua kuliah justru dikritik lewat contoh jurusan yang merekam segalanya tanpa mengubah apa pun; dan soal mahasiswa tahun pertama, teks hanya menyebut mereka tak tahu apa yang mereka lewatkan, tanpa klaim tentang hasil belajarnya.

qs: Which students does the first head of department describe?
students already least connected to the department
students who prefer to study in their own time
students who have withdrawn from the course
students with jobs, caring duties or long journeys

qs.evidence: Her cohort includes students working two evening shifts, students caring for relatives, and students commuting ninety minutes each way.
qs.answer: students with jobs, caring duties or long journeys
qs.why: Dia menyebut mahasiswa dengan dua sif malam, yang merawat keluarga, dan yang menempuh sembilan puluh menit sekali jalan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Mahasiswa yang paling tak terhubung adalah kelompok yang diamati kepala jurusan kedua, bukan dia; pilihan belajar di waktu sendiri nggak pernah jadi alasannya, karena argumennya soal keterbatasan waktu bukan selera; dan penarikan diri disebut sebagai risiko yang ingin dicegah, bukan keadaan mahasiswanya sekarang.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards the two positions?
even-handed, yet critical of departments that drift
persuaded that the second colleague has the better case
impatient with both for arguing past the evidence
optimistic that attendance will recover on its own

qs.evidence: A department that records everything and changes nothing else has made a choice without admitting it.
qs.answer: even-handed, yet critical of departments that drift
qs.why: Penulis menerima kedua argumen, lalu menegur jurusan yang membiarkan keadaan berjalan tanpa mengakui pilihannya sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keberpihakan pada kepala jurusan kedua nggak ada, sebab jurusan yang menolak merekam pun disebut sedang memilih tanpa mengakuinya; kejengkelan pada keduanya bertabrakan dengan kalimat bahwa masing-masing berargumen dari sesuatu yang nyata; dan pemulihan kehadiran dengan sendirinya nggak pernah diramalkan, malah disebut belum pulih setelah tiga tahun.

qs: What does the writer imply about a department that refuses to record lectures?
it has protected the incidental exchanges its students value
it is likely to see attendance return to earlier levels
it is also making a choice it prefers not to name
it follows the available evidence more closely than others

qs.evidence: So has one that refuses to record and calls the result community.
qs.answer: it is also making a choice it prefers not to name
qs.why: Frasa "so has" menempatkan jurusan penolak rekaman dalam posisi sama: memilih tanpa mengakui pilihannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks menyebut jurusan itu menamai hasilnya 'komunitas', bukan bahwa pertemuan tak terjadwal benar-benar terselamatkan; kembalinya angka kehadiran nggak dijanjikan di mana pun; dan penolakan merekam nggak digambarkan lebih berdasar bukti, sebab kedua pihak dinilai memilih bukti yang cocok dengan harapan masing-masing.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The second head of department agrees with his colleague's account of student circumstances."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The second head of department agrees with his colleague's account of student circumstances.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Her colleague accepts every word of that and reaches a different conclusion.
qs.why: "Accepts every word of that" sama artinya dengan menyetujui gambaran keadaan mahasiswa yang disampaikan rekannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena persetujuan itu tertulis; "Not stated" salah karena kalimatnya ada, cuma diucapkan dengan kata lain.

author: Campus debate feature
setting: one university, two heads of department

title: What the Feed Is Told to Want
text:
Debate about teenagers and recommendation feeds has settled into an unproductive pattern. One side describes an addiction; the other observes that every generation has been accused of ruining itself with a new medium. Both formulations obscure the mechanism, which is neither mysterious nor especially contested. A feed is an optimization process, and what it optimizes is measured in seconds of attention. It is worth saying plainly what such a system does, because everything else in the argument depends on that one point.

The consequence is not that harmful material is deliberately promoted. It is that content producing an intense reaction outperforms content producing a mild one, and intensity is easier to manufacture than quality. A recommendation system therefore drifts towards the extreme end of whatever category a user has already touched, because that is where the seconds accumulate. Nobody designed this outcome; it follows from the objective. An engineer optimizing for duration is doing the job as specified.

Age matters here, and not for sentimental reasons: adolescents are more sensitive to social comparison and to signals of exclusion, so a feed sorted by reaction assembles the material likeliest to unsettle them. Regulators have responded with age verification, which governs who is admitted rather than what is then served. A gate answers the wrong question, since the difficulty begins after entry. The teenager who passes the check meets exactly the system that prompted the concern. A young person told to look away will very often go back and find the same clip again.

The remedy that follows is unglamorous and technically undemanding. Require that feeds for accounts registered to minors be optimized for something other than duration, and require the chosen objective to be published. Firms will reply that such an aim is impossible to specify, yet they specify comparable objectives every quarter, in language precise enough to pay bonuses on. The impossibility is not technical; it is commercial, and it should be named as such. The point is not that these firms are wicked, only that nobody else has been asked to choose the aim.
qs: Which statement best expresses the central argument of the essay?
the harm follows from what feeds are told to maximize
age checks govern who is admitted rather than what is served
adolescents are more sensitive to signals of exclusion
harmful material is deliberately promoted to teenagers

qs.evidence: Nobody designed this outcome; it follows from the objective.
qs.answer: the harm follows from what feeds are told to maximize
qs.why: Penulis menegaskan hasil buruk itu lahir dari sasaran yang diberikan pada sistem, bukan dari niat siapa pun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Soal gerbang umur yang cuma mengatur siapa yang masuk memang benar menurut teks, tapi itu satu langkah dalam argumen, bukan pokoknya; kepekaan remaja pada tanda pengucilan juga benar dan tetap berupa satu penjelas mengapa umur penting; sedangkan promosi sengaja materi berbahaya dibantah langsung di awal paragraf kedua.

qs: What does the essay say a feed is optimized for?
the material a user is most likely to pass on to friends
the intensity a producer of content intended to create
the number of seconds a user keeps watching
the age recorded on the account at registration

qs.evidence: A feed is an optimization process, and what it optimizes is measured in seconds of attention.
qs.answer: the number of seconds a user keeps watching
qs.why: Teks menyebut yang dioptimalkan diukur dalam detik perhatian, jadi lamanya orang terus menonton.
qs.whyOthersFail: Berbagi ke teman masuk akal sebagai sasaran sistem semacam ini, tapi teks nggak pernah menyebutnya; intensitas disebut sebagai sifat konten yang menang dalam persaingan, bukan besaran yang dioptimalkan; dan umur di akun cuma urusan gerbang masuk yang menurut teks menjawab pertanyaan yang salah.

qs: How does the writer regard the claim that such an objective cannot be specified?
sympathetic, since specifying such an aim is genuinely hard
undecided, because the technical evidence is incomplete
patient, willing to let firms propose their own objective
dismissive, treating the claim as self-serving

qs.evidence: The impossibility is not technical; it is commercial, and it should be named as such.
qs.answer: dismissive, treating the claim as self-serving
qs.why: Menyebut kemustahilan itu bersifat komersial dan bukan teknis berarti penulis menganggap alasan perusahaan sebagai pembelaan kepentingan sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Simpati pada kesulitan mendefinisikan sasaran bertabrakan dengan pengingat bahwa firma menetapkan sasaran serupa setiap kuartal dengan bahasa yang cukup tepat untuk membayar bonus; sikap belum memutuskan juga nggak cocok, karena mekanismenya disebut tidak diperdebatkan; dan kesabaran menunggu usulan firma bertentangan dengan tuntutan agar sasaran itu diwajibkan dan diterbitkan.

qs: What does the essay imply about age verification?
it tends to work better for younger users than for older ones
it weakens the incentive to maximize attention
it was proposed by the firms as a cheaper remedy
it controls entry while leaving the feed untouched

qs.evidence: A gate answers the wrong question, since the difficulty begins after entry.
qs.answer: it controls entry while leaving the feed untouched
qs.why: Gerbang hanya mengatur siapa yang boleh masuk, sedangkan sistem yang jadi persoalan tetap sama begitu pintunya terlewati.
qs.whyOthersFail: Perbandingan hasil untuk pengguna muda dan tua nggak pernah dibuat; insentif durasi disebut tetap utuh karena kesulitannya mulai setelah orang masuk; dan verifikasi umur digambarkan sebagai jawaban regulator, bukan usulan perusahaan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The essay says platforms promote harmful material on purpose."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The essay says platforms promote harmful material on purpose.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: The consequence is not that harmful material is deliberately promoted.
qs.why: Teks membantah langsung: materi berbahaya bukan dipromosikan dengan sengaja.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" berlawanan dengan kalimat itu; "Not stated" salah karena bantahannya tertulis di awal paragraf kedua.

author: Argumentative essay
setting: public argument about platform regulation

title: The Form Decides First
text:
Economists once treated the decision to save as a straightforward calculation. A worker weighed present consumption against future security, and whatever choice emerged was assumed to reveal a preference. Then employers began altering one apparently trivial detail: whether joining a pension scheme required a signature to opt in or a signature to opt out. Participation shifted by tens of percentage points, and the tidy account of preference has never fully recovered.

The finding has since been replicated across countries, sectors and income levels. The effect shows up in firms of every size, and it does not fade after the first year. What changes is not the underlying wish to save but the effort required to act upon it. A default carries three things at once: it removes a decision, it signals what the employer considers normal, and it supplies an excuse for postponement in the opposite direction. Any one of the three would move behaviour; together they move it a long way.

This is not simply a convenient discovery for policy. A default set carelessly can be as consequential as one set well, and the contribution rate accompanying automatic enrolment is frequently minimal. Workers enrolled at three per cent often remain at three per cent for a decade, treating the figure as advice rather than a floor. A number printed on a form quietly turns into a piece of advice. Inertia is indifferent to direction; it holds people wherever they have been placed, and the mechanism that raised participation also freezes the amount.

The practical lesson is uncomfortable for anyone who dislikes interference. There is no arrangement without a default, because somebody must determine what happens when nothing is determined. The question is therefore not whether to nudge, but who selects the resting position and how visibly that selection is made. Silence in the design is still a decision, taken by whoever drew up the form.
qs: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the article?
workers enrolled at a low rate tend to stay there
automatic enrolment tends to raise contribution rates
defaults shape saving more than preference does
a saving decision reveals how much a worker values the future

qs.evidence: Participation shifted by tens of percentage points, and the tidy account of preference has never fully recovered.
qs.answer: defaults shape saving more than preference does
qs.why: Perubahan kecil pada formulir menggeser partisipasi puluhan poin, sehingga pengaturan bawaan lebih menentukan daripada selera menabung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pekerja yang mandek di angka rendah memang benar menurut teks, tapi itu satu akibat yang dipakai untuk memperingatkan soal besaran, bukan gagasan pokoknya; kenaikan iuran justru dibantah, karena kelambanan menahan orang di tempat mereka diletakkan; dan gagasan bahwa pilihan menabung mengungkap selera adalah pandangan lama yang dirobohkan di paragraf pertama.

qs: Besides removing a decision, what does the article say a default supplies?
a record of what the worker has chosen before
a contribution rate agreed with the worker in advance
a signal of what the employer treats as normal
a replication of the finding across countries and sectors

qs.evidence: A default carries three things at once: it removes a decision, it signals what the employer considers normal, and it supplies an excuse for postponement in the opposite direction.
qs.answer: a signal of what the employer treats as normal
qs.why: Salah satu dari tiga hal yang dibawa pengaturan bawaan adalah isyarat tentang apa yang dianggap wajar oleh pemberi kerja.
qs.whyOthersFail: Catatan pilihan sebelumnya nggak pernah disebut sebagai bagian pengaturan bawaan; iuran yang disepakati lebih dulu bertabrakan dengan gambaran pekerja yang menerima angka apa pun yang tercetak di formulir; dan replikasi antarnegara adalah status temuannya, bukan isi pengaturannya.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards automatic enrolment as it is currently set?
approving of the design but wary of the low rate
convinced that such defaults interfere with free choice
confident that workers adjust the figure once enrolled
even-handed, since three per cent suits many workers well

qs.evidence: Workers enrolled at three per cent often remain at three per cent for a decade, treating the figure as advice rather than a floor.
qs.answer: approving of the design but wary of the low rate
qs.why: Penulis memuji mekanismenya namun mengkhawatirkan besaran iuran yang bisa mandek satu dasawarsa.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tuduhan campur tangan bertabrakan dengan kalimat bahwa tak ada susunan tanpa pengaturan bawaan, jadi pilihannya cuma siapa yang menetapkannya; keyakinan bahwa pekerja menyesuaikan angka dibantah oleh contoh tiga persen selama sepuluh tahun; dan penilaian bahwa angka itu cocok untuk banyak orang nggak didukung, sebab teks menyebutnya sering minimal.

qs: What does the article imply about a scheme designed with no default at all?
it would reveal preferences more accurately than a default
it is not possible, since inaction needs a rule
it would raise participation in firms of every size
it has already been tried in several countries and sectors

qs.evidence: There is no arrangement without a default, because somebody must determine what happens when nothing is determined.
qs.answer: it is not possible, since inaction needs a rule
qs.why: Kalau tak ada yang memutuskan, tetap harus ada ketentuan tentang apa yang terjadi saat tidak ada keputusan, jadi skema tanpa pengaturan bawaan mustahil.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketepatan mengungkap selera justru diragukan sejak paragraf pertama; kenaikan partisipasi di firma segala ukuran adalah akibat dari adanya pengaturan bawaan opt-out, bukan dari ketiadaannya; dan pengujian antarnegara menyangkut temuan opt-in versus opt-out, bukan skema tanpa pengaturan bawaan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The move to opt-out enrolment was first proposed by government economists."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The move to opt-out enrolment was first proposed by government economists.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Then employers began altering one apparently trivial detail: whether joining a pension scheme required a signature to opt in or a signature to opt out.
qs.why: Teks cuma bilang pemberi kerja mulai mengubah detail itu; siapa yang pertama mengusulkannya nggak pernah disebut.

title: Review of the Rooftop Solar Grant
text:
This report reviews the rooftop solar grant after four years of operation. The scheme has funded some nineteen thousand installations, exceeded its capacity target and remained within budget. It has also delivered a distribution of benefit that the council did not intend and cannot easily defend. The failure is worth setting out precisely, because it is not a failure of administration. The point of this review is to say where the money has actually gone.

The design itself produces the pattern. The grant covers forty per cent of installation cost, which leaves an applicant to raise the remaining sixty, and it is paid in arrears against a receipt. Households able to advance several thousand pounds and wait eleven weeks for reimbursement are, predictably, not the households by which the scheme was justified. Applications from the four wards with the lowest median income account for under seven per cent of the total.

Tenants are excluded almost entirely, for a reason nobody has yet addressed. A tenant cannot fit a panel to a roof that belongs to somebody else. A grant towards a roof requires an owner, and the owner of a rented roof captures the asset while the tenant pays the bill. Two neighbouring authorities have piloted split arrangements under which the landlord receives the grant on condition that a share of the saving is passed through. The monitoring obligations of such schemes, however, are far from trivial.

None of the changes below needs new money, only a different order of payment; we recommend three amendments. First, replace reimbursement with direct payment to the installer, so that no applicant requires capital. Second, reserve a fifth of the annual allocation for the four lowest-income wards, and permit that portion to fund a larger share of cost. Third, commission an assessment of the split arrangements before extending them here, since the passed-through saving in both pilots remains unverified. Without the first amendment, the remaining two will change very little.
qs: What is the main purpose of this report?
to record that the scheme met its target within budget
to reform a grant that is reaching the wrong households
to propose that landlords receive the grant for rented roofs
to recommend closing the grant before its fifth year

qs.evidence: It has also delivered a distribution of benefit that the council did not intend and cannot easily defend.
qs.answer: to reform a grant that is reaching the wrong households
qs.why: Laporan mengakui sasaran kapasitas tercapai lalu menunjukkan manfaatnya salah sasaran, dan menutup dengan tiga usulan perbaikan.

title: The Hour That Is Counted
text:
Most undergraduate seminars in this country are taught by postgraduates, and most of those postgraduates are paid by the contact hour. The arrangement is defended as flexible, a word performing a great deal of concealment. What it means in practice is that the university purchases the visible portion of teaching and receives the remainder as a gift. The distinction between compensated and uncompensated labour is obscured, conveniently, by an accounting unit that registers only presence.

Consider what a single seminar genuinely requires. Reading the set text takes an hour if it is familiar and three if it is not; devising questions that survive contact with twenty students takes another. The marking, the message at eleven at night and the student who is plainly unwell all fall outside the counted hour. Departments understand this, which is why contracts frequently specify a preparation multiplier. The multiplier is typically two, and the honest figure is nearer four. An institution that specifies any multiplier has conceded the principle and merely disputes the magnitude.

The defence offered is that this constitutes training, and training is partly its own reward; there is something in the argument, yet it collapses under inspection. Training implies observation, feedback and a reduction in load while competence is built, and few of these appear on any timetable. What is actually being trained is a tolerance for unpaid work, on which the sector will then draw for decades.

The remedy is not complicated, merely expensive. Pay for the work the work demands: count preparation honestly, pay marking by the script rather than by the hour, and cap the number of students per seminar so that the two remain compatible. Departments will reply that budgets do not permit it. Budgets have permitted the present arrangement precisely because somebody else has been absorbing the difference. Moving the shortfall around, rather than removing it, has been the working policy throughout.
qs: Which best captures the central argument of the essay?
the preparation multiplier written into contracts is too low
seminars ought to be capped at a smaller number of students
hourly pay quietly transfers costs onto teachers
seminar teaching is best understood as paid training

qs.evidence: What it means in practice is that the university purchases the visible portion of teaching and receives the remainder as a gift.
qs.answer: hourly pay quietly transfers costs onto teachers
qs.why: Universitas hanya membeli bagian pengajaran yang terlihat dan menerima sisanya sebagai hadiah, jadi biayanya berpindah ke pengajar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pengali persiapan yang terlalu rendah memang pernyataan teks, tapi itu satu bukti dari klaim yang lebih besar; pembatasan jumlah mahasiswa per seminar adalah salah satu usulan di paragraf akhir; dan gagasan bahwa ini pelatihan berbayar justru pembelaan yang disebut runtuh begitu diperiksa.

it is set at half of what the work truly takes

qs.answer: it is set at half of what the work truly takes

title: Half the Story of a Flood
text:
Flood warnings in cities have traditionally been issued on rainfall alone. A forecast of forty millimetres in an hour triggers an alert, and the alert is the same whether the preceding fortnight has been wet or dry. Anyone who has watched water stand on one street and disappear from the next knows the rainfall figure is only half the story. An alert insensitive to antecedent conditions rapidly forfeits its credibility with residents.

The other half is whatever the ground can still absorb. Soil that has already taken up water behaves, for the purposes of a storm, much like paving: almost nothing soaks in. Networks of inexpensive buried sensors now report moisture continuously, and combining those readings with the forecast improves the prediction of surface water substantially. In one catchment the number of false alerts fell by half without any warning being missed. The ground, in other words, keeps a record of the weeks before the storm.

Two complications prevent this from being straightforward. Urban soil is extraordinarily variable, since a century of building leaves rubble beneath one garden and clay beneath the next, so a sensor speaks only for a small area around itself. Sensors also fail quietly, drifting rather than stopping, which is harder to detect than an outright breakdown. A network therefore requires redundancy and routine inspection, neither of which appears in the price of the hardware. Someone has to go out and look at the kit from time to time.

None of this makes the approach a poor investment, but it alters what is being bought. A moisture network is a maintenance commitment rather than a purchase, and the value appears only where warnings are actually acted upon. Cities that install the sensors and leave the response plan untouched have bought a better forecast of a flood they will handle exactly as before. A better number is only worth as much as the city does with it.
qs: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the article?
a moisture network is a commitment to maintenance
urban soil varies too much for sensors to be useful
ground moisture readings sharpen flood warnings
buried sensors have taken the place of rainfall forecasts

qs.evidence: A moisture network is a maintenance commitment rather than a purchase, and the value appears only where warnings are actually acted upon.
qs.answer: ground moisture readings sharpen flood warnings
qs.why: Artikel menunjukkan bacaan kelembapan tanah memperbaiki peringatan banjir, dengan syarat jaringannya dirawat dan hasilnya dipakai.
qs.whyOthersFail: Soal komitmen perawatan memang ditulis di paragraf akhir, tapi itu syarat yang menyertai manfaatnya, bukan pokok artikel; keragaman tanah disebut sebagai komplikasi yang dijawab dengan cadangan dan pemeriksaan, bukan alasan sensor tak berguna; dan sensor digambarkan digabungkan dengan ramalan hujan, bukan menggantikannya.

qs: What happens to soil that is already wet when a storm arrives?
it dries more slowly than the paving beside it
it takes up more water than dry soil does
almost none of the rain soaks in, so it runs off
it makes the buried sensors drift out of calibration

qs.evidence: Soil that has already taken up water behaves, for the purposes of a storm, much like paving: almost nothing soaks in.
qs.answer: almost none of the rain soaks in, so it runs off
qs.why: Tanah yang sudah menyerap air berlaku seperti perkerasan saat badai datang: hampir tak ada air yang masuk.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kecepatan mengering dibanding perkerasan nggak pernah dibahas; daya serap yang lebih besar justru kebalikan dari kalimat itu; dan penyimpangan sensor disebut sebagai cacat perangkat yang muncul sendiri, tanpa kaitan dengan tanah yang basah.

qs: Which result gives the strongest support for the value of a sensor network?
moisture readings are reported without interruption
one area halved its needless alarms and missed none

qs.evidence: In one catchment the number of false alerts fell by half without any warning being missed.
qs.answer: one area halved its needless alarms and missed none
qs.why: Satu daerah tangkapan air memotong separuh peringatan palsu tanpa melewatkan satu peringatan sungguhan; itu bukti manfaat paling langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pelaporan tanpa henti cuma menjelaskan cara kerja alatnya; sedangkan keragaman tanah dan penyimpangan bacaan adalah dua komplikasi yang justru mengurangi nilai jaringan, bukan mendukungnya.

qs: What does the article imply about a city that installs sensors but changes nothing else?

qs.evidence: Cities that install the sensors and leave the response plan untouched have bought a better forecast of a flood they will handle exactly as before.
qs.answer: it gains a sharper forecast and no better outcome
qs.why: Kota seperti itu membeli ramalan yang lebih baik untuk banjir yang akan ditangani persis seperti sebelumnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak menyebut peringatan jadi lebih sering terlewat; biaya pemeriksaan rutin tetap harus dibayar karena tidak termasuk harga perangkat; dan kebutuhan cadangan sensor justru disebut melekat pada jaringan mana pun.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Sensors also fail quietly, drifting rather than stopping, which is harder to detect than an outright breakdown.
qs.why: "Drifting rather than stopping" berarti bacaannya menyimpang perlahan, dan teks menyebut itu lebih sulit dideteksi.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena isinya sejalan dengan teks; "Not stated" salah karena sifat kegagalan sensor dijelaskan di paragraf ketiga.
