True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Money from the repair fund would be handed over once inspection had taken place.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: First, a repair fund covering half the cost of structural timber work, released after inspection rather than on production of receipts.
qs.why: Dana memang dilepas setelah pemeriksaan, bukan setelah kuitansi disetor; klaim ini sepadan.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena mekanismenya sama; "Not stated" salah karena syarat pencairan itu ditulis di usulan pertama.

topic: Policy options for decaying wooden shophouses in a district
author: A district planning officer preparing advice for councillors
setting: Written review submitted to a district heritage committee

title: The Number on the Wall
text:
Every newsroom now has a screen on the wall. It displays which stories are being read, for how long, and from which platform, and the figures update every few seconds. Nobody in the trade would argue for less information. What deserves an argument is the quiet promotion of a single quantity, the click, into a standard of editorial worth, a substitution which is rarely announced and almost never debated. A measure devised many years ago to price advertising space has been asked to adjudicate what matters.

The distortion is never dramatic, and it is cumulative. A reporter who has spent three weeks on a municipal water contract watches her piece fall below a list of holiday destinations within the hour. Nothing was censored and no instruction was issued; the lesson simply arrives that demanding subjects, however necessary, cost more and return less. Repeated across a year of such comparisons, the incentive reshapes commissioning without ever appearing in the minutes of a meeting. Institutional drift of this kind is difficult to detect and harder still to reverse.

Defenders of the dashboard have a case worth hearing. Editorial instinct has protected a great deal of dull, self-important journalism that nobody wanted to read, and audience data punctures that comfort usefully. The difficulty lies not in measurement itself but in the selection of what gets measured. Attention is cheap to quantify, whereas consequence is not, and a council which cancelled a procurement after one article leaves no residue on any chart. The visible proxy therefore displaces the invisible purpose.

A better arrangement exists, and it is unglamorous. Newsrooms can record outcomes alongside traffic: documents obtained, decisions reversed, corrections extracted from an agency. Such an inventory is slower to compile and considerably harder to explain to an advertiser, yet it also describes what a newsroom is actually for. Until that second column exists, the screen on the wall will go on telling editors that the cheapest story is the best one available.
qs: Which statement best expresses the writer's argument?
Newsrooms rely on audience data less than editors like to admit.
Readers prefer travel writing to reports on municipal spending.
One easily counted number has quietly become a test of editorial value.
Advertisers now decide directly what a newsroom will commission.

qs.evidence: What deserves an argument is the quiet promotion of a single quantity, the click, into a standard of editorial worth, a substitution which is rarely announced and almost never debated.
qs.answer: One easily counted number has quietly become a test of editorial value.
qs.why: Inti tulisannya: satu angka yang mudah dihitung naik pangkat jadi ukuran mutu redaksi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi redaksi kurang bergantung pada data membalik gambaran teks, yang menaruh layar angka di setiap ruang redaksi dan menyebut pengaruhnya menumpuk. Opsi selera pembaca boleh saja benar di dunia, tapi di teks perbandingan wisata versus kontrak air cuma contoh mekanismenya, bukan pokok soalnya. Opsi pengiklan mengambil alih terlalu jauh, karena teks menegaskan “Nothing was censored and no instruction was issued”.

qs: What happens to the reporter's water contract story, according to the essay?
It is taken off the site after advertisers have complained.
It is rewritten by the desk to attract a larger audience.
It holds a longer reading time than the holiday pieces do.
It slips beneath a set of travel items in under sixty minutes.

qs.evidence: A reporter who has spent three weeks on a municipal water contract watches her piece fall below a list of holiday destinations within the hour.
qs.answer: It slips beneath a set of travel items in under sixty minutes.
qs.why: Dalam satu jam, tulisan hasil tiga minggu itu sudah melorot di bawah daftar tujuan wisata.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi ditarik karena pengiklan mengeluh diblokir kalimat bahwa nggak ada yang disensor dan nggak ada instruksi turun. Opsi ditulis ulang menambah campur tangan meja redaksi yang nggak ada; yang terjadi cuma peringkatnya jatuh. Opsi waktu baca lebih lama membalik hasilnya, sebab tulisan itu justru kalah dari daftar tujuan wisata.

qs: How would you describe the writer's stance towards audience data?
Grateful that the screen has settled an old editorial quarrel
Ready to grant its usefulness while disputing what it is used for
Confident that editors judge a story better than any figure can
Untroubled by which quantity a newsroom chooses to put on the wall

qs.evidence: Editorial instinct has protected a great deal of dull, self-important journalism that nobody wanted to read, and audience data punctures that comfort usefully.
qs.answer: Ready to grant its usefulness while disputing what it is used for
qs.why: Penulis mengakui data pembaca berguna menusuk kenyamanan redaksi, tapi mempersoalkan apa yang diukur.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi bersyukur soalnya selesai bertabrakan dengan seluruh keluhan penulis bahwa penggantian ukuran itu “rarely announced and almost never debated”. Opsi yakin insting redaksi lebih baik mengabaikan pengakuannya bahwa data pembaca menusuk jurnalisme yang membosankan dengan berguna. Opsi tidak peduli persis kebalikan dari tulisan yang seluruhnya mempersoalkan kuantitas mana yang dipilih.

qs: What does the writer imply by asking for a second column of records?
Effects that are hard to count will otherwise be treated as worthless.
Newsrooms ought to publish their traffic figures for readers to see.
Advertisers would pay rather more if outcomes were reported to them monthly.
Corrections extracted from an agency show a desk has been careless.

qs.evidence: Attention is cheap to quantify, whereas consequence is not, and a council which cancelled a procurement after one article leaves no residue on any chart.
qs.answer: Effects that are hard to count will otherwise be treated as worthless.
qs.why: Kalau akibat nyata tidak pernah tercatat, ia otomatis dianggap tak bernilai dibanding klik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menerbitkan angka lalu lintas mengubah soalnya jadi keterbukaan pada pembaca, padahal keluhannya soal apa yang dihitung. Opsi pengiklan membayar lebih dibalik teks sendiri, yang bilang daftar hasil justru “harder to explain to an advertiser”. Opsi koreksi sebagai tanda kelalaian membalik nilainya, karena koreksi yang dicabut dari sebuah lembaga dihitung teks sebagai prestasi redaksi.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The essay says the shift in what a desk commissions is written into the minutes of its meetings."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The essay says the shift in what a desk commissions is written into the minutes of its meetings.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Repeated across a year of such comparisons, the incentive reshapes commissioning without ever appearing in the minutes of a meeting.
qs.why: Teks justru bilang pergeseran itu tidak pernah muncul di notulen rapat mana pun, jadi klaimnya dibalik.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena bertentangan dengan kalimatnya; "Not stated" salah karena soal notulen memang dibahas.

topic: Audience metrics and editorial judgement in newsrooms
author: A former news editor writing about newsroom practice
setting: Media comment essay in a journalism review

title: Print the Mistake Where It Happened
text:
A correction is the only part of a newspaper which concedes that the rest of it may be wrong. Most titles bury it: six lines appear at the foot of an inside page, several days after the error, in type smaller than the advertisements surrounding them. The reasoning is easy to follow, since visible mistakes are assumed to signal incompetence. Editors treat concealment as a form of damage limitation, though the calculation rests on an assumption about readers that nobody in the building has ever tested. The assumption is also backwards, and the evidence from reader surveys does not support it.

Readers do not expect a newsroom to be infallible, because nobody who has worked to a deadline believes such a condition is attainable. What they monitor is the conduct which follows an error. A paper that corrects promptly, in the same position and at the same size as the original claim, is making a promise capable of verification. Trust of that kind survives a mistake; trust constructed on silence does not survive discovery, and its collapse is rarely gradual.

The objection inside the building is practical rather than principled. Prominent corrections, editors argue, invite complaints from people whose sole purpose is to exhaust the desk, and that does happen. It is also manageable, because a published policy on what constitutes an error, and on who adjudicates, disposes of most vexatious claims in a single paragraph. Complaint volume is a management problem rather than an argument of principle, and it should not determine where a newspaper places its acknowledgement of error. The administrative cost amounts to a few hours of somebody's week.

There is a further gain, and it is internal. A desk which knows its errors will be advertised verifies differently before publication. The resulting discipline is visible throughout the copy, not merely in the disputed paragraphs. Institutional habit, not individual conscientiousness, determines how frequently a newspaper must apologize. Corrections logged where readers can find them also confer an advantage that competitors cannot claim without undertaking the same work. A newspaper which conceals its errors is asking to be believed. One which prints them is supplying a reason.
qs: What is the writer's main purpose in this piece?
To describe the page layout most newspapers use for corrections
To argue that corrections should appear as visibly as the error did
To explain how tight deadlines make some errors in reporting unavoidable
To warn readers that complaints against newspapers seldom succeed

qs.evidence: A paper that corrects promptly, in the same position and at the same size as the original claim, is making a promise capable of verification.
qs.answer: To argue that corrections should appear as visibly as the error did
qs.why: Penulis mendorong koreksi tampil di tempat dan ukuran yang sama dengan klaim aslinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menjelaskan tata letak memakai gambaran pembuka sebagai tujuan; enam baris di halaman dalam justru praktik yang dikritik. Opsi soal tenggat memang disebut sekali untuk menjelaskan kenapa pembaca tak menuntut kesempurnaan, bukan sebagai maksud tulisan. Opsi keluhan jarang berhasil nggak pernah diklaim teks; yang dibahas adalah cara mengelola keluhan lewat kebijakan terbit.

qs: According to the piece, how are corrections usually presented?
as a paragraph on the front page written by the editor in charge
as a letter from a reader printed beside the original article
as a short notice in small type on an inside page, days later
as a note in the same position and size as the disputed claim

qs.evidence: six lines appear at the foot of an inside page, several days after the error, in type smaller than the advertisements surrounding them.
qs.answer: as a short notice in small type on an inside page, days later
qs.why: Enam baris di kaki halaman dalam, beberapa hari kemudian, dengan huruf lebih kecil dari iklan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi paragraf di halaman depan itu keadaan yang penulis inginkan, bukan kebiasaan yang dia gambarkan. Opsi surat pembaca menambah bentuk yang nggak pernah disebut teks. Opsi posisi dan ukuran sama persis usulan penulis di paragraf dua, jadi ia menukar cita-cita dengan praktik sekarang.

qs: Which point is offered as evidence that the complaints problem can be handled?
A stated rule on errors and decisions settles most bad-faith claims.
Readers already accept that no newsroom can avoid every mistake.
Corrections give a title an edge over rivals who avoid the work.
Checking before publication improves the quality of the writing.

qs.evidence: It is also manageable, because a published policy on what constitutes an error, and on who adjudicates, disposes of most vexatious claims in a single paragraph.
qs.answer: A stated rule on errors and decisions settles most bad-faith claims.
qs.why: Buktinya: kebijakan terbit soal apa yang dihitung keliru dan siapa yang memutuskan menutup keluhan iseng.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pembaca sudah menerima kekeliruan menjawab keberatan lain, yaitu soal apakah kesalahan merusak kepercayaan. Opsi keunggulan atas pesaing datang dari paragraf terakhir soal manfaat jangka panjang, bukan soal menangani keluhan. Opsi pemeriksaan sebelum terbit adalah keuntungan internal yang muncul setelah kebijakan jalan, bukan alasan bahwa keluhan bisa diurus.

qs: Which statement best paraphrases the closing contrast?
Hiding errors demands faith, whereas printing them supplies grounds.
Printing errors matters less to readers than most editors imagine.
A paper should hide small errors and print only the serious ones.
Readers trust a paper that never has to correct itself at all.

qs.evidence: A newspaper which conceals its errors is asking to be believed. One which prints them is supplying a reason.
qs.answer: Hiding errors demands faith, whereas printing them supplies grounds.
qs.why: Menyembunyikan kesalahan hanya meminta dipercaya; menerbitkannya memberi alasan untuk percaya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tidak banyak beda bagi pembaca bertabrakan dengan kalimat bahwa kepercayaan yang dibangun di atas keheningan “does not survive discovery”. Opsi sembunyikan yang kecil menambah pembedaan besar-kecil yang nggak ada di teks. Opsi pembaca percaya pada surat kabar tanpa koreksi diblokir langsung oleh “Readers do not expect a newsroom to be infallible”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer accepts that visible corrections do attract complaints intended to wear the desk down."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer accepts that visible corrections do attract complaints intended to wear the desk down.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Prominent corrections, editors argue, invite complaints from people whose sole purpose is to exhaust the desk, and that does happen.
qs.why: Penulis mengakui keluhan yang bertujuan melelahkan redaksi itu nyata, lalu menyebutnya masih bisa diurus.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena penulis mengakuinya; "Not stated" salah karena pengakuannya tertulis jelas.

topic: Why newspapers should publish corrections prominently
author: A journalism lecturer and former sub-editor
setting: Opinion piece in a weekly press magazine

title: What Survives of a Headline
text:
Most people read the headline and nothing else. That is not laziness but arithmetic, given the number of items passing a reader in a single morning. Researchers who study recall have therefore begun treating the headline as the article for a majority of the audience. Their findings are less comfortable than the trade assumes, since a headline can persist in memory long after the qualification which accompanied it has decayed.

In a standard experiment, two groups read an identical report under different headlines. One states a finding flatly, while the other hedges it with a cautious verb or converts it into a question. A week later both groups tend to reproduce the flat version of the claim, and the hedge has largely disappeared. The body text was identical in each condition; memory retained the shape of the assertion and discarded the caution attached to it. Retention, the experimenters concluded, preserves propositions rather than their modifiers, which is why a qualification behaves like decoration once a week has elapsed. Comprehension, it seems, is not the same faculty as retention.

A second effect concerns quantities. A headline reporting that a risk has doubled is remembered as substantial, even where the article supplies the underlying figures as two cases in ten thousand. Relative change is easy to store, whereas base rates are not, and the smaller number is invariably the one that vanishes. Since the qualifying detail sits inside the article, it reaches fewer people than the assertion on the front. Numerical framing therefore settles the impression a reader carries away long before comprehension has any opportunity to intervene. The arithmetic of attention works steadily against accuracy.

None of this makes headline writing dishonest by nature, because a headline carrying every qualification would carry nobody's attention. It does suggest a working rule. Where a finding is provisional, the provisional element belongs in the headline rather than the third paragraph, and where a risk has doubled, both quantities belong there as well. Otherwise the article is correcting something that most of its readers will never reach.
qs: What is the article mainly about?
The way memory holds a headline's claim but drops its qualifications
The reasons newspapers employ specialists to write their headlines
The falling number of readers who buy a printed paper each day
The care with which most readers work through a whole article

qs.evidence: a headline can persist in memory long after the qualification which accompanied it has decayed.
qs.answer: The way memory holds a headline's claim but drops its qualifications
qs.why: Fokusnya: ingatan menyimpan klaim di judul dan membuang keterangan yang membatasinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi soal penulis judul memindahkan pokoknya ke ketenagakerjaan redaksi, yang nggak dibahas sama sekali. Opsi jumlah pembaca cetak menurun kedengaran seperti topik pers yang wajar, tapi teks bicara soal ingatan, bukan penjualan. Opsi pembaca membaca dengan teliti dibantah kalimat pertama: “Most people read the headline and nothing else.”

qs: What did the two groups in the experiment recall a week later?
the wording of the cautious verb used in the second headline
the underlying figures rather than the size of the change
the plain form of the claim, with the cautious wording gone
the question form in which the finding had been put to them

qs.evidence: A week later both groups tend to reproduce the flat version of the claim, and the hedge has largely disappeared.
qs.answer: the plain form of the claim, with the cautious wording gone
qs.why: Seminggu kemudian dua kelompok itu mengingat versi tanpa pagar; kehati-hatiannya hilang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kata kerja berhati-hati justru bagian yang teks bilang “has largely disappeared” setelah seminggu. Opsi angka dasar membalik temuan paragraf tiga, sebab angka kecil itu yang paling sering menguap. Opsi bentuk pertanyaan memakai salah satu perlakuan eksperimen sebagai isi ingatan, padahal yang tersisa adalah pernyataan datarnya.

qs: Which detail is used as evidence that relative change is easier to remember?
Two groups were given reports with identical body text throughout.
A doubled risk stays large in memory while two in ten thousand fades.
Readers meet a great many items during a single morning of reading.
Provisional findings sit better in a headline than in paragraph three.

qs.evidence: Relative change is easy to store, whereas base rates are not, and the smaller number is invariably the one that vanishes.
qs.answer: A doubled risk stays large in memory while two in ten thousand fades.
qs.why: Perubahan relatif mudah disimpan, sedangkan angka dasarnya justru yang menguap dari ingatan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi teks tubuh identik adalah kendali eksperimen soal pagar bahasa, bukan bukti tentang angka. Opsi banyak item tiap pagi menjelaskan kenapa orang cuma membaca judul, bukan kenapa perubahan relatif lebih lekat. Opsi temuan sementara adalah aturan kerja di paragraf terakhir, jadi ia usulan, bukan bukti.

qs: What does the phrase "the arithmetic of attention" refer to?
the number of experiments required before a finding becomes reliable
the mismatch between how many read the claim and how many the detail
the calculation an editor makes about how long a piece should be
the base rates that researchers report in the body of an article

qs.evidence: Since the qualifying detail sits inside the article, it reaches fewer people than the assertion on the front.
qs.answer: the mismatch between how many read the claim and how many the detail
qs.why: Frasa itu menunjuk selisih jumlah pembaca: klaim di depan dibaca banyak orang, rinciannya tidak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi jumlah eksperimen menyeret frasa itu ke soal metode, padahal kalimat sebelumnya bicara soal berapa orang yang sampai ke rincian. Opsi panjang tulisan menambah keputusan redaksi yang nggak disebut. Opsi angka dasar adalah salah satu isi yang tenggelam, bukan hitungan perhatian yang dimaksud frasa itu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Readers who see a hedged headline are more likely to check the original study."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Readers who see a hedged headline are more likely to check the original study.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: One states a finding flatly, while the other hedges it with a cautious verb or converts it into a question.
qs.why: Teks membahas apa yang diingat pembaca, bukan apakah judul berpagar membuat mereka mengecek studinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" dan "False" sama-sama butuh keterangan sebab-akibat yang tidak pernah ditulis di teks.

topic: How headlines shape what readers remember
author: A science writer summarising research on memory and news
setting: Psychology feature in a popular science magazine

title: A Price on the Article or on Belonging
text:
A weekly serving three river towns has exhausted its advertising. Two editors, both of whom have sustained modest titles elsewhere, were asked what should be done, and neither proposed a reversion to free distribution. They agree that the reader must now pay; what they dispute, quite sharply, is what the reader should be paying for. Neither treats the collapse of display advertising as a temporary interruption, and both regard the reconstruction of local revenue as unavoidable.

The first would meter access: five articles a month, then a charge. A price attached to the article, she argues, reveals which subjects the audience actually values, and it extracts revenue from occasional readers who would never join anything. Subscription is a transaction requiring no explanation, and it also insulates the desk from the suspicion that it owes its funders a comfortable read. Metering, she maintains, imposes a discipline of relevance which no appeal to civic duty can replicate. Nobody, she adds, resents paying for a service they have deliberately selected.

The second would solicit membership instead and leave the reporting accessible to all. He accepts that the revenue is harder to forecast, and the difference does not trouble him. A locked story about a planning decision is precisely the item a town requires, and an obstruction placed in front of the public record inflicts damage which no balance sheet registers. Where his colleague detects a signal from the market, he identifies a barrier to citizenship.

The gap between them is narrower than the argument sounds, and it does not close. Both would charge, both refuse to let advertisers commission coverage, and both accept that a paper cannot subsist on goodwill. One seeks a price on the article; the other seeks a price on belonging to the institution which produces it. The choice determines who remains outside, and no accounting exercise will resolve that. The disagreement is therefore constitutional rather than commercial, concerning the relationship between a paper and the public it claims to serve. Committees prefer disputes that arithmetic can settle.
qs: What is the writer's main purpose in this feature?
To set out two close but distinct answers to a funding problem
To show that free distribution remains the best option for weeklies
To report the closure of a weekly covering three river towns
To criticize advertisers who have withdrawn support from the press

qs.evidence: The gap between them is narrower than the argument sounds, and it does not close.
qs.answer: To set out two close but distinct answers to a funding problem
qs.why: Penulis memaparkan dua jawaban yang berdekatan namun tetap berbeda atas soal pembiayaan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi distribusi gratis diblokir kalimat kedua: “neither proposed a reversion to free distribution”. Opsi penutupan koran kedengaran seperti berita lokal yang wajar, tapi teks bilang korannya masih ada dan sedang mencari model bayar. Opsi menyalahkan pengiklan memakai satu fakta latar sebagai maksud tulisan, padahal hilangnya iklan cuma titik awal perdebatan.

qs: What does the first editor propose?
free access to everything, funded by donations from local residents
a charge on advertisers who place notices beside the news
an annual membership that leaves all the reporting open to all
a limit of five items each month, after which readers are charged

qs.evidence: The first would meter access: five articles a month, then a charge.
qs.answer: a limit of five items each month, after which readers are charged
qs.why: Editor pertama mengusulkan meteran: lima artikel per bulan, setelah itu berbayar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi akses gratis berdana sumbangan bertabrakan dengan kesepakatan keduanya bahwa pembaca harus mulai membayar. Opsi memungut dari pengiklan justru ditolak dua editor, yang sama-sama menolak pengiklan memesan liputan. Opsi keanggotaan tahunan adalah usulan editor kedua, jadi salah pemilik pendapat.

qs: Which point does the second editor use to support his position?
Occasional readers will pay for single items but never for membership.
Membership income can be forecast more reliably than metered charges.
Charging for access shuts residents out of reporting they need.
Advertisers should be allowed to commission coverage of local events.

qs.evidence: A locked story about a planning decision is precisely the item a town requires, and an obstruction placed in front of the public record inflicts damage which no balance sheet registers.
qs.answer: Charging for access shuts residents out of reporting they need.
qs.why: Alasannya konkret: berita keputusan tata ruang yang terkunci justru yang paling dibutuhkan warga kota itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pembaca sesekali adalah argumen editor pertama soal meteran, bukan alasan editor kedua. Opsi pendapatan lebih mudah diramalkan malah dibantah orangnya sendiri, yang mengakui pendapatan keanggotaan “harder to forecast”. Opsi pengiklan memesan liputan ditolak keduanya di paragraf penutup.

qs: What can be inferred about the difference between the two proposals?
It concerns who ends up excluded rather than which model earns more.
It concerns whether advertisers rather than readers should pay.
It concerns roughly how many reporters each model could employ.
It concerns whether the weekly should go on appearing in print at all.

qs.evidence: The choice determines who remains outside, and no accounting exercise will resolve that.
qs.answer: It concerns who ends up excluded rather than which model earns more.
qs.why: Kalimat penutup menegaskan yang dipertaruhkan adalah siapa yang tertinggal di luar, bukan hitungan uang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pengiklan versus pembaca sudah selesai sebelum debatnya dimulai, sebab keduanya sepakat pembaca yang membayar. Opsi jumlah reporter menambah hitungan pegawai yang nggak pernah disebut. Opsi cetak atau tidak memindahkan soalnya ke format, padahal teks menyebut perbedaannya “constitutional rather than commercial”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The second editor believes membership income is easier to predict than metered charges."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The second editor believes membership income is easier to predict than metered charges.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: He accepts that the revenue is harder to forecast, and the difference does not trouble him.
qs.why: Dia sendiri mengakui pendapatan model keanggotaan lebih sulit diramalkan, jadi klaim ini terbalik.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena bertolak belakang; "Not stated" salah karena soal ramalan pendapatan disebut.

topic: Two funding models for a local newspaper
author: A trade reporter comparing two editors' proposals
setting: Interview feature in a media trade journal

title: Paying for the Empty Press Bench
text:
This paper reviews the collapse of court and council reporting across the province and the options open to the assembly. Of the 27 district councils, 19 held no meeting last year at which a reporter was present. Six weekly titles have closed since the last review. The two survivors employ one full-time journalist between them, which is fewer than the province employed on court reporting alone a decade ago. The consequence is not a matter of taste: hearings that nobody reports leave no record for anybody to consult.

Direct grants to publishers would act quickly and would carry an obvious hazard. A newspaper whose budget is renewed each year by the body it exists to scrutinise will, in time, scrutinise it more gently. No assurance written into a funding letter prevents that drift. Experience elsewhere in the region supports the concern: where grants were awarded department by department, coverage of those departments became measurably thinner within two years. Conditional independence of that kind depends on who controls renewal, and renewal is precisely where an assembly retains its leverage over a publisher. The pattern held across four authorities.

The proposal here separates the money from the decision. A small levy on regional broadcasting licences would fund a trust, governed by a board on which the assembly holds a minority of seats. The trust would pay the salaries of reporters attached to existing titles, on three-year terms, with editorial control left entirely to the editors who receive them. Applications would be assessed on the number of hearings covered rather than on readership. The administration is modest, and comparable arrangements are already running elsewhere.

Two risks require conditions, and the first is displacement: a title given a funded reporter may simply cut a post of its own. Grants should therefore be conditional on existing staffing being maintained, verified against payroll returns. The second is capture of the trust itself, which argues for published minutes and fixed terms for board members. Neither risk is a reason to leave the press bench empty; both are reasons to write the conditions down before any money moves. Neither condition is substantive, and neither justifies postponing a decision the assembly has already deferred twice. The money involved is small, the gap in the record is large, and the choice now rests with the members.
qs: What is the main purpose of this review?
To recommend that the assembly fund local reporting at arm's length
To report how many weekly newspapers in the province have closed
To argue that district councils should publish their own newsletters
To defend the existing system of direct grants to local publishers

qs.evidence: The proposal here separates the money from the decision.
qs.answer: To recommend that the assembly fund local reporting at arm's length
qs.why: Usulan intinya: biayai liputan lokal tapi jauhkan uangnya dari tangan yang membuat keputusan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi melaporkan jumlah koran tutup memakai angka pembuka sebagai tujuan seluruh telaah. Opsi buletin dewan distrik menambah usulan yang nggak ada; yang diusulkan adalah reporter bergaji dana perwalian di koran yang sudah jalan. Opsi membela hibah langsung persis kebalikan isi paragraf dua, yang menyebut hibah langsung menipiskan liputan atas pemberi dana.

qs: How would the proposed trust be governed?
by the editors of the two surviving weekly titles in the province
by a standing committee of the assembly which meets once in three years
by a panel on which the elected members are deliberately outnumbered
by the regional broadcasters who would be paying the new levy

qs.evidence: A small levy on regional broadcasting licences would fund a trust, governed by a board on which the assembly holds a minority of seats.
qs.answer: by a panel on which the elected members are deliberately outnumbered
qs.why: Dewan pengelolanya dirancang supaya kursi majelis tinggal minoritas.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi para editor mencampur dua hal: editor memegang kendali redaksi, bukan tata kelola perwalian. Opsi komite majelis membalik rancangannya, karena majelis sengaja ditaruh sebagai minoritas. Opsi penyiar regional memakai pihak yang membayar pungutan sebagai pihak yang memerintah, padahal teks cuma menyebut sumber dananya.

qs: Which finding is offered as evidence against direct grants to publishers?
Nineteen district councils held no meeting attended by a reporter.
Reporting on funded departments grew thinner within a couple of years.
The two surviving weekly titles share one full-time journalist.
Applications would be judged on hearings covered, not readership.

qs.evidence: Experience elsewhere in the region supports the concern: where grants were awarded department by department, coverage of those departments became measurably thinner within two years.
qs.answer: Reporting on funded departments grew thinner within a couple of years.
qs.why: Pengalaman daerah lain: begitu hibah diberi per dinas, liputan atas dinas itu menipis dalam dua tahun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi sembilan belas dewan mengukur besarnya kekosongan liputan, bukan akibat dari hibah langsung. Opsi satu jurnalis untuk dua koran juga statistik keruntuhan, bukan bukti soal hibah. Opsi kriteria penilaian adalah rancangan usulan baru, jadi ia datang setelah keberatannya, bukan mendukung keberatan itu.

qs: What can be inferred about the condition on existing staffing?
It is meant to raise the number of hearings that each reporter attends.
It is meant to give the assembly a majority on the board of the trust.
It is meant to reduce the cost of the levy on broadcasting licences.
It is meant to stop titles from cutting their own posts once funded.

qs.evidence: the first is displacement: a title given a funded reporter may simply cut a post of its own.
qs.answer: It is meant to stop titles from cutting their own posts once funded.
qs.why: Syarat itu menjawab risiko penggeseran: koran bisa memotong posisi sendiri setelah dapat reporter gratis.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menambah jumlah sidang yang dihadiri adalah urusan kriteria seleksi, bukan syarat kepegawaian. Opsi mayoritas majelis bertentangan dengan rancangan dewan perwalian yang menaruh majelis sebagai minoritas. Opsi menurunkan pungutan menyangkut biaya, sedangkan syarat ini soal jumlah posisi yang harus dipertahankan dan diperiksa lewat data penggajian.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Editors receiving a funded reporter would keep full control over what that reporter writes."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Editors receiving a funded reporter would keep full control over what that reporter writes.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The trust would pay the salaries of reporters attached to existing titles, on three-year terms, with editorial control left entirely to the editors who receive them.
qs.why: Kendali redaksi disebut tetap sepenuhnya di tangan editor penerima reporter itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena sejalan dengan teks; "Not stated" salah karena kendali redaksi dinyatakan eksplisit.

topic: Public funding for local court and council reporting
author: A policy analyst advising the assembly's culture committee
setting: Policy review submitted to a provincial assembly committee

title: The Cheapest Medicine Is Cleaner Air
text:
Health budgets are debated as though the only question were how many beds a district can afford, but the arithmetic is narrower than it looks. A child admitted twice a year with breathing difficulty consumes clinical time, medication and a parent's wages. The admission is then recorded as a cost of treatment rather than as a consequence of the air outside. That accounting convention has consequences of its own, because a cost attributed to treatment attracts clinical funding and nothing else. Prevention, being invisible when it works, is the first item to be cut.

The relationship between particles and lungs is no longer contested. Where roadside concentrations fall, attendance at emergency departments for asthma falls with them, and the reduction appears within months rather than decades. One coastal city rerouted heavy freight away from three residential streets and recorded a fifth fewer childhood admissions in the following year. Nothing was spent on hospitals; a traffic order did the work. Comparable reductions have been reported wherever heavy vehicles have been separated from housing.

Objections are usually financial, and they deserve an answer. Rerouting freight imposes costs on hauliers, and cleaning up a bus fleet requires capital that a district does not hold. Yet the comparison offered is almost always the wrong one, since the expenditure avoided is counted in a different ledger from the expenditure incurred. Clinical savings accrue to the health service, while the traffic order is paid for by the transport authority, and no accountant is asked to add the two columns together. Institutional separation of that sort quietly protects the more expensive option.

A serious district would therefore publish one figure alongside the other. Admissions for respiratory illness could be reported by street, next to the monitored readings, so that residents can see the connection for themselves. Such transparency is uncomfortable, because it identifies the streets that have been neglected. It is also the only way to make prevention visible enough to survive a budget meeting. Clean air will never look like medicine, though it works rather better than most of it.
qs: Which statement best expresses the writer's argument?
Districts ought to fund a great many more hospital beds for children
Preventing illness through cleaner air costs less than treating it
Hauliers should be compensated whenever a road is closed to freight
Monitoring equipment on busy roads is too costly for most districts

qs.evidence: Prevention, being invisible when it works, is the first item to be cut.
qs.answer: Preventing illness through cleaner air costs less than treating it
qs.why: Argumennya: mencegah lewat udara bersih lebih murah daripada mengobati akibatnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menambah tempat tidur rumah sakit persis kerangka anggaran yang teks bilang terlalu sempit. Opsi ganti rugi untuk hauliers mengakui biaya mereka, tapi teks nggak pernah menuntut kompensasi, cuma menuntut dua kolom dijumlahkan. Opsi alat pemantau terlalu mahal bertabrakan dengan usulan penutup yang justru meminta bacaan pemantauan diterbitkan per jalan.

qs: What did the coastal city do, according to the essay?
It built a new emergency department close to three of the busy streets.
It moved heavy lorries away from three streets where people live.
It replaced its whole bus fleet within a single financial year.
It published admission figures for each street in the district.

qs.evidence: One coastal city rerouted heavy freight away from three residential streets and recorded a fifth fewer childhood admissions in the following year.
qs.answer: It moved heavy lorries away from three streets where people live.
qs.why: Kota itu mengalihkan angkutan berat dari tiga jalan permukiman, lalu admisi anak turun seperlima.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi membangun unit gawat darurat bertabrakan dengan “Nothing was spent on hospitals”. Opsi mengganti seluruh armada bus memakai contoh biaya dari paragraf tiga, bukan tindakan kota pesisir itu. Opsi menerbitkan angka per jalan adalah usulan penulis di paragraf terakhir, bukan yang sudah dilakukan kota itu.

qs: How would you describe the writer's treatment of the financial objections?
Dismissive, treating the objections as raised in bad faith
Unsure, since the cost of rerouting freight is not known
Hopeful that hauliers themselves will save money in the end
Willing to concede the costs while disputing the comparison

qs.evidence: Rerouting freight imposes costs on hauliers, and cleaning up a bus fleet requires capital that a district does not hold.
qs.answer: Willing to concede the costs while disputing the comparison
qs.why: Penulis mengakui biayanya nyata, tapi mempersoalkan pembandingnya yang dianggap salah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi meremehkan bertentangan dengan kalimat “Objections are usually financial, and they deserve an answer”. Opsi ragu soal biaya juga salah, sebab penulis menyebut ongkosnya nyata bagi hauliers dan bagi armada bus tanpa ragu. Opsi berharap hauliers ikut hemat menambah janji yang nggak ada; penghematan yang disebut masuk ke dinas kesehatan.

qs: What does the writer imply about publishing admissions street by street?
It would expose which streets have been left in poor condition.
It would cut the number of children admitted during the first year.
It would let the transport authority recover costs from hauliers.
It would show which districts hold the most modern monitors.

qs.evidence: Such transparency is uncomfortable, because it identifies the streets that have been neglected.
qs.answer: It would expose which streets have been left in poor condition.
qs.why: Data per jalan bikin tidak nyaman justru karena menunjuk jalan-jalan yang selama ini diabaikan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menurunkan angka admisi mencampur akibat penerbitan data dengan akibat aturan lalu lintas; yang menurunkan admisi adalah pengalihan angkutan. Opsi menagih biaya ke hauliers menambah mekanisme pembayaran yang nggak ada di teks. Opsi membandingkan alat pemantau menukar tujuannya: bacaan pemantauan dipakai supaya warga melihat kaitannya, bukan untuk menilai alatnya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Savings from fewer admissions and the cost of a traffic order fall to different authorities."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Savings from fewer admissions and the cost of a traffic order fall to different authorities.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Clinical savings accrue to the health service, while the traffic order is paid for by the transport authority, and no accountant is asked to add the two columns together.
qs.why: Penghematan klinis masuk ke dinas kesehatan, sementara ongkos aturan lalu lintas dibayar dinas perhubungan.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena persis begitu bunyinya; "Not stated" salah karena pembagian anggarannya ditulis.

topic: Air quality as a cheaper alternative to hospital treatment
author: A public health physician writing for a general readership
setting: Comment essay in a public health magazine

title: What the Drains Know First
text:
A technician collects half a litre of untreated sewage from a pumping station each morning. The sample appears unremarkable, yet it carries a combined record of what a hundred thousand people passed overnight. Within that record are traces of virus shed by people who have no symptoms at all and who have seen nobody. Sewage sampling has evolved from a laboratory novelty into a tool of routine monitoring.

Its principal advantage is timing, for clinical figures depend on a sequence of decisions: somebody must feel unwell, decide to seek advice, obtain a test and have the result registered. Each stage introduces delay, and each stage excludes the people least likely to attend a clinic. Sewage skips the sequence entirely, since nobody has to decide anything. In several outbreaks the level in the sewage rose between four and seven days before reported cases began to climb. A week is a considerable interval in an epidemic.

The method has real limits, and enthusiasts tend to understate them. Rainfall dilutes a sample, waste from a works breaks down the material being measured, and an area that includes a large factory or a prison behaves quite differently from a residential one. A rising signal shows that more material is being shed somewhere upstream. It cannot say by whom, or where exactly, or how severely anybody is affected. Reading the numbers therefore needs somebody who understands the drains as well as the virus.

None of this makes the technique a substitute for clinical reporting, and nobody serious claims otherwise; it is better understood as an early bell. Where a district can act on a week's notice, by opening testing sites or reminding clinicians what to look for, the notice is worth having. Where no such capacity exists, the sampling merely documents an epidemic that arrives on schedule. The instrument is cheap; the response is the expensive part.
qs: What is the main point of the article?
Sewage sampling has replaced the need for clinical testing.
Rainfall makes wastewater monitoring unreliable in most districts.
Technicians should collect samples more than once each morning.
Sewage sampling gives early warning but cannot stand alone.

qs.evidence: it is better understood as an early bell.
qs.answer: Sewage sampling gives early warning but cannot stand alone.
qs.why: Intinya: sinyal air limbah berguna sebagai peringatan dini, bukan pengganti pelaporan klinis.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menggantikan tes klinis diblokir kalimat “None of this makes the technique a substitute for clinical reporting”. Opsi hujan bikin tak berguna melebih-lebihkan satu batasan jadi kesimpulan; teks menyebut pengenceran sebagai hal yang harus dibaca ahli, bukan alasan membuang metodenya. Opsi ambil sampel lebih sering menambah anjuran teknis yang nggak pernah muncul.

qs: How much earlier did the wastewater signal rise in several outbreaks?
between half a week and a full week earlier than clinic figures
between one and two days ahead of the first reported cases
roughly a fortnight ahead of any rise in the reports from clinics
on the same day that reported case numbers began to climb

qs.evidence: In several outbreaks the level in the sewage rose between four and seven days before reported cases began to climb.
qs.answer: between half a week and a full week earlier than clinic figures
qs.why: Angkanya empat sampai tujuh hari sebelum kasus terlapor mulai naik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi satu sampai dua hari memperkecil jeda yang teks sebut empat sampai tujuh hari. Opsi dua pekan membesarkannya, padahal teks cuma bilang “A week is a considerable interval”. Opsi hari yang sama menghapus keunggulan waktunya, yang justru disebut kelebihan utama metode ini.

qs: Which point is offered as evidence that clinical figures arrive late?
An area containing a prison behaves unlike a residential one.
Every step from feeling ill to a registered result adds delay.
Waste from a factory can break down the material being measured.
Half a litre of sewage records a night's shedding by a whole town.

qs.evidence: Each stage introduces delay, and each stage excludes the people least likely to attend a clinic.
qs.answer: Every step from feeling ill to a registered result adds delay.
qs.why: Setiap tahap dari merasa sakit sampai hasil tercatat menambah jeda waktu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kawasan berpenjara dan opsi limbah pabrik dua-duanya batasan metode air limbah, jadi keduanya menjelaskan kelemahan sampel, bukan kenapa angka klinis datang terlambat. Opsi setengah liter menunjukkan cakupan sampelnya dan malah memuji metodenya, bukan mengukur jeda pelaporan klinis.

qs: What can be inferred about districts with no capacity to respond?
Their samples are usually spoiled by waste from a factory.
Their clinical reporting is more accurate than sewage figures.
Their laboratories should sample more pumping stations weekly.
Their sampling records an outbreak they cannot forestall.

qs.evidence: Where no such capacity exists, the sampling merely documents an epidemic that arrives on schedule.
qs.answer: Their sampling records an outbreak they cannot forestall.
qs.why: Tanpa kemampuan bertindak, pengambilan sampel cuma mencatat wabah yang tetap datang tepat waktu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi sampel rusak karena pabrik memakai satu batasan teknis untuk menjelaskan hal lain: teks bicara soal kapasitas merespons, bukan mutu sampel. Opsi pelaporan klinis lebih akurat menambah perbandingan mutu yang nggak ada; yang dibandingkan adalah kecepatan. Opsi menambah titik sampel justru sia-sia menurut logika teks, sebab masalahnya bukan datanya kurang, tapi tak ada yang bisa dikerjakan dengan data itu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "A rising wastewater signal shows how severely the people upstream have been affected."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: A rising wastewater signal shows how severely the people upstream have been affected.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: It cannot say by whom, or where exactly, or how severely anybody is affected.
qs.why: Teks tegas menyebut sinyal itu tidak bisa memberi tahu seberapa berat orang terdampak.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena membalik isi kalimatnya; "Not stated" salah karena batasannya disebut eksplisit.

topic: Wastewater surveillance as an early warning system
author: A science journalist reporting on disease monitoring
setting: Feature in a popular science monthly

title: Taking the Salt Out Slowly
text:
Most of the salt in a household diet was incorporated before the food reached the house. Bread, sauces, processed meat and instant noodles account for the bulk of it, so advice directed at cooks addresses only a fraction of the problem. Dietary advice, in other words, is aimed at the stage of the process where least of the salt is added. Two strategies have therefore competed for official attention: telling shoppers what a product contains, and quietly reducing what manufacturers put in.

Labelling is the more popular of the two, and the appeal is obvious: it respects choice, costs the public purse very little, and produces a visible symbol on a packet. Trials of front-of-pack warnings do shift purchasing, though the shift is modest. It is also concentrated among shoppers who were already attentive to what they were buying. Those consuming the most salt tend to change the least, which is an awkward finding for a policy justified by consumer autonomy. Information rewards people who were already reading.

Gradual reformulation works from the other direction. Manufacturers agree to reduce salt by a few per cent a year across a whole category. Because the reduction falls below the threshold of detection, the taste of any single loaf does not appear to change. Preference itself adjusts downwards over several years, which is why the strategy compounds. One national programme following this route recorded a fall of about fifteen per cent in average intake across a decade. Sales in the categories involved showed no measurable decline.

The comparison is not entirely fair, since the two approaches are answering different questions. Labelling addresses the shopper who wants to choose; reformulation addresses the shopper who never reads a label at all, which is most of us most of the time. A sensible programme therefore uses both instruments without pretending that they are equivalent in reach: one informs a decision. The other quietly alters what sits on the shelf before any decision is made. Reformulation operates upstream of preference, and therefore requires no participation from the consumer at all. Regulatory preference for disclosure reflects a commitment to consumer autonomy rather than any demonstrated superiority of outcome.
qs: What is the article mainly comparing?
the salt in ordinary bread against the salt in instant noodles
the cost of labelling schemes against the cost of monitoring sales
advice given to cooks against advice given to restaurant owners
two routes to less salt: informing shoppers or reformulating food

qs.evidence: Two strategies have therefore competed for official attention: telling shoppers what a product contains, and quietly reducing what manufacturers put in.
qs.answer: two routes to less salt: informing shoppers or reformulating food
qs.why: Dua strategi yang dibandingkan: memberi tahu pembeli, dan diam-diam mengurangi kadar dari pabrik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi roti versus noodles memakai daftar sumber garam di kalimat pertama sebagai pokok perbandingan. Opsi biaya label versus pemantauan penjualan menambah perbandingan angka yang nggak ada; biaya cuma disebut sebagai satu daya tarik label. Opsi nasihat untuk koki versus pemilik restoran mengarang pihak kedua, sebab teks cuma menyebut nasihat pada koki menyentuh sebagian kecil masalah.

qs: What does the article say about the effect of front-of-pack warnings?
They produce a small change, mostly among attentive shoppers.
They probably change nothing in the behaviour of ordinary shoppers.
They tend to work best on the shoppers who eat the most salt.
They cut average intake by around fifteen per cent in a decade.

qs.evidence: It is also concentrated among shoppers who were already attentive to what they were buying.
qs.answer: They produce a small change, mostly among attentive shoppers.
qs.why: Pergeserannya kecil dan terkumpul di pembeli yang sejak awal sudah memperhatikan isi kemasan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tidak mengubah apa pun terlalu keras, karena teks mengakui label “do shift purchasing”, meski sedikit. Opsi paling ampuh bagi pemakan garam terbanyak membalik temuannya: justru mereka yang paling sedikit berubah. Opsi turun lima belas persen memindahkan hasil program reformulasi ke label.

qs: Which finding is used to support gradual reformulation?
Bread and sauces usually hold most of the salt in a diet.
Front-of-pack symbols probably cost the public purse very little.
Average intake fell by roughly a seventh over ten years.
Advice aimed at cooks reaches a fraction of the whole problem.

qs.evidence: One national programme following this route recorded a fall of about fifteen per cent in average intake across a decade.
qs.answer: Average intake fell by roughly a seventh over ten years.
qs.why: Buktinya program nasional: asupan rata-rata turun sekitar lima belas persen dalam sepuluh tahun tanpa penjualan merosot.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi roti dan saus menjelaskan di mana garamnya masuk, bukan hasil sebuah program. Opsi biaya simbol kemasan adalah keunggulan label, jadi ia mendukung lawan reformulasi. Opsi nasihat pada koki menunjukkan batas pendekatan dapur, dan sama sekali nggak mengukur hasil pengurangan bertahap.

qs: Which statement best paraphrases the point about labelling?
Labels are read most carefully by people with the highest intake.
Labels become unnecessary once manufacturers have cut the salt.
Labels change the flavour of a product without shoppers noticing.
Labels help those who already look, and miss those who never do.

qs.evidence: Information rewards people who were already reading.
qs.answer: Labels help those who already look, and miss those who never do.
qs.why: Label memberi manfaat pada yang memang sudah membaca, dan melewatkan yang tidak pernah membaca.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pembaca paling teliti adalah pemakan garam terbanyak membalik temuan teks soal siapa yang berubah. Opsi label jadi mubazir bertentangan dengan usulan memakai dua instrumen sekaligus. Opsi mengubah rasa memindahkan mekanisme reformulasi bertahap ke label, padahal yang tak terdeteksi lidah adalah penurunan kadar tiap tahun.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Manufacturers who reformulated their products received a tax reduction in return."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Manufacturers who reformulated their products received a tax reduction in return.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Manufacturers agree to reduce salt by a few per cent a year across a whole category.
qs.why: Teks cuma bilang produsen bersepakat mengurangi kadar; soal insentif pajak sama sekali tidak disinggung.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" dan "False" sama-sama menuntut keterangan tentang pajak yang tak pernah muncul di teks.

topic: Salt labelling compared with gradual reformulation
author: A nutrition researcher writing for non-specialists
setting: Nutrition feature in a health science magazine

title: Buckets or Sprayers
text:
A coastal district reports dengue every wet season and has money for one campaign. Two officers with long records in vector control were asked what to do with it. Both accept that the mosquito breeds in domestic water containers rather than in swamps, and both reject the idea that the problem can be sprayed away. They disagree about where the effort should be concentrated. The disagreement is worth setting out, because the budget will not stretch to both.

The first would put everything into household clean-up. Volunteers visit each compound, empty the containers, cover the tanks and return a fortnight later to check. The reasoning is that elimination of breeding sites removes the next generation altogether, whereas killing adults postpones an outbreak by a week. Such visits also build a relationship that survives the season. People shown a larva in their own jar behave differently afterwards, and participation, on this account, is the durable part of the intervention.

The second accepts every word of that and doubts the coverage. Volunteer schemes reach the households that answer the door, she notes, and the districts where transmission concentrates are precisely the ones where nobody is at home during the day. She would fund weekly larval surveillance in fixed sites, with targeted treatment wherever the index rises above a set threshold. Her argument is not that participation fails; it is that participation is uneven, and mosquitoes exploit the gaps. Surveillance, she argues, at least measures its own coverage.

Neither would spend the money on fogging the streets, and both would publish the larval index by neighbourhood. The disagreement concerns which failure is more tolerable: a campaign that engages residents but misses the hardest districts, or one that covers those districts while teaching nobody anything. Put that way, the choice looks less like a technical question. It looks like a judgement about who the campaign is for. Committees rarely record such judgements in those terms.
qs: What is the writer's main purpose in this piece?
To recommend fogging as the most effective measure available
To explain how the mosquito responsible for dengue reproduces
To set out two similar but competing uses for one control budget
To report how many dengue cases the district records each year

qs.evidence: They disagree about where the effort should be concentrated.
qs.answer: To set out two similar but competing uses for one control budget
qs.why: Penulis memaparkan dua penggunaan anggaran yang mirip tapi bersaing, bukan merekomendasikan satu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pengasapan diblokir langsung: “Neither would spend the money on fogging the streets”. Opsi biologi nyamuk memakai premis yang kedua petugas sudah sepakati sebagai isi tulisan. Opsi jumlah kasus per tahun menambah statistik yang nggak pernah diberikan; teks cuma bilang dengue muncul tiap musim hujan.

qs: What does the first officer's plan involve?
spraying the streets of the district at the start of each wet season
visiting compounds, emptying containers, then checking again later
monitoring larvae weekly at fixed sites across the whole district
publishing the larval index for each neighbourhood every week

qs.evidence: Volunteers visit each compound, empty the containers, cover the tanks and return a fortnight later to check.
qs.answer: visiting compounds, emptying containers, then checking again later
qs.why: Rencananya: relawan datang ke tiap pekarangan, mengosongkan wadah, lalu kembali dua minggu kemudian.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi penyemprotan jalan ditolak kedua petugas, jadi ia bukan rencana siapa pun di teks. Opsi surveilans larva mingguan adalah usulan petugas kedua, bukan yang pertama. Opsi menerbitkan indeks per lingkungan justru hal yang mereka sepakati bersama, jadi ia nggak membedakan rencana pertama.

qs: Which point does the second officer use to support her position?
The areas with the most transmission are empty during work hours.
Killing adult mosquitoes only postpones an outbreak by a week.
Residents shown a larva in their own jar change their habits.
The mosquito breeds in household containers rather than swamps.

qs.evidence: Volunteer schemes reach the households that answer the door, she notes, and the districts where transmission concentrates are precisely the ones where nobody is at home during the day.
qs.answer: The areas with the most transmission are empty during work hours.
qs.why: Alasannya: kawasan dengan penularan tertinggi justru kosong pada jam kerja, jadi kunjungan relawan lewat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi membunuh nyamuk dewasa adalah alasan petugas pertama menolak penyemprotan, bukan alasan petugas kedua. Opsi warga yang melihat larva juga argumen petugas pertama soal partisipasi. Opsi tempat berkembang biak adalah premis yang keduanya sepakati, jadi ia nggak bisa mendukung salah satu pihak.

qs: What can be inferred about the nature of the disagreement?
It rests on a dispute about the way the mosquito reproduces itself.
It rests on whether fogging is worth its considerable expense.
It rests on how often the larval index ought to be published.
It rests on a choice about which group the campaign should serve.

qs.evidence: It looks like a judgement about who the campaign is for.
qs.answer: It rests on a choice about which group the campaign should serve.
qs.why: Penutupnya menyebut ini penilaian tentang untuk siapa kampanye itu dijalankan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi soal biologi nyamuk bertabrakan dengan “Both accept that the mosquito breeds in domestic water containers”. Opsi pengasapan juga sudah selesai, karena keduanya menolaknya. Opsi frekuensi penerbitan indeks memakai hal yang mereka sepakati sebagai sumber perselisihan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Both officers would make the larval index public for each neighbourhood."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Both officers would make the larval index public for each neighbourhood.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Neither would spend the money on fogging the streets, and both would publish the larval index by neighbourhood.
qs.why: Keduanya sepakat menerbitkan indeks larva per lingkungan, jadi klaim ini parafrasa langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena persetujuan itu tertulis; "Not stated" salah karena disebut di paragraf akhir.

topic: Two approaches to controlling dengue in a coastal district
author: A health bulletin editor summarising two officers' positions
setting: Discussion piece in a regional health bulletin

title: The City Has Ten Days a Year
text:
This plan concerns the ten to fourteen days each year on which this city becomes dangerous rather than merely uncomfortable. Records from the past decade show excess deaths clustering in those days, concentrated among residents over seventy living alone on upper floors. The pattern is geographical as well as demographic: three wards with the least tree cover account for a disproportionate share of them. Those same wards hold the smallest number of publicly accessible cooled rooms. The overlap is not a coincidence, and it has been visible in the records for years.

Response at present depends on the discretion of individual departments. Cooling centres open when a manager decides they should, warnings are issued through channels the affected residents do not use, and no service is obliged to alter its routine. The consequence is predictable: action begins on the second or third day of a heat episode, by which time admissions have already risen. Discretion, in an emergency of this kind, functions as delay, and nobody is at fault, which is exactly the difficulty.

The plan therefore proposes a threshold rather than a judgement. When the forecast night-time minimum exceeds a stated figure for two consecutive nights, four measures take effect automatically. Designated halls open as cooled rooms with extended hours, and home visits to registered residents move to a daily schedule. Outdoor municipal work shifts to the early morning, and water points are staffed at three named transport hubs. None of the four requires new construction. All four require a decision taken in advance.

Two weaknesses should be recorded honestly: a register of vulnerable residents is only as good as its last update, and the wards with the highest risk have the least reliable data. Planting for shade, meanwhile, will not affect this year or the next, though it remains the only measure that reduces the underlying hazard. Neither weakness argues against the threshold; both argue for beginning the slower work at the same time. A plan that admits its weaknesses is easier to correct than one that hides them.
qs: What is the main purpose of this plan?
To report the excess deaths recorded over the past decade
To propose building new cooling centres in three city wards
To replace departmental discretion with an automatic trigger
To argue that planting trees is the only measure worth funding

qs.evidence: The plan therefore proposes a threshold rather than a judgement.
qs.answer: To replace departmental discretion with an automatic trigger
qs.why: Usulan intinya: ganti kebijaksanaan tiap dinas dengan ambang batas yang memicu tindakan otomatis.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi melaporkan kematian berlebih memakai data pembuka sebagai maksud dokumennya, padahal data itu dipakai untuk membenarkan usulan. Opsi membangun pusat pendingin baru bertabrakan dengan “None of the four requires new construction”. Opsi penanaman pohon satu-satunya yang dibiayai membalik penutupnya, yang minta pekerjaan lambat itu dimulai bersamaan, bukan sebagai ganti ambang batas.

qs: Which residents does the plan identify as most at risk?
people over seventy who live by themselves on higher floors
outdoor municipal workers who start their shifts before dawn
residents of the three wards with the largest amount of shade
travellers passing daily through the three named transport hubs

qs.evidence: Records from the past decade show excess deaths clustering in those days, concentrated among residents over seventy living alone on upper floors.
qs.answer: people over seventy who live by themselves on higher floors
qs.why: Kematian berlebih terpusat pada penduduk di atas tujuh puluh yang tinggal sendiri di lantai atas.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pekerja lapangan memakai salah satu langkah tanggap (jam kerja digeser ke pagi) sebagai kelompok paling berisiko. Opsi tiga ward dengan naungan terbanyak membalik polanya, sebab yang berisiko adalah ward dengan tutupan pohon paling sedikit. Opsi penumpang di simpul transportasi mengambil lokasi titik air, bukan kelompok yang datanya menunjukkan kematian berlebih.

qs: Which observation is offered as evidence that the present arrangement is too slow?
Response starts once hospital admissions have already increased.
Three wards with little tree cover hold the fewest cooled rooms.
Measures would begin after two consecutive warm nights in the city.
A register of vulnerable residents is rarely updated in those wards.

qs.evidence: The consequence is predictable: action begins on the second or third day of a heat episode, by which time admissions have already risen.
qs.answer: Response starts once hospital admissions have already increased.
qs.why: Buktinya: tindakan baru mulai hari kedua atau ketiga, ketika angka masuk rumah sakit sudah naik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tiga ward menggambarkan ketimpangan tempat, bukan kelambatan waktu. Opsi dua malam panas berturut-turut adalah rancangan ambang batas yang diusulkan, jadi ia bagian dari obatnya, bukan bukti penyakitnya. Opsi daftar warga jarang diperbarui adalah kelemahan yang diakui usulan baru, dan bukan alasan sistem sekarang lambat.

qs: What can be inferred about the proposal to plant for shade?
It is treated as an alternative to opening cooled rooms this summer.
It is valued for the long term despite giving no relief this year.
It is expected to remove the need for a register of residents.
It is regarded as the fastest of the four automatic measures.

qs.evidence: Planting for shade, meanwhile, will not affect this year or the next, though it remains the only measure that reduces the underlying hazard.
qs.answer: It is valued for the long term despite giving no relief this year.
qs.why: Penanaman pohon tak menolong tahun ini, tapi disebut satu-satunya yang menurunkan bahaya dasarnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pengganti ruang berpendingin bertentangan dengan “Neither weakness argues against the threshold”, karena keduanya justru dijalankan bersamaan. Opsi menghapus kebutuhan daftar warga mencampur dua kelemahan yang teks sebut terpisah. Opsi langkah tercepat membalik keterangan waktunya, sebab penanaman disebut nggak berpengaruh tahun ini maupun tahun depan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The four measures in the plan depend on new buildings being completed first."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The four measures in the plan depend on new buildings being completed first.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: None of the four requires new construction. All four require a decision taken in advance.
qs.why: Teks menyatakan tak satu pun dari empat langkah itu butuh bangunan baru, hanya keputusan lebih awal.
qs.whyOthersFail: "True" salah karena bertolak belakang; "Not stated" salah karena soal konstruksi disebut jelas.

topic: A city heat action plan with automatic triggers
author: A municipal resilience officer drafting policy
setting: Action plan submitted to a city executive committee

title: The Tax Nobody Records
text:
The working week is now organized around a calendar rather than around work. A request for thirty minutes costs the sender nothing and costs the room whatever the room is worth, which is why the number of meetings grows without anybody deciding that it should. The expense is real and unrecorded, yet nobody enters the price of an hour's attention in any ledger, and so nobody defends it.

Defenders of the calendar point out, correctly, that decisions require discussion. The trouble is that most meetings are not decisions at all; they are broadcasts with an audience obliged to attend. Attendance obligations of this kind are rarely negotiable, since declining an invitation is interpreted as indifference rather than as a judgement about the value of the hour. A status update read aloud to eleven people consumes eleven hours in order to deliver information that could have been read in four minutes. Repeated across a quarter, that pattern produces exactly the exhaustion which firms then attempt to treat with wellbeing programmes. Every line of expenditure has its custodian; aggregate attention has none anywhere in the hierarchy.

Written updates are the obvious substitute, and they are harder than they look. Asynchronous composition imposes an intellectual discipline which verbal improvisation comfortably evades. A document must state its purpose in the opening line, and the writer has nowhere to hide behind tone of voice or a diagram drawn on a board. That difficulty is precisely the point, since legibility, unlike fluency, is verifiable by an independent reader. A proposal which cannot survive being read will not survive being implemented either. Writing also leaves a record, whereas a meeting leaves only the memories of whoever happened to attend it. A colleague who was never present can audit what a document claims. No such check exists for a recollection.

Some conversations resist the page, and pretending otherwise is its own kind of managerial vanity. Negotiations, disputes between colleagues who mistrust one another, and anything involving bad news belong in a room with faces in it. A serviceable rule follows from the distinction: convene when the outcome depends on how people react, and write when it depends on what is true. Most organizations have that rule inverted. Managerial preference for synchronous contact persists despite the accumulating evidence against it. Their own calendars show it plainly enough.
qs: Which statement best expresses the writer's argument?
Meetings should be abolished and replaced by written documents.
Meetings consume attention that no organization ever costs.
Wellbeing programmes are the best answer to staff exhaustion.
Written updates are easier to produce than a spoken report.

qs.evidence: yet nobody enters the price of an hour's attention in any ledger, and so nobody defends it.
qs.answer: Meetings consume attention that no organization ever costs.
qs.why: Argumen utamanya: rapat memakan perhatian yang tidak pernah dihitung siapa pun sebagai biaya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi hapus semua rapat terlalu jauh, karena penulis menyisakan ruang untuk negosiasi dan kabar buruk. Opsi program kesejahteraan justru yang dia sebut sebagai obat salah sasaran atas kelelahan yang dibuat kalender. Opsi menulis lebih gampang dibantah langsung: “Written updates … are harder than they look”.

qs: What example does the writer give of a meeting that is really a broadcast?
a negotiation between colleagues who do not trust one another
a discussion held before a difficult decision has been taken
a routine progress summary delivered by voice to a whole team
a wellbeing programme delivered to staff at a quarter's end

qs.evidence: A status update read aloud to eleven people consumes eleven hours in order to deliver information that could have been read in four minutes.
qs.answer: a routine progress summary delivered by voice to a whole team
qs.why: Contohnya laporan status yang dibacakan ke sebelas orang padahal bisa dibaca sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi negosiasi adalah jenis percakapan yang teks bilang memang harus di ruangan, jadi ia bukan siaran satu arah. Opsi diskusi sebelum keputusan justru pembelaan kalender yang penulis terima sebagai sah. Opsi program kesejahteraan adalah akibat kelelahan di teks, bukan contoh rapat siaran.

qs: How would you describe the writer's attitude towards meeting face to face?
Convinced that no discussion in a room can be justified now
Uneasy about saying which conversations belong in a room
Untroubled by how many hours a calendar quietly absorbs
Prepared to defend it for reactions while restricting its use

qs.evidence: Negotiations, disputes between colleagues who mistrust one another, and anything involving bad news belong in a room with faces in it.
qs.answer: Prepared to defend it for reactions while restricting its use
qs.why: Penulis membela pertemuan langsung untuk hal yang bergantung pada reaksi orang, tapi membatasi sisanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menolak semua pertemuan bertabrakan dengan daftar hal yang “belong in a room with faces in it”. Opsi ragu-ragu salah, karena penulis justru menyebut daftarnya dengan tegas dan memberi aturan kerja. Opsi tidak terganggu jam yang terserap kalender persis kebalikan keluhan pokoknya soal biaya perhatian yang tak tercatat.

qs: Which statement best paraphrases the writer's proposed rule?
Meet when a record is needed; write when speed matters more.
Meet when reactions matter; write when the facts are what matter.
Meet when the news is good; write when the news is going to disappoint.
Meet when a document fails; write when a meeting has failed.

qs.evidence: convene when the outcome depends on how people react, and write when it depends on what is true
qs.answer: Meet when reactions matter; write when the facts are what matter.
qs.why: Aturannya: berkumpul kalau hasilnya bergantung pada reaksi orang, menulis kalau bergantung pada kebenaran.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi soal rekaman membalik pembagiannya, sebab justru tulisan yang meninggalkan catatan dan rapat yang tidak. Opsi kabar baik versus buruk bertentangan dengan teks, yang menaruh kabar buruk di ruangan bersama negosiasi. Opsi saling menggantikan setelah gagal mengarang urutan yang nggak ada; kriterianya sifat hasilnya, bukan kegagalan format sebelumnya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer accepts that some subjects are better handled in person than on paper."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer accepts that some subjects are better handled in person than on paper.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Some conversations resist the page, and pretending otherwise is its own kind of managerial vanity.
qs.why: Penulis mengakui ada percakapan yang menolak dituliskan, jadi klaim ini parafrasa yang tepat.
qs.whyOthersFail: "False" salah karena pengakuan itu ada; "Not stated" salah karena kalimatnya eksplisit di paragraf akhir.

topic: The hidden cost of meetings and the case for written updates
author: An organisational consultant writing on working practices
setting: Management essay in a business monthly

title: Eighty Per Cent of the Hours
text:
The four-day week has moved from manifesto to measurement. Several hundred firms have now run trials in which staff worked roughly eighty per cent of their previous hours for unchanged pay, and the results were monitored rather than merely announced. The headline findings are encouraging, though the detail underneath them is considerably more interesting.

Most participating firms reported output holding steady, and a majority chose to retain the arrangement once the trial had finished. Sickness absence fell, and reported exhaustion fell further still. The caveat is straightforward, and the researchers state it themselves: firms which volunteer for an experiment of this kind are not a random sample of employers. An organization confident enough to try is probably managed competently already, and its results travel poorly to firms that are not.

Where output held, it was seldom because anybody worked faster. It held because a shorter week forced a review of activity that had continued out of habit. Recurring meetings were cancelled, approvals were delegated downwards, and reporting cycles were lengthened. The gains therefore came from removing waste which a five-day week had comfortably absorbed. That also explains why office-based firms fared better than those where a bed, a lathe or a checkout must be attended by somebody. Substitution of scheduling for effort is available only where the schedule itself belongs to the employer.

The honest conclusion is a conditional one. A shorter week appears to work where the work itself can be reorganised, and it struggles where the hours are the service being sold. Claiming more than that overstates the evidence, while claiming less ignores it. What the trials have established is narrower than the enthusiasts suggest and more subversive than the sceptics admit. The five-day week is a convention rather than a law of production, and conventions of that kind have been revised before. What the trials cannot settle is whether such a revision would hold once the novelty of being observed had worn off.
qs: What is the main point of the article?
Cutting hours suits every employer, whatever the business.
Cutting hours succeeds because employees begin to work faster.
Cutting hours succeeds where tasks and habits can be rebuilt.
Cutting hours has produced no usable evidence of any kind.

qs.evidence: A shorter week appears to work where the work itself can be reorganised, and it struggles where the hours are the service being sold.
qs.answer: Cutting hours succeeds where tasks and habits can be rebuilt.
