My grandmother watched forty years of European films in translation. She could recount their plots more accurately than I manage.

The class dimension is hard to ignore once noticed. Subtitles assume a viewer who reads quickly, sees clearly and was schooled in sustained attention, which characterizes a narrower population than the argument admits. Children, the partially sighted and anyone exhausted after a nine-hour shift are effectively told that the correct way to enjoy world cinema is unavailable to them. The purist position, held sincerely and expressed elegantly, ends up defending an audience of people who resemble the purist.

I watch subtitled films almost exclusively, which is why I am comfortable being rude about the reasoning. My preference is a preference, shaped by education and eyesight, and it acquires no moral weight from being widespread among critics. Let the dub be good, let the subtitles be well timed, and let us abandon the pretence that either route delivers the film untouched. Translation is loss arranged intelligently, and pretending otherwise merely conceals which losses we have chosen to stop noticing.
qs: What is the central claim of this essay?
Every route into a foreign film sacrifices something, so claiming purity is dishonest.
Subtitles cost a viewer less than dubbing, which is why purists prefer them.
Careful dubbing preserves more of a film than subtitles usually manage.
Watching without any translation is the only honest option for a serious viewer.

qs.evidence: Translation is loss arranged intelligently, and pretending otherwise merely conceals which losses we have chosen to stop noticing.
qs.answer: Every route into a foreign film sacrifices something, so claiming purity is dishonest.
qs.why: Kalimat “Translation is loss arranged intelligently” menutup argumennya: setiap jalur kehilangan sesuatu, sehingga mengaku murni berarti menyembunyikan kehilangan yang dipilih.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi subtitle lebih murah menukar argumen kehilangan menjadi urusan biaya; opsi sulih suara menyimpan lebih banyak memihak satu jalur, padahal teks menolak peringkat semacam itu; opsi tanpa terjemahan bertentangan dengan kalimat soal kemurnian yang murah bagi penutur aslinya.

qs: What does the remark about purity being inexpensive imply?
Viewers who read quickly lose less of the image than slower readers do.
Demanding purity costs little if translation was never your problem.
People raised inside a language judge dubbing more accurately than outsiders.
Purity became a popular demand once subtitles grew cheap to produce.

qs.evidence: Purity is inexpensive when you were raised inside the language the film was shot in.
qs.answer: Demanding purity costs little if translation was never your problem.
qs.why: Kalau kamu dibesarkan di dalam bahasa filmnya, tuntutan kemurnian tidak menuntut pengorbanan apa pun darimu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pembaca cepat memindahkan soal ke paragraf tentang subtitle; opsi penilaian lebih akurat menambahkan keunggulan yang tidak diklaim teks; opsi biaya produksi subtitle tidak pernah dibahas.

qs: What does the writer achieve by describing the cheap dub in this way?
He concedes the weakest cases with a joke before defending the practice.
He grants the purists their strongest example of a cheap dub and stops there.
He treats the cheap dub as evidence that voice work needs better funding.
He records the flapping mouths neutrally before turning to subtitles.

qs.evidence: Yes, the inexpensive dub arrives with mouths flapping out of sequence and a voice actor apparently reading from a menu.
qs.answer: He concedes the weakest cases with a joke before defending the practice.
qs.why: Dia mengakui contoh terburuk dengan lelucon, lalu melanjutkan pembelaan atas sulih suara yang dikerjakan serius.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi berhenti setelah memberi contoh terburuk bertentangan dengan paragraf berikutnya yang meneruskan pembelaan; opsi soal pendanaan menambahkan tuntutan yang tidak ada; opsi catatan netral mengabaikan lelucon mulut yang tidak sinkron dan aktor yang seperti membaca menu.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about glancing downwards?
A glance downwards costs a viewer little across a film of ordinary length.
Subtitles sit low enough to leave the composition of a shot intact.

qs.evidence: Every glance downwards is a small confiscation of the image, and the confiscations accumulate across two hours until a considerable portion of the composition has gone unwatched.
qs.answer: Reading the lines steadily removes parts of the picture you never see.
qs.why: Setiap tundukan mata disebut penyitaan kecil atas gambar, dan penyitaan itu menumpuk sepanjang dua jam.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: I watch subtitled films almost exclusively, which is why I am comfortable being rude about the reasoning.
qs.why: Dia menonton hampir selalu dengan subtitle, jadi klaim ini bertentangan langsung dengan kebiasaannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertabrakan dengan kata “almost exclusively”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena preferensinya disebut jelas.

title: Spilling the Beans at Five
text:
Children learn idioms rather later than the surrounding vocabulary, and the delay has proved unexpectedly informative for developmental linguistics. A five-year-old who handles several thousand words competently will nevertheless interpret spill the beans as an accident involving a saucepan. The literal reading is not a deficiency of intelligence. It is the sensible output of a system rewarded thousands of times for assuming that sentences mean the sum of their parts. Figurative competence requires the child to suspend that assumption selectively, which is a much harder operation.

Comprehension studies conducted with primary pupils suggest three factors govern the timing. Familiarity matters most, since frequently encountered expressions are acquired almost as single vocabulary items long before their internal logic is understood. Transparency matters next: an idiom whose literal image resembles its meaning, such as holding the reins, yields earlier than an opaque one like kicking the bucket. Context supplies the remainder, and children perform clearly better when an expression arrives inside a narrative that supports only one plausible interpretation.

The developmental sequence appears to run through a stage that researchers have described, perhaps too neatly, as productive error. Around the age of seven many children begin generating idioms of their own, announcing that a difficult classmate has lost his batteries or that a dull afternoon tasted of paper. These inventions are frequently dismissed as charming mistakes by adults, yet they demonstrate that the underlying mechanism has been grasped. The child has understood that language permits systematic borrowing between domains, and is now practising the borrowing without institutional approval.

Instructional implications follow, though cautiously. Explicit teaching of idiom lists produces reliable gains on recognition tests and disappointing gains on production, a pattern familiar from other areas of vocabulary work. Programmes that embed expressions inside repeated narrative, and that invite pupils to invent parallel figures, appear to transfer more reliably. One classroom study in a bilingual primary school reported that pupils who had invented their own metaphors retained the taught idioms considerably better nine weeks afterwards. The sample was small, however, and the effect has not yet been replicated elsewhere.

The wider point concerns what we count as linguistic knowledge. A learner who defines an idiom correctly on a written test may still fail to notice when a colleague deploys it ironically. Irony detection develops later still, extending well into adolescence. Figurative language is therefore best understood not as an ornamental layer added to a completed grammar, but as a slow negotiation between what sentences say and what speakers are doing with them. The negotiation is never entirely finished, in children or in the rest of us.
qs: What is the main conclusion of this article?
Idiom is the last layer added to a grammar that is otherwise complete.
Idiom is acquired chiefly through explicit teaching in the classroom.
Idiom develops earlier than the grammar it appears to depend upon.
Idiom belongs to learning how speakers use language, not to decorating grammar.

qs.evidence: Figurative language is therefore best understood not as an ornamental layer added to a completed grammar, but as a slow negotiation between what sentences say and what speakers are doing with them.
qs.answer: Idiom belongs to learning how speakers use language, not to decorating grammar.
qs.why: Kesimpulannya menyebut kiasan bukan lapisan hiasan di atas tata bahasa yang sudah selesai, melainkan perundingan lambat antara bunyi kalimat dan maksud pembicara.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi lapisan terakhir persis model yang ditolak kalimat itu; opsi diajarkan di kelas bertentangan dengan anak tujuh tahun yang menciptakan kiasan sendiri; opsi lebih dulu daripada tata bahasa bertentangan dengan urutan perkembangan di paragraf pertama.

Children of seven reproduce the idioms they hear at home with fair accuracy.
Children reach for figurative language before anybody teaches it to them.
Invented expressions show that a child has misheard an ordinary phrase.
Figurative invention appears mainly in children with unusually large vocabularies.

qs.evidence: Around the age of seven many children begin generating idioms of their own, announcing that a difficult classmate has lost his batteries or that a dull afternoon tasted of paper.
qs.answer: Children reach for figurative language before anybody teaches it to them.
qs.why: Anak-anak disebut “generating idioms of their own”, jadi kemampuan itu muncul tanpa diajarkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi mengulang yang didengar bertentangan dengan kata “generating”; opsi salah dengar memindahkan tahap productive error menjadi kekeliruan pendengaran; opsi kosakata besar menambahkan syarat yang tidak disebut teks.

qs: What does the aside about the researchers' label reveal about the writer's stance?
A mild reserve towards terminology that may tidy the evidence up.
Broad agreement with a label that the evidence appears to support.
Detached interest in a disagreement he considers merely verbal.
Firm rejection of a developmental sequence built on thin data.

qs.evidence: The developmental sequence appears to run through a stage that researchers have described, perhaps too neatly, as productive error.
qs.answer: A mild reserve towards terminology that may tidy the evidence up.
qs.why: Sisipan “perhaps too neatly” menandai keraguan halus pada istilahnya, bukan penolakan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi setuju penuh mengabaikan sisipan itu; opsi minat yang berjarak keliru karena dia tetap memakai urutan perkembangan itu sebagai kerangka; opsi menolak seluruh urutan jauh melampaui kata “perhaps”.

How often pupils meet the expression in ordinary classroom speech.
How clearly the surrounding story points towards one available reading.
How closely the picture inside an expression matches what it means.
How early children can define the expression in a written test.

qs.evidence: Transparency matters next: an idiom whose literal image resembles its meaning, such as holding the reins, yields earlier than an opaque one like kicking the bucket.
qs.answer: How closely the picture inside an expression matches what it means.
qs.why: Contoh holding the reins melawan kicking the bucket menunjukkan yang diukur adalah kedekatan gambar harfiah dengan maknanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi seberapa sering adalah definisi familiarity di kalimat sebelumnya; opsi cerita di sekelilingnya adalah faktor konteks; opsi tes tulis memakai detail paragraf terakhir yang membahas pengukuran, bukan transparansi.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Noticing an ironic use of an idiom develops after the ability to define it."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Noticing an ironic use of an idiom develops after the ability to define it.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Irony detection develops later still, extending well into adolescence.
qs.why: Teks menaruh deteksi ironi setelah kemampuan mendefinisikan, dan bilang itu berlanjut sampai remaja.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kata “later still”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena urutannya disebut eksplisit.

topic: how children come to understand idioms and figurative language
author: Dr Lestari Handayani
setting: an academic article on language development

title: A Story About Pens
text:
The claim that handwritten notes produce deeper learning than typed ones has travelled far beyond the evidence supporting it, which is itself a mildly interesting phenomenon. The original finding was modest and specific: students who wrote by hand recorded fewer words, paraphrased more, and performed better on questions requiring conceptual integration. Nothing in that result concerned ink, paper, or the general romance of stationery. The mechanism proposed was slowness, and slowness happens to be the one variable that popular retellings almost invariably omit.

Subsequent replications have complicated the picture considerably. Several studies found no reliable advantage once note quality was controlled statistically, and one large sample reported an advantage for typing among students who had been taught a summarizing strategy beforehand. The pattern that survives across the whole literature is not a contest between instruments. It is a contest between transcription and reformulation, which either instrument can support and either instrument can obstruct depending on how the student has been trained.

Transcription is attractive precisely because it feels so productive at the time. A verbatim record offers reassurance, it demands no decisions during the lecture, and it postpones the discomfort of discovering that a passage was never understood. Reformulation reverses each of those properties, which explains its unpopularity among students under examination pressure. The handwriting condition in the original experiments effectively imposed reformulation by physical means, since nobody can write quickly enough to transcribe a lecturer speaking at ordinary speed.

Two practical consequences deserve mention. First, interventions that teach reformulation directly appear to reduce the instrument effect towards insignificance, which suggests the instrument was never the active ingredient. Second, prohibiting laptops in lecture theatres, a policy several departments adopted enthusiastically after the initial publicity, may impose genuine costs. Students who type because handwriting is painful or slow for them lose an accommodation, while the promised benefits could be supplied by better teaching instead.

The episode illustrates a recurring hazard in educational research, and the hazard is not fraud. A carefully bounded finding acquires a memorable narrative, the narrative circulates faster than its qualifications, and the qualifications eventually arrive to an audience that has already redesigned its policies. Researchers bear some responsibility for the compression, since a paper titled after its mechanism rather than its instruments would have travelled differently. Readers bear the rest, for preferring a story about pens to a story about cognitive effort, which is admittedly the less charming of the two.
qs: How does the writer relate the choice of instrument to the quality of notes?
The instrument decides the outcome whatever training the student has had.
Handwriting helps most students, though a few type well enough to match it.
Training matters, but only after the student has settled on an instrument.
The tool matters less than whether the student rewords or copies.

qs.evidence: It is a contest between transcription and reformulation, which either instrument can support and either instrument can obstruct depending on how the student has been trained.
qs.answer: The tool matters less than whether the student rewords or copies.
qs.why: Teks menyebut pertandingan sebenarnya antara menyalin dan merumuskan ulang, dan kedua alat bisa mendukung atau menghalangi keduanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi alat menentukan membalik kalimat itu; opsi tulis tangan membantu sebagian besar mahasiswa mempertahankan keunggulan alat yang justru dibatalkan replikasi; opsi latihan menyusul pilihan alat menukar urutan sebab yang dinyatakan teks.

qs: What can be inferred about why handwriting appeared to help in the original study?
Writing by hand engages memory more directly than a keyboard manages.
Its slowness forced students to condense what they were hearing.
Students in that condition already had stronger note-taking habits.
Typing obliged those students to reword rather than to transcribe.

qs.evidence: The handwriting condition in the original experiments effectively imposed reformulation by physical means, since nobody can write quickly enough to transcribe a lecturer speaking at ordinary speed.
qs.answer: Its slowness forced students to condense what they were hearing.
qs.why: Tidak ada yang bisa menulis secepat dosen berbicara, jadi kondisi tulis tangan memaksa mahasiswa memadatkan bahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tinta dan ingatan adalah penjelasan populer yang teks sebut tidak diperlukan; opsi kebiasaan mencatat yang lebih kuat menambahkan seleksi peserta yang tidak disebut; opsi papan tombol memaksa merumuskan menukar kedua kondisi eksperimennya.

qs: What attitude does the closing sentence take towards readers?
Grateful to readers for carrying a useful finding so far so quickly.
Detached, treating the spread of the story as nobody's fault in particular.
Firmly reproachful, placing most of the blame on the audience.
Gently critical, while admitting the duller account is harder to like.

qs.evidence: Readers bear the rest, for preferring a story about pens to a story about cognitive effort, which is admittedly the less charming of the two.
qs.answer: Gently critical, while admitting the duller account is harder to like.
qs.why: Pembaca disebut menanggung sisanya karena memilih cerita soal pena, tetapi penulis langsung mengakui versi yang benar memang kurang menarik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi bersyukur membalik arah kalimat “bear the rest”; opsi berjarak mengabaikan penyaluran tanggung jawab itu; opsi teguran keras mengabaikan pengakuan “admittedly the less charming of the two” yang melunakkan kritiknya.

Careful findings travel together with all the limits attached to them.
Policies are normally revised only after the qualifications have arrived.
The catchy version outruns the small print and arrives after people have acted.
Memorable stories travel more slowly than the studies that produced them.

qs.evidence: A carefully bounded finding acquires a memorable narrative, the narrative circulates faster than its qualifications, and the qualifications eventually arrive to an audience that has already redesigned its policies.
qs.answer: The catchy version outruns the small print and arrives after people have acted.
qs.why: Narasi yang mudah diingat beredar lebih cepat daripada syaratnya, dan syaratnya tiba pada khalayak yang sudah merombak kebijakan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi batasan ikut beredar membalik kalimat itu; opsi kebijakan menunggu syarat bertentangan dengan “already redesigned”; opsi cerita lebih lambat menukar kecepatan keduanya.

True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Several studies found no reliable advantage once note quality was controlled statistically, and one large sample reported an advantage for typing among students who had been taught a summarizing strategy beforehand.

author: Dr Anwar Sulaiman

title: No Rush At All
text:
Workplace email occupies an awkward position between the memorandum and the conversation, and its politeness markers have accordingly become peculiar, a peculiarity worth documenting. A corpus of eleven thousand internal messages, collected from three organizations over two years, shows that the commonest softening device is not please but a temporal hedge. Writers postpone their demand behind expressions such as when you get a moment, no rush at all, or whenever convenient. The demand then arrives with a deadline attached two lines later, unhedged and unmistakable.

The salient property of these hedges is that recipients decode them accurately and resent them anyway. In follow-up interviews, participants described no rush as meaning today, and described just checking in as meaning you are late. This is not misunderstanding; the pragmatic content transmits perfectly, and what the hedge accomplishes instead is deniability. The sender may afterwards insist that no pressure was applied at all, since the surface text plainly says otherwise.

Frequency data reveal a hierarchy that nobody inside the three organizations ever described openly, nor indeed acknowledged privately. Hedging increases sharply when a writer addresses somebody senior, which is unsurprising, but it also increases when a writer addresses somebody in a separate department at an equivalent grade. Messages travelling downwards contain the fewest hedges and the highest proportion of bare imperatives. Politeness in this corpus therefore tracks the absence of authority rather than the presence of respect, a distinction that the everyday word politeness obscures rather badly.

Two further patterns merit comment, both distinctly unflattering. The exclamation mark functions as a class of its own, appearing four times more frequently in refusals than in messages granting a request. The extra cheerfulness apparently compensates for the disappointment it manufactures. Meanwhile apologies cluster at the outset of messages sent outside working hours, where they operate less as regret than as an announcement that the sender is virtuous, hardworking and awake at eleven.

None of this indicts anybody in particular, and senior staff hedge downwards only when a request is genuinely optional, which happens seldom. Hedged demands are a rational adaptation to a channel that preserves everything in writing and circulates it beyond the intended reader. A blunt instruction may be forwarded to a manager without further comment; a softened one presumably will not be. The corpus consequently documents an environment in which individuals write defensively, permanently, because the medium remembers and forwards. The politest sentence in the collection, offered without irony by a project lead, reads: happy to discuss whenever suits you, though I will need this before lunch.
qs: How does the corpus relate hedging to a writer's place in the hierarchy?
Hedging increases along with the respect a writer genuinely feels for the reader.
Hedging is spread fairly evenly across the grades in all three organizations.
Hedging is most frequent in the messages sent down to junior colleagues.
Hedging increases as the writer's authority over the reader decreases.

qs.evidence: Politeness in this corpus therefore tracks the absence of authority rather than the presence of respect, a distinction that the everyday word politeness obscures rather badly.
qs.answer: Hedging increases as the writer's authority over the reader decreases.
qs.why: Teks menyimpulkan kesopanan dalam korpus ini mengikuti ketiadaan wewenang, bukan kehadiran rasa hormat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi rasa hormat persis pembacaan yang dibedakan dan dibantah kalimat itu; opsi merata bertentangan dengan hierarki yang dipaparkan; opsi pesan ke bawah membalik temuan bahwa pesan ke bawah paling sedikit pelunakannya.

qs: What can be inferred about why writers prefer these temporal hedges?
The wording keeps recipients from working out when a task is really due.
The wording reflects a genuine wish to leave the recipient some room.
The wording is copied from senior colleagues without much thought.
The wording gives the sender a defence if the pressure is later challenged.

qs.evidence: The sender may afterwards insist that no pressure was applied at all, since the surface text plainly says otherwise.
qs.answer: The wording gives the sender a defence if the pressure is later challenged.
qs.why: Teks permukaannya bisa dipakai untuk bersikeras bahwa tidak ada tekanan yang diberikan, dan itulah gunanya bagi pengirim.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menyembunyikan tenggat bertentangan dengan tenggat yang dilekatkan dua baris kemudian; opsi niat tulus mengabaikan kata “deniability”; opsi meniru atasan menambahkan sebab yang tidak ada di data korpusnya.

qs: What is the effect of ending the article with the quoted message?
It lets one example expose the whole pattern with quiet humour.
It offers a model of courteous writing that readers might imitate.
It shows the corpus contained sentences the analysis could not classify.
It softens the findings by showing that the senders meant no harm.

qs.evidence: The politest sentence in the collection, offered without irony by a project lead, reads: happy to discuss whenever suits you, though I will need this before lunch.
qs.answer: It lets one example expose the whole pattern with quiet humour.
qs.why: Kalimat paling sopan dalam koleksi itu sekaligus memuat tenggat sebelum makan siang, jadi satu contoh merangkum temuan sambil membuatnya lucu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi contoh untuk ditiru salah maksud karena kalimatnya justru bukti pola yang dikritik; opsi tidak terklasifikasi menambahkan masalah metodologis yang tidak disebut; opsi melunakkan temuan bertentangan dengan frasa “offered without irony”.

qs: In the second paragraph, what does "deniability" amount to in practice?
Room to claim later that no demand was ever made.
A shared understanding that most deadlines are open to negotiation.
Protection for a recipient who misses a deadline never clearly stated.
Evidence that the sender was still working outside office hours.

qs.evidence: what the hedge accomplishes instead is deniability
qs.answer: Room to claim later that no demand was ever made.
qs.why: Yang dicapai pelunakan itu adalah ruang berkilah belakangan bahwa tidak ada tuntutan apa pun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tenggat bisa dirundingkan bertentangan dengan tenggat tegas di contoh penutup; opsi perlindungan bagi penerima membalik siapa yang dilindungi; opsi bekerja di luar jam kerja memakai detail permintaan maaf di paragraf empat yang tidak menjawab pertanyaan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Exclamation marks appear more often in messages from senior staff than from junior staff."
True
False
Not stated

qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: The exclamation mark functions as a class of its own, appearing four times more frequently in refusals than in messages granting a request.
qs.why: Teks hanya membandingkan penolakan dengan persetujuan. Perbandingan antar jenjang jabatan tidak pernah dibuat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” dan “False” butuh angka per jenjang yang tidak ada; kalimat terdekat membandingkan hal yang berbeda.

author: Dr Wulan Perdani
setting: an academic article on corpus linguistics

title: Tension Is Not Ugliness
text:
Musical dissonance is routinely described as unpleasant, and the description survives despite a century of evidence that it depends heavily on what a listener has previously heard. The physical account is elegant and incomplete. Two tones whose frequencies sit close together produce a roughness in the ear that most listeners report as tension. The effect can be measured in populations who have never received formal training. It does not follow that the tension is experienced as ugly, and the difference between tension and ugliness carries most of the argument.

A listening experiment conducted with two hundred adults illustrates the distinction. Participants rated chords for pleasantness after four weeks of daily exposure to unfamiliar harmonic material, one group hearing dense chords in a narrative film context, the other hearing identical chords in isolation. Both groups showed increased tolerance, but only the film group reported enjoyment. The chord had not changed. What had changed was the listener's sense of what the chord was for, which suggests that meaning arrives before comfort rather than after it.

Historical evidence points in a similar direction, if less tidily. Intervals now taught to beginners as consonant were once formally prohibited in liturgical composition, and audiences in several documented cases laughed at works whose harmonic language later became a standard examination text. Retrospective accounts of these episodes tend to praise the composer and patronize the audience. A less flattering reading is available: the audience heard accurately, and simply lacked the twenty years of subsequent listening that made the material legible.

The pedagogical consequence is uncomfortable for curriculum designers. If tolerance grows through exposure embedded in meaningful context, then teaching harmony as a set of rules about permitted intervals inverts the actual developmental order. Pupils would presumably acquire more if the strange chord arrived attached to a story, a film sequence or a physical gesture, with the theoretical vocabulary supplied afterwards. Several conservatories have experimented along these lines, and the reported results are encouraging without yet being conclusive.

There remains a residual puzzle that the exposure account does not dissolve. Certain combinations continue to be rated as distressing by trained listeners who have encountered them for decades and who can explain their function fluently. Familiarity has not domesticated them, which implies a floor beneath which acculturation does not reach. Where exactly that floor lies is unresolved, and the honest position is that we know considerably more about why dissonance becomes acceptable than about why a stubborn residue never does.
qs: What is the central argument of this article?
Rough-sounding chords are unpleasant for most listeners without training.
Rough-sounding chords create tension, which listeners need not hear as ugly.
Tension and ugliness turn out, on measurement, to be much the same property.
Roughness in a chord can be measured, but enjoyment cannot be studied.

qs.evidence: It does not follow that the tension is experienced as ugly, and the difference between tension and ugliness carries most of the argument.
qs.answer: Rough-sounding chords create tension, which listeners need not hear as ugly.
qs.why: Teks menyatakan ketegangan itu terukur, tetapi tidak dengan sendirinya dialami sebagai keburukan, dan pembedaan itu menopang seluruh argumennya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tidak nyaman bagi yang tidak terlatih bertentangan dengan pendengar yang menikmatinya tanpa pelatihan formal; opsi ketegangan sama dengan keburukan persis yang dibantah; opsi kenikmatan tidak bisa diteliti bertentangan dengan eksperimen empat pekan yang justru mengukurnya.

qs: What does the outcome of the four-week listening experiment suggest?
Tolerance grew only in the group that heard the chords in isolation.
Four weeks is long enough for almost any listener to enjoy such chords.
Film music teaches listeners to hear harmony rather more accurately.
Enjoyment depends on the purpose a listener can attach to a sound.

qs.evidence: Both groups showed increased tolerance, but only the film group reported enjoyment.
qs.answer: Enjoyment depends on the purpose a listener can attach to a sound.
qs.why: Kedua kelompok jadi lebih tahan, tetapi hanya kelompok film melaporkan kenikmatan, padahal akordnya tidak berubah; jadi fungsi yang bisa dibayangkan pendengar itulah yang menentukan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi hanya kelompok isolasi membalik hasilnya; opsi empat pekan cukup bagi siapa pun menggeneralisasi melampaui datanya, sebab kelompok isolasi tidak menikmati; opsi mendengar harmoni lebih akurat menambahkan kemampuan yang tidak diukur.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards the retrospective accounts of those episodes?
Broadly supportive, since the audience of the day plainly misjudged the work.
Detached, since the record of those episodes is too thin to weigh either way.
Sceptical, since they flatter the composer at the audience's expense.
Appreciative, given how fully they preserve the laughter in the hall.

qs.evidence: Retrospective accounts of these episodes tend to praise the composer and patronize the audience.
qs.answer: Sceptical, since they flatter the composer at the audience's expense.
qs.why: Kata “patronize” menandai penilaian penulis: laporan belakangan itu memuji komposer sambil merendahkan pendengar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi mendukung membalik sikap itu; opsi berjarak menambahkan keraguan pada kelengkapan catatan yang tidak diajukan teks; opsi menghargai pelestarian tawa salah arah karena keberatannya justru pada cara catatan itu memperlakukan pendengar.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about a floor in the final paragraph?
Some sounds stay disturbing however long a listener lives with them.
Long exposure softens almost any combination in the end.
Trained listeners lose the words to explain what such chords do.
Acculturation reaches every combination once its floor has been identified.

qs.evidence: Familiarity has not domesticated them, which implies a floor beneath which acculturation does not reach.
qs.answer: Some sounds stay disturbing however long a listener lives with them.
qs.why: Kalimat soal “a floor beneath which acculturation does not reach” berarti sebagian kombinasi tetap mengganggu meski sudah lama dikenal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi semuanya melunak membalik kalimat itu; opsi kehilangan kemampuan menjelaskan bertentangan dengan pendengar yang bisa menjelaskan fungsinya dengan lancar; opsi menjangkau semuanya menolak kata “does not reach”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Listeners with no formal training can also register the roughness of close tones."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Listeners with no formal training can also register the roughness of close tones.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The effect can be measured in populations who have never received formal training.
qs.why: Efek itu terukur pada orang yang belum pernah dilatih, jadi klaimnya parafrasa yang benar.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena datanya disebut di paragraf pertama.

topic: why listeners come to accept musical dissonance
author: Dr Bening Larasati
setting: an academic article on music perception

title: Two Kinds of Variety
text:
Recommendation systems are commonly accused of narrowing taste, and the accusation is popular partly because it is easy to picture. The listener is imagined descending a tunnel, each selection slightly more similar to the last, until the whole musical world has contracted to a single mood. Measurement complicates that picture considerably without entirely refuting it. Aggregate consumption on the platforms studied has become more diverse by several standard metrics, while individual consumption has frequently become less so, and both statements describe the same population.

The apparent contradiction resolves once diversity is defined carefully. Catalogue diversity counts how many distinct works receive attention across all users. The figure rises when a system surfaces obscure material to the small audiences likely to accept it. Individual diversity counts how far a single listener travels within a period, and this figure falls when the system successfully predicts preference. A platform can therefore expand the collective repertoire while confining each subscriber to a comfortable corner of it, and marketing departments may honestly cite whichever number flatters the product.

Longitudinal data introduce a further wrinkle concerning the direction of causation. Listeners whose diversity declined most sharply after adopting algorithmic playlists were, in one analysis of three years of logs, already among the least exploratory beforehand. The system amplified an existing disposition rather than creating it, which is a weaker claim than the tunnel metaphor implies and a more difficult one to legislate against. Regulation designed for a machine that manufactures narrowness will miss a machine that merely rewards it.

Interventions have nevertheless been tested, with mixed and instructive outcomes. Inserting deliberately unfamiliar items at a low rate increases exploration modestly and reduces satisfaction scores immediately, which explains why few commercial systems retain the feature after trialling it. Explanations perform better than surprises: telling a listener why an item was chosen raises willingness to accept the unexpected. An unexplained recommendation feels like an error, whereas an explained one feels like an invitation.

The broader lesson concerns what these systems are optimizing, and they are not optimizing for the listener a critic has in mind. They are optimizing for continuation, a measurable proxy that correlates with satisfaction in the short term and with something closer to sedation over longer intervals. Nobody in the industry ever chose sedation. It emerged from a reasonable objective, pursued diligently, in the absence of any metric capable of noticing the difference between contentment and mild anaesthesia.
qs: How are the two kinds of diversity related on these platforms?
Both measures rise together whenever the system predicts preference well.
The shared catalogue can widen while each listener's range narrows.
Each listener's range widens while the shared catalogue quietly contracts.
The two measures are close enough that either can stand for the other.

qs.evidence: A platform can therefore expand the collective repertoire while confining each subscriber to a comfortable corner of it, and marketing departments may honestly cite whichever number flatters the product.
qs.answer: The shared catalogue can widen while each listener's range narrows.
qs.why: Sebuah platform bisa memperluas repertoar bersama sambil mengurung tiap pelanggan di sudut yang nyaman, jadi dua angka itu bisa bergerak berlawanan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi bergerak bersama membalik temuan itu; opsi kebalikan menukar kedua ukurannya; opsi keduanya bisa saling mewakili menghapus pembedaan yang justru dipakai bagian pemasaran untuk memilih angka yang menyanjung produk.

qs: What can be inferred from the three years of listening logs?
The system narrowed the taste of listeners who had been exploring widely.
The system seems to intensify habits its users brought with them.
Three years is too short an interval for any change to show up.
Listeners who explored least were the ones least affected by the playlists.

qs.evidence: Listeners whose diversity declined most sharply after adopting algorithmic playlists were, in one analysis of three years of logs, already among the least exploratory beforehand.
qs.answer: The system seems to intensify habits its users brought with them.
qs.why: Yang keragamannya jatuh paling tajam justru sudah paling jarang menjelajah sebelumnya, jadi sistemnya memperkuat kecenderungan lama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi penjelajah luas yang menyempit membalik datanya; opsi tiga tahun terlalu singkat bertentangan dengan penurunan tajam yang dilaporkan; opsi penjelajah paling sedikit paling tidak terpengaruh membalik hasil analisis itu.

qs: What does the writer imply by describing the long-term result as sedation?
That endless continuation dulls listeners rather than pleasing them.
That the industry chose to dull its listeners once the measure existed.
That satisfaction and continuation amount to much the same measurement.
That short-term measures track wellbeing closely enough for practical use.

qs.evidence: They are optimizing for continuation, a measurable proxy that correlates with satisfaction in the short term and with something closer to sedation over longer intervals.
qs.answer: That endless continuation dulls listeners rather than pleasing them.
qs.why: Kata itu penilaian: mendengarkan yang terus berlanjut akhirnya menumpulkan, bukan menyenangkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi industri sengaja bertentangan dengan kalimat bahwa tidak ada yang memilih sedasi; opsi dua ukuran sama menghapus pembedaan jangka pendek dan panjang; opsi ukuran pendek memadai bertentangan dengan seluruh paragraf itu.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the closing point of the fourth paragraph?
A suggestion feels much the same whether or not a reason is supplied.
Explaining a choice makes listeners suspect the system has slipped.
Give a reason and an odd suggestion reads as an offer, not a fault.
Unexpected items are accepted most readily when nothing is explained.

qs.evidence: An unexplained recommendation feels like an error, whereas an explained one feels like an invitation.
qs.answer: Give a reason and an odd suggestion reads as an offer, not a fault.
qs.why: Rekomendasi tanpa penjelasan terasa seperti kesalahan, sedangkan yang dijelaskan terasa seperti tawaran.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi terasa sama menghapus perbedaan itu; opsi penjelasan memancing curiga membalik arahnya; opsi tanpa penjelasan lebih mudah diterima menukar kedua kondisi.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Most commercial systems have kept the feature that inserts unfamiliar items."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Most commercial systems have kept the feature that inserts unfamiliar items.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Inserting deliberately unfamiliar items at a low rate increases exploration modestly and reduces satisfaction scores immediately, which explains why few commercial systems retain the feature after trialling it.
qs.why: Teks bilang hanya sedikit sistem komersial yang mempertahankan fitur itu, jadi klaim ini bertolak belakang.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertentangan dengan kata “few”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena nasib fitur itu dilaporkan.

topic: how recommendation systems affect the diversity of listening
author: Dr Iqbal Nurhadi
setting: an academic article on algorithmic recommendation

title: Going Beautifully
text:
Irony presents an unusual problem for models of comprehension, because the listener must reject the sentence that was actually uttered. When a colleague surveys a collapsed schedule and remarks that this is going beautifully, no dictionary entry has been violated. Every word retains its ordinary sense, and the intended meaning nevertheless sits at some distance from the sum of those senses. Any adequate account must therefore explain how a hearer selects a reading that the words do not encode.

Response-time studies indicate that ironic interpretation is not uniformly slower than literal interpretation, contrary to earlier expectations. Delays appear when the context is thin and vanish when the situation strongly supports the ironic reading, which suggests that hearers are not first computing a literal meaning and then discarding it. Instead they appear to weigh several candidate readings against expectation. The relevant expectation concerns what a reasonable speaker would plausibly be doing here, and mismatch with that expectation functions as the trigger.

Prosody supplies powerful cues in speech, though the cues are less standardized than folk accounts assume. A flattened contour, a lengthened vowel and a slight pause before the evaluative word all raise the probability of an ironic reading, yet none is necessary and none is sufficient. Written contexts lack these signals altogether, which is why irony in text depends disproportionately on shared background and why it fails so spectacularly across audiences that do not share it. The failure is informative rather than accidental, since it exposes how much of the work was being done by assumed common ground.

Developmental findings suggest a long acquisition curve, extending far past the mastery of metaphor. Children of eight typically detect that a speaker is being unkind before they can articulate that the speaker means the opposite of the utterance. The ability to detect gentle self-directed irony emerges later still. Adults vary considerably as well, and the variation correlates less with vocabulary size than with familiarity with the speaker. That places a social relationship rather than a lexicon at the centre of the phenomenon.

One methodological caution deserves emphasis. Almost all experimental materials are constructed by researchers who already know which reading is intended, and constructed irony tends to be tidier than the spontaneous variety. Recordings from unscripted conversation contain a substantial proportion of cases in which participants themselves later disagreed about whether the remark had been ironic. If competent native speakers cannot always adjudicate, then irony may be better modelled as a negotiated outcome than as a message successfully decoded.
qs: What is the main conclusion of this article?
Irony is recognized reliably by listeners who know the speaker well.
Irony is worked out between speakers rather than sent as a fixed message.
Irony is a coded message that hearers recover from the words themselves.
Irony follows rules that the research has by now largely written down.

qs.evidence: If competent native speakers cannot always adjudicate, then irony may be better modelled as a negotiated outcome than as a message successfully decoded.
qs.answer: Irony is worked out between speakers rather than sent as a fixed message.
qs.why: Karena penutur jati yang kompeten tidak selalu bisa memutuskan, ironi lebih tepat dimodelkan sebagai hasil yang dirundingkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pendengar yang mengenal pembicara menambahkan syarat yang tidak diuji teks; opsi pesan terkode persis model yang ditolak kalimat itu; opsi aturan sudah tertulis bertentangan dengan catatan bahwa bahan penelitiannya sendiri terbatas.

qs: What do the response-time findings suggest about how hearers process irony?
Hearers weigh possible readings at once instead of working in stages.
Hearers compute the literal sense first and then set it aside.
Ironic readings take longer whatever the situation supplies.
A thin context makes the ironic reading arrive faster than the literal one.

qs.evidence: Delays appear when the context is thin and vanish when the situation strongly supports the ironic reading, which suggests that hearers are not first computing a literal meaning and then discarding it.
qs.answer: Hearers weigh possible readings at once instead of working in stages.
qs.why: Jeda muncul saat konteksnya tipis dan hilang saat situasi mendukung, jadi pembacaan ditimbang serentak, bukan bertahap.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi berurutan persis model yang dibantah kalimat itu; opsi selalu lebih lama bertentangan dengan kata “vanish”; opsi konteks tipis lebih cepat membalik datanya.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards the standard experimental materials?
Confident, since such materials are built to exclude the researcher's own reading.
Dismissive, treating experiments of this kind as beside the point.
Cautious, treating them as neater than the speech they stand for.
Appreciative, since they capture spontaneous conversation closely enough.

qs.evidence: Almost all experimental materials are constructed by researchers who already know which reading is intended, and constructed irony tends to be tidier than the spontaneous variety.
qs.answer: Cautious, treating them as neater than the speech they stand for.
qs.why: Dia mencatat bahan eksperimen dibuat oleh peneliti yang sudah tahu pembacaan yang dimaksud, dan ironi buatan lebih rapi daripada ironi spontan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi percaya penuh bertentangan dengan catatan itu; opsi membuang semua eksperimen jauh melampaui peringatannya, karena dia tetap memakai temuan waktu reaksi; opsi menangkap percakapan spontan justru kebalikan dari yang dinyatakan teks.

qs: What makes "going beautifully" a problem for models of comprehension?
One of the words has taken on a new sense in office speech.
The remark is too short for a hearer to place it in context.
The remark passes no judgement on the timetable at all.
Each word keeps its usual sense, yet the meaning comes out inverted.

qs.evidence: When a colleague surveys a collapsed schedule and remarks that this is going beautifully, no dictionary entry has been violated.
qs.answer: Each word keeps its usual sense, yet the meaning comes out inverted.
qs.why: Teks menegaskan tidak ada entri kamus yang dilanggar, padahal maksud ucapannya justru kebalikan dari bunyinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi arti baru bertentangan dengan “no dictionary entry has been violated”; opsi terlalu singkat menambahkan alasan yang tidak disebut; opsi tanpa penilaian menghapus inti ironinya, sebab ucapan itu menilai jadwal yang runtuh.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Knowing the speaker predicts irony detection better than the size of a listener's vocabulary."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Knowing the speaker predicts irony detection better than the size of a listener's vocabulary.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Adults vary considerably as well, and the variation correlates less with vocabulary size than with familiarity with the speaker.
qs.why: Teks bilang variasinya lebih terkait keakraban dengan pembicara daripada ukuran kosakata, dan klaim ini menyatakan hal yang sama.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan perbandingan itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena keduanya dibandingkan langsung.

author: Dr Farhan Alwi
setting: an academic article on pragmatics

title: A Performance With No Archive
text:
The karaoke booth is the last place in the city where an audience is contractually obliged to be generous, and this may explain its extraordinary survival. Streaming demolished the recorded music economy, the neighbourhood record shop and much of the pleasurable suspense that once preceded a release. Yet the cramped booth with its tacky remote control and its appalling wallpaper continues to prosper. Something is being purchased there that no immaculate recording could ever underwrite: the transient, unindexed thrill of an amateur running a risk aloud.

Critics of the genre habitually arrive brandishing an argument about authenticity, and the argument is remarkably fragile. Singing somebody else's song is described as passive consumption, as though the cover version were a modern disgrace rather than the ordinary condition of music for most of recorded history. Standards had always existed in order to be reinterpreted, their authority residing in the accumulation of imperfect attempts rather than in one definitive rendition. The notion that a song belongs permanently to whoever recorded it first is a recent invention, roughly contemporary with the technology that made first recordings profitable.

What actually happens inside the booth is stranger than either the critics or the defenders admit. Participants select songs they cannot sing, deliberately, and the failure is the entertainment. A colleague of mine, an accountant of famous composure, performs one enormous ballad every December with an intensity that would embarrass a professional. Nobody ever discusses the performance afterwards at work, an omission everyone honours without negotiation, as though discretion were the price of admission. The booth operates as a small licensed exemption from ordinary self-presentation, and the licence expires at the door.

There is a generational shift worth recording, since the practice keeps mutating. Younger patrons increasingly film the performance, which introduces exactly the audience the room was designed to exclude. A recording that may later be circulated changes the whole calculation: risk returns, ambition retreats, and people select the safe song. Several booths in my district now advertise a no-filming policy in large letters, an intervention that would have been incomprehensible fifteen years ago and is now apparently a commercial advantage.

I am no advocate of nostalgia, and the wallpaper genuinely is appalling. But the booth preserves something that our better-documented culture has been steadily eliminating, which is a performance with no archive attached. You sing badly, everybody applauds insincerely, and the evidence evaporates before anyone thinks to preserve it for subsequent ridicule. If that arrangement now requires a printed policy on the door to survive, then the policy is not a quaint restriction. It is a small piece of infrastructure for the increasingly rare experience of doing something imperfectly in front of people who will not keep the file.
qs: What is the writer's central claim about the karaoke booth?
It survives because a booth costs a customer less than a streaming subscription.
It gives customers the practice they need to sing familiar songs better.
It protects the chance to perform badly without leaving any record.
It offers a stage to people who would never be given one elsewhere.

qs.evidence: It is a small piece of infrastructure for the increasingly rare experience of doing something imperfectly in front of people who will not keep the file.
qs.answer: It protects the chance to perform badly without leaving any record.
qs.why: Bilik itu disebut infrastruktur kecil bagi pengalaman melakukan sesuatu dengan buruk di depan orang yang tidak akan menyimpan berkasnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi lebih murah daripada langganan tidak pernah dijadikan alasan di teks; opsi melatih menyanyi bertentangan dengan pilihan lagu yang tidak bisa mereka nyanyikan; opsi panggung bagi yang tidak punya panggung memindahkan intinya dari ketiadaan rekaman ke soal kesempatan tampil.

qs: What can be inferred about the effect of filming inside the booth?
Filming encourages singers to attempt the most demanding material they know.
Filming pushes singers towards the choices that cannot embarrass them.
Safe songs were the usual choice long before phones entered the booth.
Filming matters less than the number of people listening in the room.

qs.evidence: A recording that may later be circulated changes the whole calculation: risk returns, ambition retreats, and people select the safe song.
qs.answer: Filming pushes singers towards the choices that cannot embarrass them.
qs.why: Rekaman yang bisa disebarkan mengubah seluruh perhitungan: risiko kembali, ambisi surut, dan orang memilih lagu yang aman.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi materi paling sulit membalik kalimat itu; opsi lagu aman sejak dulu bertentangan dengan paragraf yang menyebut pilihan berani muncul justru tanpa rekaman; opsi jumlah pendengar menambahkan faktor yang tidak diukur teks.

qs: What is the writer's tone in describing his colleague's December performance?
Faintly uncomfortable at a colleague who takes the evening too seriously.
Admiring of a performance he considers better than professional work.
Measured, reporting a yearly habit that the office simply accepts.
Fond amusement at a controlled man briefly abandoning his composure.

qs.evidence: A colleague of mine, an accountant of famous composure, performs one enormous ballad every December with an intensity that would embarrass a professional.
qs.answer: Fond amusement at a controlled man briefly abandoning his composure.
qs.why: Kontras antara akuntan yang terkenal tenang dan balada yang meledak setahun sekali digambarkan dengan geli yang bersahabat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tidak nyaman salah membaca kata “embarrass”, yang di teks menggambarkan intensitasnya bukan rasa malu penulis; opsi memuji melampaui perbandingan itu; opsi laporan terukur mengabaikan pilihan kata yang jelas geli.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about a licence in the third paragraph?
Inside, you may drop the face you keep in public; outside, it returns.
The room asks for the same self-control that the office already requires.
The permission granted inside lasts well beyond the end of the session.
Customers need permission from the staff before they are allowed to sing.

qs.evidence: The booth operates as a small licensed exemption from ordinary self-presentation, and the licence expires at the door.
qs.answer: Inside, you may drop the face you keep in public; outside, it returns.
qs.why: Bilik itu disebut pengecualian berizin dari cara kita menampilkan diri, dan izinnya berakhir di pintu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kontrol yang sama membalik kata “exemption”; opsi izin berlanjut bertentangan dengan “expires at the door”; opsi izin dari petugas membaca kiasan izin sebagai prosedur.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Booth owners say the no-filming rule was introduced because customers demanded it."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Booth owners say the no-filming rule was introduced because customers demanded it.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Several booths in my district now advertise a no-filming policy in large letters, an intervention that would have been incomprehensible fifteen years ago and is now apparently a commercial advantage.
qs.why: Teks cuma bilang kebijakan itu dipasang dan tampak menguntungkan. Siapa yang meminta dan apa kata pemiliknya tidak pernah disebut.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” menambahkan atribusi yang tidak ada, dan “False” juga salah karena teks tidak membantah asal-usul aturannya.

topic: karaoke booths, cover versions and filming
author: Selia Mahendra
setting: a cultural commentary on karaoke

title: The Voice in Your Ear
text:
There is a voice that did not exist twenty years ago and now inhabits several million headphones. It is warm without being loud, confidential without being intimate, and it pauses before adjectives in a manner suggesting that the adjective was arrived at reluctantly. Everybody recognizes it instantly, and nobody has ever admitted to practising it. The uniformity is the interesting part, since no institution issued a directive and no examination certifies the delivery.

The origins are not mysterious, since broadcasting simply discovered an acoustic solution to a technological constraint. Public radio developed a register for the ear rather than the hall, and the register worked. The technology then distributed it to anybody possessing a microphone and an opinion. What arrived with it was a set of implied credentials. The voice signals that its proprietor has consulted the literature, has deliberated, and is far too reasonable to raise the volume. That is a considerable quantity of authority to obtain through breath control alone. Credibility, previously assembled from evidence and affiliation, became available as an acoustic property.

My objection concerns the transfer of that authority to content it has not earned. I have heard a supplement salesman discuss mitochondria in the same thoughtful cadence a historian reserves for the partition of an empire. My ear, conditioned by several thousand hours of respectable programmes, manufactured trust before my judgement had been consulted, and the trust was retracted within a minute. It should never have been extended, and the fact that it was extended tells me something unflattering about how I actually evaluate claims. Persuasion accomplished through timbre bypasses the machinery we normally reserve for evaluating propositions.

Defenders point out, fairly, that every medium develops a house style and that nobody complains about the conventions of the lecture theatre. The difference is intimacy, and intimacy alters the arithmetic of scepticism. A lecturer stands at a distance and is visibly performing a role. The voice in your ear at half past eleven imitates a companion thinking aloud, and the imitation disables the sceptical apparatus that visible performance retains switched on. Warmth is not a neutral delivery mechanism; it is an argument made before any arguments arrive, disguised as an absence of rhetoric.

I offer all this as a devoted listener holding four subscriptions and no intention of cancelling any of them. The register has genuinely improved public explanation, and I would not return to the era of the shouting broadcaster for any consideration. But I have instituted a modest private discipline, recommended here without much expectation of adoption. Once a week I read a transcript instead of listening, and roughly half the time the argument proves thinner than the voice implied. That is a humbling proportion for anybody who considers himself a careful thinker.
qs: What is the writer's main claim about this style of speaking?
A soothing delivery works only on listeners already inclined to agree.
A soothing delivery persuades before any claim has been examined.
Public radio built the register in order to sell what its advertisers wanted.
Listeners have learnt to allow for the warmth and judge the argument alone.

qs.evidence: Warmth is not a neutral delivery mechanism; it is an argument made before any arguments arrive, disguised as an absence of rhetoric.
qs.answer: A soothing delivery persuades before any claim has been examined.
qs.why: Teks menyebut kehangatan bukan saluran netral melainkan argumen yang datang sebelum argumen mana pun, menyamar sebagai ketiadaan retorika.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi hanya bekerja pada yang sudah setuju bertentangan dengan pengakuan penulis yang langsung percaya pada penjual suplemen; opsi radio publik menukar asal-usul register dengan contoh penjual; opsi pendengar sudah bisa mengabaikan kehangatan bertentangan dengan percobaan transkripnya sendiri.

qs: What can be inferred from his reaction to the supplement salesman?
He examined the claims about mitochondria before deciding what to think.
Years of listening have taught him to distrust a warm voice on principle.
He was persuaded because the salesman's evidence was unusually specific.
His trust was produced by habit rather than by any assessment.

qs.evidence: My ear, conditioned by several thousand hours of respectable programmes, manufactured trust before my judgement had been consulted, and the trust was retracted within a minute.
qs.answer: His trust was produced by habit rather than by any assessment.
qs.why: Telinganya yang terlatih ribuan jam memproduksi kepercayaan sebelum penilaiannya dimintai pendapat, lalu kepercayaan itu ditarik dalam satu menit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi memeriksa klaim lebih dulu membalik urutan itu; opsi curiga secara prinsip bertentangan dengan kata “manufactured trust”; opsi bukti yang spesifik menambahkan mutu bukti yang tidak dinilai teks.

qs: What does the writer's weekly habit with transcripts reveal about his stance?
He has given up the medium after finding the arguments so thin.
He counts himself among the listeners this register manages to fool.
He trusts his own ear rather more than other listeners' judgement.
He believes the printed argument is usually stronger than it sounds.

qs.evidence: Once a week I read a transcript instead of listening, and roughly half the time the argument proves thinner than the voice implied.
qs.answer: He counts himself among the listeners this register manages to fool.
qs.why: Sekali sepekan dia membaca transkrip alih-alih mendengarkan, dan separuh waktu argumennya lebih tipis daripada yang disiratkan suara; jadi kritiknya termasuk untuk dirinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi meninggalkan medium bertentangan dengan empat langganan yang dia sebut; opsi memercayai telinganya sendiri membalik alasan percobaan itu; opsi argumen cetak lebih kuat membalik hasilnya, yaitu justru lebih tipis.

qs: What are the "implied credentials" that arrive with this register?
Formal qualifications that broadcasters obtain before they are allowed to record.
A reputation earned across years of programmes on a respected network.
An impression of study and care the voice never has to prove.
Evidence and affiliation of the ordinary academic kind.

qs.evidence: What arrived with it was a set of implied credentials.
qs.answer: An impression of study and care the voice never has to prove.
qs.why: Yang datang bersama register itu adalah kesan sudah membaca dan menimbang, padahal tidak ada yang pernah diuji.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kualifikasi formal bertentangan dengan teks yang menyebut tidak ada ujian menyertifikasi cara bicara itu; opsi reputasi jaringan memindahkan sumbernya ke lembaga, padahal teks menyebut teknologi menyebarkannya ke siapa pun; opsi bukti akademik justru hal yang digantikan oleh suara.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer has cancelled the podcast subscriptions he used to hold."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer has cancelled the podcast subscriptions he used to hold.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: I offer all this as a devoted listener holding four subscriptions and no intention of cancelling any of them.
qs.why: Dia menyebut masih punya empat langganan dan tidak berniat berhenti, jadi klaim ini bertentangan langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertabrakan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena langganannya disebut eksplisit.

topic: the persuasive style of podcast narration
author: Tirta Anggraeni
setting: a cultural commentary on audio narration

title: Thursday Night for Saturday Morning
text:
The queue forms on Thursday evening for a shop that opens on Saturday, and by midnight it has acquired a social structure of remarkable complexity. There are veterans who bring folding chairs and share a thermos, and there are newcomers who underestimated the temperature and are suffering discreetly in fashionable jackets. Somewhere near the front sits a teenager remunerated for occupying a position on behalf of somebody arriving at dawn by taxi. Everybody understands the arrangement, and nobody objects noticeably.

Commentators reliably characterize the scene as evidence of hollow materialism, a verdict I consider simultaneously accurate and entirely beside the point. The shoes are not the reason anybody sleeps on a pavement. Were the objects the objective, the resale market would satisfy the appetite immediately and at moderate expense, since identical items reach the internet within hours. What the queue supplies cannot be dispatched by courier, and the participants understand this rather better than the columnists do. Scarcity organizes the entire performance, and scarcity is manufactured deliberately by whoever prints the announcement.

Consider what actually occurs overnight. Strangers compile an informal register of position and legitimacy, adjudicate disputes without any authority, and negotiate rotas for the lavatory of a neighbouring restaurant. They construct a temporary society whose entire purpose expires at ten in the morning. Nobody applies for permission, and a visitor from another century would recognize the pattern instantly, presumably enquiring which saint was involved. Improvised institutions of this kind are rarely documented, since they dissolve before any administrator notices their existence.

The manufacturers have of course noticed, and their response has been to industrialize the scarcity that produced the queue in the first place. Ballots, apps and timed releases now distribute the same objects with far less inconvenience, and the queues are dwindling accordingly. Efficiency has arrived and taken the ritual away with it. Convenience, once installed, discreetly dismantles the inconvenience through which strangers previously became acquaintances. A friend who has queued for eleven years reports that the ballot feels fairer and that he has acquired no new acquaintance whatever since its introduction. He delivered both halves of that sentence in an identical flat tone.

I have never queued for footwear and expect I never shall, my own irrationalities being quieter and considerably more extravagant. But I would resist the confident diagnosis that these gatherings represent consumerism at its emptiest. On the two occasions I passed at four in the morning, they resembled people manufacturing a community out of the only shared object available to them. That is no triumph of our culture, though it is certainly an achievement of theirs. Sociability apparently requires an obstacle, and our economy has become remarkably efficient at removing obstacles.
qs: How does the writer relate convenience to the social life of the queue?
Convenience preserves those friendships even after the queue has gone.
Removing the difficulty removes what brought these strangers together.
The queue survives because ballots have made buying harder than before.
Obstacles keep strangers apart, which is why the queues were never social.

qs.evidence: Sociability apparently requires an obstacle, and our economy has become remarkably efficient at removing obstacles.
qs.answer: Removing the difficulty removes what brought these strangers together.
qs.why: Teks menyimpulkan pergaulan tampaknya membutuhkan hambatan, sementara ekonomi kita makin efisien menghapus hambatan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi pertemanan tetap awet bertentangan dengan laporan kawan yang tidak lagi mendapat kenalan baru; opsi undian mempersulit pembelian membalik faktanya, sebab undian justru memudahkan; opsi hambatan menjauhkan orang membalik kalimat penutup.

qs: What can be inferred from the friend's report about the ballot?
A fairer system can still cost participants something they valued.
The ballot has produced acquaintances of a different and slower kind.
Eleven years of queuing had left him with very few acquaintances anyway.
He considers the ballot unfair as well as socially costly.

qs.evidence: A friend who has queued for eleven years reports that the ballot feels fairer and that he has acquired no new acquaintance whatever since its introduction.
qs.answer: A fairer system can still cost participants something they valued.
qs.why: Kawan itu menyebut undiannya terasa lebih adil dan sekaligus mengaku tidak mendapat kenalan baru sejak undian diberlakukan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kenalan jenis lain menambahkan hasil yang justru ditolak kata “no new acquaintance whatever”; opsi sedikit kenalan selama sebelas tahun membalik sebab kenalan lamanya berasal dari antrean itu; opsi menganggap tidak adil bertentangan dengan kata “fairer”.

qs: Why does the writer point out the flatness of his friend's delivery?
To show that the friend had grown bored with the conversation.
To suggest that the friend had never much enjoyed queuing.
To suggest the loss registers without being openly mourned.
To indicate quiet anger at the way the ballot was introduced.

qs.evidence: He delivered both halves of that sentence in an identical flat tone.
qs.answer: To suggest the loss registers without being openly mourned.
qs.why: Kedua bagian kalimat itu disampaikan dengan nada yang sama datar, dan justru kedataran itu menandai kehilangan yang tidak diratapi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi bosan menyederhanakan nada datar menjadi ketidakpedulian; opsi tidak pernah menikmati bertentangan dengan sebelas tahun mengantre; opsi marah menambahkan emosi yang tidak ada di kalimat itu.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about the resale market?
Resale prices put the shoes out of reach for most people in the queue.
The objects really are the only thing these participants are after.
Identical items take several weeks to reach the resale sites.
If people only wanted the shoes, they could simply buy them online.

qs.evidence: Were the objects the objective, the resale market would satisfy the appetite immediately and at moderate expense, since identical items reach the internet within hours.
qs.answer: If people only wanted the shoes, they could simply buy them online.
qs.why: Teks menyatakan kalau barangnya yang jadi tujuan, pasar sekunder sudah bisa memenuhinya segera dan dengan biaya sedang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi harga di luar jangkauan bertentangan dengan “moderate expense”; opsi barangnya memang tujuan membalik logika kalimatnya; opsi berminggu-minggu bertentangan dengan “within hours”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer has never joined one of these queues himself."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer has never joined one of these queues himself.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: I have never queued for footwear and expect I never shall, my own irrationalities being quieter and considerably more extravagant.
qs.why: Dia menyatakan belum pernah mengantre untuk sepatu dan tidak berniat, jadi klaimnya benar.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena posisinya disebut di paragraf terakhir.

author: Rendra Kusnadi
setting: a cultural commentary on release-day queues

title: The Candles Subsidize the Poetry
text:
The bookshop on my corner now devotes its entire display table to candles, and after a period of ugly resentment I have concluded that I do not mind, since the candles subsidize the poetry. This is not the sentence I anticipated composing when the display initially materialized. My initial reaction involved several remarks about the demise of literary culture that I would prefer not to have delivered publicly.

The economics are unforgiving and widely misunderstood, since a hardback yields the retailer a margin that would embarrass a grocer. The purchaser spending forty minutes deliberating in the establishment is frequently the purchaser who subsequently orders the item online for less. A candle carries a margin four times superior and has never been discounted by a warehouse, and the tote bags, the metal pins and the ceramic dishes are not evidence of surrender. They are the mechanism by which a room full of unprofitable objects continues to exist on a costly street. Retail arithmetic of this description is dull, unglamorous and entirely decisive.

What genuinely deserves scrutiny is a subtler substitution. Retailers discovering the profitability of ornament occasionally begin selecting books that photograph well, and the criterion relates only loosely to whether a volume has merit. Certain covers now advertise an aesthetic rather than a subject, and curation by photograph substitutes surface for judgement. My local shop resists this admirably, and the poetry section has expanded rather than contracted, though I have visited establishments elsewhere whose entire stock appeared to have been selected by somebody arranging a colour palette.

The staff constitute the variable determining which species of establishment you are standing in. In a genuine bookshop somebody glances up from the counter, enquires what you have been reading, and then dissuades you from your intended purchase in favour of something superior. That conversation is the actual product, and cannot be photographed, ranked or reproduced by an algorithm. Candles do not threaten that conversation; understaffing does, and understaffing is what happens when margins fail. Skill delivered conversationally remains the one commodity the warehouses have never managed to replicate.

So I have adjusted my objections, and I now buy a candle every December without embarrassment. It is a curious form of support, indirect and slightly ridiculous, in which I purchase an object I do not require to sustain an institution I could not replace. The alternative arrangement, in which the shop refuses all ornament and closes within two years to universal regret, would preserve my aesthetic principles perfectly. It would also eliminate the only establishment within walking distance where somebody argues with me about a novel. Purity of principle, in retailing as elsewhere, is generally financed by somebody else.
qs: What is the writer's central claim about the candles?
Ornaments have crowded out the books that once justified the shop.
Ornaments matter less to the shop than the advice its staff can give.
Books earn the retailer a better margin than candles ever will.
Ornaments pay the rent that keeps unprofitable books on the shelves.

qs.evidence: They are the mechanism by which a room full of unprofitable objects continues to exist on a costly street.
qs.answer: Ornaments pay the rent that keeps unprofitable books on the shelves.
qs.why: Lilin dan pernak-perniknya disebut mekanisme yang membuat ruangan penuh barang tak menguntungkan tetap bisa berdiri di jalan yang mahal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi mendesak buku keluar adalah reaksi pertama penulis yang kemudian dia tarik; opsi pernak-pernik kurang penting daripada nasihat staf membalik hubungan yang dinyatakan teks, sebab marginlah yang menjaga staf; opsi margin buku lebih baik membalik angka di paragraf dua.

qs: What can be inferred about the real threat to the bookshop?
Fewer candles would leave more room for the staff to shelve books.
The conversation with the staff survives whatever happens to the margins.
Protecting the margins is how a shop protects its staff and their advice.
Understaffing follows from customers who deliberate too long over a purchase.

qs.evidence: Candles do not threaten that conversation; understaffing does, and understaffing is what happens when margins fail.
qs.answer: Protecting the margins is how a shop protects its staff and their advice.
qs.why: Teks menyebut lilin tidak mengancam percakapan itu; yang mengancam adalah kekurangan staf, dan kekurangan staf terjadi ketika margin gagal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi lebih sedikit lilin membalik sebab-akibatnya; opsi percakapan aman bertentangan dengan “understaffing does”; opsi pembeli yang lama memakai detail paragraf dua yang tidak menjelaskan kekurangan staf.

qs: What does the writer's admission about his first reaction contribute?
A wry acknowledgement that his earliest verdict was overheated.
A quiet insistence that his first remarks have held up rather well.
A polite complaint about the people who repeated those remarks.
A measured warning that the shop may not last another year.

qs.evidence: My initial reaction involved several remarks about the demise of literary culture that I would prefer not to have delivered publicly.
qs.answer: A wry acknowledgement that his earliest verdict was overheated.
qs.why: Dia mengaku pernah melontarkan komentar soal matinya kebudayaan sastra yang kini lebih baik tidak pernah diucapkan di depan umum.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi bertahan pada komentar awal membalik pengakuan itu; opsi mengeluh soal orang lain menambahkan pihak yang tidak ada di teks; opsi peringatan tutup bertentangan dengan penutup yang menyebut toko itu tetap berdiri karena lilinnya.

qs: What does "curation by photograph" mean in the third paragraph?
Photographing each new title before it reaches the front table.
Choosing stock for how it looks instead of how good it is.
Letting customers choose which covers the shop puts on display.
Ranking novels with an algorithm trained on their contents.

qs.evidence: Certain covers now advertise an aesthetic rather than a subject, and curation by photograph substitutes surface for judgement.
qs.answer: Choosing stock for how it looks instead of how good it is.
qs.why: Frasa itu dijelaskan sebagai penggantian penilaian oleh permukaan: sampul mengiklankan estetika, bukan pokok bahasan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi memfoto tiap judul membaca frasa itu secara harfiah; opsi pembeli memilih sampul menambahkan mekanisme yang tidak disebut; opsi algoritma memakai bahan paragraf lain yang tidak menjelaskan frasa ini.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer refuses to buy any of the shop's ornaments."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer refuses to buy any of the shop's ornaments.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: So I have adjusted my objections, and I now buy a candle every December without embarrassment.
qs.why: Dia justru membeli lilin setiap Desember tanpa malu, jadi klaim ini bertentangan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertabrakan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena kebiasaan belanjanya disebut.

topic: why independent bookshops sell candles and gifts
author: Maritza Sudibyo
setting: a cultural commentary on bookshop retailing

title: Ninety Seconds of Calm
text:
