The photographs arrive in an endless quiet procession: a pale room, a solitary chair, a bowl containing nothing. Light falls across a floor that has clearly never encountered a satchel, a spillage or a deadline. The captions describe such interiors as calm, a euphemism chosen with commercial precision. What they mostly are is unoccupied, and the distinction is more consequential than the vocabulary of the captions permits us to notice. Terminology of that kind performs concealment rather than description, quietly and rather effectively.

I hold no grievance against restraint, which constitutes a genuine achievement in an overcrowded world, nor against the photographers who satisfy the appetite for it. The trouble is that these images have quietly hardened into instructions rather than depictions. A photograph of an empty surface documents a moment, whereas a thousand of them quietly legislate a standard for everybody else. Ordinary readers then apply that standard to interiors containing children, hobbies, elderly relatives and the accumulated paraphernalia of actual biographies. Judged against an empty surface every inhabited room fails, and comparison with an uninhabited photograph is a competition arranged so that nobody living can possibly win it.

Notice what the aesthetic conceals about expenditure, because the concealment is systematic rather than incidental. Emptiness requires storage, and storage requires either square metres or a monthly fee, so the visible absence of objects generally indicates the invisible presence of a second room. Meanwhile the household with fewer possessions and no storage is not photographed at all, since genuine scarcity does not resemble the aesthetic. It resembles a chair with a coat draped across it, photogenic to nobody and therefore unrepresented. The aesthetic of minimal ownership is expensive, and the outlay is precisely what the frame excludes. Invisibility of expenditure is the characteristic achievement of the entire genre.

There is also a temporal deception at work, since every one of these interiors was tidied immediately before the photograph and will be disordered within the hour, exactly like mine. What we are shown is not a way of living but a condition lasting ninety seconds, presented as a permanent state that other people have somehow achieved. Aspiration directed at a ninety-second condition produces a low but persistent sense of failure, which is an unusual arrangement to construct for oneself deliberately. Permanence is exactly what the medium cannot photograph, and exactly what its audience infers regardless of the caption.

My own compromise is inelegant, provisional and thoroughly unphotogenic, and I recommend it warmly to anybody contemplating a similar capitulation. One shelf in the sitting room remains clear, as a modest daily demonstration that domestic order is intermittently attainable. The remaining eleven accommodate everything else in a condition I would characterize, with some indulgence, as affectionate chaos. Visitors occasionally photograph the clear shelf, and never anything adjacent to it. Nobody has ever photographed the others, and I have come to regard that asymmetry as the most honest commentary anybody has offered on the entire genre and its glossy prescriptions.
qs: How does the writer relate these photographs to rooms that people live in?
They set a standard that no occupied room could ever satisfy.
They give tidy households a fair standard to measure themselves against.
They record rooms much like the ones most readers actually occupy.
They flatter inhabited rooms, which photograph better than empty ones.

qs.evidence: Judged against an empty surface every inhabited room fails, and comparison with an uninhabited photograph is a competition arranged so that nobody living can possibly win it.
qs.answer: They set a standard that no occupied room could ever satisfy.
qs.why: Teks menyebut perbandingan dengan foto ruang tak berpenghuni sebagai kompetisi yang disusun agar tidak mungkin dimenangi siapa pun yang hidup di dalamnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi standar adil membalik kalimat itu; opsi mirip ruang pembaca bertentangan dengan ruang yang belum pernah bertemu tas sekolah; opsi ruang berpenghuni lebih fotogenik bertentangan dengan rumah tanpa penyimpanan yang tidak difoto sama sekali.

qs: What can be inferred about the cost of the empty look?
The bare look shows a household that genuinely owns very little.
Households with little furniture are the ones photographed most often.
The bare look usually signals money that the picture keeps out of frame.
The bare look is cheaper to achieve than the cluttered rooms it replaced.

qs.evidence: Emptiness requires storage, and storage requires either square metres or a monthly fee, so the visible absence of objects generally indicates the invisible presence of a second room.
qs.answer: The bare look usually signals money that the picture keeps out of frame.
qs.why: Kekosongan menuntut penyimpanan, dan penyimpanan menuntut meter persegi atau biaya bulanan, jadi ketiadaan barang yang terlihat menandakan ruang kedua yang tidak terlihat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi memiliki sangat sedikit barang persis pembacaan yang dibantah; opsi rumah minim perabot paling sering difoto bertentangan dengan “is not photographed at all”; opsi lebih murah membalik hitungan biaya penyimpanan itu.

qs: What is the writer's tone in reporting what visitors photograph?
Faintly put out that guests overlook the rest of his sitting room.
Quietly amused, since the habit proves his point for him.
Pleased that visitors notice how much care the shelf takes.
Measured, simply recording what guests tend to photograph.

qs.evidence: Visitors occasionally photograph the clear shelf, and never anything adjacent to it.
qs.answer: Quietly amused, since the habit proves his point for him.
qs.why: Tamu memfoto rak yang bersih dan tidak pernah apa pun di sebelahnya, dan kebiasaan itu justru membuktikan argumennya sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tersinggung menambahkan rasa yang tidak ada; opsi senang diperhatikan membalik maksud pengamatannya; opsi laporan terukur mengabaikan kata “never anything adjacent to it” yang dipasang untuk efek lucu.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about a ninety-second condition?
The picture records how such households look for most of the year.
These rooms stay orderly rather longer than visitors tend to assume.
The picture freezes a brief tidy moment and sells it as daily life.
Photographers now admit that the tidiness lasts only a minute or two.

qs.evidence: What we are shown is not a way of living but a condition lasting ninety seconds, presented as a permanent state that other people have somehow achieved.
qs.answer: The picture freezes a brief tidy moment and sells it as daily life.
qs.why: Yang diperlihatkan bukan cara hidup melainkan kondisi berdurasi sembilan puluh detik yang disajikan sebagai keadaan permanen.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi sepanjang tahun membalik kalimat itu; opsi bertahan lebih lama bertentangan dengan keadaan yang runtuh dalam satu jam; opsi fotografer mengakui menambahkan pengakuan yang tidak ada di teks.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Collections of these photographs contain more kitchens than sitting rooms."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Collections of these photographs contain more kitchens than sitting rooms.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: The photographs arrive in an endless quiet procession: a pale room, a solitary chair, a bowl containing nothing.
qs.why: Teks tidak pernah menghitung jenis ruangan dalam foto-foto itu, jadi perbandingan jumlahnya tidak bisa dinilai.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” dan “False” sama-sama butuh hitungan yang tidak ada; kalimat terdekat hanya menyebut isi satu foto.

topic: minimalist interior photography and lived-in rooms
author: Kirana Danastri
setting: a cultural commentary on interior aesthetics

title: Salt Through Bread
text:
My grandmother commanded a dialect containing roughly four separate terms for the particular grey of the sky before rain, none of which I acquired properly. What survived in me was the music: a rising contour on interrogatives, the habit of addressing children in the plural, and a formidable noise of disapproval manufactured entirely at the rear of the throat. She died when I was nineteen, during the second week of a term I declined to interrupt. The dialect departed with her, in the sense that actually matters.

It survives in recordings, obviously, since a university project preserved forty hours of speakers from her generation. I have listened to portions of it inside a cramped booth with the volume wound excessively high. Every vowel is present, the grammar is intact, and something essential is nevertheless entirely absent: nobody in the recordings is reprimanding anybody. Preservation and transmission are separate operations, and the archive accomplishes only the first. Documentation preserves a language and cannot preserve the ordinary occasions that supplied its weight, which is no accusation against documentation but a characterization of what any language largely consists of.

My father, raised inside the dialect, resolved to educate us in the national language, and I decline to brand that decision a betrayal. He had witnessed an intelligent cousin humiliated in a government bureau over a provincial vowel. He performed a calculation with the intelligence available, and the calculation was sound. I have benefited from it in ways I had no occasion to register, which is roughly the definition of a successful sacrifice. Assimilation was an insurance policy, purchased at a premium nobody itemized at the outset. The cost remained invisible to him for decades and then arrived in a single afternoon, at his mother's funeral, where he delivered the address in a language she had never entirely trusted.

I have been trying to learn it now, at thirty-eight, from an application and an exceptionally patient neighbour. The progress is humiliating: my accent apparently resembles that of a tourist attempting a compliment, and I have twice deployed the affectionate form of a verb in circumstances that reduced a shopkeeper to helpless laughter. I persist regardless, expecting no fluency whatever, because the undertaking has generated something I had not anticipated. Humiliation, it appears, is the standard tuition fee for an inheritance recovered belatedly.

The something is not the language itself; it is a sudden and repeated recognition of my grandmother's phrasing inside my own Indonesian, structures I had assumed were mine emerging as translations she performed decades before my birth. Loss is less total than the vocabulary implies: she is distributed through my sentences like salt through bread, undetectable and structural. Every clumsy tutorial supplies me with fresh evidence that I never entirely failed to learn her at all. Inheritance of that kind requires no fluency whatsoever, which is fortunate, since fluency remains improbable.
qs: How does the writer relate the recordings to the survival of the dialect?
They pass the dialect on more effectively than family speech ever did.
They preserve the vowels while losing the grammar of the speakers.
They keep the forms alive but cannot pass on their daily use.
They show the dialect was never lost, only moved into an archive.

qs.evidence: Preservation and transmission are separate operations, and the archive accomplishes only the first.
qs.answer: They keep the forms alive but cannot pass on their daily use.
qs.why: Teks memisahkan pelestarian dari penerusan dan menyebut arsip hanya menyelesaikan yang pertama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi lebih efektif daripada keluarga membalik kesimpulan itu; opsi tata bahasa hilang bertentangan dengan “the grammar is intact”; opsi tidak pernah hilang bertentangan dengan kalimat bahwa dialek itu pergi bersama neneknya dalam arti yang benar-benar penting.

qs: What can be inferred about the cost of his father's decision?
The price of that choice only became clear to him at the graveside.
He regretted the decision from the moment that he made it.
He had weighed the cost carefully beforehand and accepted it.
The funeral address was delivered in the dialect his mother had used.

qs.evidence: The cost remained invisible to him for decades and then arrived in a single afternoon, at his mother's funeral, where he delivered the address in a language she had never entirely trusted.
qs.answer: The price of that choice only became clear to him at the graveside.
qs.why: Biayanya tetap tidak terlihat selama beberapa dekade lalu tiba dalam satu sore, di pemakaman ibunya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menyesal sejak awal bertentangan dengan “remained invisible to him for decades”; opsi sudah menimbang biayanya bertentangan dengan premi yang tidak dirinci siapa pun pada mulanya; opsi pidato dalam dialek membalik teks, yang menyebut bahasa yang tidak pernah sepenuhnya dia percaya.

qs: What is the writer's tone in describing his own progress with the dialect?
Quietly bitter about neighbours who laugh at his pronunciation.
Confident that fluency will arrive within a year or two.
Detached about an accent he has stopped trying to improve.
Self-mocking, yet with no suggestion of abandoning the attempt.

qs.evidence: my accent apparently resembles that of a tourist attempting a compliment, and I have twice deployed the affectionate form of a verb in circumstances that reduced a shopkeeper to helpless laughter
qs.answer: Self-mocking, yet with no suggestion of abandoning the attempt.
qs.why: Dia menyebut kemajuannya memalukan dan menertawakan aksennya sendiri, tetapi pelajarannya diteruskan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi getir salah sasaran karena tetangganya disebut luar biasa sabar; opsi yakin lancar bertentangan dengan pengakuan bahwa dia tidak mengharapkan kelancaran; opsi berhenti berusaha bertentangan dengan pelajaran yang masih berjalan.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the image of salt through bread?
Her speech can be picked out easily in almost every sentence he writes.
Her way of speaking sits inside his own, invisible but holding it together.
Her dialect has gone from his speech, leaving only its rhythm behind.
He borrows her phrasing deliberately whenever he writes at length.

qs.evidence: she is distributed through my sentences like salt through bread, undetectable and structural
qs.answer: Her way of speaking sits inside his own, invisible but holding it together.
qs.why: Dia menyebut neneknya tersebar dalam kalimat-kalimatnya seperti garam dalam roti: tidak terdeteksi, tetapi struktural.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi mudah dikenali bertentangan dengan kata “undetectable”; opsi hanya ritmenya yang tersisa bertentangan dengan kata “structural”; opsi meniru dengan sengaja mengubah sifatnya yang tidak disadari menjadi pilihan gaya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer stayed at university rather than going home when his grandmother died."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer stayed at university rather than going home when his grandmother died.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: She died when I was nineteen, during the second week of a term I declined to interrupt.
qs.why: Dia bilang tidak memotong masa kuliahnya waktu itu, jadi klaim ini parafrasa yang tepat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan “declined to interrupt”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena kejadiannya disebut jelas.

topic: losing and relearning a family dialect
author: Arum Setiabudi
setting: a reflective essay on language and family

title: Preparation and Postponement
text:
The desk reached me in March, second-hand, from a retired surveyor who observed its descent of the stairs with open scepticism. It offers a generous surface, three drawers requiring persuasion, and a scar along one edge resembling a coastline. The absence of such an object had supposedly explained the absence of the manuscript, and the reasoning was so comfortable that it escaped examination for years. Six months subsequently the desk is admirable and the volume remains approximately where it began.

What the desk eventually demonstrated was the difference between preparation and postponement. Preparation has an end; postponement is a renewable resource, and it renews itself most vigorously in the presence of stationery catalogues. My purchases include a lamp of considerable elegance, a chair recommended by physiotherapists, and a modest ceramic pot containing exactly those pencils that remain unused. Every acquisition felt like progress and functioned as delay, which is a difference the credit card statement cannot register, since consumption disguised as commitment is the characteristic vice of the ambitious amateur.

The mornings themselves prove stranger than the purchasing, since I arrive at the desk each day with real intent. Within four minutes I am investigating something adjacent and defensible: the etymology of a word I have not yet required, or the ferry timetable for an island the chapter may never reach. The research is real research, and that is exactly its usefulness, since no observer accuses an industrious writer of avoidance, least of all himself. Avoidance dressed as diligence is almost undetectable from the inside, because legitimacy, once acquired, protects an activity from examination indefinitely.

A neighbour who paints suggested a remedy of brutal simplicity, and I resented it immediately, which is generally a reliable indication. She records the single next physical action before departing the studio each evening, and permits herself no revision of that instruction in the morning. It removes the negotiation, she said, and the negotiation is what consumes the day. Negotiation flourishes wherever a decision has been left renegotiable overnight. The discipline was adopted in June, abandoned in July, and resumed recently with the sheepishness of a returning patient.

No conclusion about a wasted purchase is available here, partly because the purchase was not wasted. Some mornings the wide surface and the peculiar scar and the unused pencils assemble themselves into a room where work becomes conceivable. On such mornings nine hundred words appear and the whole cost seems vindicated. But the desk did not supply those mornings, and it merely made their absence more conspicuous, which may be the most any object can honestly promise, and is more than most of them deliver. Equipment cannot manufacture the appetite that the equipment was purchased to serve.
qs: What is the central point of this reflection?
A better working surface removes most of the excuses a writer can find.
Serious research is the part of writing that readers tend to underrate.
Preparation and postponement are, in practice, the same activity.
Getting ready for work can quietly become a way of avoiding it.

qs.evidence: What the desk eventually demonstrated was the difference between preparation and postponement.
qs.answer: Getting ready for work can quietly become a way of avoiding it.
qs.why: Meja itu akhirnya memperlihatkan perbedaan antara bersiap dan menunda, sehingga persiapan bisa menjadi bentuk halus dari menghindar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi permukaan yang lebih baik bertentangan dengan seluruh cerita mejanya; opsi riset yang diremehkan pembaca memakai bahan paragraf dua tetapi bukan kesimpulan esainya; opsi keduanya sama menghapus pembedaan yang justru menjadi intinya.

qs: What can be inferred about the morning research he describes?
The research is invented, so nobody is in a position to object.
Industrious writers are the people least likely to avoid their own work.
The work is genuine, which is exactly what makes it such good cover.
Observers accuse him of avoidance rather more often than he admits.

qs.evidence: The research is real research, and that is exactly its usefulness, since no observer accuses an industrious writer of avoidance, least of all himself.
qs.answer: The work is genuine, which is exactly what makes it such good cover.
qs.why: Risetnya disebut riset sungguhan, dan justru itu kegunaannya, sebab tidak ada pengamat yang menuduh penulis rajin sedang menghindar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi riset palsu bertentangan dengan “real research”; opsi penulis rajin paling kecil kemungkinan menghindar membalik argumennya; opsi sering dituduh bertentangan dengan “no observer accuses”.

qs: What does the writer suggest by noting his immediate resentment of the advice?
That the suggestion had probably struck something true in him.
That the neighbour had misread how his working day is arranged.
That advice from another trade is rarely worth much to a writer.
That he adopted the remedy at once and without argument.

qs.evidence: A neighbour who paints suggested a remedy of brutal simplicity, and I resented it immediately, which is generally a reliable indication.
qs.answer: That the suggestion had probably struck something true in him.
qs.why: Dia menyebut rasa kesalnya sendiri sebagai penanda yang biasanya dapat dipercaya, jadi nasihat itu kemungkinan tepat sasaran.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tetangga salah paham menambahkan penilaian yang tidak ada; opsi nasihat lintas profesi tidak berguna bertentangan dengan cara dia memperlakukan saran itu; opsi langsung menerima bertentangan dengan kata “resented it immediately”.

qs: What does "adjacent and defensible" describe about those morning tasks?
They belong to the chapter he is currently drafting.
They are errands he performs quietly and cannot defend.
They sit close to the real work and are easy to justify.
They were suggested to him by his very patient neighbour.

qs.evidence: Within four minutes I am investigating something adjacent and defensible: the etymology of a word I have not yet required, or the ferry timetable for an island the chapter may never reach.
qs.answer: They sit close to the real work and are easy to justify.
qs.why: Contohnya etimologi kata yang belum dibutuhkan dan jadwal kapal untuk pulau yang mungkin tidak pernah dicapai bab itu: bersebelahan dengan pekerjaan asli dan mudah dibela.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi bagian dari bab bertentangan dengan “may never reach”; opsi tidak bisa dibela membalik kata “defensible”; opsi usul tetangga memakai tokoh dari paragraf lain yang mengusulkan obat, bukan tugas pagi ini.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer concludes that buying the desk was a mistake."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer concludes that buying the desk was a mistake.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: No conclusion about a wasted purchase is available here, partly because the purchase was not wasted.
qs.why: Dia menyatakan pembelian itu tidak sia-sia, jadi klaim ini bertentangan langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertabrakan dengan kalimat tersebut, dan “Not stated” gagal karena sikapnya soal pembelian itu ditulis jelas.

topic: buying a desk and the habit of putting off writing
author: Galih Ramadhan
setting: a reflective essay on procrastination

title: The Last Bus and Its Logic
text:
The final bus of the evening operates according to a logic entirely its own, and I have been scrutinizing that logic, unwillingly, for eleven months. It departs when the driver has concluded a conversation and materializes whenever the traffic permits. Its passengers number between four and nine, and each has performed the same calculation concerning the expense of a taxi. Nobody aboard is travelling for pleasure, and that shared condition produces a courtesy I have not encountered on any daytime service.

A woman boards two stops beyond mine, invariably bearing a plastic container of a dish she has prepared, and she has twice offered it to strangers. A student dozes with an alarm configured for his halt, rouses himself with the precision of an instrument, and appears briefly ashamed. A security guard concluding a shift reads paperbacks whose covers have been removed, and none of us converses. The arrangement is not unfriendly, merely economical with reserves that a working day has already depleted. It required several weeks of travelling before I recognized that the silence constitutes a species of consideration rather than its inversion. Reticence of that kind is an urban competence, acquired without instruction, rarely acknowledged and impossible to counterfeit.

What the route offers, at that hour, is an urban landscape with its performance suspended. Shopfronts that devote the daylight hours to insisting on their own importance become simply lit rectangles. A man sweeps the pavement outside a restaurant with the unhurried competence of an individual who has performed the operation four thousand times. Two adolescents argue about a film beneath a broken streetlight, and their disagreement is more genuinely engaged than anything I encountered in the office that afternoon, while nothing whatsoever is being staged for anybody, because the audience has departed. Municipal existence continues regardless of observation, indifferent to whether anybody remains available to admire it.

I did not select this route, and for the first several months I resented every minute of it, a resentment thoroughly documented in my messages to acquaintances. What dissolved it was not acceptance in any noble sense but a small technical discovery: the bus is the only interval in my day that no application can subdivide. The signal fails between the third and seventh halts, and nobody expects a reply from a passenger travelling at midnight. Unavailability, imposed externally, accomplished within eleven months what my own discipline had repeatedly failed to arrange.

I will move closer to the office eventually, and the arrangement will end, and I suspect I will miss it in the dishonest way one misses difficulty. Nevertheless, something has been rearranged in me by those eleven months, and it concerns attention rather than transport. The metropolis was invariably conducting itself in this manner after eleven, sweeping and arguing and offering sustenance to strangers. It required an inconvenient timetable and a failing signal to compel me to notice. Attention apparently requires an enclosure, and enclosures are increasingly hard to obtain voluntarily.
qs: How does the writer link the passengers' reason for travelling to their behaviour?
Because none of them wants to be there, they treat each other well.
Because the journey is long, the passengers eventually fall into conversation.
Their shared tiredness makes them shorter with each other than day passengers.
Daytime services show the same courtesy for much the same reasons.

qs.evidence: Nobody aboard is travelling for pleasure, and that shared condition produces a courtesy I have not encountered on any daytime service.
qs.answer: Because none of them wants to be there, they treat each other well.
qs.why: Tidak ada yang naik bus itu untuk bersenang-senang, dan kondisi bersama itulah yang menghasilkan kesopanan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi percakapan yang tumbuh bertentangan dengan penumpang yang justru pendiam dan menjaga jarak; opsi lebih kasar membalik kata “courtesy”; opsi layanan siang sama bertentangan dengan “I have not encountered on any daytime service”.

qs: What can be inferred about why his resentment faded?
He learnt to accept the journey through patience and quiet reflection.
It faded for practical reasons rather than because he grew wiser.
Applications have begun breaking the interval into shorter useful pieces.
The resentment faded once the fare on that route was reduced.

qs.evidence: What dissolved it was not acceptance in any noble sense but a small technical discovery: the bus is the only interval in my day that no application can subdivide.
qs.answer: It faded for practical reasons rather than because he grew wiser.
qs.why: Yang melarutkan kekesalannya bukan penerimaan yang mulia melainkan penemuan teknis kecil: bus itu satu-satunya jeda yang tidak bisa dipotong aplikasi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kesabaran persis yang ditolak frasa “not acceptance in any noble sense”; opsi aplikasi memotong jeda membalik penemuan itu; opsi tarif turun menambahkan sebab yang tidak disebut, sebab biaya perjalanan di teks dipakai untuk hal lain.

qs: What does the writer admit about the nostalgia he expects to feel?
That he will genuinely regret losing the cheaper journey.
That he intends to keep the commute for as long as he can.
That fondness for past hardship is never quite honest.
That difficulty is remembered rather more accurately than comfort.

qs.evidence: I will move closer to the office eventually, and the arrangement will end, and I suspect I will miss it in the dishonest way one misses difficulty.
qs.answer: That fondness for past hardship is never quite honest.
qs.why: Dia menduga akan merindukannya dengan cara tidak jujur seperti orang merindukan kesulitan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menyesali tarif memindahkan alasan kerinduan ke soal biaya; opsi mempertahankan rute bertentangan dengan rencana pindah lebih dekat ke kantor; opsi ingatan lebih akurat membalik kata “dishonest”.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the remark about shopfronts?
By night the shops stop advertising themselves and are simply lit shapes.
The shops look rather more impressive once the working day has ended.
Shopfronts press their own importance hardest in the late evening.
During business hours these shops are little more than lit rectangles.

qs.evidence: Shopfronts that devote the daylight hours to insisting on their own importance become simply lit rectangles.
qs.answer: By night the shops stop advertising themselves and are simply lit shapes.
qs.why: Toko yang sepanjang siang sibuk menegaskan kepentingannya sendiri, pada malam hari tinggal menjadi persegi bercahaya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tampak lebih megah membalik nada kalimatnya; opsi paling berisik pada malam menukar waktunya; opsi jam kerja memindahkan kapan mereka menjadi persegi bercahaya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The mobile signal is unreliable along part of the route."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The mobile signal is unreliable along part of the route.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The signal fails between the third and seventh halts, and nobody expects a reply from a passenger travelling at midnight.
qs.why: Teks menyebut sinyal mati di antara pemberhentian ketiga dan ketujuh, jadi klaimnya parafrasa yang benar.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena kegagalan sinyalnya disebut eksplisit.

topic: riding the last bus home and noticing the night city
author: Ayu Prameswari
setting: a reflective essay on a nightly commute

title: The Pencil and the Metronome
text:
My piano teacher possessed a metronome she never used and a pencil she employed constantly, remorselessly. Its tap against the music stand remains audible to me three decades afterwards. She taught in a front room that smelled of camphor, above a tailor's premises, and her instruction consisted virtually entirely of interrogation. What did I intend by that phrase, and had I observed the composer's marking, and why had I accelerated precisely where a competent musician would have waited.

I was not a gifted pupil and she never suggested otherwise, which I regard now as an extraordinary act of respect. Other adults were busily assuring me of talents I did not possess. She told me instead that my hands were adequate, my patience insufficient, and my listening capable of improvement, and attached a timetable to each judgement. Nothing in the arrangement was cruel; it was merely the first honest account of myself anybody had offered. Accurate description, delivered without cruelty, is a rarer gift than encouragement, and considerably less popular.

The lessons themselves were predominantly failure, arranged deliberately: she would set a passage marginally beyond my capacity and attend to my collapse in the fourth bar. Then she enquired which finger had betrayed the intention, and the question assumed an intention, which was flattering, and it assumed the collapse was analysable rather than shameful, which was liberating. Across four years I mastered perhaps eleven compositions adequately, none brilliantly. I also learned that difficulty is information, tasting considerably better than reassurance once you develop the palate, since diagnosis converts humiliation into data.

I abandoned the instrument at fifteen for reasons that seemed urgent and now seem administrative, and two decades elapsed without a keyboard. When I seated myself anew, in a rented flat with a borrowed piano, my hands recalled a Bach invention I could not have named. They recalled her corrections equally well, and a phrase would begin accelerating before some interior authority declined, the refusal arriving in the tempo of a pencil tapping on wood. Muscular memory apparently preserves instruction, unprompted, long after the instructor has been forgotten.

She died before any of this could be communicated to her, which is the ordinary shape of such stories and not a tragedy requiring commentary. What survives is not the eleven compositions. It is a particular attention, transferable to arguments, to recipes, to the sentences of this paragraph, asking what you intended and whether the acceleration was earned. I inherited a method rather than a skill, and the method has outlasted virtually everything else instructed in that decade. Methods migrate between unrelated domains, whereas repertoire remains stubbornly where it was acquired.
qs: What does the writer identify as the lasting result of those lessons?
A way of paying attention that he still applies elsewhere.
A repertoire of eleven pieces he can still perform from memory.
A method he set aside once the lessons came to an end.
A performing skill that has proved more durable than the method.

qs.evidence: I inherited a method rather than a skill, and the method has outlasted virtually everything else instructed in that decade.
qs.answer: A way of paying attention that he still applies elsewhere.
qs.why: Dia menyebut mewarisi sebuah metode alih-alih keterampilan, dan metode itulah yang bertahan melampaui hampir semua yang diajarkan sepanjang dekade itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi sebelas karya bertentangan dengan kalimat bahwa yang bertahan bukan komposisinya; opsi metode ditinggalkan membalik kata “outlasted”; opsi keterampilan bermain lebih tahan lama menukar dua hal yang dibedakan teks.

qs: What can be inferred about how she chose the passages he practised?
The passages were chosen to sit comfortably inside his existing reach.
She was mildly surprised each time the fourth bar collapsed.
The failure was arranged deliberately as part of the teaching.
His collapse in the fourth bar usually brought the lesson to an early end.

qs.evidence: she would set a passage marginally beyond my capacity and attend to my collapse in the fourth bar
qs.answer: The failure was arranged deliberately as part of the teaching.
qs.why: Dia sengaja memilih bagian yang sedikit di luar kemampuan lalu memperhatikan titik jatuhnya di bar keempat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi dalam jangkauan bertentangan dengan “marginally beyond my capacity”; opsi terkejut bertentangan dengan “attend to”, yang menunjukkan hal itu diantisipasi; opsi pelajaran berakhir lebih awal menambahkan akibat yang tidak ada di teks.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards her honesty about his ability?
Mildly wounded, since her verdict discouraged him for years afterwards.
Grateful, since he now reads that refusal to flatter as respect.
Amused at an adult who understated what a child could manage.
Doubtful about whether her assessment was ever quite accurate.

qs.evidence: I was not a gifted pupil and she never suggested otherwise, which I regard now as an extraordinary act of respect.
qs.answer: Grateful, since he now reads that refusal to flatter as respect.
qs.why: Dia menyebut kejujuran itu tindakan penghormatan yang luar biasa, jadi sikapnya rasa syukur.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi terluka bertentangan dengan kata “respect”; opsi geli pada penilaian yang merendah bertentangan dengan pengakuannya bahwa dia memang bukan murid berbakat; opsi meragukan ketepatan penilaiannya tidak didukung teks.

qs: What does the writer mean by "difficulty is information"?
A breakdown tells you something usable about your own playing.
Difficult passages are best postponed until the technique is ready.
Knowing about music matters rather more than the sound itself.
Encouragement from a teacher teaches more than any struggle does.

qs.evidence: I also learned that difficulty is information, tasting considerably better than reassurance once you develop the palate, since diagnosis converts humiliation into data.
qs.answer: A breakdown tells you something usable about your own playing.
qs.why: Teks menyebut diagnosis mengubah rasa terhina menjadi data, jadi kesulitan berfungsi sebagai keterangan tentang permainan sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menunda bagian sulit bertentangan dengan cara mengajarnya yang justru memilih bagian di luar kemampuan; opsi pengetahuan di atas bunyi tidak dibahas; opsi pujian lebih mengajari bertentangan dengan “better than reassurance”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "He gave up the instrument at fifteen because his teacher had moved away."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: He gave up the instrument at fifteen because his teacher had moved away.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: I abandoned the instrument at fifteen for reasons that seemed urgent and now seem administrative, and two decades elapsed without a keyboard.
qs.why: Teks menyebut usianya dan menyebut alasannya terasa administratif, tapi sebab yang sebenarnya tidak pernah dirinci.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” menambahkan sebab yang tidak ada di teks, dan “False” juga salah karena tidak ada kalimat yang membantahnya.

author: Wisnu Aditama
setting: a reflective essay on childhood lessons

title: A Collection of Borrowed Equipment
text:
The notebook is not a diary, and I have wearied of clarifying the distinction at dinner parties. A diary records whatever occurred to its author, a subject of limited interest even to the author. This volume records sentences composed by other people: a phrase from a court report, an argument overheard in a queue. It also holds three expressions a colleague employed about her father that have not ceased operating inside my head since February. It is a collection of borrowed equipment, assembled without a system and consulted without ceremony.

The practice is ancient and thoroughly unoriginal, which constitutes a substantial portion of its appeal. Readers have maintained such volumes for centuries, and the surviving examples reveal what the polished essays conceal, namely which sentences a particular mind judged unaccountably sticky. My own contains four separate entries concerning weather characterized in unflattering terms, which reveals more about my instincts than any personality inventory has managed. The collection registers what I return to, and I merely operate the pen. Preference reveals itself statistically, in repetition, rather than in any declaration of taste, and the statistics are unflattering.

What surprised me was the effect upon attention rather than upon composition, an unforeseen consequence of mere accumulation. Transporting a receptacle for other people's sentences converts ordinary listening into a variety of harvesting, and the conversion is not entirely benign. There are afternoons when I catch myself anticipating that an acquaintance will phrase her grief memorably. That is a shabby discovery to register about oneself, and I possess no defence except that the noticing continues regardless. Collectors are invariably compromised by their collections, and acquisition alters perception irreversibly, as any curator will concede.

The retrieval, meanwhile, works nothing like a filing system and everything like a rummage. I consult the collection expecting to locate the entry I require, and instead encounter an unrelated one that dismantles the paragraph I had intended, which is not a malfunction, and after seven years I have ceased characterizing it as one. A commonplace book is not a database but an unhurried companion with its own opinions, and it has been arguing with my intentions since a summer when I owned considerably fewer of them. Disorder of that description performs a service no indexation could conceivably supply.

I have devised no arrangements for what becomes of it, and the omission is deliberate rather than careless. An executor will eventually examine four hundred pages of other people's remarks, and will glean very little about my biography and rather a great deal about my ear. That seems the appropriate proportion, and anything genuinely mine in there arrived by accident, in the margins, in handwriting I can barely decipher. It habitually takes the form of an objection to something I had transcribed approvingly the year before. Attribution, in the end, matters less than the accumulated evidence of an ear at work.
qs: How does the writer describe the relationship between himself and the notebook?
The notebook reveals his preferences more reliably than he could.
He decides in advance which sentences the notebook is allowed to keep.
The notebook records his days while he supplies the opinions.
Neither the book nor its keeper shows any pattern worth reading.

qs.evidence: The collection registers what I return to, and I merely operate the pen.
qs.answer: The notebook reveals his preferences more reliably than he could.
qs.why: Koleksi itu disebut mencatat apa yang dia kembali kepadanya, sementara dia sendiri hanya mengoperasikan pena.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi memutuskan lebih dulu membalik pembagian peran itu; opsi mencatat hari-harinya bertentangan dengan penegasan bahwa buku itu bukan buku harian; opsi tanpa pola bertentangan dengan “registers what I return to”.

qs: What can be inferred from the afternoons he describes in the third paragraph?
He has grown rather more attentive to his friends than he used to be.
His friends know that their remarks are sometimes written down.
The habit has begun to shape the way he listens to other people.
He now avoids conversations that offer him nothing to collect.

qs.evidence: There are afternoons when I catch myself anticipating that an acquaintance will phrase her grief memorably.
qs.answer: The habit has begun to shape the way he listens to other people.
qs.why: Dia menangkap dirinya mengantisipasi bahwa seorang kenalan akan merumuskan kesedihannya dengan berkesan, jadi kebiasaan mengumpulkan kalimat sudah mengubah cara dia mendengarkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi lebih perhatian membalik nada pengakuannya, yang dia sebut temuan memalukan; opsi teman-temannya tahu tidak disebut di teks; opsi menghindari percakapan tertentu melampaui teks, sebab dia tetap mendengarkan dan justru itu yang mengganggunya.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards this discovery about himself?
Quiet pride in an instinct most collectors would envy.
Honest discomfort, offered without any attempt at an excuse.
Reassured, since the habit harms nobody in the end.
Detached, since the discovery has changed nothing in practice.

qs.evidence: That is a shabby discovery to register about oneself, and I possess no defence except that the noticing continues regardless.
qs.answer: Honest discomfort, offered without any attempt at an excuse.
qs.why: Dia menyebutnya temuan yang memalukan tentang dirinya dan mengaku tidak punya pembelaan apa pun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi bangga bertentangan dengan kata “shabby”; opsi merasa tenang mengabaikan pengakuan tanpa pembelaan itu; opsi berjarak bertentangan dengan kalimat yang menyatakan pengamatan itu tetap berlanjut meski dia tahu.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the description of the book as a companion?
The notebook behaves like a slow friend who disagrees with him.
The notebook works much as a well-kept database would.
The notebook confirms whatever he had intended to write next.
His intentions have hardly changed since the summer he began it.

qs.evidence: A commonplace book is not a database but an unhurried companion with its own opinions, and it has been arguing with my intentions since a summer when I owned considerably fewer of them.
qs.answer: The notebook behaves like a slow friend who disagrees with him.
qs.why: Buku itu disebut bukan basis data melainkan kawan yang tidak tergesa dengan pendapatnya sendiri, dan sudah lama membantah rencana penulisnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi seperti basis data persis yang ditolak kalimat itu; opsi selalu menyetujui membalik kata “arguing”; opsi rencananya tidak berubah bertentangan dengan penutup yang menyebut dia dulu punya jauh lebih sedikit rencana.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The notebook is a record of the writer's own daily experiences."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The notebook is a record of the writer's own daily experiences.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: The notebook is not a diary, and I have wearied of clarifying the distinction at dinner parties.
qs.why: Teks menegaskan itu bukan buku harian, jadi klaim ini bertentangan langsung dengan kalimat pertamanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertabrakan dengan kata “not a diary”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena perbedaannya justru dijelaskan.

topic: keeping a commonplace notebook of other people's sentences
author: Larissa Danuwira
setting: a reflective essay on notebooks and attention

title: The Arithmetic in the Margins
text:
My father produced each item in block capitals, from the earliest postcard through to the concluding inventory of the toolshed, and I assumed for three decades that the habit reflected idiosyncratic taste. It reflected nothing of the sort, since relentless correction at school for an irregular script had been resolved by abandoning the lower case entirely. He never divulged the decision, which reached me only through an aunt, three months after the funeral, in a kitchen crowded with unwashed crockery.

The letters themselves were not affectionate in any recognizable idiom, and no plausible reading extracts tenderness from their surfaces. He reported on the roof channels, the outlay on cement, the performance of a second-hand water pump he mistrusted throughout. Sentences began with the item and concluded with the expense, and read at twenty they demonstrated that my father had no message whatever to convey. Read at forty-one, they establish that the channels were the ostensible subject and simultaneously beside the point. Emotional information, in his correspondence, invariably travelled disguised as household maintenance, and the disguise was never once lifted.

What I had failed to observe, across two decades of dutiful reading, was the arithmetic in the margins. Every missive harbours a minute calculation in the left-hand corner, invariably the same shape: an amount, a subtraction, a remainder. It required my sister to decode what had been present for two decades. He was establishing, monthly, precisely what remained once the household expenditure had been discharged. That surplus could then be dispatched towards a daughter at university plus a son who had elected an unremunerative discipline. The surplus was the affectionate portion, expressed in the only notation he entirely trusted. Provision constituted the available vocabulary for affection, and the vocabulary proved adequate once somebody consented to translate it.

His handwriting survives across twenty-three letters plus one recipe, and not a single envelope has been discarded. This is not sentiment of the manageable variety, but something closer to evidence, retained against the temptation to reconstruct him as warmer or colder than he actually was, since both revisions remain available and both would be comprehensively false. Sentimentality simplifies a father into caricature, whereas documentation resists that simplification entirely.

He signed each item with his complete name, including the postcards, a habit formerly comic and now legible as something else entirely. A man corrected for his handwriting was unlikely to tolerate any ambiguity about the identity of the speaker. Legibility, for a man once humiliated over his penmanship, was never a neutral preference but a modest daily refusal. I compose in a minute illegible cursive that nobody can decipher, its author included, and no schoolmaster has ever once corrected it, which summarizes the entire inheritance within a single line. He purchased my carelessness, and he performed the calculation in the corner monthly for eleven years without once disclosing the arrangement to anybody.
qs: What does the writer come to understand about his father's letters?
His father wrote about money because the family finances were precarious.
His father's care showed up in figures rather than in words.
His father's affection was plain enough in the letters all along.
The letters mattered less to him than the monthly sums they carried.

qs.evidence: The surplus was the affectionate portion, expressed in the only notation he entirely trusted.
qs.answer: His father's care showed up in figures rather than in words.
qs.why: Sisa hitungan di margin disebut bagian yang penuh kasih, dinyatakan dalam satu-satunya notasi yang sepenuhnya dia percaya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi keuangan keluarga rapuh menambahkan keadaan yang tidak disebut; opsi kasih sayang sudah jelas sejak awal bertentangan dengan surat yang disebut tidak penuh kasih dalam bentuk yang bisa dikenali; opsi surat kalah penting dari uangnya membalik kesimpulan penulis, yang justru menemukan maknanya di angka itu.

qs: What can be inferred about how long the margins went unread?
His sister supplied an explanation that the letters do not really support.
The calculations were added to the letters only in the final years.
He had been looking at the evidence for years without reading it.
He had understood the margins some time before his sister spoke.

qs.evidence: It required my sister to decode what had been present for two decades.
qs.answer: He had been looking at the evidence for years without reading it.
qs.why: Teks menyebut butuh kakaknya untuk membaca sandi yang sudah hadir selama dua dekade.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi penjelasan yang tidak didukung bertentangan dengan hitungan yang memang ada di margin; opsi baru ditambahkan pada tahun-tahun terakhir bertentangan dengan “present for two decades”; opsi sudah paham lebih dulu membalik kalimat itu.

qs: How has the writer's view of his father's full signature changed?
What once seemed formal now strikes him as a merely careless habit.
What once seemed funny now reads as a claim to be recognized.
What once seemed touching now looks like ordinary business practice.
He still finds the full signature comic, postcards included.

qs.evidence: He signed each item with his complete name, including the postcards, a habit formerly comic and now legible as something else entirely.
qs.answer: What once seemed funny now reads as a claim to be recognized.
qs.why: Kebiasaan menandatangani dengan nama lengkap disebut dulu lucu dan sekarang terbaca sebagai sesuatu yang sama sekali lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi jadi terkesan sembarangan membalik arah perubahan itu; opsi jadi tampak sebagai praktik bisnis biasa mengosongkan kalimat “something else entirely”; opsi masih lucu bertentangan dengan kata “formerly”.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the final sentence about carelessness?
His father wrote badly because nobody had ever bothered to correct him.
The arrangement was discussed openly with the rest of the family.
He paid for his own education across those eleven years.
His freedom to write badly was paid for quietly by his father.

qs.evidence: He purchased my carelessness, and he performed the calculation in the corner monthly for eleven years without once disclosing the arrangement to anybody.
qs.answer: His freedom to write badly was paid for quietly by his father.
qs.why: Ayahnya disebut membeli kelalaian penulis, dan melakukan hitungan itu setiap bulan selama sebelas tahun tanpa pernah memberitahukannya kepada siapa pun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi ayah yang menulis buruk menukar siapa yang lalai; opsi dibicarakan terbuka bertentangan dengan “without once disclosing the arrangement”; opsi membiayai sendiri bertentangan dengan kata “purchased”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer learnt the reason for the capital letters from a relative."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer learnt the reason for the capital letters from a relative.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: He never divulged the decision, which reached me only through an aunt, three months after the funeral, in a kitchen crowded with unwashed crockery.
qs.why: Alasan huruf kapital itu sampai kepadanya lewat bibinya, jadi klaim ini parafrasa yang tepat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena sumber informasinya disebut.

topic: a father's letters and the calculations in their margins
author: Ilham Setyanto
setting: a reflective essay on family letters

title: The Comfort of the Single Number
text:
Each week a headline proclaims that researchers have finally settled something of importance. The verb is revealing: to settle a dispute is to conclude an argument and restore the furniture to its accustomed position. Yet the studies that lie beneath such headlines seldom conclude anything whatever. They narrow a range, adjust a probability, and bequeath to the following investigator a marginally sharper question. What reaches the public, however, is a solitary figure, stripped of the modest brackets that formerly enclosed it.

Those brackets are not ornament, since a confidence interval registers how far a measurement might wander were the same study repeated. Suppose a bulletin asserts that a treatment diminishes risk by twelve per cent, the interval extending from three to twenty-one. The candid summary is therefore that the effect is probably genuine and probably rather slight. Editors dislike such a sentence, which possesses no shape you can insert into a coloured panel above a photograph. So the brackets are silently deleted, and the twelve survives alone, appearing far sturdier than it ever was.

The practice is not merely negligence, because audiences reward certainty and pay remarkably little for honest doubt. So do funding bodies, ministers, and committees obliged to determine something before Friday afternoon. A researcher announcing mixed evidence invariably sounds weaker than a colleague announcing unambiguous evidence. That holds even where the cautious speaker is describing the world considerably more faithfully. Uncertainty, in short, is expensive to articulate and cheap to disregard, and the market for it remains thin.

A further penalty exists, and it descends upon the sciences rather than upon the newspapers that shorten them. If every finding is proclaimed a settlement, every subsequent revision begins to resemble a scandal. The public thereby absorbs a peculiar lesson concerning the very institutions it is invited to trust. It concludes that researchers constantly alter their opinions, as though revising a judgement under fresh evidence were a defect of character rather than the entire method. Confidence erodes, then, not because the science was mistaken, but because it was oversold from the outset.

None of this argues for retreat into fog, and the scientist sheltering behind qualifications fails in the contrary direction. The valuable discipline is to state what is known, to state how firmly it is known, and to hold both claims within a single sentence. That is considerably harder than it sounds, and it will never sit comfortably atop a crowded page. Audiences, however, are not infants, and a declared range is no confession of failure. It is simply the shape that an honest answer has always assumed.
qs: Which statement best captures the essay's central argument?
Editors are the sole obstacle, since researchers themselves report doubt willingly.
Erasing stated ranges flatters an audience and slowly corrodes confidence in research.
Results should be withheld from the press until their ranges have narrowed.
Confidence in published research falls chiefly because the findings keep being revised afterwards.

qs.evidence: Confidence erodes, then, not because the science was mistaken, but because it was oversold from the outset.
qs.answer: Erasing stated ranges flatters an audience and slowly corrodes confidence in research.
qs.why: Inti esainya: kepercayaan runtuh bukan gara-gara sainsnya salah, tapi gara-gara dijual kelewat yakin. Kunci ini ngomongin hal yang sama pakai kata lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang praktik ini bukan cuma kelalaian editor: pembaca, pemberi dana, dan komite juga membayar mahal buat kepastian. Menahan hasil sampai rentangnya sempit justru ditolak paragraf penutup, yang minta pernyataan disertai derajat keyakinannya. Dan kepercayaan disebut runtuh karena hasilnya dijual kelewat yakin, bukan karena revisinya sendiri.

qs: What does the essay suggest about the editors who remove the brackets?
They act largely out of contempt for readers they take to be poor at arithmetic.
They answer a demand for tidy claims rather than invent false figures.
They usually consult the researcher before any bracket is dropped from a summary.
They print the stated interval whenever the page layout leaves room for it.

qs.evidence: Editors dislike such a sentence, which possesses no shape you can insert into a coloured panel above a photograph.
qs.answer: They answer a demand for tidy claims rather than invent false figures.
qs.why: Alasan yang dikasih soal editor itu soal bentuk yang gampang dipajang, bukan niat menipu. Jadi yang disimpulkan: mereka ngikutin permintaan pasar akan klaim rapi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Alasan yang dikasih teks soal bentuk yang bisa dipajang di panel berwarna, bukan penghinaan ke pembaca. Konsultasi ke peneliti nggak pernah disebut — tanda kurungnya dihapus diam-diam. Dan editor justru digambarkan nggak suka kalimat berisi rentang, jadi bukan soal ruang di halaman.

qs: How would you describe the writer's tone in the third paragraph?
Drily ironic about the low market value of honest hesitation.
Coolly analytical, setting out the incentives with no evident irony.
Quietly indignant on behalf of researchers who report mixed evidence.
Wearily nostalgic for readers who once tolerated a stated range.

qs.evidence: Uncertainty, in short, is expensive to articulate and cheap to disregard, and the market for it remains thin.
qs.answer: Drily ironic about the low market value of honest hesitation.
qs.why: Penulis pakai bahasa dagang buat ngomongin keraguan, dan itu sinis yang dingin, bukan marah-marah. Ironinya kelihatan dari “cheap to ignore”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Paragrafnya pakai bahasa pasar — mahal diucapkan, murah diabaikan, pasarnya tipis — buat hal yang jelas dinilai penulis, jadi bukan uraian netral tanpa ironi. Nggak ada kemarahan yang dibela atas nama peneliti, dan nggak ada masa lalu yang dirindukan: paragraf itu ngomongin insentif yang berlaku sekarang.

qs: In the opening paragraph, what does "settled" convey about the promised result?
That the finding has quietly been absorbed into standard practice.
That a noisy dispute has calmed although the evidence is unchanged.
That an unresolved question has been sent back for further work.
That the question is now closed and needs no further argument.

qs.evidence: The verb is revealing: to settle a dispute is to conclude an argument and restore the furniture to its accustomed position.
qs.answer: That the question is now closed and needs no further argument.
qs.why: Penulis sendiri ngasih glosnya: menutup perdebatan dan menaruh kembali perabot. Artinya soalnya dianggap kelar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis ngasih glosnya sendiri: menutup perdebatan dan menaruh perabot kembali ke tempatnya. Jadi bukan temuan yang diserap praktik, bukan keributan yang mereda tanpa bukti baru, dan jelas bukan pertanyaan yang dikembalikan buat diteliti lagi.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Audiences usually receive one bare figure, with the surrounding range removed."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Audiences usually receive one bare figure, with the surrounding range removed.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: What reaches the public, however, is a solitary figure, stripped of the modest brackets that formerly enclosed it.
qs.why: Teks bilang yang sampai ke publik cuma satu angka, dilepas dari tanda kurung yang tadinya nemenin. Klaimnya cuma ganti pilihan kata, isinya sama, jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh teks yang nyatakan kebalikannya, dan itu nggak ada. “Not stated” juga gagal karena kalimat itu terang-terangan nyebut angka tunggal tanpa rentangnya.

author: Adila Rahmawati
setting: the science pages of the daily press

title: How a Journey Became an Ascent
text:
Keywords seldom arrive fully formed; they are assembled gradually, out of older quarrels, and then presented to subsequent generations as plain common sense. The term progress supplies a particularly instructive instance of the process. During the seventeenth century it still bore its literal sense of a journey, a royal procession advancing from one town to the next. Only afterwards did it acquire the meaning of ascent, a movement upward through time, in which each century supposedly surpassed the one preceding it.

The transformation depended upon two borrowed ideas that had remarkably little to do with each other. The first emerged from the workshop, where instruments and techniques genuinely did accumulate, so that a later craftsman commenced where an earlier one had halted. The second descended from theology, which had long conceived history as a single narrative possessing a destination. Once the accumulating workshop was fitted into the theological narrative, a formidable hybrid emerged. History could now be depicted as an upward road, furnished with measurable milestones and no serious prospect of return.

Nineteenth-century writers found this hybrid extremely convenient, and they applied it far beyond the workshop. Legal codes, languages, diets, and entire societies were arranged along the same imagined road. Those situated near its terminus recognized themselves as advanced, and the arrangement conveniently justified whatever they were already undertaking. The term had thereby become an argument, although it continued to resemble a mere description. Such is the hushed power of a keyword: it settles a contest before the contest has been declared.

Historians of ideas therefore treat such vocabulary as evidence rather than as neutral instruments. When a nineteenth-century official records that a province is making progress, the sentence documents his standards, not the province's condition. Reading it as a fact repeats his verdict; reading it as a claim exposes that verdict to inspection. The distinction matters most where the vocabulary still feels natural, because a word that feels natural is a word that has ceased to be examined. Few terms feel more natural presently than the one traced here.

This is not an argument that nothing improves, which would be a foolish position to defend. Water supplies improve, techniques sharpen, and certain cruelties genuinely recede within a single lifetime. The argument is narrower and considerably more awkward than that. It concerns the transition from numerous separate improvements, each with its own measure, to a solitary upward line along which everything is supposed to travel together. That line was drawn by particular individuals for particular purposes, and it can be redrawn.
qs: What is the relationship between the workshop idea and the theological idea in this account?
Their combination produced the upward road that later writers took for granted.
The theological narrative absorbed the workshop idea and then discarded it.
The workshop idea was the older of the two and gave theology its destination.
Both ideas were resisted by nineteenth-century officials who preferred separate local measures.

qs.evidence: Once the accumulating workshop was fitted into the theological narrative, a formidable hybrid emerged.
qs.answer: Their combination produced the upward road that later writers took for granted.
qs.why: Teks nyebut dua gagasan itu digabung sampai lahir “hybrid” yang lalu dipakai luas. Jadi hubungannya penggabungan, bukan pergantian.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang bengkel dipasang ke dalam cerita teologis sampai lahir hibrida, jadi nggak ada yang dibuang. Tujuan sejarah justru sudah lama ada di teologi, bukan warisan bengkel. Dan pejabat abad ke-19 memakai kosakata itu buat menilai provinsi, bukan menolaknya.

qs: What does the article imply about words that feel entirely natural to us?
They have been examined so often that a further inspection would add nothing.
They survive in official prose precisely because they carry no judgement whatever.
They tend to disappear from official documents within a generation or two.
They are the least likely to be questioned, and therefore most need inspection.

qs.evidence: The distinction matters most where the vocabulary still feels natural, because a word that feels natural is a word that has ceased to be examined.
qs.answer: They are the least likely to be questioned, and therefore most need inspection.
qs.why: Kalau kata yang terasa wajar itu kata yang berhenti diperiksa, kesimpulannya justru kata itulah yang paling perlu diperiksa.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalimat kuncinya bilang kata yang terasa wajar adalah kata yang berhenti diperiksa, jadi bukan kata yang sudah kelewat sering diperiksa. Seluruh esai justru nunjukin kata semacam itu memuat penilaian, bukan bebas nilai. Soal kata menghilang dari dokumen resmi nggak pernah disinggung.

qs: Which description best fits the writer's stance towards nineteenth-century usage?
Respectful, treating their usage as largely an honest attempt at plain description.
Impatient, presenting the upward road as only a plain intellectual error.
Sceptical but measured, granting the usefulness while exposing the interest.
Detached, since the article treats old usage as largely a verbal matter.

qs.evidence: Those situated near its terminus recognized themselves as advanced, and the arrangement conveniently justified whatever they were already undertaking.
qs.answer: Sceptical but measured, granting the usefulness while exposing the interest.
qs.why: Kata “conveniently” nunjukin curiga, tapi penulis tetap ngakuin gagasan itu berguna banget buat penulis abad ke-19. Jadi skeptis yang terukur.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kata “conveniently” dan kalimat bahwa istilah itu sudah menjadi argumen nunjukin penulis mencurigai kepentingan di baliknya, jadi bukan sikap hormat yang nganggep itu deskripsi jujur. Dia juga nggak menyebutnya kekeliruan belaka: hibridanya disebut “extremely convenient”. Dan urusannya bukan cuma kata, tapi verdik yang diselundupkan kata itu.

qs: Which sentence best restates the final paragraph's argument?
Improvements are real, so the single upward line deserves its wide acceptance.
Separate gains are real, but merging them into one shared ascent is a choice.
Only material gains such as water and medicine count as genuine improvement.
Improvements cannot be measured separately, which is why one line was drawn.

qs.evidence: It concerns the transition from numerous separate improvements, each with its own measure, to a solitary upward line along which everything is supposed to travel together.
qs.answer: Separate gains are real, but merging them into one shared ascent is a choice.
qs.why: Paragraf akhir ngaku ada perbaikan nyata, lalu mempersoalkan langkah dari banyak perbaikan terpisah jadi satu garis naik. Itu tepatnya isi kunci ini.
qs.whyOthersFail: Paragrafnya justru mempersoalkan garis naik tunggal itu, jadi bukan pembenaran atas garisnya. Air dan teknik cuma contoh, bukan daftar tertutup kemajuan yang sah. Dan teks bilang tiap perbaikan punya ukurannya sendiri, jadi bukan alasan bahwa mengukurnya terpisah nggak mungkin.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "In the seventeenth century the word already meant an upward movement through time."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: In the seventeenth century the word already meant an upward movement through time.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: During the seventeenth century it still bore its literal sense of a journey, a royal procession advancing from one town to the next.
qs.why: Teks bilang di abad ke-17 kata itu masih berarti perjalanan harfiah, dan makna naik-ke-atas baru datang belakangan. Klaimnya jadi kebalikan langsung, alias False.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bakal nabrak kalimat tentang prosesi kerajaan itu. “Not stated” juga salah karena kronologinya disebut terang-terangan.

author: Bram Setiadi
setting: a study in the history of ideas

title: Rehearsed Surprise
text:
The encore is the least spontaneous spontaneous act in all of public life. Everyone in the auditorium is aware it is imminent, including the performer who has already selected the piece. The applause that summons it is not a request but a cue, delivered punctually by an audience that has learnt its part. And yet the fiction holds: the player appears briefly astonished, the hall performs its delight, and something authentic somehow survives the entire transparent arrangement.

Part of the explanation resides in what the printed programme simply cannot accomplish. A concert is a formal object, timed and published, and its architecture must be honoured from the opening note. The encore sits outside that architecture, which is precisely why it may be brief, eccentric, or sentimental without reproach. Here the cellist offers a folk tune from her grandmother's village; there the pianist supplies ninety seconds of something composed for a forgotten film. Nothing is at stake, and the absence of stakes constitutes the entire point, since this is the one moment when the evening is permitted to be merely likeable.

The ritual also settles a debt that the printed programme leaves permanently outstanding. For two hours the audience has been silent, obedient, and largely invisible in the darkness. Nobody has spoken; nobody has been observed; the transaction has proceeded in a single direction. The encore inverts that arrangement briefly, because the clamour of the auditorium now produces the music rather than merely accompanying it. The performer, for one piece, is responding rather than delivering. The gesture, however slight, converts an audience from a collection of ticket holders into a body that has accomplished something collectively.

Cynics observe how thoroughly the whole affair is managed, and they are not mistaken. Encores are timed against the final train; the folk tune has been performed in eleven cities this month; the astonishment on the performer's countenance is a rehearsed skill like any other. But this objection confuses ritual with outright deception. Nobody attends a wedding supposing the vows were composed that morning, and the rehearsed quality of the phrases is precisely what permits them to carry weight.

What would be forfeited if the encore were simply printed in the programme, honestly and in advance? Something modest, certainly, but not nothing at all. The listener would still hear the folk tune, yet would no longer have summoned it, and the distinction between receiving and requesting is the distinction the ritual protects. An audience that never requests anything eventually ceases to expect a response. That may explain why the pretence survives every generation of critics who patiently expose it.
qs: What is the main point the writer makes about the encore?
Its effect depends on listeners not knowing the piece has been chosen.
Its openly staged quality is what lets it do genuine work for a hall.
It survives because programmes are too formal to include a folk tune.
It gives the performer a lighter piece after two hours of demanding work.

qs.evidence: But this objection confuses ritual with outright deception.
qs.answer: Its openly staged quality is what lets it do genuine work for a hall.
qs.why: Penulis ngakuin semuanya diatur, lalu bilang keberatan itu keliru nyamain ritual sama tipu-tipu. Justru sifat yang dipentaskan itulah yang bikin encore berfungsi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang semua orang di auditorium tahu encore-nya bakal datang dan fiksinya tetap jalan, jadi efeknya nggak bergantung pada ketidaktahuan penonton. Paragraf akhir malah membayangkan lagu rakyat itu dicetak di program, jadi bukan soal program yang nggak boleh memuatnya. Dan istirahat pemain sama sekali nggak disebut.

qs: What can be inferred about the audience's silence during the main programme?
It leaves the audience passive, which the encore then briefly reverses.
It shows that most listeners prefer the encore to the works printed in the programme.
It is what allows the hall to hear the folk tune clearly at the end.
It is enforced by ushers in the halls the writer has in mind.

qs.evidence: For two hours the audience has been silent, obedient, and largely invisible in the darkness.
qs.answer: It leaves the audience passive, which the encore then briefly reverses.
qs.why: Dua jam duduk diam dan nggak kelihatan itu posisi pasif, dan teks bilang encore membalik susunan itu sebentar. Kesimpulannya nyambung langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak pernah membandingkan selera penonton antara encore dan karya utama. Keheningan dua jam itu digambarkan sebagai transaksi satu arah, bukan syarat supaya lagu rakyat kedengaran jernih. Dan nggak ada petugas yang memaksa siapa pun diam; yang disebut cuma penonton yang sudah hafal perannya.

qs: How does the writer handle the cynics' objection?
By largely accepting the objection and narrowing the claim to accommodate it.
By setting it aside as only a matter of taste that argument cannot settle.
By conceding the facts while rejecting the conclusion drawn from them.
By answering it with figures showing how rarely encores are planned.

qs.evidence: Cynics observe how thoroughly the whole affair is managed, and they are not mistaken.
qs.answer: By conceding the facts while rejecting the conclusion drawn from them.
qs.why: Penulis bilang para sinis itu “not wrong” soal faktanya, tapi langsung nolak simpulan mereka lewat perbandingan janji pernikahan. Itu mengakui sekaligus menolak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis bilang para sinis “are not mistaken” soal faktanya, tapi keberatan mereka dia sebut keliru menyamakan ritual dengan penipuan — jadi klaimnya nggak dipersempit dan nggak dibiarkan sebagai soal selera. Dia juga nggak menyajikan angka apa pun; alatnya perbandingan janji pernikahan.

qs: In the second paragraph, what does "stakes" refer to?
The reputation that a soloist may risk with an unfamiliar short piece.
The formal obligations that a published programme can impose on a hall.
The share of the ticket income that the visiting soloist receives.
Anything of consequence that a performance might risk losing.

qs.evidence: Nothing is at stake, and the absence of stakes constitutes the entire point, since this is the one moment when the evening is permitted to be merely likeable.
qs.answer: Anything of consequence that a performance might risk losing.
qs.why: Konteksnya: encore boleh pendek, aneh, atau sentimental “without damage”, jadi “stakes” di sini soal hal berharga yang bisa hilang kalau gagal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalimatnya justru menaruh “nothing is at stake” sebagai inti: encore boleh pendek, aneh, atau sentimental tanpa kerugian, jadi reputasi solois bukan maksudnya. Kewajiban formal itu urusan arsitektur program di paragraf sebelumnya. Bagi hasil tiket makna lain kata yang sama dan nggak muncul di teks.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The applause before an encore functions as a signal rather than a genuine plea."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The applause before an encore functions as a signal rather than a genuine plea.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The applause that summons it is not a request but a cue, delivered punctually by an audience that has learnt its part.
qs.why: Teks bilang tepuk tangan itu bukan permintaan tapi isyarat yang datang tepat waktu. Klaimnya sama, cuma pakai kata lain, jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” perlu teks yang bilang tepuk tangan itu permohonan sungguhan, dan itu justru yang dibantah. “Not stated” gagal karena kalimatnya eksplisit.

topic: the ritual of the concert encore
author: Citra Wibowo
setting: a concert hall after the printed programme ends

title: Nine Metres Behind the Depot
text:
There is a strip of neglected ground behind the bus depot that belongs to nobody in particular. It measures nine metres across, is fenced along one flank, and appears on the district survey as an unshaded interval between two numbered plots. I have trudged past it for eleven years, and recently I began pausing there, largely because I had exhausted my pretexts for hurrying.

Nothing whatever has been designed here, and that is the initial circumstance any attentive observer registers. Buddleia has colonized the brickwork, willowherb the gravel, and a fig has established itself beneath a leaking downpipe. Somebody deposited two crates, which were subsequently adopted as a seat and then abandoned again to the weather. Cigarette stubs trace a rough circle, which suggests that individuals congregate here in twos and threes, beyond the sightlines of the depot itself. None of this was planned by anyone, yet it possesses an unmistakable order, and that order was inscribed by use rather than by drawing.

Architects possess a term for such locations, and the term amounts to a modest professional confession. They are termed residual, as though the metropolis were an arithmetical calculation and these were the figures remaining once the sum had been completed. The label is accurate and faintly clinical: residual space is whatever the drawings could not absorb, and every scheme generates some, however meticulous the planner has been. An urban fabric containing no residual ground would be a settlement in which every square metre had been assigned a purpose by an individual who does not reside there.

I shall not pretend that the strip behind the depot is attractive, because it is not, and the assertion would be sentimental nonsense. In humid conditions it smells distinctly of diesel and rotting cardboard. But it is the only ground within a kilometre where a pedestrian may loiter without purchasing anything, awaiting anything, or being ushered politely along. Its value consists precisely in its lack of function, and function is the one commodity that improvement unfailingly imports.

In April the fence was renewed, the brambles were cut back and the crates vanished. A notice announced a forthcoming scheme of tidying, comprising three trees and a paved path. I discovered that I minded considerably more than I could justify to anybody who enquired. Three mature trees are preferable to none, and a paved path is unquestionably preferable to February mud. Nevertheless, once the path materializes, the strip will ultimately have been granted a function. Those who once gathered there in twos and threes will migrate to some further gap that the plan has not yet registered.
qs: What is the relationship between the absence of a plan and the order the writer finds?
The order arose from repeated use precisely because nothing was drawn first.
The order was imposed later by the officials who surveyed the two plots.
The order survives only in the writer's memory of an earlier arrangement.
The order would have been firmer if a designer had set the ground out properly first.
