qs.answer: Expose how narrative convention overrides observation of the animal.
qs.why: Kalimat pendek itu menohok: yang kita kenali dulu adalah pola cerita, bukan hewannya. Fungsinya membongkar dominasi konvensi naratif.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalimat “we recognize the plot before we recognize the species” dipakai buat membongkar dominasi konvensi cerita, bukan memuji narator. Teks nggak bilang penonton nggak bisa mengenali spesies, cuma bilang polanya dikenali lebih dulu. Dan reformasi yang diusulkan adalah menampilkan kerjanya, bukan membuang narasi.

qs: Which statement best restates the writer's response to the argument from consequence?
The claim is false, since petitions follow beauty rather than science.
The claim has been tested carefully by the film-makers who rely on it.
The claim matters less than how the finished sequence looks on screen.
The claim may well be sound, yet its defenders leave it untested.

qs.evidence: The objection is not that the argument is erroneous but that it has never been examined by the individuals who make it most often.
qs.answer: The claim may well be sound, yet its defenders leave it untested.
qs.why: Penulis nggak bilang argumennya salah; dia bilang argumen itu nggak pernah diuji sama orang yang paling sering memakainya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis bilang keberatannya bukan bahwa argumen itu keliru, jadi bukan “jelas salah”. Justru intinya argumen itu nggak pernah diperiksa oleh orang yang paling sering memakainya. Dan keindahan hasil akhir diakui, tapi bukan alasan menolak argumennya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The six camera teams worked in the three locations at the same time."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The six camera teams worked in the three locations at the same time.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: The sequence is exquisite, extravagant, and constructed from footage gathered over fourteen months by six camera teams in three locations.
qs.why: Teks nyebut enam tim, tiga lokasi, dan empat belas bulan, tapi nggak pernah bilang apa mereka kerja serentak atau bergantian. Jadi Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” nambahin keterangan waktu yang nggak ada. “False” juga salah karena teks nggak menyangkal kerja serentak; dia cuma nggak menyinggungnya.

author: Nadira Wisesa
setting: a wildlife series and its production

title: A Genius, Not Genius
text:
Before the middle of the eighteenth century, a person did not have genius; a person had a genius, in the way that a place had one. The term denoted an attendant spirit, external and local, which visited and might depart, unannounced. Within two generations the grammar had inverted, and genius had become an interior property, unevenly distributed, possessed by particular individuals from birth. The change appears minor on the page and proved consequential in virtually every institution touching the arts.

The older arrangement carried an implication we have largely lost, and lost unnoticed. If inspiration arrived from outside, the maker was a channel, and craft consisted in being reliably available. Workshops therefore trained pupils in procedure, and a competent pupil might be trusted with a commission bearing the master's name. Nobody found this fraudulent, because the work was understood as the product of a method rather than of a personality, and attribution mattered for payment and not for authenticity, a distinction subsequently inverted.

Romantic writers reversed the polarity deliberately, and their motives were partly commercial, partly polemical. A market in printed works required something to distinguish one supplier from another, and interior genius performed that task admirably. It also solved a difficulty about rules, since a figure exceeding the rules cannot be judged by them. Originality became the criterion, the biography became evidence, and the childhood of the artist acquired a significance it had never previously held, and every subsequent complaint about difficult art descends from that settlement, unmistakably.

The consequences for the individuals so described were less enviable than the vocabulary suggests, considerably less. A property held from birth cannot be acquired, nor legitimately explained by effort. Practice therefore had to be concealed, and letters from the period display an increasing anxiety about appearing to have worked. The concealment was not hypocrisy so much as an occupational requirement, professionally enforced, and a doctrine devised to elevate the artist obliged the artist to lie about the mornings, daily.

The category has proved unusually durable, and continues to organize prizes, curricula, and the marketing of biographies. Its costs are apparent in what it excludes: collaborative labour, revision, and every tradition in which a name is not the unit of value. None of this establishes that talent is evenly distributed, which would be a separate argument, unpromising and unnecessary. It establishes only that a particular explanation of talent was constructed at a particular moment, by identifiable interests. Attendant spirits, whatever their other faults, at least did not have to pretend they were self-made.
qs: What is the relationship between the older idea of genius and workshop practice?
Treating inspiration as external obliged the masters to sign each commission themselves.
Workshop training built the print market the Romantics later exploited.
Pupils were barred from work that carried the master's name on it.
Treating inspiration as external made shared production perfectly respectable.

qs.evidence: Nobody found this fraudulent, because the work was understood as the product of a method rather than of a personality
qs.answer: Treating inspiration as external made shared production perfectly respectable.
qs.why: Kalau ilham datang dari luar, karya dianggap hasil metode, bukan kepribadian. Makanya kerja bersama di bengkel nggak dianggap penipuan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang atribusi penting buat pembayaran, bukan buat keaslian, jadi nggak ada kewajiban tanda tangan. Pasar cetak muncul di paragraf Romantik sebagai penyebab pembalikan, bukan buah pelatihan bengkel. Dan murid yang cakap justru dipercaya mengerjakan pesanan bernama gurunya.

qs: What does the essay imply about artists writing letters in that period?
They treated revision as the most admirable part of the work.
They were instructed by patrons never to mention any effort.
They had reason to understate the hours their work required.
They described their childhoods in order to attract commissions.

qs.evidence: Practice therefore had to be concealed, and letters from the period display an increasing anxiety about appearing to have worked.
qs.answer: They had reason to understate the hours their work required.
qs.why: Latihan harus disembunyikan dan surat-surat memperlihatkan kecemasan kelihatan bekerja. Jadi mereka punya alasan mengecilkan jam kerjanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Revisi disebut termasuk yang tersingkir oleh kategori genius, bukan yang dipuji. Larangan dari pelindung nggak ada di teks: penyembunyian disebut tuntutan pekerjaan. Dan masa kecil seniman jadi bukti bagi kritikus, bukan alat memancing pesanan.

qs: What does the closing sentence achieve?
It ends the argument on a note of deliberate irony.
It proposes, in earnest, a revival of the older belief.
It admits the essay has proved less than it set out to.
It credits Romantic writers with commercial ingenuity.

qs.evidence: Attendant spirits, whatever their other faults, at least did not have to pretend they were self-made.
qs.answer: It ends the argument on a note of deliberate irony.
qs.why: Penulis muji roh pendamping cuma buat nyindir doktrin yang bikin seniman harus pura-pura mandiri. Itu ironi yang disengaja.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pujian pada roh pendamping dipakai buat menohok doktrin yang memaksa seniman berpura-pura mandiri, jadi bukan usulan serius. Paragraf itu justru menyatakan apa yang berhasil ditunjukkan esainya. Dan motif komersial Romantik dibongkar, bukan dipuji.

qs: What does "property" mean in the third sentence?
A quality belonging to a person rather than an owned possession.
A workshop building that a master may hold under a legal title.
A stage object handled by performers rather than by a workshop.
An agreement transferring a commission between two workshops.

qs.evidence: Within two generations the grammar had inverted, and genius had become an interior property, unevenly distributed, possessed by particular individuals from birth.
qs.answer: A quality belonging to a person rather than an owned possession.
qs.why: Kata itu dipakai bareng “interior” dan “possessed from birth”, jadi maksudnya sifat yang melekat pada orang, bukan harta yang dimiliki.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kata itu berdiri di sebelah “interior” dan “possessed from birth”, jadi soal sifat yang melekat pada orang. Tanah bersertifikat, perlengkapan panggung, dan akta pengalihan hak sah dalam kamus tapi nggak nyambung sama sesuatu yang dibawa sejak lahir.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The idea of inborn genius served a commercial need to tell rival producers apart."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The idea of inborn genius served a commercial need to tell rival producers apart.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: A market in printed works required something to distinguish one supplier from another, and interior genius performed that task admirably.
qs.why: Teks bilang pasar cetak butuh pembeda antar pemasok, dan gagasan genius batiniah menjalankan tugas itu. Klaimnya sama, cuma pilih kata lain, jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh bantahan atas motif komersial, dan itu nggak ada. “Not stated” gagal karena fungsi komersialnya disebut langsung.

topic: the invention of the modern idea of genius
author: Oka Prasetyo
setting: the European arts between two centuries

title: Eight Metres of Patience
text:
The bog begins where the path stops pretending to be a path, somewhere short of the ridge. The surface sinks by a couple of centimetres and then refuses, the experience of standing on eight metres of accumulated vegetation that never fully decayed. Sphagnum moss grows at the surface and dies beneath it, and the waterlogging excludes the oxygen that would normally complete the transaction. What results is neither soil nor lake but an archive, laid down at approximately one millimetre a year, in strict chronological order.

That figure is the entire difficulty of peatland restoration, and no quantity of enthusiasm removes it. A drainage ditch cut in nineteen sixty-three took an afternoon; the surface it lowered will require several centuries to recover its former height. Contractors can block the ditches, reintroduce the moss, and monitor the water table; every such intervention is valuable, and none of them alters the millimetre. The vocabulary of projects, with its milestones and reporting cycles, conflicts with a process indifferent to funding rounds.

I have visited the same hectare in four consecutive Novembers, and the honest assessment is that virtually nothing visible has altered. The pools are marginally wider, a cotton-grass has colonized a formerly bare bank of peat, and one dead pine, drowned by the rising water, has toppled. To a funder they represent disappointing deliverables, unquantifiable and unphotographable. To the bog they are the opening clauses of an extremely long sentence whose grammar is not ours to hurry.

The temptation to convert this slowness into consolation is one I intend to resist. Slowness is not a virtue here; it is merely the rate at which repair becomes possible, and rates are not moral qualities. It follows that the individuals who drained this ground will never witness it healed, and neither shall we. Restoration on this timescale is an act performed for strangers, which is uncomfortable rather than encouraging, and the discomfort is the accurate response.

What the bog offers is a challenge to a habit of attention formed elsewhere. Standing on it, you cannot perceive the process you are standing on, and the wish to declare the visit uneventful is powerful. The uneventfulness is the event. Carbon that would otherwise occupy the atmosphere is instead beneath my boots, held there by waterlogging and by nothing else, and the arrangement persists only while the water remains. Everything the site requires from us is a matter of leaving the water alone, a strangely difficult instruction to present as work.
qs: What is the main point the writer makes about restoring the bog?
Blocking the drainage ditches restores the surface to its old height within a decade.
Repair here runs at a rate that funding rounds and reporting cycles cannot match.
Four Novembers of visible change show the restoration has already worked.
The slowness of the bog is a consoling lesson in conservation patience.

qs.evidence: The vocabulary of projects, with its milestones and reporting cycles, conflicts with a process indifferent to funding rounds.
qs.answer: Repair here runs at a rate that funding rounds and reporting cycles cannot match.
qs.why: Teks bilang kosakata proyek, dengan milestone dan siklus pelaporannya, nggak nyambung sama proses yang cuma jalan satu milimeter setahun. Itu inti keluhannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang permukaan yang diturunkan butuh beberapa abad buat pulih, jadi bukan satu dekade. Empat November berturut-turut justru menghasilkan penilaian bahwa hampir nggak ada yang berubah. Dan penulis terang-terangan menolak godaan mengubah kelambatan itu jadi penghiburan.

qs: What does the writer imply about who will benefit from the work?
Funders will see a return once the present reporting cycle has closed.
The contractors who blocked the ditches will watch the surface recover.
Nobody benefits from the work, so the moss is better left alone.
The people alive today will hand the result to strangers they cannot know.

qs.evidence: Restoration on this timescale is an act performed for strangers
qs.answer: The people alive today will hand the result to strangers they cannot know.
qs.why: Kalau pemulihan disebut tindakan untuk orang asing, dan yang mengeringkan lahan ini nggak akan lihat hasilnya, maka penerima manfaatnya generasi yang belum kamu kenal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Siklus pelaporan disebut bertabrakan dengan proses yang nggak peduli putaran dana, jadi bukan tempat hasilnya muncul. Pemulihannya butuh berabad-abad, jadi kontraktor nggak akan menyaksikannya. Dan teks bilang manfaatnya nyata tapi jatuh ke orang asing, bukan nggak ada.

qs: What is the writer's attitude to the slowness of the process?
Unsentimental, refusing to convert the slowness into any consolation.
Triumphant about the widening pools and the pine that has toppled.
Despairing, treating the drained ground as beyond any repair at all.
Impatient with contractors who monitor the water table so slowly.

qs.evidence: The temptation to convert this slowness into consolation is one I intend to resist.
qs.answer: Unsentimental, refusing to convert the slowness into any consolation.
qs.why: Dia sebut godaan mengubah kelambatan jadi penghiburan, lalu nolak godaan itu, dan bilang rasa nggak nyaman adalah respons yang tepat. Itu nada tanpa sentimentalitas.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kolam yang sedikit melebar dan pinus tumbang justru disebut hasil yang mengecewakan buat pemberi dana, jadi bukan bahan kemenangan. Teks bilang kelambatan itu laju saat perbaikan jadi mungkin, jadi bukan keputusasaan. Dan kontraktor disebut mengerjakan hal yang berharga, tanpa kritik sama sekali.

qs: Which sentence best restates the point about a visit feeling uneventful?
A visit feels quiet because the pools have widened only slightly.
The site is genuinely inactive until somebody blocks the drainage ditches again.
Nothing appearing to happen is precisely what the site's function looks like.
Anyone standing on the bog should expect dramatic change in time.

qs.evidence: The uneventfulness is the event.
qs.answer: Nothing appearing to happen is precisely what the site's function looks like.
qs.why: “The uneventfulness is the event” artinya justru ketiadaan kejadian itulah kerja rawa: karbon tetap tersimpan selama airnya nggak diganggu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kesan sepi itu datang karena prosesnya nggak bisa dilihat sambil berdiri di atasnya, bukan karena kolamnya cuma melebar sedikit. Rawa itu justru sedang bekerja menahan karbon, jadi nggak pasif. Dan perubahan dramatis mustahil pada laju satu milimeter setahun.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Cutting the drainage ditch in nineteen sixty-three was itself a task of several centuries."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Cutting the drainage ditch in nineteen sixty-three was itself a task of several centuries.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: A drainage ditch cut in nineteen sixty-three took an afternoon; the surface it lowered will require several centuries to recover its former height.
qs.why: Teks bilang parit itu digali dalam satu sore. Yang butuh beberapa abad adalah pemulihannya, bukan penggaliannya, jadi klaimnya salah.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” cuma jalan kalau kamu menukar dua angka waktu itu. “Not stated” gagal karena kedua durasi disebut eksplisit di kalimat yang sama.

topic: peatland restoration and the timescale of repair
author: Panji Kusumo
setting: a drained upland bog under slow restoration

title: The Acoustics of Applause
text:
Applause has attracted less scholarly attention than the music it interrupts, which is odd, since it is the only sound in a concert hall produced by the audience deliberately. A recent series of measurements in four European halls treated it as an acoustic phenomenon rather than a social one, recording onset, duration, and decay across two hundred and eleven performances. The resulting data set is small but suggestive. It indicates that applause behaves less like noise than like a collective instrument with predictable properties.

The most consistent finding concerns latency. In halls with a reverberation time above two seconds, the interval between the final chord and the first clap extended by roughly four hundred milliseconds compared with drier rooms. The investigators attribute this to ambiguity: where the sound persists, listeners cannot determine when the performance has ended, and nobody wishes to be the individual who applauds into a note. The measurements were taken at the same height in each room. Latency, on this reading, is not reverence but uncertainty rendered audible.

A second finding is harder to interpret and correspondingly more interesting. Duration correlated only weakly with any independent measure of the performance, including critical reception and ticket resale prices. It correlated strongly, however, with the proportion of the audience seated in the stalls rather than in the upper tiers. The authors propose a mechanism involving sightlines and mutual visibility, since clapping is partly imitative and imitation requires observing what others do. Whether the effect survives replication in halls with different geometries remains unestablished.

The methodological limitations deserve emphasis, because the study has been reported more confidently than it was written. Four halls is a small sample, all four are in cities with comparable concert-going conventions, and the microphone arrays were positioned for convenience rather than for uniformity. The authors state these constraints plainly in a section that few summaries have troubled to read. They do not pretend otherwise. Their claim concerns measurement, not musical value, and the distinction has been widely collapsed.

What the work does establish is that a behaviour dismissed as simple convention possesses a physics, and that the physics changes from hall to hall. If latency is produced by reverberation rather than by feeling, then a hall partly composes the response it receives. Architects have long known that a room shapes what performers do; the suggestion here is that it shapes what listeners do as well. That is a narrower conclusion than the headlines permitted, and a more durable one.
qs: What relationship does the study report between a hall's acoustics and its applause?
Longer reverberation lengthens the delay before an audience begins to clap.
Longer reverberation shortens how long the applause in the stalls lasts.
Critical reception decides the delay measured in the drier of the halls.
Ticket resale prices predict when the first clap arrives in each hall.

qs.evidence: In halls with a reverberation time above two seconds, the interval between the final chord and the first clap extended by roughly four hundred milliseconds compared with drier rooms.
qs.answer: Longer reverberation lengthens the delay before an audience begins to clap.
qs.why: Di aula dengan reverberasi di atas dua detik, jeda antara akord terakhir dan tepuk pertama memanjang sekitar empat ratus milidetik. Itu persis hubungan yang ditanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Durasi tepuk disebut cuma berkorelasi lemah dengan ukuran luar mana pun dan kuat dengan proporsi penonton di stalls, bukan dengan reverberasi. Resepsi kritikus dan harga tiket sekunder justru dua contoh korelasi lemah itu, jadi nggak bisa menentukan jeda apa pun.

qs: What can be inferred about the finding concerning the stalls?
It shows that listeners in the stalls enjoy the music more than others.
Its explanation remains provisional and awaits testing in other buildings.
It rules out sightlines as an influence on imitative clapping.
It was treated by press summaries as the firmest result of the study.

qs.evidence: Whether the effect survives replication in halls with different geometries remains unestablished.
qs.answer: Its explanation remains provisional and awaits testing in other buildings.
qs.why: Penulis bilang efeknya belum diketahui bertahan atau nggak di aula dengan geometri berbeda. Artinya mekanismenya masih dugaan yang perlu diuji ulang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Studinya mengukur bunyi, bukan kenikmatan, dan penulis bilang klaimnya soal pengukuran bukan nilai musik. Garis pandang justru mekanisme yang diusulkan, bukan yang dikesampingkan. Dan temuan paling konsisten disebut latency, bukan temuan soal stalls.

qs: How does the article characterize the authors' own handling of their limits?
As confident that four halls are enough for a general conclusion.
As dismissive of reverberation as an explanation of anything.
As candid, with the weaknesses of the sample stated openly.
As irritated by architects who ignore acoustic measurement.

qs.evidence: The authors state these constraints plainly in a section that few summaries have troubled to read.
qs.answer: As candid, with the weaknesses of the sample stated openly.
qs.why: Kendalanya ditulis terang-terangan oleh penulis studi; yang bermasalah justru ringkasan yang nggak membacanya. Jadi sikap mereka terbuka soal batas datanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Empat aula justru mereka sebut sampel kecil, jadi bukan sikap percaya diri. Reverberasi adalah variabel penjelas utama mereka, bukan yang ditolak. Dan arsitek disebut sudah lama tahu ruang membentuk perilaku, tanpa nada kesal apa pun.

qs: What does "latency" mean in the second paragraph?
The loudness reached at the peak of applause.
The time a sound needs to decay in a hall.
The delay before a response begins.
The share of listeners seated in the stalls.

qs.evidence: The measurements were taken at the same height in each room. Latency, on this reading, is not reverence but uncertainty rendered audible.
qs.answer: The delay before a response begins.
qs.why: Konteksnya jeda antara akord terakhir dan tepuk pertama, diukur dalam milidetik. Jadi latency di sini artinya tundaan sebelum respons dimulai.
qs.whyOthersFail: Konteksnya jeda dalam milidetik antara akord terakhir dan tepuk pertama. Kenyaringan puncak, waktu peluruhan bunyi, dan proporsi penonton di stalls memang diukur di studi yang sama, tapi ketiganya besaran lain.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The four halls in the study were all located in the same country."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The four halls in the study were all located in the same country.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Four halls is a small sample, all four are in cities with comparable concert-going conventions, and the microphone arrays were positioned for convenience rather than for uniformity.
qs.why: Teks cuma bilang keempatnya di kota dengan kebiasaan berkonser yang mirip, dan bahwa aulanya Eropa. Negara yang sama sekali nggak disebut, jadi Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” butuh pernyataan negara yang nggak ada. “False” juga butuh bukti bahwa negaranya berbeda, dan itu sama-sama nggak ada.

topic: measuring applause as an acoustic rather than social event
author: Ratna Sembiring
setting: a study across four European concert halls

title: Two Translations Too Many
text:
Every forecast reaching the public has been translated twice, and both translations lose something the audience is never informed about. The first converts a distribution into a number, because a distribution cannot be spoken aloud in fourteen seconds. The second converts the number into a verb: rain will fall, cases will rise, the deficit will widen. By the time the sentence arrives, the uncertainty constituting the actual finding has been filed away as a technicality.

Practitioners defend the compression on grounds of comprehension, and the defence is not absurd. Probability is genuinely arduous, percentages are misread routinely, and a forecaster insisting on intervals will be replaced by one who does not. Yet the empirical support for the assumption is thinner than its confidence suggests, and thinner than practitioners tend to concede. Studies of flood warnings and of medical prognosis both indicate that lay audiences handle stated ranges tolerably well, and that what they resent is not complexity but the discovery, afterwards, that complexity was withheld.

The cost of withholding it falls due at the first failed prediction, invariably in public. A hurricane that turns aside, an epidemic curve that flattens early, a recession forecast for a quarter that instead produced growth: each is entirely compatible with a competent probabilistic statement, and entirely incompatible with the flat declarative in which it was delivered. The forecaster is then accused of error when the genuine fault was rhetorical, a distinction nobody rewards. Trust erodes not because the science was wrong but because the grammar promised more than the science ever offered.

One obvious objection holds that hedged language invites paralysis. If the public is informed a storm might arrive, some proportion will decline to evacuate, and that proportion may include individuals who die. This is a serious argument deserving better than the slogan it has become. Nothing about stating a range requires abandoning a recommendation; the two operate at distinct levels of the same utterance. A warning can specify a seventy per cent chance and still instruct everybody to leave, provided the instruction is framed as a decision rather than as a description.

The situation demands a division of labour institutions have been reluctant to attempt. Scientists should report distributions, including the awkward extremes; communicators should convert distributions into decisions without pretending they are certainties; and audiences should be permitted to observe the seam between the two. The alternative, refined over several decades, is a public trained to treat every confident forecast as an overstatement and to discount accordingly. That habit is rational, it was taught deliberately, and it will be expensive to unteach.
qs: What is the central argument of the essay?
Probabilistic language should be dropped, because percentages are misread anyway.
Stripping uncertainty out of forecasts damages trust when a prediction fails.
Forecasters are usually incompetent when a hurricane changes its course.
Communicators should drop recommendations and publish raw distributions.

qs.evidence: Trust erodes not because the science was wrong but because the grammar promised more than the science ever offered.
qs.answer: Stripping uncertainty out of forecasts damages trust when a prediction fails.
qs.why: Kalimat kuncinya bilang kepercayaan runtuh bukan karena sainsnya keliru, tapi karena tata bahasanya menjanjikan lebih dari yang sains tawarkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis justru minta distribusi tetap dilaporkan, jadi bukan membuang bahasa probabilistik. Peramal dibela: kesalahannya disebut retoris, bukan ketidakcakapan. Dan rekomendasi tetap harus ada, cuma dibingkai sebagai keputusan, bukan deskripsi.

qs: What does the essay imply about the claim that audiences cannot cope with uncertainty?
It is confirmed by the studies of flood warnings that are cited.
It explains why a warning should never contain any instruction.
It holds for medical prognosis but not for warnings about floods.
It is an assumption that the available evidence does not support.

qs.evidence: Studies of flood warnings and of medical prognosis both indicate that lay audiences handle stated ranges tolerably well, and that what they resent is not complexity but the discovery, afterwards, that complexity was withheld.
qs.answer: It is an assumption that the available evidence does not support.
qs.why: Dua bidang studi yang dikutip nunjukin orang awam cukup sanggup membaca rentang. Jadi asumsi bahwa publik nggak sanggup itu justru nggak didukung bukti.
qs.whyOthersFail: Studi peringatan banjir dan prognosis medis justru menunjukkan orang awam cukup sanggup membaca rentang, jadi asumsinya dibantah bukan dikonfirmasi, dan keduanya memberi arah yang sama. Instruksi pun tetap dianjurkan sepanjang dinyatakan sebagai keputusan.

qs: How does the writer treat the objection about paralysis?
As something communicators invented with no evidence behind it.
As a decisive reason to keep every forecast flatly declarative.
As a genuine argument that has degenerated into a slogan.
As a minor issue beside the question of public trust.

qs.evidence: This is a serious argument deserving better than the slogan it has become.
qs.answer: As a genuine argument that has degenerated into a slogan.
qs.why: Penulis menyebutnya argumen serius, lalu bilang argumen itu pantas diperlakukan lebih baik daripada slogan yang sekarang jadi wujudnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis menyebutnya argumen serius yang pantas diperlakukan lebih baik daripada slogan, jadi bukan bikinan tanpa dasar dan bukan soal sampingan. Dia juga langsung bilang menyebut rentang nggak menuntut rekomendasi dibuang, jadi keberatan itu bukan alasan mempertahankan kalimat deklaratif.

qs: What does "compression" mean in the second paragraph?
The reduction of a complex finding into a brief statement.
The physical squeezing of air inside a storm system.
The shortening of a forecast to a single quarter ahead.
The habit of misreading percentages that are stated aloud.

qs.evidence: Practitioners defend the compression on grounds of comprehension, and the defence is not absurd.
qs.answer: The reduction of a complex finding into a brief statement.
qs.why: Yang dibela praktisi adalah dua penerjemahan yang memampatkan distribusi jadi satu angka lalu satu kata kerja. Jadi compression di sini pemadatan temuan rumit jadi pernyataan singkat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang dibela praktisi adalah pemadatan distribusi jadi satu angka lalu satu kata kerja. Pemampatan udara badai itu makna teknis lain; horizon satu kuartal cuma contoh ramalan; dan salah baca persentase adalah alasan pembelaan, bukan arti katanya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer regards the public's habit of discounting confident forecasts as a reasonable one."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer regards the public's habit of discounting confident forecasts as a reasonable one.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: That habit is rational, it was taught deliberately, and it will be expensive to unteach.
qs.why: Kalimat terakhir menyebut kebiasaan itu rasional, walau mahal untuk dibongkar. Rasional dan reasonable di sini sepadan, jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh penulis menyebutnya irasional, dan dia nggak. “Not stated” gagal karena penilaiannya ada eksplisit.

topic: how public forecasting strips out uncertainty
author: Sabrina Adiwijaya
setting: an essay on risk communication

title: Forty-Three Brass Rectangles
text:
The plaque on the former market street informs passers-by that the premises operated as a ribbon manufactory from eighteen forty-one, and constitutes a proud element of the town's industrial heritage. Every noun in that sentence was selected by a committee, and nothing on the plaque is untrue, a distinct property from being informative. The difference is precisely where municipal storytelling earns its income; the town maintains forty-three such plaques.

Consider what such a plaque must accomplish simultaneously: it must compress a century into thirty words and satisfy a conservation officer. It must equally avoid alarming the ground-floor tenant, and produce in a stranger mild warmth towards a locality he quits within the hour. Those objectives are not simply distinct; several are opposed. Committee prose of this kind endures because nobody involved is ever obliged to defend a single clause publicly. The resulting genre is recognizable universally: passive verbs, an unspecified plural of employees, and an adjective performing the labour of an absent fact.

The ribbon manufactory, for instance, employed a workforce predominantly female and predominantly under twenty, and ceased trading in eighteen ninety-four following an eleven-week dispute over piece rates. None of this contradicts the term proud, though all of it complicates the term, which is precisely why thirty words cannot accommodate it. The omission is not a conspiracy; it is a consequence of a format selected for economy and subsequently defended as tradition.

I am sceptical of the official remedy, a longer plaque. Length invites a second committee, and a second committee produces the same prose at additional expense. A brass rectangle is brief not because the metal is valuable but because a brief text is approved without delay. What the format actually lacks is not room but candour about its own limits. One clause would accomplish more than another paragraph of warmth. It would concede that the account is partial, that a fuller version exists elsewhere, and that the reader might reasonably distrust a notice bolted to a wall by the authority collecting the rents.

The most useful plaque in the town is on a wall behind the bus station, and was not installed by the council. Somebody has attached a laminated sheet listing the names of the eleven women who organized the eighteen ninety-four dispute, with a note explaining that the official plaque a hundred metres away omits them. It is ugly and will not survive the season, yet performs more historical labour than the brass. Municipal heritage would benefit immediately by treating that sheet as a standard rather than as vandalism. It will not, of course, because the sheet is evidence that the format was a decision.
qs: What relationship does the writer draw between the plaque's brevity and its content?
The committee hid the dispute on purpose when it drafted the wording.
A longer plaque would settle the problem the writer has identified.
The conservation officer wrote the wording used on all the plaques.
The brevity was a budgetary choice later justified as a tradition.

qs.evidence: The omission is not a conspiracy; it is a consequence of a format selected for economy and subsequently defended as tradition.
qs.answer: The brevity was a budgetary choice later justified as a tradition.
qs.why: Teks bilang formatnya dipilih karena biaya, lalu dipertahankan dengan alasan tradisi. Jadi keringkasannya soal anggaran, bukan penyembunyian.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang penghilangan itu bukan konspirasi, jadi bukan penyembunyian yang disengaja. Plakat lebih panjang justru ditolak penulis karena cuma memanggil komite kedua. Dan petugas konservasi cuma satu pihak yang harus dipuaskan, bukan penulis naskahnya.

qs: What does the writer imply about the laminated sheet behind the bus station?
The council will adopt the laminated sheet as a formal standard before winter.
It is better because laminated paper outlasts brass on a wall.
Its usefulness comes from admitting what the official version leaves out.
It proves the ribbon manufactory employed no women at all.

qs.evidence: Somebody has attached a laminated sheet listing the names of the eleven women who organized the eighteen ninety-four dispute, with a note explaining that the official plaque a hundred metres away omits them.
qs.answer: Its usefulness comes from admitting what the official version leaves out.
qs.why: Lembar itu menyebut nama-nama yang dihilangkan plakat resmi dan menyatakan penghilangan itu terang-terangan. Persis kejujuran yang penulis bilang kurang di format resmi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis bilang dewan kota nggak akan mengadopsinya, justru karena lembar itu bukti bahwa formatnya sebuah pilihan. Lembar itu disebut jelek dan nggak akan bertahan semusim, jadi bukan soal daya tahan bahan. Dan pabriknya jelas mempekerjakan tenaga kerja yang kebanyakan perempuan.

qs: What is the writer's tone when he discusses the proposal for a longer plaque?
Drily sceptical about repeating one process at greater expense.
Keen on the prospect of appointing a second committee.
Indignant at the conservation officer's repeated interference.
Nostalgic for the ribbon manufactory and its piece rates.

qs.evidence: Length invites a second committee, and a second committee produces the same prose at additional expense.
qs.answer: Drily sceptical about repeating one process at greater expense.
qs.why: Dia bilang panjang cuma memanggil komite kedua yang menghasilkan prosa sama dengan biaya lebih besar. Itu skeptisisme kering, bukan usulan serius.
qs.whyOthersFail: Komite kedua disebut cuma menghasilkan prosa yang sama dengan biaya lebih besar, jadi bukan hal yang disambut. Petugas konservasi cuma disebut sebagai salah satu syarat format, tanpa kemarahan. Dan pabrik itu dibahas lewat upah satuan dan perselisihan, bukan dengan kerinduan.

qs: What does "candour" mean in the fourth paragraph?
The approval a municipal committee grants to a text.
The brightness of polished brass fixed to a wall.
The mild warmth a stranger feels towards a town.
Openness about what the text itself cannot do.

qs.evidence: What the format actually lacks is not room but candour about its own limits.
qs.answer: Openness about what the text itself cannot do.
qs.why: Penulis menjelaskannya sendiri di kalimat berikutnya: satu kalimat yang mengakui bahwa keterangannya sebagian dan versi lengkapnya ada di tempat lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penulis menjelaskan sendiri maksudnya di kalimat berikutnya: satu klausa yang mengakui keterangannya sebagian dan versi lengkapnya ada di tempat lain. Persetujuan komite, kilau kuningan, dan kehangatan pengunjung semuanya muncul di teks, tapi sebagai hal lain.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The laminated sheet behind the bus station was put up by the town council."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The laminated sheet behind the bus station was put up by the town council.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: The most useful plaque in the town is on a wall behind the bus station, and was not installed by the council.
qs.why: Teks bilang lembar itu bukan pasangan dewan kota, dan kalimat berikutnya menyebut “somebody” yang menempelkannya. Jadi klaimnya salah.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertentangan langsung dengan kalimat itu. “Not stated” gagal karena penulis menyatakan asal-usulnya secara eksplisit.

topic: heritage plaques and the limits of municipal storytelling
author: Tegar Nugroho
setting: a small industrial town with an official plaque scheme

title: Twenty-Four Volumes of Certainty
text:
The set occupies two shelves in my hallway, twenty-four volumes bound in a green that has faded unevenly, printed in nineteen twenty-nine. I acquired it for the equivalent of a modest lunch, roughly what an exhaustive and superseded survey of the universe currently commands. Nobody currently consults it as a source, and it would be imprudent to attempt it. Its value lies in something the compilers would have deemed insulting: a record of how certainty sounds immediately before refutation.

The entry on the atom is the salient instance, and also the least instructive of the set. Far more revealing are the entries where the confidence is grammatical rather than factual, embedded in syntax. Confidence of that kind is invisible to its author, since nothing in the surrounding literature contradicts it. Continents are described as fixed, not because the compilers had examined and rejected the alternative, but because the possibility of their movement did not yet occupy a position from which it could be rejected. The prose contains no hedge, since a hedge requires an opponent, and what one encounters there is not error but the absence of an enquiry.

This is more elusive in one's own period, for precisely the reason that renders it worth attempting. I cannot list the propositions I currently hold that will resemble the fixed continents; if I could list them they would already be under revision. The exercise available to me is weaker and nonetheless serviceable: to notice where my own prose declines to hedge, and to interrogate whether the confidence is earned or merely inherited. Those volumes are a device for that noticing, performing it more effectively than any argument.

There is a self-congratulatory way of reading obsolete encyclopedias, and I have caught myself at it repeatedly. It consists of scoring points against the dead, who cannot revise, and it flatters the reader with a superiority he did nothing to earn. The compilers were not obtuse; they were early, which is a different accusation altogether, since priority in sequence is not a moral defect, though it reliably resembles one from a distance. Virtually every misjudgement they made arose from standing where they stood, the sole position anybody ever occupies.

What remains of them is a tone, the instructive residue of the whole enterprise. Twenty-four volumes were produced by compilers who imagined a general account of everything could be completed and thereafter maintained by supplements. That belief is now unavailable, and its unavailability is a genuine loss as well as a correction. We know more and expect less, and the second clause of that sentence deserves more attention than it customarily receives. The green volumes are not a monument to ignorance but to a confidence structurally impossible to sustain.
qs: What is the writer's main claim about the value of the set?
The set is still a dependable source on the structure of the atom.
It is valuable as a record of unexamined confidence rather than of facts.
The compilers were less able than the reference writers who followed.
Twenty-four volumes show that supplements can keep an account current.

qs.evidence: Its value lies in something the compilers would have deemed insulting: a record of how certainty sounds immediately before refutation.
qs.answer: It is valuable as a record of unexamined confidence rather than of facts.
qs.why: Penulis bilang nilainya bukan pada isinya, tapi pada bagaimana bunyi kepastian ketika kepastian itu hampir terbukti salah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang nggak ada yang memakainya sebagai sumber dan mencobanya pun kurang bijak. Penyusunnya disebut bukan tumpul, cuma datang lebih awal. Dan keyakinan bahwa suplemen bisa merawat satu keterangan umum justru disebut sudah nggak tersedia lagi.

qs: What does the writer suggest about the description of continents as fixed?
It shows the compilers largely suppressed a rival theory they had examined.
It was hedged carefully in the prose that surrounds the entry.
It reflects a question that had not yet been posed, not one rejected.
It makes the entry on the atom equally reliable for most readers today.

qs.evidence: Continents are described as fixed, not because the compilers had examined and rejected the alternative, but because the possibility of their movement did not yet occupy a position from which it could be rejected.
qs.answer: It reflects a question that had not yet been posed, not one rejected.
qs.why: Teks bilang kemungkinan benua bergerak belum menempati posisi yang bisa ditolak. Artinya pertanyaannya belum ada, bukan sudah dijawab keliru.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalimatnya bilang mereka bukan memeriksa lalu menolak alternatifnya, jadi nggak ada teori saingan yang ditindas. Prosanya justru disebut tanpa hedge sama sekali. Dan entri atom disebut contoh yang paling sedikit mengajarkan sesuatu, bukan yang paling bisa dipercaya.

qs: How does the writer regard the habit of mocking obsolete encyclopedias?
As a cheap superiority the writer admits to repeatedly indulging.
As a fair response to compilers who were simply not clever enough.
As a small matter beside what the twenty-four volumes cost.
As a method worth recommending for noticing one's own confidence.

qs.evidence: It consists of scoring points against the dead, who cannot revise, and it flatters the reader with a superiority he did nothing to earn.
qs.answer: As a cheap superiority the writer admits to repeatedly indulging.
qs.why: Dia menyebutnya cara membaca yang menyanjung diri, lalu mengaku ketangkap melakukannya berulang kali. Jadi kritiknya termasuk ke dirinya sendiri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penyusunnya justru disebut bukan tumpul, jadi cemoohan itu nggak adil. Harga setara makan siang sederhana cuma detail pembuka, bukan pokok penilaiannya. Dan metode yang dianjurkan adalah memperhatikan di mana prosa sendiri menolak berhedge, bukan mencemooh yang sudah mati.

qs: What does "hedge" mean in the second paragraph?
A row of shrubs planted along the edge of a field.
A confident assertion of the kind the atom entry makes.
A supplement issued to correct a volume already printed.
A qualifying phrase that limits the force of a claim.

qs.evidence: The prose contains no hedge, since a hedge requires an opponent
qs.answer: A qualifying phrase that limits the force of a claim.
qs.why: Teks bilang hedge butuh lawan: kamu cuma memasang pembatas kalau ada posisi tandingan. Jadi maksudnya frasa pembatas yang melunakkan klaim.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang hedge butuh lawan, jadi maksudnya frasa pembatas yang melunakkan klaim. Barisan perdu makna harfiah yang salah konteks, pernyataan percaya diri justru kebalikannya, dan suplemen adalah terbitan tambahan bukan frasa.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer regards the disappearance of that belief as something regrettable and not merely an improvement."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer regards the disappearance of that belief as something regrettable and not merely an improvement.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: That belief is now unavailable, and its unavailability is a genuine loss as well as a correction.
qs.why: Kalimatnya menyebut hilangnya keyakinan itu kerugian sungguhan sekaligus koreksi. Klaimnya cuma menyusun ulang kalimat itu, jadi True.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh dia menyebutnya semata kemajuan. “Not stated” gagal karena dua sisi penilaiannya ada di satu kalimat.

topic: an obsolete encyclopedia as a record of unexamined confidence
author: Untari Widodo
setting: a second-hand set from nineteen twenty-nine on a hallway shelf

title: Priced as a Commodity, Behaving as a Promise
text:
The arithmetic of an avoided-deforestation credit rests on a counterfactual, and a counterfactual cannot be measured. The claim is that a particular hectare would have been cleared and was not, which requires an account of what a landowner intended to do in a year that never occurred. Verification bodies handle this by constructing a baseline from regional trends, and the baseline is then treated, in the resulting certificate, as though it were an observation, so everything downstream of that substitution inherits its uncertainty.

Nothing about this is fraudulent in itself, and the alternative is not obviously preferable. Conservation has always been financed by arguments that resist audit, and the older arguments about beauty and duty raised considerably less money. The offset market has channelled substantial sums towards forests that would otherwise have attracted none, and purity is a luxury available to anybody who never has to raise a budget. Defenders of the mechanism are entitled to point at intact canopy and ask what the objection actually amounts to.

The objection is that the instrument is priced as a commodity while behaving as a promise. A tonne of carbon dioxide is fungible by definition; the avoided clearance of one particular ridge is not. Fungibility is a property of the accounting unit rather than of the ridge itself. When an airline retires a credit, it acquires something resembling a delivered good, and its accountants treat it accordingly. The asymmetry registers on the buyer's balance sheet as certainty and on the forest as a hope, and only one of those parties is audited annually.

Reform proposals cluster around improved baselines, and improved baselines will not resolve a category error. Sharper statistics narrow the interval around an unobservable quantity; they do not convert it into an observed one. Nobody in the sector disputes the arithmetic, and almost everybody disputes the label. What might genuinely assist is a candid change of vocabulary: describing the payment as a subsidy for stewardship rather than as the purchase of an offset. The sums would remain, the forests would remain, and the accounting fiction would not.

That proposal will be resisted, and the reason is instructive rather than sinister. A subsidy has to be justified politically each year, whereas an offset discharges an obligation instantly and requires no further conversation. The awkwardness is therefore not technical but political: the market exists in its present form because it converts a moral question into a settled transaction. Anybody wishing to reform it must first explain what becomes of the demand once the settlement is withdrawn.
qs: What is the writer's central objection to the offset instrument?
Better baselines would remove the uncertainty in the counterfactual.
An offset is sold as a delivered good although it remains a promise.
Conservation raised more money from arguments about beauty and duty.
Airlines should be audited annually by the verification bodies.

qs.evidence: The objection is that the instrument is priced as a commodity while behaving as a promise.
qs.answer: An offset is sold as a delivered good although it remains a promise.
qs.why: Keluhan intinya: instrumennya dihargai seperti komoditas padahal isinya janji. Pembeli mencatatnya sebagai barang yang sudah diterima.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang baseline yang lebih tajam cuma menyempitkan interval di sekitar besaran yang nggak teramati, tanpa menyelesaikan kesalahan kategori. Argumen keindahan dan kewajiban justru disebut mengumpulkan uang jauh lebih sedikit. Dan usul penulis adalah mengganti kosakata jadi subsidi, bukan mengaudit maskapai.

qs: What does the writer imply about why his own proposal will be resisted?
Verification bodies would lose the fees their baselines earn them.
The forests would be cleared as soon as the payments stopped.
A subsidy would reopen each year a question that an offset closes.
Airlines take no interest in the condition of intact canopy.

qs.evidence: A subsidy has to be justified politically each year, whereas an offset discharges an obligation instantly and requires no further conversation.
qs.answer: A subsidy would reopen each year a question that an offset closes.
qs.why: Subsidi harus dibenarkan ulang tiap tahun, sedangkan offset melunasi kewajiban seketika. Jadi penolakannya soal enggan membuka lagi perdebatan yang sudah ditutup.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ongkos badan verifikasi nggak pernah disebut. Teks bilang uang dan hutannya tetap ada kalau kosakatanya diubah, jadi bukan penebangan begitu pembayaran berhenti. Dan pembeli digambarkan mencatat kredit itu di neracanya sebagai barang yang sudah diterima, jadi bukan tanpa kepentingan.

qs: How does the writer treat the defenders of the offset market?
As dishonest people who know the baselines have been invented.
As victims of accountants who misread what a certificate says.
As beside the point next to the arithmetic of a tonne of carbon.
As making a fair point the writer's objection has to survive.

qs.evidence: Defenders of the mechanism are entitled to point at intact canopy and ask what the objection actually amounts to.
qs.answer: As making a fair point the writer's objection has to survive.
qs.why: Dia bilang pembela mekanisme itu berhak menunjuk tajuk hutan yang masih utuh dan menanyakan bobot keberatannya. Itu pengakuan bahwa argumen mereka valid.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang nggak ada yang curang dalam mekanisme itu, jadi bukan orang yang berdusta. Akuntan disebut memperlakukan kredit sesuai wujudnya, bukan salah baca. Dan keberatannya bukan soal aritmetika satu ton, yang justru disebut nggak dipersoalkan siapa pun.

qs: What does "fungible" mean in the third paragraph?
Able to be confirmed by verification from outside.
Interchangeable with any other unit of the same kind.
Priced above the level a subsidy would ever reach.
Legally binding on the party issuing the document.

qs.evidence: A tonne of carbon dioxide is fungible by definition; the avoided clearance of one particular ridge is not.
qs.answer: Interchangeable with any other unit of the same kind.
qs.why: Satu ton karbon dioksida sama nilainya dengan ton mana pun, sementara satu bukit tertentu nggak bisa ditukar. Jadi fungible artinya bisa saling ganti.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalimatnya mempertentangkan satu ton karbon dioksida dengan satu bukit tertentu, jadi artinya bisa saling ganti. Verifikasi eksternal, tingkat harga, dan keterikatan hukum semuanya soal lain yang lewat di paragraf sekitarnya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The verification bodies that construct baselines are paid by the buyers of credits."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The verification bodies that construct baselines are paid by the buyers of credits.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Verification bodies handle this by constructing a baseline from regional trends
qs.why: Teks cuma bilang badan verifikasi menyusun baseline dari tren regional. Siapa yang membayar mereka sama sekali nggak disebut, jadi Not stated.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” butuh keterangan pendanaan yang nggak ada. “False” butuh bukti pembayarnya pihak lain, dan itu juga nggak ada.
